Building on the structural results of Koolen, Yang and Yang, this improves the known clique-number bound to the optimal leading constant $1/4$, whose asymptotic sharpness follows from Yang and Koolen's construction.

papers.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal, and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions. As a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop. These results suggest that a poor actor can still teach well, because judging an action after the episode ends reveals the consequences that acting must anticipate. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/decision-agents.

papers.title: The de Haas--van Alphen effect in a two-dimensional nematic Fermi fluid
papers.abstract: Quantum oscillations are widely used to probe the Fermi surface of metals, but their behavior becomes more complex when electronic interactions can spontaneously deform that surface. We investigate this interplay in a two-dimensional model of interacting electrons capable of developing nematic order, using a uniform mean-field approximation in a perpendicular magnetic field. We show that Landau quantization can favor or suppress nematic order as the field varies, producing alternating isotropic and nematic regions near a Pomeranchuk instability, with both continuous and first-order transitions. Conversely, the evolving nematic order modifies the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations in ways that depend on the thermodynamic conditions. At fixed chemical potential, the oscillation frequency can change significantly even when the cyclotron mass varies only modestly. At fixed particle density, conservation of the Fermi-surface area preserves the leading Onsager frequency, while the cyclotron mass and harmonic amplitudes remain sensitive to nematic order. The magnetization and magnetic susceptibility provide additional signatures of the nematic transitions. These results show how quantum oscillations can both reveal and influence electronic order, offering a framework for interpreting experiments in strongly correlated metals.

papers.title: Solovay's Construction via Proof Search
papers.abstract: Solovay's celebrated result establishes the arithmetical completeness of GL by embedding Kripke models into arithmetic. We provide an alternative proof of the arithmetical completeness of GL, in which we instead embed failed proof searches into arithmetic. Our methodology requires only a well-behaved sequent calculus and does not rely on completeness with respect to Kripke semantics or any of its variants. This approach is particularly interesting for logics that do not behave well semantically, such as ER, for which we also provide a new proof of arithmetical completeness.

papers.title: From Metric to Strong Metric Regularity: A Second Subderivative Criterion for Definable Prox-regular Subdifferentials
papers.abstract: We investigate when metric regularity of a subdifferential mapping rules out multiple local inverse branches and therefore upgrades to strong metric regularity. Let $h:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]$ be proper, lower semicontinuous, definable, prox-regular, and subdifferentially continuous at $(\bar x,\bar v)\in\operatorname{gph}(\partial h)$. We characterize this ``upgrade'' through the second subderivative $q = \mathrm{d}^2h(\bar x|\bar v)$ of $h$. If $\partial h$ is metrically regular, then it is strongly metrically regular if and only if the set of negative curvature directions of $q$ on the unit sphere of $\operatorname{span}(\operatorname{dom}(q))$ has Euler characteristic $0$ or $2$. We also prove a simpler and directly verifiable sufficient condition: nonnegativity of $q$ on the lineality space $\operatorname{dom}(q)\cap(-\operatorname{dom}(q))$ forces a quadratic lower bound for $q$ on its entire domain and hence yields strong metric regularity. In particular, if $\bar x$ is a local minimizer and $\bar v=0$, the second subderivative is nonnegative on its domain $\operatorname{dom}(q)$, which proves a conjecture of Drusvyatskiy, Mordukhovich, and Nghia in the definable setting. The derived principle strengthens this conjecture by replacing local minimality with a weaker second-order condition on the lineality space.

papers.title: UAV-Flow++: A Unified Suite for Benchmarking and Learning Language-Guided UAV Flight
papers.abstract: Language-guided UAV navigation has largely focused on long-horizon route planning, leaving short-range, object-relative flight maneuvers underexplored. To address this gap, we formulate Flying-on-a-Word (Flow), a task requiring a UAV to convert concise natural-language instruction, egocentric visual observation, and current state dynamics into continuous flight actions. Flow encompasses both primitive motion commands and complex object-interactive behaviors, assessing motion intent comprehension and spatial context grounding. To enable policy learning and closed-loop evaluation, we introduce UAV-Flow, a comprehensive dataset comprising 30,692 expert-piloted real-world trajectories across eight distinct motion categories, alongside 10,109 simulation trajectories in the UAV-Flow-Sim environment equipped with task-specific completion criteria. Furthermore, we develop FlowVLA, which undergoes imitation pretraining on mixed real-sim demonstrations and online post-training via Tail-Aware GRPO (TGRPO). By leveraging group reward distributions, TGRPO effectively reinforces high-reward action sequences. Evaluated on 273 held-out UAV-Flow-Sim episodes, pretrained FlowVLA achieves a mean success rate of 75.58%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 6.72 percentage points, which TGRPO post-training further elevates to 93.16% with superior sample efficiency. Physical UAV experiments demonstrate robust execution of object-relative commands in both indoor and outdoor real-world scenes. Together, Flow establishes a novel benchmark and learning framework for language-conditioned flight maneuvers.

papers.title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
papers.abstract: State space models (SSMs) are an emerging alternative to Transformers. SSMs offer linear-time inference and parallel training, but most implementations make the parallel scan efficient by making the recurrence diagonal: each channel of the hidden state is multiplied by an input-dependent real or complex number. These numbers commute, so the state records which inputs occurred but not their order. We formalize this with representation theory, which explains and fixes the state-tracking failures previously reported for SSMs. The state update defines a linear representation of the monoid of input sequences, and we show that an SSM tracks a group at every sequence length exactly when that group is a quotient of the group generated by its transition matrices. Two consequences follow. Diagonal real- and complex-valued SSMs can track only commutative groups, while the transition matrices of any SSM that can track a group must split into independent blocks over the real, complex, and quaternion numbers. We then introduce HyperSSM, which adds quaternion channels while keeping linear-time inference and parallel training. Trained only on final answers, HyperSSM solves the group tasks of recent state-tracking benchmarks exactly with at most five state numbers. This includes $S_5$ with 32 generators, where previous SSMs are at chance, and HyperSSM generalizes to sequences 25 times longer than those seen in training. Because the theory says what the transitions must encode, the learned weights of the linear recurrence can be interpreted directly. We demonstrate this by recovering the calibration of a real gyroscope, the rotations of imperfect qubit gates and the geometry of protein backbones.

papers.title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation systems attach citations to attribute claims to their sources. These citations frequently misstate provenance, and standard verification cannot detect this. We measure provenance by counterfactual value substitution: a fact in the retrieved passages is replaced with a false variant and the model re-queried. We find that across five sizes of one model family and a second comparator family, 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims derive from parametric memory rather than the retrieved context. At the most conservative substitution distance these figures are 4.6% and 8.5% on the two models we tested at it, with the rate rising with model size within a family. We further find that natural language inference verification, the standard approach, gives results indistinguishable from chance across models, even when restricted to the cited passage. We determine that the cause is structural: a model answering from memory selects a citation that agrees with its output. Comparing ten attribution methods on identical claims, the contrast between the model's distribution with and without context best separates provenance. Acting on that signal does not improve provenance honesty at these base rates. The resulting detector is hence still not accurate enough to act on: it measures what the model knew rather than what it used, and separating those remains the open problem.

papers.title: XBot-Omni: An Omni-Modal Model for Embodied Understanding and Interaction
papers.abstract: Embodied interaction requires an agent to integrate multimodal perception with verbal and nonverbal behaviors to effectively communicate its intentions, including speech, body motion, and facial expressions. We present XBot-Omni, a Thinker--Talker--Actor architecture that extends the Omni paradigm to robotic modalities, including body motion and facial expressions, with ``X'' representing the extensibility to robotic-specific modalities. The Thinker processes text, images, audio, and video to formulate contextually appropriate responses, which are then realized by the Talker and Actor through speech and coordinated bodily expressions, respectively. In this report, we innovatively introduce the concept of ``Actor'' as a dedicated component for embodied agents: a coordinated, streaming module that leverages the native representations of the Thinker and Talker within an end-to-end pipeline, introducing only modest latency overhead. This unified architecture enables multimodal generation conditioned on omni-modal inputs directly to prevent information loss in staged designs. We comprehensively evaluate XBot-Omni across seven benchmarks, demonstrating strong multimodal understanding capabilities on both general-domain and robot-centric videos, as well as high-quality, natural, and well-coordinated motion generation. Furthermore, our results validate its capability to generate embodied multimodal responses directly from omni inputs, meeting the diverse requirements of embodied interaction. XBot-Omni enables robots not only to perceive the omni world but also to express themselves through speech and bodily behaviors, extending Omni models from conversational interaction to embodied communication in physical environments.

papers.title: Inner Product Regularization for Imitation Learning
papers.abstract: Robots that learn from demonstrations should extrapolate their policy despite state perturbations such as sensor noise, scene variation, and compounding errors. One approach to this robustness is regularization. Prior regularizers consider each state on its own and limit how sensitive the policy is to any perturbation at that state. By contrast, we explore how the policy's output shifts when given the same perturbation at different states. Our insight is that, locally, the robot should respond to state perturbations in a consistent manner: e.g., if changing an irrelevant object position does not impact the policy at one state, that same change should not shift the policy output at a nearby state. Applying this insight, we develop inner product regularization (InneR). We show that the inner product on action space induces an inner product on state space through the policy Jacobian (the Fisher information for stochastic policies), and that the null space of this inner product governs which state perturbations have a first-order effect on the policy. By clustering states whose inner products are aligned, averaging the inner products within each cluster, and minimizing the smallest eigenvalues of that average, InneR shapes the learned policy so that nearby states share a common null space. InneR enforces consistent responses to perturbations without limiting policy expressiveness, and can be appended to existing imitation learning pipelines for deterministic or stochastic policies. In simulated experiments, InneR makes learned policies more robust to irrelevant state dimensions and shifts between training and test distributions, whereas norm penalties often perform worse than behavior cloning. On a real robot arm performing three manipulation tasks, InneR raises the average success rate of a diffusion policy from 18% to 57% without additional data.

papers.title: Efficient computation of PEPS gradients for optimized quantum state preparation on 2D topologies
papers.abstract: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental subroutine for quantum computation. For complex, entangled initial states it is, however, difficult to prepare shallow quantum circuits approximating the state with sufficient accuracy. Tensor networks provide a promising avenue of synthesis of such circuits, but most approaches employ 1D Matrix Products States, which struggle to accurately express entangled states in higher dimensions. Here we present a hardware topology-aware quantum state preparation method based on gradient optimization of 2D projected entangled pair states (PEPS). Our approach combines local disentanglement, with global fine tuning based on PEPS gradient optimization. Towards this end we describe an efficient procedure for PEPS gradient computation. We test the convergence and performance of our method in numerical simulations.

papers.title: Covering numbers and pcf theory
papers.abstract: We develop a general technique for deriving covering theorems from pcf-theoretic information by refining sequences of partitions. The method gives a direct proof of Shelah's cov vs. pp theorem and analogous results for diagonal coverings associated with normal ideals and covering modulo arbitrary $σ$-complete ideals, where $σ$ is regular and uncountable. In each setting, we characterize the covering invariant through pseudopowers, true cofinalities of reduced products of progressive sets, and appropriate notions of cofinality in (possible non-progressive) intervals of regular cardinals.

papers.title: A hierarchical graph neural network for efficient particle-resolved prediction of granular flow dynamics
papers.abstract: Graph neural surrogates for granular flow can resolve the motion of individual grains, but propagating information across a large amount of grains requires repeated, costly updates on the full particle graph. This study introduce a Hierarchical Coarse-Grained Graph Neural Network (HCG-GNN) that couples direct interactions between neighboring grains with information exchange on two coarser graphs of occupied spatial cells. In discrete element method (DEM) benchmarks of granular flows down incline planes, HCG-GNN captured key flow characteristics, including front propagation, lateral spreading, deposition morphology, free surface evolution, internal shear behavior, and energy conversion. Results also show that preserving grain-specific features as coarse information returned to the particle graph and integrating predicted accelerations to advance particle motion both improved multi-step accuracy. With 5 of its 7 message-passing steps performed on coarse graphs, HCG-GNN achieved accuracy comparable to a conventional particle-level GNN with a 6.47-fold training speedup and 46.2% lower GPU memory use. A model trained on up to 5000 grains predicted a 2 s release of 10000 grains in 31 s, compared with 2000 s for DEM under the benchmark conditions. This combination of speed and grain-scale resolution supports particle-resolved inverse design, with prescribed runout or discharge targets guiding the search for suitable geometries and grain dynamics revealing the basis for differences in performance.

papers.title: Algebraic and geometric aspects of Demazure weaves
papers.abstract: These are notes to supplement my talks at the Current Developments in Mathematics Conference in 2026. They are an expository account of recent work in the study of braid varieties and their relation to low-dimensional contact and symplectic topology. A driving theme is the development and use of Demazure weaves to construct cluster algebra structures on the coordinate rings of such braid varieties.

papers.title: Higher integrability for parabolic $p$-Laplace equations with gradient-dependent sources
papers.abstract: This paper aims to establish higher gradient integrability away from the initial time for solutions to parabolic $p$-Laplace equations with general gradient-dependent lower-order terms throughout the singular and degenerate regimes. For this purpose, we develop an elliptic reconstruction argument based on an $L^2$-valued temporal Hölder estimate, thereby transferring the problem to elliptic estimates and quantitative control of the reconstruction error. In particular, our approach yields an explicit higher-integrability exponent. We further construct counterexamples illustrating that bounded continuous initial data alone are insufficient to ensure higher gradient integrability up to the initial time. Finally, we provide counterexamples demonstrating that gradient-dependent lower-order terms can prevent temporal Lipschitz regularity.

papers.title: Effects of Lensing by Sgr A* on Semicoherent Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves. I. Signal Model and Mismatch Studies
papers.abstract: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.

papers.title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are trained and ranked on datasets that each vary one design family in one flow domain. Such datasets cannot test the least that an aerodynamic foundation model must do: predict CFD-quality incompressible flow in seconds for new shapes in new enclosures. On DrivAerML, larger models and longer training barely lower Transolver's error; doubling the training cases cuts it by about 12% up to 400 cases, exhausting the dataset. We introduce AeroZoo, a benchmark and training corpus of 3,815 time-mean solutions to the unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) equations with a transition model, across seven geometry families, eight enclosure configurations and Reynolds numbers from $10^3$ to $10^8$. Each sample poses a well-posed PDE problem in the form a solver receives it: the boundary meshes grouped by condition type, the prescribed values and the fluid properties. The 2,816 samples with a stable time mean form the canonical benchmark: two tasks, engineering metrics and 22 frozen splits, disjoint in geometry, that hold out geometry families, enclosures, boundary-condition layouts and Reynolds ranges. On the random split, boundary-condition tokens cut GeoTransolver's median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of the inlet speed in single-seed runs (uniform inlet flow: 11.0%). ISLA, a transformer for boundary-driven PDEs, reaches 5.3% over four seeds, about 4 times the change from a finer mesh. On the same test samples, a held-out geometry family barely changes ISLA's error relative to uniform flow, and a held-out enclosure or boundary-condition layout raises it 2.4 to 9.2 times. The data and the scoring code will be released.

papers.title: Convergence rates for smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) with nonlinear pressure
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative convergence results for the smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) method approximating the compressible Euler equations with nonlinear pressure laws $ρ^γ$, $γ\geq 2$. Our approach is based on a nonlocal approximation of the pressure force that preserves the energy structure of the original system, including an exact energy balance. Using the relative entropy method, we prove convergence towards smooth solutions of the compressible Euler equations as the nonlocality parameter $\varepsilon\to0$, with algebraic convergence rates and an explicit algebraic relationship between $\varepsilon$ and the number of particles $N$. In particular, we obtain quantitative convergence rates for the density in the Wasserstein distance and negative Sobolev norms, and for the momentum in the flat metric. A key feature of our analysis is that it applies to measure-valued densities in the nonlocal system, providing a unified framework for both continuum and particle solutions. Our results extend the existing rigorous convergence theory for SPH beyond quadratic pressure ($γ=2$) to general nonlinear pressure laws with $γ\geq 2$ on the periodic domain.

papers.title: Reentrant Nematicity from Landau Quantization near a Pomeranchuk Instability
papers.abstract: Landau quantization can induce nematic order in a two-dimensional Fermi liquid that is isotropic at zero magnetic field. Using a mean-field theory near a quadrupolar Pomeranchuk instability, we show that varying the magnetic field produces alternating nematic and isotropic regions, with transitions that can be either continuous or first order. The resulting nematic state also leaves distinctive signatures in the de Haas--van Alphen oscillations. At fixed chemical potential, the field-dependent deformation of the Fermi surface can produce substantial changes in the oscillation frequency, even when the cyclotron mass varies only modestly. At fixed particle density, conservation of the Fermi-surface area preserves the leading oscillation frequency, while the cyclotron mass and harmonic amplitudes remain sensitive to nematic order. These contrasting behaviors provide experimentally relevant signatures of field-induced nematicity and reveal the importance of thermodynamic constraints in quantum-oscillation measurements.

papers.title: K3 tails in the KSBA moduli of Kunev surfaces
papers.abstract: In the context of compact moduli spaces of Kollár, Shepherd-Barron, and Alexeev stable surfaces, a degeneration can acquire an exceptional K3 component in the limit, or more simply a K3 tail. We study this phenomenon for Kunev surfaces: minimal surfaces of general type with $K^2=p_g=1$ that arise as $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^2$-covers of the projective plane branched along two general cubics and a line. We classify the K3 tails that occur when the branch curve degenerates to a singular curve with a non-log canonical isolated semi-quasihomogeneous singularity, and describe the corresponding boundary strata. This builds on the Kerr-Laza classification of K3 tails arising from isolated semi-quasihomogeneous hypersurface singularities.

papers.title: Learning Dynamics of the Influencer's Game in Resource Landscapes
papers.abstract: Across domains as varied as ecology, economics, and online platforms, individuals are incentivized to position themselves within resource-rich strategy spaces. In this work we introduce a new spatial game framework called the influencer's game. Within this new framework players' strategies are represented as positions within a trait space. Players then receive a share of a portion of a resource based on their relative influence at that resource's points traits. For the influencer's game, we show that there is a unique symmetric Nash equilibrium that exists under strict log-concavity of the influence kernel. Using the unique equilibrium we show that the stability of the system depends on the influence kernel's parameters, number of players, and the resource distribution shape. For any dimension we demonstrate a stability threshold that depends on both the scatter and curvature of the players. When this threshold is crossed, the symmetric equilibrium destabilizes and gives way to a variety of bifurcation types; including, specialist clusters, limit cycles, and sub-games that reproduce the larger game's structure. We ground these results using real-world data for resources as a demonstration of the game's application. Finally we extend the game dynamics to use multi-agent reinforcement learning and further show that the predicted bifurcation structure persists under partial observability and discretized strategy spaces. In all, the influencer's game provides a novel framework for predicting when competitive pressure drives convergence versus fragmentation with possible applications across domains.

papers.title: Gauge aspects of teleparallel gravity and Noether's second theorem
papers.abstract: We examine the gauge structure of the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) from the perspective of Noether's second theorem. We show that diffeomorphisms and local Lorentz transformations are the gauge symmetries of TEGR, as these are the only variational symmetries that give rise to Noether identities. We then discuss the distinct roles of these two symmetries and their implications for the gauge-theoretic interpretation of gravity. Finally, we discuss consequences of these observations for the role of translations in gauge theories of gravity and the coupling of matter in TEGR. In particular, we demonstrate that the matter coupling prescription is uniquely determined and coincides with that of general relativity, including in the case of spinor fields.

papers.title: HiVE-VQA: Hierarchical Interaction via Volumetric Embedding for Video Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: The proliferation of user-generated video content has made accurate and robust no-reference video quality assessment (NR-VQA) a highly important challenge. Existing research increasingly relies on architecturally complex multi-branch pipelines or computationally intensive fine-tuning of single-branch backbones. In this paper, we investigate whether a single frozen video foundation model can serve as an effective NR-VQA backbone, and propose HiVE-VQA, the first framework (to our knowledge) to apply a JEPA-based video encoder to this task. HiVE-VQA extracts token grids from multiple depths of a pre-trained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder and stacks them into a hierarchical spatio-temporal volume, which a compact 3D convolutional head fuses across its layer, spatial, and temporal axes, combining low-level distortion cues from shallow layers with the semantic and temporal context captured at greater depths. The encoder remains frozen throughout, so only the head is trained: 5.2M parameters (5.7\% of the total), with no auxiliary multi-modal models and an inference cost that is invariant to video resolution. Trained solely on LSVQ and evaluated without any fine-tuning, HiVE-VQA outperforms 17 state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods in SROCC and PLCC on both intra-dataset (LSVQ-test, LSVQ-1080p) and cross-dataset (KoNViD-1k, LIVE-VQC) benchmarks. These results indicate that hierarchical, depth-wise fusion of features from a single frozen video foundation model provides a more effective and efficient basis for NR-VQA than task-specific multi-network fusion. Code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/RobHam99/HiVE-VQA.

papers.title: Enhancing Preference Detection using Eye Movement Cascade and Multilayer Combinatorial Fusion
papers.abstract: Understanding how visual attention influences human preference formation is a fundamental problem in consumer behavior and cognitive science. In this work, we investigate how eye movement patterns can be used to predict preference decisions when subjects compare two alternatives. To address this problem, we analyze an eye-tracking dataset, where subjects view pairs of face images and their gaze behavior is recorded throughout the decision process. We model this problem using multiple machine learning classifiers and apply the Multi-layer Combinatorial Fusion (MCF) framework to iteratively combine diverse models. The MCF framework expands models to a large pool of model fusions and then reduces them based on cognitive diversity, repeating this process across layers until diversity diminishes. Experimental results show that MCF significantly improves performance over individual models. The best single model achieves a Pre@k of 0.90, which is improved to 0.9143 after the first layer of MCF, and further increased to 0.9286 in the second layer. This progression demonstrates that the second layer not only surpasses the performance of the first layer but also outperforms the best individual model, highlighting the effectiveness of leveraging diversity through multi-layer fusion.

papers.title: A neural quantum state variational Monte Carlo study of Aharonov-Casher bands
papers.abstract: We use neural-network-based variational Monte Carlo to investigate the competition between fractional Chern insulators and generalized Wigner crystals in the Aharonov-Casher Hamiltonian, a continuum model for moiré materials. We introduce a variational wave function inspired by flux attachment that captures fractionalized phases and, by comparing its energy with that of a Slater--Jastrow ansatz that captures crystalline phases, we determine the phase diagram at fractional fillings in regimes of strong band mixing and for system sizes beyond the reach of other methods. We find that discrete translation symmetry, encoded in a nonuniform quantum geometry, affects fractionalized states at filling fractions $ν=1/3$ and $ν=2/3$ differently, and that band mixing can stabilize incommensurate crystalline ground states. Our results further reveal the delicate competition between topological and non-topological crystalline phases.

papers.title: A Convex-Analytic Reformulation for Poisoning Attacks on Logistic Regression
papers.abstract: We study data poisoning attacks on logistic regression with $\ell_2$-regularization, where an attacker chooses the features of a fixed number of injected observations with prescribed labels to maximize the logistic loss on the clean training data. Strong convexity of the defender's problem yields an exact reformulation through its first-order optimality conditions. Using convex conjugacy of the softplus function, we replace the sigmoid relations by a single convex optimality-gap inequality and express the attacker's objective as a concave function. A change of variables makes the stationarity condition affine, leaving bounded bilinear equalities as the only nonconvex constraints. We derive finite bounds on all variables involved in these equalities, including a global bound on the coefficient norm and tighter bounds obtained by preprocessing based on convex optimization. Experiments on eight binary classification datasets evaluate attack effectiveness and compare the two reformulations when solved with \textsf{SCIP}. Attacks obtained by local optimization degrade predictive performance on most datasets, while the convex-analytic formulation produces substantially stronger reported dual bounds within a fixed time limit.

papers.title: FORGE: Force-Aware Multi-Granularity Control for Efficient Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.abstract: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires coordinated locomotion, balance regulation, and manipulation under frequent contacts, making teleoperated demonstration collection difficult: a practical controller must simultaneously provide precision, stability, and contact awareness. We propose FORGE, a force-aware multi-granularity control system with a coarse-to-fine command space spanning velocity navigation, planar foot placement, wrist-pose tracking, and optional force-conditioning inputs. Policy training requires no full-body human motion trajectories or joint-angle references; deployment consumes only sparse bilateral wrist poses relative to the pelvis, coarse motion commands, and optional desired wrist-load inputs. For sustained contact, FORGE combines a momentum observer with a learned correction trained using simulator contact-force supervision. At deployment, it estimates low-frequency, wrist-equivalent interaction forces from proprioception and reconstructed low-level arm PD torques, without wrist force/torque sensors. A quasi-static virtual-target loop uses this estimate and an optional desired applied-force input to adapt the wrist target. A frozen locomotion prior and asymmetric residual actions stabilize manipulation-induced whole-body corrections. Experiments evaluate unified-control stability, task-space tracking, quasi-static wrist-equivalent force estimation, squeezing forces during sustained contact with a rigid box, and downstream diffusion-policy execution of a squat-and-lift task across payload conditions. Website: https://bb0928.github.io/forge/.

papers.title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
papers.abstract: A foundational principle of physics is that all coordinate systems are equally valid: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the origin or orientation of the frame, nor on the units or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet the neural surrogates with the lowest errors on today's aerodynamics benchmarks lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation) and from one mesher, rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs in which no learned operation receives a coordinate and every sum over the boundary is a quadrature. Positions enter only as distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, lengths are measured in a unit computed from the boundary, and interior points query the boundary through a tree-accelerated learned kernel without influencing one another. With every boundary cell a token and an exact boundary read, ISLA is equivariant to rigid motions and reflections, invariant to the units of its declared data, and consistent under mesh refinement, while at every setting each query is independent of all other queries. On AeroZoo, 2,816 flows that vary in shape, size, speed, and boundary conditions, its mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1 and 3.3 times lower than any baseline's. On AirfRANS its errors are second only to those of a boundary-integral model (GLOBE) and at least 1.6 times lower than those of Transolver and GeoTransolver.

papers.title: Hardy Spaces and Toeplitz operators on the Hexablock
papers.abstract: The hexablock is a domain in $\mathbb{C}^4$ given by \[ \mathbb{H}=\left\{(a,x_1,x_2,x_3)\in \mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{E}: \sup_{z_1,z_2\in\mathbb{D}} \left| \frac{a\sqrt{(1-|z_1|^2)(1-|z_2|^2)}} {1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2} \right|<1 \right\}, \] where $\mathbb{E}=\left\{(x_1,x_2,x_3)\in\mathbb{C}^{3}: 1-x_1z_1-x_2z_2+x_3z_1z_2\neq 0 \ \text{for all}\ z_1,z_2\in\overline{\mathbb D}\right\}$ is the tetrablock. We introduce a Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb H)$ associated with a canonical measure $μ_{\mathbb H}$ on the distinguished boundary $b\mathbb H$ of the hexablock. We identify $H^2(\mathbb H)$ with a closed subspace of $L^2(b\mathbb H,μ_{\mathbb H})$ and show that it is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. We prove that $\mathbb H$ is the interior of the polynomial convex hull of $Ψ_{\mathbb H}(\overline{\mathbb D}^4)$, where \[ Ψ_{\mathbb H}(ξ_1, ξ_2,λ_1,λ_2) = \left(\frac{λ_1(ξ_1-1)}{2}, \frac{ξ_2(ξ_1+1)}{2}, \ \frac{λ_1λ_2(ξ_1+1)}{2}, \ ξ_1 ξ_2λ_1λ_2 \right). \] We obtain a Brown-Halmos type characterization of Toeplitz operators on $H^2(\mathbb H)$ and a commutant lifting theorem for $\mathbb H$-isometries. We characterize $\mathbb H$-unitaries as the images of commuting quadruples of unitaries under $Ψ_{\mathbb H}$ and present a class of $\mathbb H$-contractions from commuting quadruples having $\overline{\mathbb D}^4$ as a spectral set. We prove an analogous characterization of $\mathbb E$-unitaries and present a class of $\mathbb E$-contractions arising from commuting triples of contractions having $\overline{\mathbb D}^3$ as a spectral set. En route, we also study a weighted Hardy space on the hexablock.

papers.title: Three-body dynamics of the Roper resonance
papers.abstract: The enigmatic Roper resonance is notoriously difficult to determine in lattice QCD. Its quantum numbers, $J^P=1/2^+$, allow for two pions and a nucleon in relative $S$-waves. This absence of a centrifugal barrier leads to strong three-body $ππN$ effects on top of the two-body $πN$ channel -maybe the reason why the Roper is obscured in lattice QCD close to physical masses. Guided by unitarity, an amplitude is constructed in which three-body states are populated through channels in $f_0(500)N(939)1/2^+$, $πΔ(1232)3/2^+$, and $πN(1440)1/2^+$ configurations. The latter channel is required by unitarity in the presence of nucleon exchange, and it contains the nucleon as a bound state, generating the $πN$ channel automatically. With the sub-channels matching the corresponding two-body amplitudes from experiment and nucleon properties, the $P_{11}$ amplitude from SAID is fitted, allowing for an accurate determination of the Roper poles close to the complex $πΔ$ threshold. The Roper poles and residues are, for the first time, determined by explicitly including this and other non-analyticities in combination with strict two- and three-body unitarity. Contour deformation allows for a direct pole search. Systematic uncertainties from the parametrization dependence are quantified. The result for the Roper $S$-matrix pole is $\sqrt{s_R}/{\rm MeV} =1346\pm 2^{+6}_{-3} - i(81\pm 2^{+7}_{-8})$. The amplitude developed here will serve as the central input for a quantization condition that allows for future determinations of the Roper resonance from lattice QCD.

papers.title: Quantum loop symmetric pairs and meromorphic abelian K-matrices
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra, let $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not be a root of unity, and let $\mathbf{U}=U_q(L\mathfrak{g})$ be the corresponding quantum loop algebra, equipped with Hernandez' deformed Drinfeld coproduct. For every diagram involution $τ$ of $\mathfrak{g}$, we introduce a coideal subalgebra $\mathbf{B}$ in a topological completion of $\mathbf{U}$, obtained by adapting the Letzter-Kolb construction of quantum symmetric pairs to the Drinfeld generators of $\mathbf{U}$. We derive necessary constraints on the parameters defining $\mathbf{B}$ from a minimality condition on its intersection with the quantum loop Cartan subalgebra $\mathbf{U}^0\subset\mathbf{U}$. We show that $\mathbf{B}$ yields a topological realization of the quasi-split $\imath$quantum loop group $\mathbf{U}^\imath$ associated with $τ$, in the presentation recently obtained by Lu-Pan, building on work of Chen-Lu-Pan-Ruan-Wang on $\imath$Hopf algebras. By pullback, this gives rise to a rational restriction functor on category O representations. For modules with rational weights and generic values of the spectral parameter, every $\mathbf{U}^\imath$-submodule of a restricted module is stable under the derived quantum loop algebra $\mathbf{U}'$. In particular, irreducibility is generically preserved under restriction for such modules. For $|q|\neq1$ and under explicit assumptions on the quantum Cartan matrix, we construct meromorphic abelian K-matrices whose tensor counterparts yield boundary $q$-characters for both $\mathbf{U}$-modules and $\mathbf{U}^\imath$-modules. Finally, we extend the coideal construction and Drinfeld coaction to shifted $\imath$quantum loop algebras with arbitrary coweight shifts, providing a new approach to $\imath$GKLO representations by restriction from ordinary shifted quantum loop algebras.

papers.title: Augmented Dynamical Sampling under unmodeled Forcing
papers.abstract: We study recovery of an initial state from dynamical samples of a trajectory driven by unknown additive forcing. Measurements against both the original sensors and their images under the adjoint nominal evolution yield one-step residuals that cancel the initial state exactly. These residuals separate forcing estimation from initial-state reconstruction. For a centered Gaussian forcing model with fixed covariance parameters, we combine Gaussian conditioning with canonical dual-frame reconstruction and derive an exact unconditional second-moment identity, including the correlation between the forcing-estimation error and the measurement noise. We also obtain high-probability bounds and identify the irreducible forcing uncertainty through a conditional covariance in the geometry induced by the prior. A hierarchy of augmented sensor systems separates the role of sampling depth in forcing visibility from that of the observation horizon in nominal observability. An image-transport experiment and finite-dimensional and periodic-convolution experiments illustrate the residual correction and the separate roles of sampling depth and observation horizon.

papers.title: On the multidimensional polynomial Szemerédi theorem
papers.abstract: We study the multidimensional polynomial Szemerédi theorem over prime fields. Let $P_1,\dots,P_m\in\F_p[t]^k$ be block independent vector polynomials of degree at most $d$, with $P_i(0)=0$ for every $i$. We prove that there is a constant $c=c(k,m,d)>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large prime $p$, every set $A\subset\F_p^k$ with $|A|\ge p^{k-c}$ contains a configuration $x,x+P_1(t),\dots,x+P_m(t)$ with $t\in\F_p\setminus\{0\}$.

papers.title: Bidimensional Exploration of the warm-Temperature Ionised gaS (BETIS) III. The impact of eDIG on strong-line abundance determinations in galactic halos
papers.abstract: The extraplanar diffuse ionised gas (eDIG) is a key tracer of the feedback processes that connect galactic discs and halos. We present the first study of spatially resolved gas-phase chemical abundances in the eDIG of edge-on galaxies, based on integral field spectroscopy obtained with MUSE. Using a sample of four galaxies from the BETIS sample, we derived maps of the oxygen abundance, 12+log(O/H), the nitrogen-to-oxygen ratio, log(N/O), and the ionisation parameter, log(U), with the HII-CHI-Mistry v5.5 code, and we tested the reliability of this method when different ionisation sources are present. We separated the eDIG into star-formation-dominated and shock-contaminated regimes according to the relative contribution of photoionisation and shocks, and investigated their impact on the derived chemical abundances. We find that HII-CHI-Mistry returns systematically lower O/H and N/O values in shock-contaminated regions, especially for N/O, with typical offsets of ~0.1-0.15 dex relative to star-formation-dominated regions, together with a more homogeneous and lower ionisation state (log(U) ~ -3.1). In contrast, star-formation-dominated regions span a wider range of ionisation parameters (log(U) ~ -3.3 to -2.8) while maintaining approximately solar oxygen abundances. Despite these differences, the abundance offsets are comparable to the sampling step of the HII-CHI-Mistry model grid. The inferred oxygen abundance shows little variation between discs and halos. This is compatible with a scenario in which star formation feedback and galactic fountains efficiently recycle oxygen-rich gas between both components, in agreement with hydrodynamical simulations. In contrast, the N/O ratio shows significant radial and vertical variations, particularly in environments with weaker star formation feedback.

papers.title: Support-Constrained Offline Policy Improvement for Pediatric ECMO from Limited Clinical Data
papers.abstract: Managing children on ECMO (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation) requires balancing short-term physiological stability with the long-term goal of preventing neurological injury. Standard reinforcement learning can propose risky, out-of-distribution actions, while imitation learning is limited to reproducing clinician behavior. We introduce Support-Constrained Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI-SC), an offline reinforcement learning framework that cautiously improves upon expert behavior by restricting optimization to empirically supported state-action pairs and defaulting to the clinician baseline in low-data regions. On 78 pediatric trajectories totaling over 6,000 hours of clinical data, we evaluate our framework using Fitted Q-Evaluation (FQE) and a behavioral disagreement. Additionally, we formalize the performance-safety trade-off by introducing a unified Balance Score ($S(π)$). Our empirical evaluation shows that support-constrained policy improves the Balance Score by 38\% relative to FQI, improves estimated value by 1.28 FQE units over imitation learning, and reduces disagreement with clinician actions by 71\% relative to FQI.

papers.title: $Z_\infty$-algebras: Zinbielification of $B_\infty$ and quasi-shuffle algebras
papers.abstract: Commutative $B_\infty$-algebras provide a natural generalisation of the shuffle and quasi-shuffle algebras, giving deformations of the shuffle algebra. We introduce a Zinbiel analogue in $Z_\infty$-algebras, giving deformations of the half-shuffle Zinbiel algebra. All commutative $B_\infty$-algebras have been shown to be isomorphic to the shuffle algebra, though this isomorphism is not canonical. We show that all $Z_\infty$-algebras are canonically isomorphic to the half-shuffle algebra, which gives a canonical isomorphism to the shuffle algebra for $B_\infty$-algebras arising from $Z_\infty$-algebras. Finally, we explore which $B_\infty$-algebras can be ``Zinbielified'' to a $Z_\infty$-algebra, working through a number of explicit examples in the case of quasi-shuffle algebras and uncovering a very explicit classification of simple Zinbielifications via semigroup cocycles.

papers.title: Rings with unequal $\operatorname{slip-spli}$
papers.abstract: For a unital associative ring $R$, let $\operatorname{silp}(R)$ be the supremum of the injective dimensions of all projective right $R$-modules, and let $\operatorname{spli}(R)$ be the supremum of the projective dimensions of all injective right $R$-modules. We construct an explicit non-Noetherian unital algebra \[R=k1\oplus \frac{k(0\longrightarrow1\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow\cdots)} {\langle\text{all paths of length }2\rangle}\] over any field and prove that $\operatorname{silp}(R)=1$ and $\operatorname{spli}(R)=\infty. $ The algebra is the unitization of the non-unital path algebra of the one-sided infinite ray modulo paths of length two. The example answers the question whether $\operatorname{silp=spli}$ raised by Gedrich and Gruenberg.

papers.title: Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition for Multitemperature Gas Mixtures on Unstructured Meshes
papers.abstract: We present a dynamic domain decomposition method for gas mixtures described by a multi-species BGK model in the regime where collisions between particles of the same species are dominant. In this regime the hydrodynamic limit is a system of Euler equations in which every species keeps its own velocity and temperature, the species being coupled through momentum and energy exchange terms. To decide locally whether this multi-velocity, multi-temperature Euler description is accurate, we extend the moment realizability criterion of Levermore, Morokoff and Nadiga: for each species, a realizability matrix is derived from the Chapman--Enskog expansion of the kinetic model, and its zeroth- and first-order approximations are compared. The indicator involves only macroscopic quantities and is evaluated species by species, so that in the same cell one species may be described by the Euler equations and another one by the kinetic equation. The kinetic solver is therefore used only where, and for the species for which, the indicator detects non-equilibrium effects, such as across shocks or near obstacles in rarefied flows. Both solvers are discretized on unstructured triangular meshes with second-order accuracy in space and time. The kinetic equation is integrated by an asymptotic-preserving IMEX Runge--Kutta scheme, whose limit for vanishing Knudsen number is a consistent discretization of the multi-velocity, multi-temperature Euler system. In the numerical tests the hybrid solution stays close to the kinetic one, while the computational time is reduced by a factor between about three and almost five.

papers.title: Library of peptides: Analysis of a complex reactive mixture with the use of statistical physics and inference
papers.abstract: Self-assembled mixtures enable the exploration of vast chemical diversity, yet characterizing the hundreds of coexisting species they contain remains a major challenge. Standard analytical techniques such as chromatography and spectroscopy produce overlapping signals that cannot be resolved by conventional deconvolution methods, which neglect the concentration correlations imposed by the reactive network. Here, we introduce a framework that bridges statistical physics and analytical chemistry to deconvolute complex self-assembled mixtures from partial spectral data. Inspired by Potts models of protein folding, we express the chemical potential of each compound as a function of a reduced set of parameters-intrinsic building-block energies and pairwise coupling terms between neighboring building blocks in the sequence. Coupling this model with the law of mass action yields equilibrium concentrations across the entire reactive network. The model parameters can be infered by fitting predicted spectroscopic signals to experimentally measured partial data. We demonstrate this approach using dynamic combinatorial libraries (DCLs) of peptides as a model system. Applied to a DCL of 81 peptides, our method resolves the full mixture composition from just 13 overlapping peaks, revealing that lateral couplings dominate the assembly energetics. Beyond DCLs, this strategy offers a general route for analyzing self-assembled systems from partial data and extends naturally to target-driven identification of high-affinity binders.

papers.title: Paper-Faithful Federated Learning: Scientific Checks for Practitioner and Agent Development
papers.abstract: Federated learning experiments can produce reasonable-looking results even when the experiment implementation differs from the intended experimental protocol. Small errors in configuration, data partitioning, aggregation, randomness, evaluation, or checkpoint recovery may therefore affect a comparison without causing the program to fail. We present FedBrew, a research codebase for controlled and reproducible federated learning experiments. Its focus is controlled simulation with checks of specified conditions of the intended experimental protocol. FedBrew uses configuration checks, identifiable client data partitions, checkpoint recovery checks, self-describing run records, and development-time checks of scientific conditions. These checks assess, for example, whether client partitions are disjoint and exhaustive and aggregation weights match the prescribed rule; numerical and recovery checks examine non-finite client model states and interrupted runs. The same structure also provides clear extension points and automated checks for new algorithms, datasets, models, and tasks, whether they are added by researchers or AI coding agents. FedBrew therefore supports reproducible and inspectable FL experiments through checks of specified software and scientific conditions and the run records associated with reported results.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation: Differentiable Length Control for Concise Clinical Reasoning in Smaller Language Models
papers.abstract: Smaller language models (SLMs) make it feasible to deploy clinical natural language processing where large proprietary models are too costly, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning allows them to be specialised on commodity hardware. One obstacle persists after training: on medical tasks these models answer at far greater length than the clinical question requires. In clinical decision support and point-of-care use, where time is short, such verbosity is hard to act on even when the underlying reasoning is sound. Existing length-control methods depend on preference optimisation, reward models, or proprietary teachers that undercut the accessibility making SLMs attractive. We introduce Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation (PECA), which adds a single differentiable conciseness term to the QLoRA supervised fine-tuning objective. Because the token count is discrete and non-differentiable, PECA instead raises the end-of-sequence probability once generation exceeds a token budget, a smooth signal optimised during ordinary training, with no preference data, no auxiliary model, and a single commodity GPU. On a 1.7-billion-parameter model fine-tuned on the medical-o1-reasoning-SFT corpus, PECA reduces mean response length by 72.8% while improving multiple-choice diagnostic accuracy from 40.8% to 44.0%. A sweep over the conciseness strength traces an interpretable accuracy-to-length frontier for balancing brevity and diagnostic completeness.

papers.title: Graded Intersection Types
papers.abstract: We introduce graded intersection types, in which arrow domains are multisets of types with coefficients in a semiring. Boolean and natural number grades recover idempotent and non-idempotent intersection types. We give algebraic conditions on the semiring for subject reduction and expansion in finite systems and in locally finite systems with guarded infinite types. We construct a lifting to multisets of grades corresponding, in this general setting, to lifting the idempotent system to the non-idempotent one. We recall the main existing operational characterisations from the literature, and show some general extensions.

papers.title: STeP-C: Real-Time Neural Compression for Distributed Fiber-Optic Sensing at Scale
papers.abstract: Distributed fiber-optic sensing (DFOS) technologies such as Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) generate continuous, high-resolution spatio-temporal data at rates exceeding hundreds of megabytes per second, creating severe challenges for real-time storage and transmission. While neural compression methods can achieve strong rate-distortion performance on sensing data, prior approaches either require per-segment retraining incompatible with streaming, or have only been validated offline. None have been demonstrated end-to-end on a continuously streaming DAS acquisition system at scale. We present STeP-C (Spatio-Temporal Predictive Compression), a neural compression framework that decouples spatial encoding, temporal prediction, and entropy-optimized residual coding, trained end-to-end with a rate-distortion objective motivated by conditional entropy reduction. Critically, we identify entropy coding as the dominant bottleneck for streaming deployment. We address it through GPU-side symbol computation, cached probability tables, and parallel GIL-free arithmetic coding, together with FP16 inference and batched entropy coding, enabling a full real-time pipeline built around a GPU ring buffer. We validate this pipeline on a live DAS testbed, achieving a 98.85% file size reduction at 31.04 dB full-band PSNR and an average throughput of 535 MB/s, exceeding the 324 MB/s requirement for 1 kHz, 81 km DAS streams. We further show that STeP-C substantially outperforms conventional codecs at practical streaming bitrates, can be applied to unseen channel ranges within the same acquisition system without retraining, and largely maintains downstream detector consistency, with 96.62% high-confidence class agreement and 100% Jaccard similarity on detected event types.

papers.title: AGB Atmospheres in Binary Environments: A First Step with CO5BOLB
papers.abstract: Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars are characterized by complex atmospheric dynamics driven by convection and pulsations. In binary systems, the presence of a companion can further influence these dynamics, potentially affecting mass-loss processes and the morphology of the circumstellar environment, yet this influence on the atmosphere itself remains poorly quantified. This study aims to fill this gap by employing CO5BOLD simulations with a modified gravitational potential to explore how companion mass affects the atmospheric structure of AGB stars. We used radiative hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations with CO5BOLD to model the convective interior and atmosphere of AGB stars. We modified the gravitational potential to include a secondary mass and a centrifugal term, representing the companion as a point-mass potential on a steady, tidally locked circular orbit outside the computational domain, with the Coriolis force neglected. We performed simulations with different companion masses and using singular value decomposition (SVD), we identified the spatial distribution of pulsation energy and quantified its properties. We also examined the density structure to identify anisotropies induced by the companion. We isolate two dynamically distinct regimes, a pulsation-dominated layer and an outer, low-frequency outflow region, whose pulsation properties remain largely unaffected by the companion: their frequency, amplitude, and coherence stay consistent across all models. The density structure, by contrast, responds clearly to the companion, forming a pronounced anisotropy along the binary axis that strengthens with companion mass. This indicates that the intrinsic pulsational dynamics of the AGB star dominate over the tidal influence of the companion within the explored parameter space, while the density structure remains the most sensitive tracer of binarity.

papers.title: Why should $\mathbb{Z}$ be Diophantine in $\mathbb{Q}$?
papers.abstract: We give a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers conditional on the $abc$ conjecture, Dickson's conjecture, and finiteness of $2$-primary parts of Shafarevich--Tate groups. We also discuss some consequences of the existence of a Diophantine definition of the integers in the rational numbers. The goal of this work is to serve as an entry point to recent developments around Hilbert's tenth problem for the rational numbers.

papers.title: Preserve the Vulnerability, Break the Alert: Testing the Robustness of CodeQL Taint Tracking with Natural Rewrites
papers.abstract: Static application security testing (SAST) tools such as CodeQL serve as security gates in continuous integration and code review, and a gate is also read in reverse. When a previously reported alert disappears after a change, developers and the tools around them often take the vulnerability to be gone. That inference holds only if the analyzer is robust to changes that keep the vulnerability. We test this robustness for CodeQL's JavaScript taint tracking with natural, vulnerability-preserving rewrites. A large language model, given only the alert CodeQL exposes and no knowledge of its implementation, rewrites one function along a reported flow as a plausible maintenance change, and we verify by manual audit and controlled experiments that the flaw survives and the alert does not. On 172 flows that CodeQL detects in real npm vulnerabilities, three rewrites per flow silence 26.2% of them, at about USD 0.51 per silenced flow. The same generator, asked only to refactor the same functions with no knowledge of the alert, silences none of them. Every silencing rewrite traces to one of seven gaps at the library-modeling boundary, and 64 of the 70 rewrites cross a gap inside an API CodeQL already models. The largest is the WHATWG URL constructor, which propagates taint to a URL's query components but not to its pathname. The boundary is not specific to CodeQL. 74% of the silencing rewrites also silence an independently built taint analyzer, and 53% escape three analyzers combined. A disappearing alert after an ordinary-looking change is therefore weak evidence that a vulnerability has been fixed, the gaps point SAST developers to narrow and concrete repair targets, and robustness to natural rewrites belongs alongside detection rate in how taint analyzers are evaluated.

papers.title: Exact characterization of three-terminal fermion counting under one-body scattering
papers.abstract: Quantum scattering is a fundamental probe of the scattering region and the quantum dynamics of outgoing particles. In two terminals, the statistics of non-interacting fermions is described by a generalized binomial distribution, that arises from the Pauli exclusion principle, while deviations are a signature of interactions. In this work, we extend this result to a scattering region coupled to three outgoing terminals (or channels), obtaining exact bounds for the statistics of the outgoing fermions. In particular, for two fermions and three terminals, four inequalities involving six measured probabilities determine whether a non-interacting scatterer can explain the observed statistics. Applying these inequalities to recent scattering experiments in cold atoms, we are able to identify a regime where interactions have a significant contribution on the outgoing particles. Therefore, our work opens up the possibility of identifying fermion interactions at the nanoscale in systems that range from mesoscopic conductors to optical traps in cold atoms.

papers.title: Using an energy pixels approach to estimate the size a 2nd Generation DEL must be to train a high-resolution binding model
papers.abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) are commonly used to find small-molecule binders to a target protein. But the hard part is no longer finding a hit. It is building a machine-learning model good enough to guide the medicinal chemistry that follows, one that can resolve the shift in affinity when a chemist changes a single atom. Such a model needs two things from its training data: dense sampling of the small patch of chemical space around the hit, and an adequate number of genuinely tight binders within it. A diverse naive DEL gives neither. It samples an enormous space, so any one neighborhood is covered far too thinly, and the tightest binders are rare. A model trained on that naive DEL data must extrapolate to binders tighter than any it has seen, and that is where models can fail. One way to get training data with both properties is a second-generation DEL built around the hit. We ask how complex that library must be. We treat binding as a sum of small, independent interactions, called pixels on the target and antipixels on the ligand. From the spread of affinities measured in the naive library, with no structural information and nothing yet synthesized, we estimate the complexity such a library must have to supply that dense sampling and those tight binders. The method does two useful things. It turns the number of tight binders a model needs into the number of compounds a library must contain. And it estimates the expected yield of a randomly designed second-generation DEL, so the gain from designing the library with machine learning or active learning can be measured against a baseline, without the expense of a control library as large as the experiment itself.

papers.title: Equidistribution of curves in hypersurfaces of low degree
papers.abstract: We prove that over $\mathbb{C}$, for any smooth projective curve $\mathscr{C}$ and any smooth hypersurface $V \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of degree $d$ such that $n \geq 2^d(d-1)$, Faisant's equidistribution principle holds for $(\mathscr{C},V)$. In other words, for any reasonable set of jet conditions $W$, the moduli space $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ of degree $e$ maps $\mathscr{C} \to V$ satisfying conditions $W$ converges in the Grothendieck ring of complex varieties, after renormalisation, as $e \to \infty$. This provides the dimension and decomposition into irreducible components of $\mathrm{Hom}^e(\mathscr{C},V|W)$ for $e$ large enough. The strategy follows Bilu and Browning's motivic version of the circle method, and Hase-Liu's framework for genus $\geq 1$.

papers.title: Mass gap for the fractional $Φ^4_2$ model
papers.abstract: We present a new, simple and self-contained technique for proving a mass gap for Euclidean quantum field theories in the high-temperature regime using the stochastic quantisation approach. As an application, we establish exponential decay of spatial correlations for the fractional $Φ^4$ model on the plane in the Wick-ordering regime. The key idea is to analyse the propagation of perturbations using the linearised stochastic quantisation equation. Spatial propagation is controlled by an auxiliary random walk, while the potentially destabilising effect of the renormalised nonlinearity is controlled by combining dissipative energy estimates for the nonlinear dynamic with the Boué-Dupuis variational formula.

papers.title: Universal sampling rules for the signed friendship paradox
papers.abstract: The friendship paradox describes a bias in mean degree induced by neighbour sampling. We study signed weighted networks, with transitions proportional to edge magnitudes and signed strength as the vertex score. We characterize all positive initial weights, depending on total strength and score, that guarantee a nonnegative one-step mean change on every connected graph. Without regularity assumptions, the same condition yields stochastic dominance at every fixed time. Continuous admissible rules are precisely total strength multiplied by a positive continuous nonincreasing function of the score. It is enough to test connected graphs with at most five vertices and two vertex types. The bound of five is optimal even for continuous rules; the proof uses a sharp four-vertex energy inequality. The complete score vector alone cannot determine a universally valid initial law with full support. Under marked local convergence and suitable integrability assumptions, we also obtain joint limits for local conditional mean score increments and compute an explicit limiting law and mean for independently signed random regular graphs. Under joint cut-norm convergence of the magnitude and signed kernels and uniformly bounded normalized strengths, we also obtain Wasserstein convergence of the sampling-weighted distributions of normalized local biases and convergence of their means.

papers.title: Generalized ladder operators and construction of families of superintegrable systems with Painlevé VI
papers.abstract: We study quantum Hamiltonians whose separated angular component is expressed through a generic Painlevé VI transcendent. We construct generalized ladder operators for one-dimensional Schrödinger operators with a quadratic spectral variable. For the Painlevé VI angular Hamiltonian these operators satisfy $[N,J_\pm]=\pm2kJ_\pm$, where $N=\sqrt M$, and close through an eighth-degree norm polynomial. Combining the angular shifts with the radial shift operators of the oscillator, Coulomb and free Bessel systems yields higher-order integrals and deformed Racah-type polynomial algebras for the two-dimensional superintegrable models. This construction provides new families of Tremblay-Turbiner-Winternitz (TTW)- and Post-Winternitz (PW)-like Hamiltonians with integrals of arbitrarily high order and Painlevé VI in the potential. This framework also recovers models from the classification of third- and fourth-order integrals as particular cases. For a representative oscillator extension we compute the Casimir explicitly and recover the finite-dimensional energy spectrum from a deformed-oscillator realization. We then analyze the special-solution sector using the explicit families collected by Gromak, Laine and Shimomura. The resulting potentials are organized into a small number of spectral classes, and the distinction between formal zeros of the ladder norm and physical self-adjoint representations is made explicit. The regular nonclassical rational examples are rational Darboux deformations of the trigonometric Pöschl--Teller system and lead to strictly isospectral exceptional-Jacobi sectors or to state-adding representations with an isolated angular level. A singular branch produces an interior inverse-square barrier and a split-domain problem. For one regular exceptional sector and two state-adding sectors we display the polynomial algebras.

papers.title: Bellman Contraction under MMD: A Unified Framework
papers.abstract: We introduce a mathematical framework for studying contraction of the distributional Bellman operator under Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). We show that contraction reduces to conditional positive definiteness of an associated kernel constructed from the base kernel, which we call the Bellman difference kernel. Focusing on radial kernels, we use Schoenberg's theorem to connect this condition to Bernstein functions. This gives contraction criteria that hold in any dimension and can be verified analytically or tested numerically. Our framework unifies known results for the Gaussian RBF, power-distance, and multiquadric kernels. A numerical search identifies 11 new kernels that induce contraction. We also propose chaining, a general construction that produces kernels inducing contraction with any prescribed factor. To reconcile theory with practice, we show that contraction on a set only requires conditional positive definiteness on that set. This explains why the RBF kernel can remain a valid choice when rewards are bounded, despite its lack of global contraction. Finally, we identify a fundamental tradeoff between contraction rate and discriminative power, where kernels that contract faster tend to discriminate less between distributions. Code is available at https://github.com/BaptisteDebes/BellmanContractionMMD

papers.title: CapLite: Prompt-Injection Defense for Small Language Model Agents without Model-Written Security Artifacts
papers.abstract: Enforcement defenses against prompt injection, such as CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard and DRIFT, ask the agent's own model to write a security artifact (a program, a privilege policy, a dependency graph or a constraint list) that code then enforces. We ask whether small language model (SLM) agents can be trusted to write these artifacts. Across 15 open-weight models, 13 of them between 1.7B and 12B parameters, they cannot: the policies, graphs and constraints that the agent's model writes admit attacks on 14 (Progent), 13 (IPIGuard) and 11 (DRIFT) of the models, and CaMeL's programs fail to run in up to 68% of episodes. We present CapLite, which derives its policy from the tool schemas, commits the write calls before any tool result is read, and admits a write only if every argument that decides whom or what it affects is stated in the user's request. This guarantees write integrity: injected text cannot add a write, and no write reaches a recipient, amount, object or destination that the user did not state. No attack succeeds in 13,935 attacked AgentDojo episodes. CapLite reaches utility under attack comparable to CaMeL's (29.0% vs. 27.2%) with fewer tokens than every other enforcement defense and than the undefended agent: 17.1k per episode, 18% of CaMeL's, and the highest utility per token of all enforcement defenses.

papers.title: Designing Institutions for Autonomous AI
papers.abstract: As autonomous AI agents increasingly interact in persistent populations, their collective capabilities and alignment depend not only on individual models, but also on the institutions governing their interactions. Yet AI research has largely focused on individual agents. In this Perspective, we argue that institutional design must become a distinct focus of AI research. Drawing on institutional political economy, social epistemology and organizational theory, we develop seven principles for designing AI institutions that sustain cooperation, enable reliable collective judgments and remain accountable to legitimate human purposes. These address reciprocal contributions, accountable authority, functional differentiation, epistemic pluralism, criticism and correction, human direction, and institutional adaptation. We illustrate their application through machine science, where autonomous research challenges institutions developed around human capabilities and constraints. We then propose an experimental research programme in which matched populations of AI agents operate under alternative institutional arrangements, and describe MoltJournal, an API-first journal for autonomous research agents, as an illustration of how such institutions can be made programmable and observable. Together, these contributions establish institutional design as a research agenda concerned not only with aligning autonomous agents, but with understanding how institutions can transform them into capable, reliable and accountable collectives.

papers.title: Quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces via Sierpiński spaces
papers.abstract: We study quasi-isometry classes of automorphism groups of K3 surfaces using Sierpiński spaces. We introduce K3 surfaces of Sierpiński type and prove that their limit sets are round Sierpiński spaces. For such K3 surfaces, the quasi-isometry class of the automorphism group is equivalent to the rational isometry class of the Néron--Severi lattice together with its integral roots. As an application of this rigidity, we construct infinitely many quasi-isometry classes of hyperbolic automorphism groups in Picard rank 4. This reveals a new phenomenon in Picard rank 4, sharply contrasting with the finiteness of quasi-isometry classes in Picard ranks at most 3 and at least 6.

papers.title: Acoustically driven motion of single molecules at hBN surfaces
papers.abstract: Developments in single-molecule imaging and sensing techniques have enabled direct observation of biomolecular dynamics at interfaces, which has important implications for the fields of membrane biophysics, nanofluidic sensing and transport. However, integrating active surface transport, localization and control over molecule motion remains challenging, limiting further progress in the realization of single-molecule devices. Here, we introduce an integrated surface acoustic wave (SAW)-hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) platform as a contactless actuation platform for directional transport of biomolecules over hBN surfaces. hBN provides an atomically flat surface on which DNA can be confined and still retain in-plane mobility, whereas SAW actuation enables active and guided transport without requiring specific electrical, dielectric or magnetic properties of the biomolecules. Trajectory- and jump-based analyses show that increasing the SAW power leads to higher displacement bias in the streaming direction, resulting in transport velocities along increasingly more linearized trajectories. We thus demonstrate that SAWs can induce tunable directional transport of DNA molecules confined on hBN surfaces, providing a new approach for the on-chip manipulation of biomolecules in nanofluidic systems. Our findings have important implications for the development of advanced single-molecule sequencing platforms and other technologies for biomolecular manipulation and analysis.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal learning improves quantification of pore-space evolution and fluid displacement
papers.abstract: Pore-space evolution and fluid displacement influence how rocks transmit and store fluids, affecting geological carbon storage, underground hydrogen storage and groundwater contaminant transport. A single time-resolved micro-CT experiment may produce tens to hundreds of three-dimensional images, and segmentation is required to quantify physical properties and run image-based simulations. Traditional methods such as thresholding perform poorly on noisy, low-contrast images and need manual adjustment per image; 3D deep learning networks segment each image without temporal information, so their errors vary between images and could be mistaken for physical change. Here we introduce a transformer-based 4D segmentation framework combining spatial and temporal information. It uses sequential images to resolve ambiguous phase assignments and separate physical change from segmentation error. The method is tested on images of mineral dissolution: it measures pore-volume growth and rock boundaries more accurately than an equivalent 3D model that ignores temporal information. It also captures the increase in permeability verified against reference segmentations and flow simulations. The advantage transfers to another dissolution sample without retraining. On two other datasets of fluid displacement, it reduces spurious changes in predicted rock and porosity fluctuations and accurately identifies filling events.
