We evaluate this approach across four prediction tasks on the MIMIC-IV dataset and pancreatic cancer prediction on the CPRD dataset at 1 to 12 month horizons, with tEHR using the Mistral-7B-v0.3 backbone achieving the strongest overall performance. Ablations show that performance declines when clinical descriptions are removed or misaligned, when numerical values are omitted, and when either stage of adaptation is removed, while explicit elapsed-time descriptions provide little additional benefit. Analysis of the learned patient representations further reveals clinically coherent structure associated with distinct patterns of disease risk and clinical history.

papers.title: Auditing AI peer reviewers: a benchmark on real scientific papers
papers.abstract: LLM-based peer review is now used at production scale, but its evaluation remains limited. We introduce a benchmark that injects objective, localisable errors of four types (general issues, mathematics, numerics, citations) at three severity levels into real papers and measures each reviewer's detection rate by error type and severity, together with its false-positive rate on clean copies. We also present Skepthical, a multi-agent reviewer that verifies citation-backed claims by retrieving the cited papers, mathematics with computer algebra, and numerical claims with executed code. We apply the benchmark to two corpora of 15 recent arXiv preprints each, one in astrophysics and one in machine learning (ML), injecting a total of 357 errors, and evaluate twelve reviewer systems: six single-LLM reviewers, two Claude Code configurations, three publicly available reviewers, and Skepthical. The choice of model has the largest impact on detection rate: given the same prompt, three frontier LLMs differ by about 50 percentage points in total detection on both corpora. Tools and scaffolding help when they contribute what the model cannot supply on its own. In particular, on astrophysics, Claude Code improves on a single Claude call in mathematics and numerics detection, and enforced citation retrieval gives Skepthical the highest citation error detection rate of all systems by a large margin. This citation lead, however, is not observed on ML, where the models appear to know the literature better and Skepthical's citation detection rate is statistically indistinguishable from that of the best single LLM. False-positive rates are below 10% for most systems, but vary with prompt, model, and scaffolding, with mathematics flags the main source of false positives. The evaluation pipeline, the injected errors, and the adjudication logs are released as a benchmark.

papers.title: Physical Observables and Superselection
papers.abstract: It is well-known that a physical state may be represented by a unit vector in a Hilbert space, whilst a physical observable may be represented by a self-adjoint operator on that same space. However, the introduction of a superselection rule on a Hilbert space imposes constraints such that not all self-adjoint operators can represent observables, which has further consequences for the states themselves as well as the physical processes that transform them. In this article, we review the concept of superselection from the view of how such rules would affect what we consider to be physical. Arguments for the existence of a superselection rule due to charge or possibly energy conservation are given and the emergence of effective superselection rules due to decoherence or the lack of a shared reference frame are also discussed.

papers.title: Finding the Farthest in High Dimensions: Dynamic Diameter and Farthest-Neighbor Search
papers.abstract: We give faster algorithms for diameter and farthest-neighbor search in high-dimensional Euclidean space. For every fixed $1<c<\sqrt2$, we maintain an actual factor-$c$ diameter pair under arbitrary point insertions and deletions, with worst-case update time $n^{2/c^2-1}\poly(d,\log n)$ and space $n^{2/c^2}\poly(d,\log n)$, suppressing logarithmic dependence on the execution length and failure probability. Here $n$ bounds the number of active points. The update exponent improves Indyk's algorithm~\cite{indyk} (SODA'03) bound from $1/c^2$ to $2/c^2-1$, while the space exponent improves from $1+1/c^2$ to $2/c^2$. At $c=\sqrt{3/2}$, the update exponent decreases from $2/3$ to $1/3$. A separate construction achieves approximation exactly $\sqrt2$ with update time polynomial in $d$ and $\log n$. All these guarantees hold against adaptive updates, even when every previous random choice is exposed. We also improve the time--space tradeoff near linear space. This construction has an always-correct variant with expected amortized update bounds and requires no advance bound on the number of updates. The dynamic structures store a current answer, so reporting its two point identifiers takes constant time. The geometric method also gives static diameter algorithms and a farthest-neighbor structure for a fixed set that answers arbitrary adaptive queries. At approximation $\sqrt2-\varepsilon$, the diameter time is $n^{1+O(\varepsilon)}$, and the query time is $n^{O(\varepsilon)+o(1)}$ with near-linear preprocessing and space, up to polynomial input-parameter factors. On binary points, this improves the $n^{O(\sqrtθ)}$ overhead of the algorithm that Andoni, Jiang, and Zharkov~\cite{ajz2026} (STOC'26) for Hamming approximation $2-θ$ to $n^{O(θ)+o(1)}$.

papers.title: Irreversible dynamics for ideal fluids on Riemannian manifolds: metriplectic energy-conserving alternatives to Navier-Stokes
papers.abstract: For modelling dissipative phenomena such as friction, diffusion and viscosity, the Hamiltonian framework has a key limitation: once the Casimir invariants are fixed, Hamiltonian flows preserve phase-space volume, which rules out relaxation to equilibrium. Thus modelling dissipation requires modifying the Hamiltonian structure. Following the metriplectic (equivalently, GENERIC) approach, we add to the Hamiltonian vector field a dissipative term generated by a symmetric bracket, here constructed from a Riemannian metric. The resulting flow conserves the energy, and optionally further invariants, while driving a chosen generalised entropy monotonically, which makes the dynamics irreversible; when the entropy is bounded on energy level sets in the direction in which it is driven, it acts as a Lyapunov functional. We apply this construction to ideal fluids on compact Riemannian manifolds, choosing Casimirs of the Lie-Poisson bracket as entropies. In two dimensions, dissipating enstrophy yields the already-known energy-constrained Navier-Stokes equations, which include a nonlocal term restoring energy balance. In three dimensions, where enstrophy is no longer a Casimir, we derive new irreversible models. For incompressible and compressible fluids carrying an advected scalar, dissipating potential enstrophy or higher potential-vorticity moments gives a nonlinear, anisotropic diffusion that acts to align the gradients of the scalar and of the potential vorticity. For a purely incompressible fluid, taking helicity as the entropy gives a first-order, non-smoothing dissipative term whose stationary states are Beltrami fields.

papers.title: AURA 2.0: From User-Driven Responses to Model-Initiated Conversations in Streaming Video
papers.abstract: Most AI assistants respond only when prompted, remaining silent even when events in the video stream offer meaningful opportunities for conversation. To move beyond purely user-driven interaction, we present AURA 2.0, a streaming video large language model that introduces three core upgrades to AURA. The key advance is Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC), which enables the model to identify topics worth discussing in the evolving visual stream and initiate conversations at appropriate moments without a user query. Stream-Aware Tool Calling (SATC) enables the model to invoke external tools using the current visual and conversational context and incorporate returned information into the ongoing interaction. Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG) supports visual grounding in both user inputs and model outputs. The model can identify objects marked by users on video frames and produce frame-aligned bounding boxes to link its responses to specific objects and regions. To develop these capabilities, we construct a dedicated streaming interaction dataset and adopt a three-stage training scheme to integrate the new behaviors with AURA's existing streaming interaction abilities. We further incorporate Long-Horizon Interaction Memory (LHIM) to maintain contextual continuity over extended video streams. Evaluations on public streaming benchmarks show that AURA 2.0 achieves leading performance among open-source streaming models, while targeted evaluations further validate its new interaction capabilities. We open-source the model weights and inference code.

papers.title: Integer Decomposition Property of Edge Polytopes of Weighted Oriented Graphs
papers.abstract: We classify the lattice polytopes arising from vertex-weighted oriented graphs that have the integer decomposition property (IDP). Allowing vertex weights and edge orientations introduces non-vertex lattice points in the polytope which need to be accounted for when studying the IDP. We can then identify forbidden induced subgraphs in the sense that their presence obstructs the IDP for the supergraph. We establish positive results for several families of graphs under suitable orientation and coprimality conditions, including weighted oriented paths and cycles, and show that any weighted oriented tree with a unique sink has the IDP.

papers.title: Robust Control Design for LTI Systems with Sampling-Time Jitter
papers.abstract: Sampling-time jitter makes a sampled-data control loop time-varying, so standard LTI robust-control synthesis does not apply directly. This paper reformulates dynamic output feedback design under bounded, unmeasured sample-to-sample jitter as a robust-control problem. The exact zero-order-hold model is decomposed into a nominal time-invariant plant and a memoryless, time-varying uncertainty block with a norm bound representing the sampling-time jitter. As the block is memoryless, the operator small-gain condition for the time varying loop reduces to a standard robustness test with a matrix norm bound. It is shown that the same test also guarantees uniform exponential stability for every admissible jitter sequence. Embedding the decomposition into a generalized plant with performance channels serves two synthesis objectives with standard robust-control tools: Robust stability with optimized nominal performance through structured H-inf synthesis, and robust performance through mu synthesis with constant scalings. A numerical example shows that jitter can destabilize a control loop with a nominal H-inf controller, whereas both robust designs remain stable and the robust-performance design is less sensitive to jitter at the cost of nominal performance.

papers.title: De Sitter Gravity and Emergent Time from Fusion Matrix Product States and SYK
papers.abstract: We propose a quantum-mechanical model dual to two-dimensional de Sitter (dS) gravity. It is a quantum channel, defined by a matrix product state that fuses one spin at each step, and is related to a limit of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model without chord crossings. Its simplest part is a random walk with an emergent $SL(2,\mathbb R)$ symmetry, which we identify with the symmetry of the future boundary of dS. It selects a time variable in which the walk obeys the Schwarzian action and yields the disk amplitude of dS Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity. As the simplest case, we consider free massless scalar fields in the fixed background of dS$_2$. We find the agreement of the two-point function in the Bunch-Davies vacuum and the matching of symmetry. Our construction provides a concrete model for the dS/CFT correspondence for two-dimensional de Sitter gravity.

papers.title: [Experiment, Analysis, and Benchmark] How well do LLMs comprehend and design relational database schemata?
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for database tasks, yet most work, such as Text2SQL, assumes that the relational schema already exists. We ask whether LLMs can design a schema from natural language requirements (Text2Schema), verbalize an existing schema (Schema2Text), and preserve its structure through a Schema-to-Text-to-Schema round trip. We present SchemaBridge, a benchmark of 902 schemata from three collections, stratified by size and constraint complexity, that scores fidelity separately for tables, attributes, domain (data types and nullability), entity, and referential integrity. Evaluating six open-weight and proprietary LLMs, we find that: (i) human-written requirements under-specify schemata, with no model exceeding 0.27 referential integrity F1; (ii) LLM-generated descriptions carry far more structure when explicitly asked to be complete, raising GPT-5.4-mini's referential F1 on SchemaBench from 0.228 to 0.909, even as BLEU, ROUGE-L, and BERTScore decrease; (iii) controlled experiments show that both constructor and describer choices influence round-trip fidelity under fixed settings; and (iv) masked schema experiments show that structural cues support recovery of keys and relationships, while joint data-type and nullability information is poorly retained through verbalization. Code and data are available at https://github.com/iamsriom/SchemaBridge

papers.title: Pseudovortex-assisted generation of first-order vector modes
papers.abstract: A practical method of generating first-order vector modes like radially and azimuthally polarized modes is using the so-called vortex waveplates. Shining these plates with Gaussian beams produces parasitic higher-order modes besides the target vector beam. The reason is that there is a mismatch between the incident Gaussian mode and the doughnut-shaped profile required for the vector beam. This imposes a limit on the fidelity of the generated mode with respect to the target vector beam. In this work we demonstrate theoretically and experimentally that this limit can be overcome if the input Gaussian beam is replaced with a pseudovortex beam, which is a doughnut-shaped mode without topological charge. We use a spatial light modulator to generate this input mode and a geometric-phase-compensated triangular cavity for mode analysis. We demonstrate vector mode fidelity as high as $0.921 \pm 0.013$, which is considerably better than $0.815 \pm 0.003$ obtained with Gaussian input. We also investigate the fidelity as a function of the input beam waist, leading to a theoretical upper bound for the fidelity of $8π/27 \approx 0.931$, in close agreement with the experimental results. This approach presents a reliable method of generating high-fidelity vector modes.

papers.title: Infrastructure for Verifiable AI: Where Proof Costs Go and How Hardware Can Help
papers.abstract: Users of artificial intelligence services, including those powered by large language models and other transformer-based models, need assurance that inference and training follow the declared computation without exposing private models or data. Zero-knowledge proofs can provide this assurance, but proof generation remains expensive. Hardware acceleration research often reports gains for individual cryptographic operations, leaving their effect on the full cost of proving neural-network workloads, particularly large transformer models, unclear. We introduce a four-layer framework linking verifiable AI workloads, proof systems, cryptographic kernels and hardware platforms, use it to review the literature, and add original measurements of six provers and seven kernels to identify which costs matter in practice. Our measurements show that the dominant cost changes with the proof system and input length. In low-rank fine-tuning, the cost of opening commitments to fixed model weights remains nearly constant across input lengths from 64 to 2048, while the work associated with intermediate values grows. A 13-billion-parameter fine-tuning configuration exceeds the capacity of a 40-gigabyte graphics processor but completes on an 80-gigabyte device, showing why capacity must be assessed alongside execution time. Our kernel profiling further identifies instruction issue and synchronization limits that a bandwidth-only model misses. We use these findings to assess graphics processors, reconfigurable logic, custom chips and existing artificial intelligence accelerators. The resulting research agenda connects proof-friendly numeric formats, reuse of fixed-weight commitments, heterogeneous execution and shared benchmarks to the measured bottlenecks. Effective acceleration requires selecting hardware and proof-system optimizations around the cost profile of the target workload.

papers.title: From Delegation to Coordination: Learning Efficient Multi-Agent Deep Research
papers.abstract: Multi-agent deep-research systems use delegation to parallelize search and keep long tool traces out of the main agent's context. Yet delegation helps only when task allocation and subtask execution are coordinated: the main agent must issue useful subtasks, while subagents must return reliable evidence. Existing training either optimizes only the main agent or broadcasts the same team advantage to all agents, which can reward misleading subagent reports and penalize useful ones. We introduce LEAD-RL (Learning Effective Agent Delegation with Reinforcement Learning), a joint main-agent-subagent training framework with contribution-aware credit assignment. A training-time rubric evaluates the research utility of each subagent report and gates its inherited team advantage, while final-answer correctness remains the only team reward; no token, step, or speedup reward is used. Across five benchmarks and two model families, LEAD-RL improves answer quality. On BrowseComp, it improves accuracy by 2.49 percentage points and reduces critical-path cost by 24.5% over joint training with shared team credit. During validation, accuracy increases by 6.78 points at approximately constant critical-path cost. These results show that contribution-aware credit assignment improves the quality-efficiency trade-off of multi-agent deep research.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): The Euclid surveys at DR1
papers.abstract: Euclid is a surveying mission that is progressively imaging and spectroscopically mapping a wide area of extragalactic sky in visible and near infrared bands. The Euclid mission is, however, not restricted to the Euclid Wide Survey, but it includes data from various other survey components. This paper presents the Data Release 1 (DR1) status of the multiple Euclid surveys and fields, including the Euclid Deep Survey, Euclid Auxiliary Fields, calibration fields, the Euclid Medium-Deep Survey, the Euclid Ecliptic Survey, and the Independent Legacy Scientists' field, in addition to the Euclid Wide Survey. Some of these fields were observed during the initial Performance-Verification phase, others during the Phase-Diversity calibration campaign, and the majority during the subsequent science operations phase. This paper describes the different procedures of survey implementation applied in the various phases of the mission, from the set of requirements, constraints, and limitations, to the final operational products used to operate the spacecraft and execute the science surveys. The resulting main component of the Euclid surveys, the Euclid Wide Survey, covers at DR1 an area of 2100$\,{\rm deg}^2$, in two separate regions, of which 1900$\,{\rm deg}^2$ corresponds to data validated in higher-level processing.

papers.title: Hinge comparison and excess estimates via modified Hessian bounds on manifolds with density
papers.abstract: We study geometric consequences of modified Hessian estimates on Riemannian manifolds with density. For general radial functions, we derive tensorial, spectral, and trace identities for the modified Hessian in the original metric. We also establish a comparison identity relating the modified Hessians of two radial functions and characterize when they are proportional. We then prove a hinge comparison theorem under an upper bound on the modified Hessian, yielding a weighted law of cosines and lower bounds for the excess function. Finally, under nonnegative weighted sectional curvature and suitable density control assumptions, we obtain an Abresch-Gromoll-type upper excess estimate.

papers.title: Rapid Multiparameter Gravitational-Wave Tests of General Relativity with Neural Posterior Estimation
papers.abstract: Multiparameter gravitational-wave tests of general relativity (GR) are limited by strong correlations among post-Newtonian (PN) phase deformations and the computational cost of Bayesian inference. We present DINGO-TGR, a neural posterior estimation framework that jointly infers binary-source parameters and six PN phase deformations within the TIGER parametrization, using IMRPhenomXPHM waveforms with spin precession and higher-order modes. Importance sampling reweights the neural proposal samples, while principal component analysis (PCA) identifies two well-constrained combinations of PN deformations. We validate the framework using 16 zero-noise GR injections and 12 beyond-GR injections, recovering GR-consistent posteriors in the former and leading-mode shifts consistent with the injected deformations in the latter. For GW150914 and GW250114, our results agree with independent \texttt{bilby-tgr} analyses using \texttt{dynesty}. After training, inference including importance sampling takes approximately 38 minutes and 4.4 hours, respectively, compared with 177 and 238 hours for conventional sampling. GW150914 exhibits a mild offset from GR in the leading PCA mode, whereas GW250114 is consistent with GR. To assess the significance of the GW150914 offset, we analyze 1000 GW150914-like GR injections with independent Gaussian-noise realizations and fixed detector power spectral densities. The resulting empirical upper-tail $p$-value is $11.5\%$, indicating that the observed offset does not reject the adopted GR null model at the 5\% significance level. Our results demonstrate the potential of importance-sampling-corrected neural inference for efficient multiparameter GR tests and large-scale injection-based significance assessments.

papers.title: UV and deep-UV ultrafast harmonic generation enhanced by resonant gold nano-pillar metasurface
papers.abstract: We report experimental observations and full-vector numerical simulations of second and third-harmonic generation from a two-dimensional periodic gold nano-pillar metasurface, for efficient ultrafast light conversion from near-infrared to the UV and deep-UV spectral ranges. The metasurface is designed to support an angle-tunable plasmonic resonance in the near-infrared spectral range, with its resonance wavelength shifting as a function of the pump angle of incidence. Under resonant conditions, strong electromagnetic-field confinement near the nano-pillar corners enhances the nonlinear light-matter interactions. Compared with a flat gold mirror, the nanostructured metal exhibits enhanced nonlinear frequency conversion, with conversion efficiencies of second and third-harmonic generation increased by two and three orders of magnitude, respectively. Full-wave theoretical modeling of linear and nonlinear light-matter interaction in nanoscale structures validates the experimental results. We demonstrate that periodically arranged square gold pillars can be engineered to achieve enhanced second and third-harmonic generation at wavelengths that can be tailored through the structural design, without requiring complex geometries or hybrid structures that pose fabrication challenges. The close agreement between theoretical predictions and experimental measurements further advances our understanding of surface-mediated nonlinear optical processes in metals and highlights the potential of metallic nanostructures as ultrafast light sources in the UV and deep-UV.

papers.title: Ergodicity breaking for data classification in a dissipative Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions
papers.abstract: We explore the close relationship between the processing of data and the dynamics of interacting many-body systems. For example, certain classes of quantum neural networks can be mapped onto dissipative quantum Ising models whose evolution is described by a Lindblad master equation. In these architectures, emergent nonlinearities lead to non-ergodic dynamics under which initial states located in different basins of attraction evolve towards distinguishable stationary states. This mechanism underlies the classification of quantum data. Motivated by this connection, we consider an Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions. Using a combination of mean-field calculations and exact small-scale numerics, we show that the stationary state manifold can be designed to enable multi-class classification. We also investigate the structure of the ensuing basins of attraction, thereby showing that these systems allow for the classification of quantum states with nonlinear decision boundaries.

papers.title: Prevalence Bounds for Edited Watermarked Text: Power Envelopes and Calibration Sensitivity
papers.abstract: Watermark detectors decide whether one document came from a watermarked language model. Auditors often need a different number: the share of a corpus that did. We study this share for Gumbel-max and green-list (KGW) watermarks when every document may have been edited by an unknown amount. Without restrictions on the edits, the upper end of the identified set is 1. Combining a known least-favourable next-token distribution with a sequential coupling, we derive a power envelope indexed by three budgets: a retention floor, an entropy budget, and a budget for in-place substitutions, which for Gumbel-max make edited positions look less watermarked than human text. The envelope gives an identified set that is sharp for the alternatives it dominates, finite-sample bounds on the realized share of a fixed corpus with either the exact null or a null calibrated on an independent human sample, and confidence sequences for streams. In Gumbel-max simulations where the envelope binds, the bounds cover, and the threshold that maximizes the gap between envelope and null is generally as tight as twelve thresholds. On text from OPT-1.3B and Qwen3-1.7B, 12,000 fresh human documents scored under three keys show no robust departure from the exact null, and all bounds covered in resampling trials from finite pools of documents with random edits, substitutions and paraphrases; at a share of 0.2 the exact-null bound is about [0.14,0.38]. These results are fragile in two ways we make precise. LLM-paraphrased KGW pools fall below the envelope, yet at 2000 documents the bounds still covered in these trials. A simulated null error of 0.01, comparable to the largest deviation we observed at our thresholds, is likewise harmless at 2000 documents but breaks exact-null coverage at 100,000; a null calibrated on an independent human sample keeps coverage there, but needs a large reference sample to stay narrow.

papers.title: Control-Gibbs Distribution: Sampling for Optimal Control and Diverse Actions
papers.abstract: While conventional optimal control selects an optimal input sequence, probabilistic control assigns probability mass over all possible inputs and exploits a distribution of control sequences. Control distributions help enable exploration, capture diverse solutions, and solve deterministic optimal control problems. This work reviews an important probabilistic model for control distributions, the control-Gibbs distribution, i.e., the Gibbs distribution with an optimal control objective as the energy function. We point out its fundamental role in various probabilistic control frameworks, e.g., maximum entropy control, control-as-inference framework, model predictive path integral control, and energy-based models for control. This provides a model-central perspective to unify these probabilistic control frameworks. We also review the associated extensions of dynamic programming for computing closed-loop control distributions. To sample the control-Gibbs distribution, we consider projected Langevin sampling and develop non-asymptotic guarantees. The guarantees show the dual benefits of sampling the control-Gibbs distribution: obtaining diverse control solutions and solving the deterministic optimal control problem. We provide a numerical example where diverse arm trajectories are sampled from a control-Gibbs distribution.

papers.title: A Variable Compact Millimeter Excess in the Type-1 Seyfert Galaxy NGC 985: Implications for a Black-Hole Corona
papers.abstract: Compact millimeter emission from radio-quiet active galactic nuclei has been proposed as a probe of magnetized accretion-disk coronae. We present three epochs of ALMA observations of the type-1 Seyfert galaxy NGC 985, together with archival post-upgrade VLA data presented here for the first time, to investigate its compact millimeter excess. The millimeter flux density decreased strongly between the first two ALMA epochs separated by approximately one month, while the component was detected again at an intermediate level in the third epoch. This variability demonstrates an intrinsically variable compact component and implies a model-independent size limit of $\lesssim 0.024$ pc ($\simeq 1.1\times10^3 R_{\rm S}$). Spectral decomposition requires a compact, self-absorbed synchrotron component to reproduce the millimeter-wave data. A hybrid thermal/nonthermal coronal model reproduces the radio-millimeter spectra, with the two broadly sampled ALMA epochs favoring different nonthermal electron distributions. The estimated radiative cooling times are comparable to or shorter than the light-crossing time, implying continuous injection or reacceleration of nonthermal electrons; a change in particle injection is the most natural driver of the observed spectral changes. We conclude that NGC 985 hosts a recurrent and variable compact millimeter synchrotron component. A magnetized corona provides a plausible origin, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish a coronal origin from alternatives such as a jet base.

papers.title: Proton Spin Fluctuation Decomposition
papers.abstract: We formulate a fluctuation decomposition of proton spin in terms of the variances and covariances of the spin and orbital angular momentum of quarks and gluons. We derive their representations in terms of single- and double-parton distributions. The definite proton spin imposes sum rules requiring the variances of its spin and orbital contributions to be compensated by their covariances. This framework reveals correlations and fluctuations that are invisible to the conventional proton spin decomposition.

papers.title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on thousands of hours of recordings, yet their frozen features transfer poorly to downstream tasks, and this transfer does not consistently improve with larger models or more pretraining data. We show that a vision foundation model that has never seen EEG is a stronger frozen EEG encoder than these specialized models, once the signals are rendered as images that a vision transformer can read. Our method, SeeEEG, keeps the vision backbone frozen and learns only how EEG is displayed to it. Each channel occupies a dedicated row of patches and is drawn either as a waveform at a fixed gain or as a scalogram whose frequency range spans the patch height, so that task-relevant patterns fall within individual tokens. The montage, filtering, and contrast parameters of this display are initialized from a standard clinical montage and optimized with the task loss through the frozen backbone, which amounts to at most 1,113 trainable parameters per view. We compare SeeEEG with seven EEG foundation models on eight clinical, sleep, affective, and brain-computer interface datasets, with every encoder frozen and paired with identical readout heads. With a frozen DINOv3 ViT-B, SeeEEG outperforms every EEG foundation model in balanced accuracy on all eight datasets and reaches a mean rank of 1.3 in Cohen kappa or AUROC, compared with 2.9 for the strongest baseline, REVE. The learned displays transfer without further optimization to the video encoder V-JEPA 2.1, which outperforms every EEG foundation model on both metrics on six of the eight datasets. Replacing DINOv3 with a randomly initialized ViT-B lowers the score by 15.2 points on average, so the ability to read rendered EEG comes from visual pretraining.

papers.title: Similar but Not Redundant: Embedding-Gated Refinement for High-Granularity Topic Models
papers.abstract: High-granularity topic modelling extracts hundreds of niche topics from a corpus, yet this regime is rarely studied and is more commonly framed as a failure mode: "over-clustering," in which coherent themes fragment into redundant subtopics. We argue that this framing conflates genuine redundancy with topics that are semantically similar but meaningfully distinct, and that the central challenge in high-granularity modelling is separating the two. Recent post-hoc refinement methods address topic redundancy through either embedding-based similarity thresholding or LLM-guided merging. We show that neither suffices in high-granularity settings and propose embedding-gated iterative merge (EGIM), a hybrid approach that iteratively generates context-rich topic representations, uses embedding similarity to propose candidate merges across the topic space, then applies LLM judgement to accept only genuinely redundant pairs while preserving niche distinctions. Across two patent corpora and one legal corpus, LLM judgement rejects 83% of embedding-identified candidates as non-redundant. EGIM improves discriminability on merged topics by 25-55% over a prior iterative LLM baseline while better preserving the original topic distribution.

papers.title: Contractual Structure and Obvious Manipulation in Many-to-Many Matching
papers.abstract: We study how contractual structure affects worst-case and best-case obvious manipulation in many-to-many matching with substitutable preferences. Efficient individually rational mechanisms rule out best-case obvious manipulations on both the full substitutable domain and the unitary domain. Under simple and economically natural conditions on hospitals' choices, every stable mechanism on the full domain admits obvious manipulations in both cases; hospital-proposing deferred acceptance can admit both types even under unitary doctors' preferences. A further sufficient condition makes efficient stable-dominating mechanisms obviously manipulable in the worst case. On the unitary domain, doctor-proposing deferred acceptance is not obviously manipulable. If each doctor--hospital pair has at most one feasible contract, this positive conclusion extends to every stable-dominating mechanism.

papers.title: ALMA quiet Sun observations compared with a simulated MURaM-ChE chromosphere
papers.abstract: Aims. We assess the ability of the MURaM-ChE enhanced network simulation to reproduce the chromospheric millimeter brightness observed with ALMA and investigate the properties of the simulated emission. Methods. We analyze synthetic brightness temperatures from the MURaM-ChE model in ALMA Bands 3 (3.2 mm) and 6 (1.3 mm) and compare them with ALMA observations of quiet-Sun, network, and enhanced network regions. We examine the statistical properties of the brightness distributions, their dependence on magnetic field strength, and their variation with wavelength, using results from Bifrost enhanced network snapshots as additional reference cases. Results. The MURaM-ChE model reproduces the range and variability of brightness temperatures observed in enhanced network regions, with particularly close agreement found for the 23 April 2017 data set. The reference Bifrost snapshots produce lower brightness temperatures in both bands, with values below even those measured by ALMA in the quiet Sun. The systematic offset between the models is present in both bands and is likely associated with differences in atmospheric density stratification and the resulting effective formation heights. Both the observations and simulations show an overall increase in brightness temperature with magnetic field strength and wavelength, although significant scatter is present. Conclusions. The results indicate that the MURaM-ChE model provides a physically consistent representation of chromospheric conditions in enhanced network regions and captures key properties of the observed millimeter emission. The comparison highlights the sensitivity of millimeter brightness to atmospheric stratification and magnetic structure and demonstrates the diagnostic potential of ALMA observations for constraining chromospheric models.

papers.title: Spin to win: enhancing the quantum Otto cycle with the circular Unruh effect
papers.abstract: We study a quantum Otto cycle whose working medium is a qubit Unruh-DeWitt detector undergoing uniform circular motion in $(3+1)$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, interacting with a massless scalar field in a thermal state during the isochoric strokes. We compute the detector's transition rate and determine its energy gap-dependent effective temperature, showing that the effective temperature can be higher than the ambient bath temperature in the small energy gap limit and lower in the high bath temperature limit. We then investigate how these motion-induced effective temperatures affect the operating conditions and performance of the quantum Otto cycle as a heat engine or a refrigerator. We show that the engine efficiency and refrigerator performance coefficient can exceed their standard Carnot bounds based on the bath's rest-frame temperatures, while remaining bounded by generalised Carnot limits expressed in terms of the effective temperatures experienced by the detector. In the high-temperature limit, the effective temperature coincides with that of an inertial detector moving through a thermal bath, and a comparison with the small-gap limit reveals that circular motion allows the standard Carnot bounds to be exceeded at lower speeds than in the inertial case.

papers.title: Accelerated Transformed Primal Dual Methods for Smooth Convex Optimization Problems with Affine Equality Constraints
papers.abstract: Accelerated transformed primal--dual (ATPD) methods are proposed for smooth convex optimization problems with affine equality constraints. The methods combine primal--dual dynamics with a transformation designed to accelerate convergence. In the strongly convex case, ATPD achieves an accelerated linear convergence rate and matches the known lower bounds on first-order oracle complexity in terms of gradient evaluations and matrix--vector products. The analysis distinguishes these two types of computational work when assessing the complexity of the method. For general convex objectives, a homotopy perturbation strategy is introduced, and an accelerated sublinear rate for the modified Lyapunov energy is proved under a uniform boundedness condition on the primal iterates at all homotopy stages. The acceleration mechanism is based on an exponentially stable ATPD flow and a modified discrete Lyapunov function. This continuous-time perspective guides the construction and analysis of the discrete methods. Numerical experiments on policy evaluation and constrained signal reconstruction problems support the theory and illustrate the efficiency of the proposed methods.

papers.title: Spin-Boson Hamiltonians as Generators of Spin-Dressed Bogoliubov Dynamics
papers.abstract: Following Bach, Lieb and Solovej, quadratic Hamiltonians can be defined as generators of unitary groups implementing one-parameter groups of Bogoliubov transformations. We develop an analogous dynamical definition of generalized spin--boson Hamiltonians. For a single spin level, we review results of Guichardet and Dereziński: the van Hove Hamiltonians, including the renormalized ones, are exactly the generators of affine Bogoliubov dynamics that do not mix creation and annihilation operators. For several spin levels, there is no analogue of this group, and we introduce spin-dressed implementations, that is to say the free flow of the fields is implemented up to bounded operator-valued displacements, which vanish at a rate measured by a so-called regularity scale and have a spin observable, the coupling map, as derivative at time zero. The one-particle Hamiltonian $Υ$ and the coupling map are determined by the Hamiltonian, and the field obeys a quantum Langevin equation. Spin-dressed implementations in Fock space, at the finest scale and for form factors in $D(Υ^{-1/2})$, are exactly the generalized spin--boson Hamiltonians, unique up to the spin Hamiltonian. At the roughest scale, the renormalized spin--boson Hamiltonian of a two-level system with ultraviolet-singular form factor and arbitrary tunnelling is a spin-dressed implementation, and the definition alone yields asymptotic Weyl operators on the test functions along which the coupling map is integrable, a dense set under standard assumptions.

papers.title: Clustering professional football players using Gaussian mixture models: A case study of the English Premier League 2024/25
papers.abstract: The increasing availability of detailed football performance data has created new opportunities for identifying player archetypes and informing recruitment and tactical decision-making. Most existing clustering approaches assign each player to a single group, despite the reality that many modern footballers perform hybrid roles spanning multiple stylistic categories. Performance data for 314 outfield players from the 2024/25 English Premier League season are analysed using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM) applied to principal component representations of player statistics. Unlike hard-assignment methods such as k-means, the GMM provides probabilistic cluster memberships, allowing uncertainty and role hybridity to be quantified. Seven player archetypes are identified in the full dataset. Posterior membership probabilities reveal a subset of players whose profiles span multiple clusters, providing an objective measure of tactical flexibility and stylistic ambiguity. Further analyses within defender, midfielder, and forward groups recover position-specific sub-archetypes and highlight exceptional outliers. The results demonstrate that model-based clustering provides a flexible and interpretable framework for identifying latent structure in high-dimensional performance data while explicitly quantifying uncertainty in cluster membership. More broadly, the approach is readily transferable to other sports and domains in which individuals exhibit overlapping characteristics and cannot be adequately represented by hard cluster assignments alone.

papers.title: Sedimentation of flexible fibers through an ordered array of pillars
papers.abstract: In this study, we extend our previous work [Makanga \textit{et al.}, Physical Review Fluids 8, 044303 (2023)] to investigate the effects of a periodic array of pillars on the settling dynamics of a flexible fiber in a viscous fluid. By means of numerical simulations, we show that the fiber trajectory falls at long times into one of two migration modes, ``zigzag" and ``displacement", which are determined by the short-time scattering dynamics induced by fiber-pillar interactions. In the zigzag mode, there is no average displacement relative to the direction of gravity; the center of mass of the fiber follows a quasi-straight line. Conversely, in the displacement mode, there is a net displacement relative to the direction of gravity; the fiber center of mass follows a cyclical skew-bumping path. We show how this long-time behavior can be predicted using a theoretical model with minimal ingredients. These findings, together with the long-time transport properties of the fiber, provide insights into future experiments, as well as the design of gravity-based deterministic lateral displacement (DLD) devices to sort elongated particles based on their geometric and/or mechanical properties.

papers.title: Large diameter for $(Δ+2)$-colouring reconfiguration
papers.abstract: Given a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{R}_{k}(G)$ has the proper $k$-colourings of $G$ for vertices, two of which are adjacent if and only if they differ on precisely one vertex of $G$. In $2022$, Cambie, Cranston and the author proved that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{Δ+2}(G)$ is at most $n+2μ$, and put forth a collection of conjectures that in its strongest and most beautiful form would imply that the diameter of $\mathcal{R}_{Δ+2}(G)$ is precisely equal to $n + μ$, for every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, matching number $μ$ and maximum degree $Δ$. Here we disprove most of those conjectures. Our constructions have reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{3}{2}μ-2$. We also provide counterexamples that are $Δ$-regular, we show that every graph has reconfiguration diameter at least $n+\frac{1}{2} μ$, and we advertise an extension to hypergraphs. It is now much more mysterious how the diameter behaves, so we propose a number of open problems.

papers.title: Entanglement detection from moments of the realigned state: application to continuous-variable quantum systems
papers.abstract: Certifying entanglement is a central problem in quantum information sciences, especially for continuous-variable quantum systems where full state tomography is experimentally demanding. We introduce a family of separability criteria based on the singular moments and weak moments of the operator obtained by applying the realignment map to the density operator. In practice, we find that the criterion based on the second-order moments of the realigned operator is already sufficient to witness the entanglement of a wide range of quantum optical states. The realigned moments can be readily accessed using an optical scheme consisting of a linear interferometer that couples several identical copies of the state, similarly to the multicopy technique used to measure the partial-transpose moments of a state [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064 (2026)]. We illustrate the detection capability of the second-order realigned-moment method for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, including lossy NOON states.

papers.title: Maximizing LLM Utility While Managing LLM Fallibility
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can supply autonomous systems with plans, predictions, and judgments, but these contributions are sometimes wrong. This review asks how a system can maximize an LLM's utility while managing its fallibility. Our answer is to adapt the system's reliance on the LLM as evidence about the LLM's performance accumulates. Systems built from imperfect components, such as noisy sensors and faulty software, have long worked in this way, and the classical methods they use can be applied to LLM-based systems as well. A system can change its reliance on an LLM in several ways, depending on the LLM's role and on the other components in the system. Each change needs an estimate of the LLM's reliability, and the LLM's role and the kind of contribution it makes determine what to estimate. Classical methods from decision theory, estimation, and online learning then turn these estimates into reliance decisions. These decisions can reduce how often LLM errors affect the system. However, some errors matter even when they are rare. An independently verified mechanism can prevent such errors from being executed. Without one, adapting reliance using reliability estimates can still keep their risk within a bound. Studies on adapting reliance on LLMs are emerging but limited, and the reviewed comparisons suggest that adapting reliance can improve system performance.

papers.title: Temporal Regularized Learning: Self-Supervised Learning Local in Space and Time
papers.abstract: Layer-local self-supervised objectives remove the backward pass between layers, but almost all still compute their loss over a batch of samples and are therefore local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), a spatially and temporally local learning rule for self-supervised representation learning from sequential input streams. The key idea is to instantiate a VICReg-style objective with temporally adjacent positives and non-differentiated running population statistics, yielding a per-neuron online loss with bounded state. The objective is a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis, and its gradient is a Hebbian update of the feedforward weights and an anti-Hebbian update of one lateral matrix per layer. The aim of the experiments is to show that the rule works in a small network, not to compete with backpropagation. On a class-chunked MNIST stream, a two-layer fully connected network trained with batch size one outperforms random features (96.48% versus 95.09% linear-probe accuracy) and classical SFA, and a variant that relaxes both locality constraints is comparable to supervised backpropagation. Because training and inference use the same computation, the network can keep learning from unlabeled data during inference without loss of accuracy.

papers.title: Exploring Socially Acceptable 3D Feedback Design for Inclusive Small-Group Conversation
papers.abstract: Prior research has shown that providing feedback on group dynamics can improve the quality of small-group conversations. However, publicly delivered feedback that targets specific individuals may reduce social acceptability due to negative experiences such as social pressure, embarrassment, and resistance. This work investigates how public feedback can be designed to remain socially acceptable while maintaining its effectiveness in XR-based small-group conversations. Informed by social science and HCI literature, we identified three design strategies (incorporate humor, reduce social attention, and use indirectness) and proposed a set of metaphor- and agent-based 3D feedback probes. We then conducted a two-phase study: (1) an online survey with 50 participants to examine how such feedback designs are perceived under public and private delivery, and (2) follow-up interviews with 14 participants who completed the survey to better understand their interpretations and elicit additional insights. Results show that metaphor- and agent-based feedback can reduce social discomfort while maintaining effectiveness. Interview findings further highlighted the role of three strategies in making feedback easier to accept, while requiring careful balance. We also discussed design implications for creating socially acceptable 3D feedback to support inclusive small-group conversations in XR.

papers.title: Continuum space hierarchical Cannings process: II. Genealogies and ancestral web
papers.abstract: The present paper is the second in a series of three papers in which we consider a \emph{spatial multi-type population model} arising as the many-individuals-per-site limit of individual-based models. The evolution mechanisms in this model are: migration, Fleming-Viot resampling, $Λ_0$-Cannings resampling, and $(Λ_k)_{k \in \N}$-Cannings block-resampling. This evolution leads to a collection of \emph{measure-valued} processes indexed by a continuum geographic space $Ω_N^\infty$, called the \emph{continuum hierarchical group}, obtained as the limit of a discrete hierarchical group $Ω_N^L$ as $L\to\infty$, where $Ω_N^L = \oplus_{k \geq -L} Z_N$ with $Z_N$ the cyclical group of order $N$. On this geographic space, each component is a probability measure on a type space $\K$. In the first paper \cite{gh1}, we \emph{constructed} the measure-valued process on $Ω_N^\infty$ describing the type frequencies in the population and identified its main properties. We found a \emph{dichotomy} between this process being \emph{stochastic} (= locally monotype) or \emph{deterministic} (= locally multitype). In the present paper we turn to the \emph{genealogies} of the population on $Ω_N^\infty$.

papers.title: Control Variates to reduce the variance of the empirical Moment Generating Function: an extreme value perspective
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of Moment Generating Functions is fundamental in many applications, but empirical estimators have high variances. Within a control variate setup, Extreme Value Theory is leveraged to identify how extreme values affect the variance reduction method's optimality.

papers.title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how biological research is done. Biological foundation models trained on millions of nucleotides, protein, and single-cell measurements predict protein structures, mutation effects, and cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Agentic systems, AI assistants built on large language models, can run multistep analyses from plain-language requests and increasingly call foundation models as tools. Yet it is often unclear when these models' outputs can be trusted. We frame this as a model's knowledge boundary: the range of inputs, tasks, and conditions over which its outputs are reliable. This review explains how foundation models are built and proposes that five design elements (data, architecture, training scheme, evaluation scheme, and post-analysis) define this boundary. We examine evidence on where current models succeed or fail and present standardized descriptions of model limits so that researchers, and the agents acting for them, can use these tools reliably.

papers.title: Poincaré polynomials of nilmanifolds associated with path graphs
papers.abstract: We give explicit and recursive formulas for the Poincaré polynomials of Dani--Mainkar nilmanifolds associated with path graphs. We also prove that these polynomials are unimodal, and we calculate a range of Betti numbers asymptotically. As an application, we derive a sharp lower bound for the dimension of the total de Rham cohomology of a Dani--Mainkar nilmanifold.

papers.title: DiffSSMEye: Conditional High-Frequency Eye Movement Synthesis with Structured State-Space Diffusion
papers.abstract: Synthesizing high-frequency eye movements requires preserving long-range temporal dependencies and subject-specific oculomotor dynamics. However, methods based on generative adversarial networks (GANs) and variational autoencoders (VAEs) can struggle to preserve these characteristics simultaneously. We introduce DiffSSMEye, a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model with bidirectional Structured State Space Sequence (S4) layers for generating five-second gaze-velocity sequences at 1,000 Hz. Generation is conditioned on a coarse gaze reference, user identity, and task, where identity and task embeddings are incorporated through feature-wise linear modulation. Identity-preservation, multi-resolution spectral, and integrated-drift losses complement noise prediction to constrain biometric consistency, frequency structure, and displacement error. Subject-disjoint evaluation on GazeBase across seven tasks yields mean real--synthetic embedding cosine similarities of 0.91--0.95. DiffSSMEye also achieves the lowest median spatial errors among these baselines for horizontal and random saccade tasks. These results demonstrate improved spatial accuracy and biometric feature consistency for subject-specific gaze synthesis.

papers.title: Anonymous in Name Only: A Critical Review and a Reidentification Exercise on the European Commission's Anonymization Measures for Google Search Data under Article 6(11) of the DMA
papers.abstract: In July 2026, the European Commission (EC) set out the anonymization measures Alphabet must implement to share Google Search data with competing search engines under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act. As the first concrete illustration of how the EC operationalizes anonymization under the EU digital rulebook, this methodology could become a regulatory benchmark. In this paper, we show why it should not. We critically review the anonymization measures proposed by the EC, from the characterization of residual risk to the suppression thresholds and the reliance on contractual safeguards. For each of those issues, we highlight significant conceptual flaws, and, where applicable, we illustrate these flaws with empirical observations from real Google Search data provided by Alphabet and protected under the EC's measures. Importantly, we present examples of low-effort reidentification, record linkage, and confidential attribute inference achieved through straightforward and automatable attack patterns. Our findings show that the approach of the EC relies on unjustified heuristics rather than formal privacy guarantees, underestimates the risks inherent in free-text search queries, and sacrifices data utility without achieving meaningful protection. We also demonstrate that the proposed measures do not meet any of the three anonymization criteria established by the European Data Protection Board (EDPB): no record isolation, no linkage, and no inference. Practitioners and regulators are therefore cautioned against treating these measures as a sound anonymization practice.

papers.title: Random Exploration is Random
papers.abstract: Decision making often requires balancing exploitation of familiar options with exploration of uncertain alternatives. One strategy for exploration is random exploration, in which choices become more variable and less tied to the option that currently appears best. However, it remains unclear whether this variability reflects genuine stochasticity or instead a deterministic structure that traditional cognitive models fail to capture. We examined this question using the Horizon Task in an aggregated dataset of 1,392 participants completing over 1,270,695 trials. In this task, exploration becomes more valuable when participants have more future choices, and choice variability increases under longer horizons. We tested whether more expressive neural network models could recover deterministic structure from this additional variability. Although neural networks provided better overall fits to behavior than the traditional model, long-horizon choices remained consistently less predictable than short-horizon choices. These findings show that limited model expressiveness cannot fully account for the increased variability associated with random exploration, suggesting random exploration truly is substantially random.

papers.title: Observation of the $Λ(1520)$ suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV
papers.abstract: A suppression of the baryonic $Λ(1520)$ resonance yield relative to the $Λ$ ground state by $0.589 \pm 0.015^{\rm stat} \pm 0.086^{\rm syst}$ is observed in central relative to peripheral Pb-Pb collisions, with a significance of $6.8σ$. The $Λ(1520)$ production at midrapidity is measured in six centrality classes in Pb-Pb collisions for the first time at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV with ALICE. The $Λ(1520)$ is a sensitive probe of late-stage hadronic interactions since its lifetime is comparable to that of the hadronic phase in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC. Statistical hadronization model calculations, predicting yields at chemical freeze-out, overestimate the measured ratio. The transverse-momentum spectra and the centrality dependence of the suppression are reproduced by the MUSIC hydrodynamic model only when coupled to the SMASH hadronic transport afterburner, which implements rescattering and regeneration in the late hadronic stage. The measurement, which represents the first observation of resonance suppression within a single collision system, provides a stringent test of the late-stage dynamics and evidence that hadronic interactions substantially modify reconstructible resonance yield.

papers.title: Modelling redshift-space distortions with tracer-centred split densities
papers.abstract: Analysing galaxy clustering in split environmental densities has been demonstrated to offer an advantage over standard two-point clustering for extracting cosmological information. A major challenge to realising this potential with the density-split (DS) technique is that the observations are in redshift space. This complicates its modelling, primarily because the density-split centres may not be conserved between real and redshift space. We develop a modelling framework that splits on the tracer-centred density PDF, rather than the volume-weighted density PDF commonly used in previous studies. We derive the linear bias associated with the threshold density in redshift space, enabling us to connect large-scale DS clustering to the density PDF. We find that the threshold density field consists of doughnut-like structures, which we term `Island(s)'. We propose an empirical model, analogous to the halo model framework, that comprises linear, non-linear, and stochastic terms and accurately reproduces the anisotropic redshift-space clustering of tracers in each DS bin. Using this model, we confirm that DS clustering can provide tighter constraints on cosmological parameters than the standard two-point statistic. Furthermore, we show that the gain in cosmological information from DS analyses relative to standard two-point statistics arises primarily from knowledge of the density PDF, which incorporates small-scale perturbation modes below the smoothing scale.

papers.title: Sticky Manifold Piecewise Deterministic Monte Carlo for Bayesian Model Averaging
papers.abstract: Assigning positive prior probability to lower-dimensional submodels enriches the range of uncertainty that Bayesian models can represent. The resulting posterior distributions combine continuous parameter uncertainty with discrete model uncertainty. Efficient movement between these submodels, however, can be difficult to design. We propose the sticky manifold construction as a principled, modular framework for combining piecewise deterministic Markov processes (PDMPs) across different submodels. The integration is rejection-free, requires no additional likelihood evaluations, and retains the non-reversible and ballistic nature of the component PDMP dynamics. We prove that the resulting process leaves the intended mixed-dimensional target invariant. We also develop a manifold PDMP algorithm based on coordinate charts to provide the within-submodel dynamics and a blow-up procedure that resolves singular sets into codimension-one sticky boundaries. This geometric construction makes the remaining design choices explicit; component dynamics and unsticking kernels can be chosen freely, subject to easily verifiable velocity compatibility conditions. Finally, we demonstrate the sticky manifold algorithms in Bayesian model averaging examples, propagating uncertainty over pure versus mixed states in quantum state tomography, rank in Bayesian principal component analysis, and parametric families in survival extrapolation.

papers.title: Skill Adapter: Personalized Modification and Online Routing of General-Purpose Skills
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents use external skills to reuse task procedures and experience with tools. General-purpose skills describe shared execution procedures, while specific tool choices, operating practices, and output requirements vary across users. In long-horizon tasks, subgoals, available inputs, and environmental states change as execution progresses. Agents must select currently applicable skills from an expanding skill pool and prepare candidates for subsequent steps. We propose Skill Adapter, which enables personalized modification and online routing of general-purpose skills. The system distills local adjustments from user requirements and execution feedback and stores them as Adapters linked to general-purpose skills. The routing agent selects general-purpose skills and applicable Adapters based on the current subtask, execution progress, and environmental feedback, incrementally maintaining a task-level online skill library that the main LLM reads on demand. The system preloads candidates for subsequent nodes and rechecks their applicability once actual inputs are determined. Reinforcement learning optimizes the two types of decisions using modification gains and routing outcomes, respectively. We evaluate Skill Adapter on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SkillsBench. Compared with SkillRL, it improves task success rates by an average of 11.43 percentage points and reduces mean execution time on all three benchmarks. Skill Adapter retains its performance advantage when the skill pool grows to 1,000 skills.

papers.title: Infinite spin superparticles
papers.abstract: We obtain infinite spin representations of the super-Poincaré algebra from a higher-derivative superparticle action on a super-Minkowski background in 3, 4, 6 and 10 dimensions. Super-twistor transforms are performed, and used to deduce first-quantised spectra.

papers.title: An Integrated Architecture for Data-Efficient Real-Time Neural Imitation of Nonlinear Time-Optimal Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) enables highly performant control of constrained systems, but its computational cost prohibits real-time use on fast dynamical systems. Neural network imitation of the TOMPC control law can reduce online computational costs, yet existing work mostly targets quadratic cost formulations in simulation and addresses the challenges of neural controllers in isolation. This work imitates a long-horizon nonconvex TOMPC with hard terminal constraints, whose high computational cost limits training-data generation. We present (i) \emph{self-informed sampling (SIFS)}, a data-efficient expert-sampling strategy that uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert only where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior, (ii) a complete training and control architecture that jointly addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal expert labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction and model mismatch, and (iii) real-world validation on a Furuta pendulum. SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz. On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.

papers.title: Real log canonical tresholds and real log canonical tresholds with signs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the properties of the real log canonical threshold $\text{rlct}(X,Y)$ associated with a pair $(X,Y)$ and the real log canonical thresholds with signs $\text{rlct}^{\pm}(f)$ associated with a polynomial function $f: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we relate these invariants to other invariants arising from the theory of motivic integration. We also show how to compute these invariants in several particular cases, including the Newton non-degenerate case and the case of analytically irreducible plane curve germs.

papers.title: Maturity$^2$: Assessing the Maturity of Crypto Agility Maturity Models
papers.abstract: Crypto agility maturity models aim to support organizations in preparing for cryptographic transitions, such as migrating to post-quantum cryptography. Recognizing the importance of measurable maturity, NIST references several such models in its guidance. Given NIST's influence on cybersecurity practice, these models may shape organizational planning and governance mechanisms. However, their design quality has not been systematically evaluated. In this work, we assess three industry-driven maturity models against established design principles. Our analysis reveals recurring weaknesses, particularly the lack of measurable, reproducible assessment criteria and limited prescriptive guidance for improving crypto agility. At the same time, we highlight individual strengths that can assist practitioners in choosing among the models and derive concrete recommendations for strengthening future crypto agility maturity models.

papers.title: Hausdorff measures of planar Brownian level sets
papers.abstract: For any Hausdorff gauge \(h\), we prove that all level sets of planar Brownian motion have zero \(h\)-measure almost surely if and only if \(\liminf_{r\to0^+}h(r)\log(1/r)=0\). This resolves Taylor's question for arbitrary Hausdorff gauges. The proof yields \(0<\HH^{h_0}(L_x)<\infty\) for some \(x\) almost surely, where \(h_0(r)=1/\log(1/r)\). The Hausdorff dimensions of the spatial mass superlevel sets form a deterministic, strictly decreasing bi-Lipschitz spectrum. For each fixed positive mass below the supremum, the exact-mass set almost surely has the same dimension as the corresponding superlevel set.

papers.title: Reflection Zeros Set the Scattering Invariant of Finite Majorana Wires
papers.abstract: Majorana modes, zero-energy excitations of superconducting wires that are their own antiparticles, could store quantum information protected from local noise. In transport experiments, however, ordinary bound states mimic their signature, a conductance peak at zero voltage, and whether Majorana modes have been observed remains debated. A sign, $Q$, of the electron reflection at zero energy marks the topological phase of a long wire, but what $Q$ certifies in a finite device has been unclear. Here we show for the first time that $Q$ counts reflectionless states, waves that enter through one contact and leave entirely through the other: $Q=-1$ when an odd number of them lie in the lower half of the complex energy plane. In a finite wire this means that the two Majorana modes are split by less than their coupling to the contacts. With equal contacts, every sign change of $Q$, including the bulk topological transition, is an exceptional point at which two such states merge and transmission is maximally flat. At zero temperature, $Q=-1$ exactly when the zero-bias conductance measured at a contact exceeds $e^2/h$. These results show what transport can certify about a Majorana device and how to read the invariant from conductance.

papers.title: Macroscopic $L^\infty$ bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation
papers.abstract: We establish an instantaneous global $L^\infty(\R^3)$ bound at positive times for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions to the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, where the upper bound depends solely on the initial mass, momentum, energy, and entropy. This resolves an open problem posed by Golding, Gualdani, and Loher \cite{GGL} without requiring any initial higher velocity moments, Fisher information, or Lebesgue integrability. The proof builds on two main analytical ingredients. First, we establish the instantaneous generation of the negatively weighted Fisher information with weight $\la{v}^{-1}$. On the lifted two-particle phase space, we compare the separable weight matrix against a collision-invariant pair weight and control the rotational commutator near the diagonal via the quadratic local mass decay supplied by the conserved energy, closing a Riccati differential inequality at the second-moment threshold. Second, to overcome the $\la{v}^{-3}$ radial degeneracy of the diffusion matrix at large velocities, we prove a truncated anisotropic mixed Nash inequality on upper level sets of the density that recovers longitudinal regularity from two transverse Fisher directions and the nonlinear high-density part of the Coulomb entropy dissipation. Localizing this functional inequality to radially aligned velocity cells with the critical weight $\la{v}^{3/2}$ and coupling it with a weighted truncated entropy identity across nested exterior domains yields a superlinear De Giorgi recurrence that bounds the velocity tail uniformly in $\R^3$.

papers.title: Dynamical mean-field theory of latching Potts networks
papers.abstract: Spontaneous transitions between memories, as observed in internally generated cognition such as mind-wandering and free association, require neural dynamics capable of destabilizing one attractive memory state and moving towards another. We ask what minimal representational structure is required for such transitions to emerge in random associative networks. To address this question, we study Potts associative networks with $S$ active states per unit and slow adaptive thresholds. The $S=1$ case can model a standard Hopfield-like network of binary units. We employ dynamical mean-field theory in the extensive-load regime, where the number of stored patterns scales linearly with network size and connectivity, and we focus on transitions between two condensed memories, which are singled out in the connectivity matrix. In the finite-load regime, we show that transitions are governed by an effective drive term, whose sign and temporal evolution distinguish high-latching (structured), low-latching (random), and non-latching regimes. The resulting phase diagram shows that adaptation alone is not sufficient: transitions only occur within certain ranges of the overlap between the two memories. In the binary case $S=1$, in particular, no unit can be active in both memories but in different Potts states, thus strongly supressing the high-latching, structured transitions that exist for $S>1$. In the extensive-load regime, non-condensed memories generate colored fluctuations and retarded self-interactions through an effective memory kernel. We find that latching trajectories change the effective timescale of this kernel, a dynamical signature of transitions in the extensive-load regime. These results indicate that multi-state Potts-like representations are essential for structured memory-to-memory transitions, a hallmark of spontaneous thought.

papers.title: Achiral-Chiral Dissociation and Structural Zero of the Current in the Spinterface Model of CISS
papers.abstract: We study the transport sector of the spinterface model of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) under spin-resolved dissipation, extending the quantum non-equilibrium Green's function formulation of Ref.~\cite{Alwan2026QSpinterface} to spin-resolved lead broadenings. The spin current decomposes into an achiral part, driven by the interfacial moment, and a chiral part, driven by the Rashba spin flip. Under increasing lead spin asymmetry, the achiral part grows linearly while the chiral part follows the geometric-mean suppression, so the two sectors dissociate; they also peak at different coupling scales along the lead broadening. The coupling and bias optima are operating points of the reference configuration, not universal scaling laws. A structural zero appears at $λ_R\sin(ϕ/2)=t_{\mathrm{mol}}$ in the collinear-lead configuration, where the chiral signal collapses to machine precision universally across chain lengths, frequency resolutions, and twist angles; the zero originates from the rank-one singular bond matrix, whose null eigenvector traps an electron in a spin-superposition dark state that does not hop. With non-collinear ferromagnetic leads, the zero is broken in a controlled way: the residual is generically linear in the transverse polarization, arising from a single coherent spin flip at a boundary, and becomes quadratic at a tuned cancellation angle where two boundary contributions interfere destructively, with the scaling exponent jumping sharply from one to two. These results establish the spinterface model as a transport platform with a two-axis dissociation structure, non-scaling operating optima, and an exact structural zero whose non-collinear deformation is a clean linear-plus-quadratic hierarchy.

papers.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
papers.abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

papers.title: Channel-Chart-Driven Antenna Activation for Energy-Efficient Cell-Free Massive MIMO
papers.abstract: Cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) can provide uniformly high system performance across the coverage area through distributed cooperation. However, keeping all antennas active leads to high circuit and fronthaul power consumption. This paper studies energy-efficient uplink reception through antenna activation, where only a subset of distributed antennas is selected to serve the users. To enable network-wide activation with low signaling overhead, each access point (AP) maps its locally estimated channel state information (CSI) into a lowdimensional channel-chart (CC) embedding and forwards this representation to the central processing unit (CPU) instead of the full CSI. Based on the received embeddings, we formulate a binary antenna-activation problem for network EE maximization and propose three low-overhead strategies: (i) direct embeddingdomain activation using a proxy EE metric without CSI reconstruction, (ii) nearest chart-point CSI approximation, which estimates CSI from a reference chart database for greedy EE optimization, and (iii) decoder-based CSI reconstruction using a pre-trained autoencoder. The proposed approaches further enable a systematic comparison of antenna activation techniques in terms of achieved performance, computational complexity, and signaling overhead. Numerical results show substantial EE gains over the all-active baseline, with only a minor degradation in sum spectral efficiency and a significant reduction in signaling overhead. Moreover, the proposed greedy framework achieves EE performance close to that of the simulated annealing baseline, confirming its effectiveness for low-complexity antenna activation.

papers.title: Entire sig-jump-diffusions, their expected signature and applications to score-based generative modeling
papers.abstract: We develop score-based generative models for time series and standard finite-dimensional data, building on the analytical computation of the expected signature of a new class of jump-diffusions, called entire sig-jump-diffusions. These are semimartingales whose characteristics are given by linear combinations of potentially infinitely many components of their own signature.
