We extend the result to smooth functions of GMM parameters, allowing the different moment components to exhibit different dependence regimes. In simulations, the proposed confidence intervals achieve coverage close to the nominal level across the dependence regimes considered.

papers.title: ReFineR: Single image to dense point cloud registration at pixel level with point splatting
papers.abstract: Cameras and LiDARs (Light Detection and Ranging) provide complementary observations of the same scene: cameras capture rich appearance cues while LiDAR sensors provide accurate geometric measurements. In this work, we address the problem of fine image-to-point cloud registration from a single image and a roughly estimated camera pose. On robotic platforms, residual reprojection errors of several pixels are commonly observed even after calibration due to temporal desynchronization, mechanical vibrations, or inaccuracies in point cloud reconstruction. Such errors can lead to decimeter-level geometric discrepancies at moderate distances and significantly affect multiple downstream tasks, such as dense cross-modal supervision, texture mapping, and semantic label transfer. To address this challenge, we introduce ReFineR: an offline framework to finely register individual images to pre-reconstructed point clouds. ReFineR builds upon differentiable point splatting rasterization and a smooth Gradient Orientation Measure (GOM) to iteratively refine the camera pose through analysis-by-synthesis optimization. We evaluated the method on a curated dataset of manually calibrated images collected from heterogeneous data sources. Furthermore, we show that an automatic point cloud rescale factor can be estimated prior to optimization, enabling robust refinement across a wide range of scenarios using a single scale-invariant formulation. The project page can be found at https://refiner-project.github.io/

papers.title: Phonon-mediated visible upconversion luminescence in femtosecond 1030-nm pumped Tm3+ -doped silica fibres
papers.abstract: We investigate multiphoton absorption-driven visible luminescence in a thulium-doped aluminosilicate optical fiber excited by an ultrafast 1030-nm femtosecond pulse train in the {MHz domain}. We report the observation of an unusual spectral crossover: the predominance of an emission band centered at 457-nm (deep blue) is progressively overtaken by a second emission, centered at 475-nm (cyan), as launched average power increases. Concurrently, a third near-infrared emission around 792~nm exhibits persistent, monotonic growth characterized by a well-defined bilinear slope transition. By combining calibrated spectral band integration with a structure-informed rate-equation model based on host thermodynamics, we show that the visible spectra evolution is governed by non-radiative multi-phonon transfer and phonon-assisted cross-relaxation activated by cumulative core heating, rather than permanent color-center solarization. These results offer new predictive insights into the thermal and spectroscopic stability of high-power ultrafast fiber systems.

papers.title: Do the Details Help the Whole? One-Way Transfer from Person Actions to Group Intent in VLMs on JRDB-Social
papers.abstract: Social scene datasets label people at two levels: what each person is doing and what the group is there for. Training on both levels at once is often assumed to help each of them. We test this assumption for vision-language models (VLMs) on JRDB-Social, treating person actions as the details and group intent as the whole. We fine-tune Qwen3.5 4B under eight training arms with three seeds, repeat the core arms on Qwen3.5 9B and Qwen3-VL 4B, and judge every arm with a verdict rule fixed before testing. Writing each member's actions before the intent raises intent macro-F1 from 30.1 to 31.0, and writing the intent first reaches 31.2, while action F1 stays within 0.2 points of an action-only model. Under the selected recipe, no arm trained with intent improves actions. The gain requires correct, image-grounded actions: empty action lists or actions borrowed from another group with the same intent lower intent F1. Forced-prefix tests, occlusion, member masking, linear probes and component grafting show that the intent follows the written actions, relies more on people and partly resides in the vision tower. Supplying actions as input instead of as targets hurts both levels.

papers.title: Scaling limits of Chebyshev polynomials at a hard edge
papers.abstract: Let $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be compact. We derive local scaling limits of the Chebyshev polynomials associated to $\mathsf{E}$ at a gap edge. We describe the scaling limits by a one parameter family of functions explicitly given by elliptic integrals. We show that for the union of two generic intervals all functions in this family are in fact attained as limits. As a consequence, we describe the local scaling behavior of the zeros of the Chebyshev polynomials at the gap edge.

papers.title: ActWorld-JEPA: Action-Conditioned JEPA World Models Meet Latent Planning for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) enable future prediction in latent space without pixel reconstruction. However, latent predictive consistency alone does not establish the relative driving quality of candidate plans. We present ActWorld-JEPA, a joint-embedding formulation for candidate-based driving. Where Plan-Conditioned JEPA (PC-JEPA) uses global and step-wise trajectory intentions to guide recurrent latent prediction, then combines the predicted future with the current scene through gated cross-attention; Relational Residual Reranking ($R^3$) models agreement and discrepancy between plan and future representations under planning supervision, yielding bounded, gated residual corrections to the base planning scores. This formulation connects latent prediction to candidate selection using only observed context and proposed trajectories at inference. Benchmark-specific implementations report 94.1 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, with the final selector calibrated using aggregate NAVTEST feedback, and 91.6 and 42.7 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navtest and navhard, respectively. The nuScenes evaluation reports a mean $L_2$ error of 1.20 m and a predicted collision rate of 0.76% over 1--6 s. This work provides an effective path from JEPA's predictive representations to driving decisions informed by anticipated consequences.

papers.title: Asymptotic Attainability of the Channel RLD Fisher-Information Bound
papers.abstract: The channel right-logarithmic-derivative (RLD) Fisher information is a computable upper bound on the optimal asymptotic symmetric-logarithmic-derivative (SLD) Fisher information per channel use over causally ordered, parameter-independent strategies. The bound is not always attained, even if the Choi matrix is positive definite. We determine exactly when equality holds using a semidefinite feasibility condition involving only the Choi matrix and its first derivative. The condition allows a degenerate largest eigenvalue of the RLD matrix and rank-deficient Choi matrices with derivatives supported on their range. The original channel family may change rank nearby. For generalized dephasing channels with a positive-definite correlation matrix at the evaluation point, the condition becomes a system of linear equations for nonnegative certificate weights that sum to one. At a completely dephasing point we also calculate the optimal SLD information for every finite number of uses and show that a repeated, ancilla-free probe attains it, even against adaptive strategies. Explicit examples give an unbounded ratio of the channel RLD information to the optimal asymptotic SLD information per use, either as the dimension grows or at fixed qubit dimension as the smallest Choi eigenvalue tends to zero. We derive the equality criterion and its consequences from the asymptotic optimization of Zhou and Jiang.

papers.title: Estimation and Inference for Multiplicative Error Models via Analytical Derivatives
papers.abstract: Maximum Likelihood Estimates (MLEs) of the parameters of a Multiplicative Error Model are typically computed through a standard gradient method, an iterative procedure usually based on numerical approximations to derivatives of the log-likelihood function, owing to the complexity of the analytical derivatives, which involve recursive terms. Building on previous work developed mainly in the GARCH framework, we derive analytical expressions for the score vector and the Hessian matrix of the Multiplicative Error Model log-likelihood by adopting the Gamma distribution for estimation purposes. Then, we illustrate how the iterative algorithm based on the analytical derivatives should be computationally implemented. After maximizing the log-likelihood, we also provide explicit formulas for several estimators of the asymptotic covariance matrix of the MLE. Additionally, we provide analytic formulas for robust covariance estimators that remain valid under distributional misspecification, which are also referred to as the asymptotic variance of the Quasi-Maximum Likelihood Estimator. We also propose a covariance estimator that is consistent under general forms of heteroskedasticity of the error term, while the usually adopted estimators rely on a specific variance assumption. The finite-sample performance of the covariance estimators is assessed through a Monte Carlo investigation. An application on real data completes the analysis.

papers.title: Low-lying doubly charmed strange baryons via QCD sum rules
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the masses of the low-lying doubly heavy baryons and their $B^*(3/2^+)\to B(1/2^+)γ$ radiative transitions within QCD sum rules and light-cone sum rules (LCSR). By constructing mixed interpolating currents, we obtain $M_{Ξ_{cc}}=3.62^{+0.14}_{-0.15}$ GeV, $M_{Ξ_{cc}^*}=3.72^{+0.14}_{-0.13}$ GeV, $M_{Ω_{cc}}=3.72^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, and $M_{Ω_{cc}^*}=3.82^{+0.13}_{-0.15}$ GeV, together with their doubly bottom partners around $10.27$--$10.34$ GeV. The extracted masses are compatible with the observed $Ξ_{cc}$ and $Ω_{cc}$ states and predict hyperfine splittings of about $101^{+27}_{-11}$ MeV and $99^{+11}_{-12}$ MeV for the $Ξ_{cc}$ and $Ω_{cc}$ systems, respectively. Using these inputs, we derive the LCSR for the electromagnetic form factors and obtain radiative widths $Γ(Ξ_{cc}^{*++}\toΞ_{cc}^{++}γ)=5.25^{+8.57}_{-3.62}$ keV, $Γ(Ξ_{cc}^{*+}\toΞ_{cc}^{+}γ)=0.31^{+0.84}_{-0.25}$ keV, and $Γ(Ω_{cc}^{*+}\toΩ_{cc}^{+}γ)=0.41^{+0.67}_{-0.30}$ keV, while the corresponding doubly bottom widths are at the $0.002$--$0.01$ keV level. We find that the magnetic-dipole contribution dominates, whereas the electric-quadrupole form factor is numerically small. The light- and heavy-quark photon-emission terms can interfere or enhance significantly, and the heavy-quark contribution cannot be neglected in radiative transitions. These results provide useful theoretical guidance for future searches for spin-$3/2$ doubly heavy baryons through radiative decay modes at LHCb, Belle II, and other experimental facilities.

papers.title: Elasto-inertial force exerted on a sphere oscillating in a fluid near a soft interface
papers.abstract: Fluid inertia can remain important in confined flows, even at low Reynolds number when convective inertia is negligible; yet its coupling with interface deformability is an open problem. Here, we theoretically investigate the high-frequency oscillations of an immersed sphere near an elastic wall in the lubrication regime. We first reconcile previous predictions for the added mass near a rigid wall by consistently matching the inner lubrication flow with the outer flow. Using this rigid-wall problem as a reference, we then develop a perturbative analysis of wall deformation and derive the leading elasto-inertial correction to the hydrodynamic force. Our results reveal that the coupling between interface softness and fluid inertia produces a dominant non-dissipative force contribution scaling as the power four of the frequency in the high-frequency limit, thus corresponding to the fourth time derivative of the sphere's position. This finding may have implications regarding the short-time dynamics of colloidal particles near deformable interfaces in biological and soft-matter settings.

papers.title: HALight: Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Traffic Signal Control under Lane-Level Missing Observations
papers.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning has shown great promise for traffic signal control. However, most existing methods rely on two key assumptions: (i) agents are assumed to be homogeneous with unified observation/action spaces; (ii) full and reliable lane-level traffic observations are available to all agents. In practice, urban road networks exhibit substantial structural heterogeneity (e.g., lane configurations and phase designs), while sensor failures and incomplete detector coverage often result in missing incoming lane measurements. Such issues can severely impair coordination and destabilize learning. To address these challenges, we propose HALight, a communication-enhanced heterogeneous multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for traffic signal control under lane-level missing observations. HALight supports intersection-specific observation and action modeling to accommodate heterogeneous intersections, and incorporates a lightweight one-hop neighborhood communication module to enrich spatial context when lane-level observations are partially unavailable. Moreover, HALight adopts a sequential policy update scheme to improve coordination among heterogeneous agents. Experimental results on two real-world road networks demonstrate that HALight outperforms representative homogeneous and heterogeneous baselines in terms of traffic efficiency and convergence behavior. The code and datasets used in this work are available at https://github.com/Huchenkaii/HALight.

papers.title: Tight Cycle-Cover Inequalities and Improved Approximation for Shortest Common Superstring with Reverse Complements
papers.abstract: The Shortest Common Superstring (SCS) problem is a classical idealized model of genome assembly. However, SCS does not account for the double-stranded nature of DNA: sequencing reads may originate from either strand without a known orientation. This motivates a natural variant, Shortest Common Superstring with Reverse Complements (SCS-RC), which asks for a shortest string containing each input string or its reverse complement as a substring. For SCS, the MGREEDY algorithm constructs an optimal cycle cover of the overlap graph and concatenates the strings obtained by breaking each cycle at its minimum-overlap edge. This algorithm was recently shown to achieve a tight $3$-approximation. Its reverse-complement extension, MGREEDY-RC, also constructs an optimal cycle cover of the overlap graph augmented with reverse complements, but its best known approximation guarantee was $3.75$ (CPM 2026). We extend this cycle-cover inequality to SCS-RC and show that MGREEDY-RC achieves a $3$-approximation, which is tight even over the DNA alphabet. The $3$-approximation guarantee for MGREEDY-RC yields a $2.5$-approximation for TGREEDY-RC, which greedily merges the strings derived from the cycle cover. By replacing this greedy merging step with an algorithm based on a reduction to a maximum-weight Hamiltonian path problem constrained to contain a given perfect matching, we obtain a $(22/9+\varepsilon)$-approximation for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. This improves upon the previous best ratio of $8/3$ (WABI 2026), establishing the best known polynomial-time approximation guarantee for SCS-RC.

papers.title: Critical mass for infinite-time blow-up in a Keller-Segel system with indirect signal production on closed Riemannian surfaces
papers.abstract: We study a parabolic-elliptic-ODE chemotaxis system with indirect signal production on closed connected Riemannian surfaces. For all sufficiently regular nonnegative initial data, the system admits a unique global classical solution. We show that the solution remains globally bounded if the total mass $M<8π$. For each $M>8π$, we find initial data of mass $M$ that yield infinite-time blow-up solutions. We then adapt the argument to the corresponding Neumann problem in a smooth bounded planar domain and obtain infinite-time blow-up solutions for any mass $M>4π$. At the critical mass $M=8π$, we show that the solutions are globally bounded on spheres equipped with the canonical spherical metric, and we construct a solution blowing up in infinite time on the Riemann sphere equipped with a special metric.

papers.title: Kobayashi distance to submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold
papers.abstract: We prove that totally geodesic hypersurfaces are at infinite Kobayashi distance in a Kobayashi hyperbolic Riemannian manifold. To do this, we prove a Schwarz lemma on minimal maps with a uniform control on their Laplacians. Finally we give a full characterisation of submanifolds at infinite distance on spaces of constant sectional curvature in dimension at least 4.

papers.title: On graceful labeling of Jahangir graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph with q edges, a graceful labeling assigns distinct integers from {0,...,q} its vertices so that the absolute differences across the edges are exactly 1,...,q. A Jahangir graph J_{n,m}, with n >= 2 and m >= 3, consists of an outer cycle on nm vertices and a hub joined to m equally spaced vertices of that cycle, with q = (n+1)m edges. This family of graphs is known to be graceful. In this paper we strengthen the gracefulness property of such graphs by assigning labels to their vertices through a parametric formula. These labeled graphs have a mono tonicity property: deleting an edge from the outer cycle leaves a path whose edge differences, in the negative orientation, are strictly increasing for even n and strictly decreasing for odd n. The starting observation is that large differences admit few endpoint pairs and require adjacencies between high and low labels. This suggests a construction based on alternating two separated label sets along the outer cycle. The formula has two parity branches, each with two cases modulo 4. Applications are given for every case.

papers.title: Can STATCOM and UPS-Based Voltage Support Mitigate Fault-Induced Reductions in AI Data Center Grid Power Draw?
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs) are rapidly increasing in number and capacity. These large electronic loads are interfaced through power electronic devices and can sharply reduce grid power intake during fault-induced voltage sags. Disturbances exceeding equipment ride-through capabilities may also trigger protective disconnection, posing risks to power system security. Static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) and appropriately controlled AIDC uninterruptible power supply (UPS) rectifiers can provide reactive power support during voltage sags. This paper compares the individual and combined effectiveness of STATCOM and UPS-based voltage support in mitigating fault-induced reductions in grid power intake through electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1 GW AIDC connected to an IEEE nine-bus system. Simulation results show that STATCOM support better preserves short-term intake in milder tested faults, whereas UPS coordination maintains rectifier operation under deeper sags by reducing active intake to reserve reactive current capacity. Combined support improves auxiliary load retention and recovery in selected cases. However, severe tested sags still cause substantial grid-demand reductions even with combined support.

papers.title: Accelerating solitons in Rindler space
papers.abstract: Relativistic nonlinear field theories that are integrable in two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime remain integrable in Rindler space. We investigate the properties of classical sine-Gordon (SG) solitons in Rindler space. Accelerating observers in each of the two Rindler wedges can see only a portion of the full soliton in Minkowski spacetime; this portion itself forms a soliton carrying a partial topological charge. The soliton solution admits the following interpretation: a soliton incoming from the horizon decelerates to stop at some point, then falls back and accelerates to the speed of light toward the horizon. Energy can flow into and out of the Rindler horizon. The higher energy soliton gains energy from the horizon while the lower one loses energy.

papers.title: Micromagnetic modelling and simulation of inertial magnetization dynamics in ferromagnets
papers.abstract: Magnetization dynamics at sub-picosecond time scales can exhibit inertial effects beyond the conventional Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert description, giving rise to nutational motion at terahertz frequencies. Following its theoretical prediction and experimental observation in ferromagnets, magnetic inertia has attracted increasing interest for understanding and controlling ultrafast spin dynamics. In this topical review, we discuss the theoretical modelling and micromagnetic simulation of inertial magnetization dynamics in ferromagnetic nanostructures. Starting from the mechanical analogy underlying the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, we introduce its spatially inhomogeneous micromagnetic formulation and discuss its main properties, including magnetization-length conservation, angular-momentum relaxation, and the generalized free-energy balance. We then review the linear dynamics of inertial spin waves, highlighting the coexistence of GHz precessional and THz nutational branches, the inertial redshift of precessional modes, spectral linewidths, and the effects of exchange, magnetostatic interactions, confinement, curvature and torsion. Particular attention is devoted to the large-wavenumber regime, where magnetic inertia leads to a finite limiting spin-wave propagation velocity. Finally, we address frequency- and time-domain micromagnetic simulation techniques for spatially nonuniform inertial dynamics, including geometric midpoint integrators preserving the fundamental constraints and energy properties of the continuous dynamics. Applications to the excitation and propagation of ultrashort nutational spin waves and ultrafast inertial magnetization switching illustrate the role of micromagnetic modelling in connecting inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert theory with experimentally accessible nanoscale magnetization dynamics.

papers.title: Towards Automated Recommendation of Steady-State Detection Algorithms for Software Performance Benchmarks
papers.abstract: Steady-state detection is a central step in software performance benchmarking, yet different detection methods rely on different assumptions and may perform best on different execution profiles. This paper formulates steady-state detection as an algorithm-recommendation problem: given a benchmark time series, predict which of two complementary detectors is more appropriate. The first, CP-SSD, identifies steady state through changepoint-based segmentation of the execution trace, whereas the second, KB-KSSD, uses a kernel-based approach to identify stable behaviour. We propose a data-driven recommender that characterises benchmark time series using automatically extracted features and combines supervised prediction with information derived from groups of time series exhibiting similar behaviour. The approach is evaluated on 407 labelled benchmark time series for which one of the two detectors can be identified as preferable with respect to a reference steady-state index. The proposed recommender selects the better detector correctly for 72.97% of the series, compared with 62.65% when always selecting the detector that performs best most often, corresponding to an absolute improvement of 10.32 percentage points. Paired statistical testing and bootstrap confidence intervals support this improvement. A comparison with a recommender using time-series features alone shows that the cluster-derived information mainly improves interpretability rather than predictive accuracy. Recommendations also remain highly stable when the unsupervised representation is learned from either the labelled subset or the full collection of 5,860 time series. These results demonstrate the feasibility of per-series steady-state detector recommendation while highlighting the need for broader labelled data, particularly for execution profiles favouring the changepoint-based detector.

papers.title: Look Here, Then Decide: Small Decision Models in a Harness Find Memory-Safety Vulnerabilities at Scale on Commodity GPUs
papers.abstract: We ask whether small, open-weight decision models can support vulnerability discovery in open-source software at scale and what the surrounding system must provide. These models answer a typed question in one forward pass, returning scores for the permitted answers rather than text. Our harness selects widely packaged C and C++ projects and uses deterministic incomplete-fix miners and shape localizers to decide where to look. Intern-Decision-4B, a 4B-parameter open-weight decision model, then scores every candidate function. The scores rank the queues rather than accept or reject candidates, apart from a low reach-score floor that some queues kept. The search uses no frontier model. Alone, the model is weak: it separates vulnerable from benign functions with AUC 0.73, but a vulnerable function from its own patch with only 0.56. It is more useful for ordering candidates. On 75 public CVEs from projects without any of our findings, the fixed function reached its repository's top 25 in 21% of cases, 1.4 times as often as under random order of the same queues. Recall is bounded mainly by where the localizers look. On the campaign's own queues the model's order placed 7.5 times more confirmed findings in the top 10 than random order, an observed, selection-biased upper bound. On three GB10 systems, the harness searched more than 4,000 projects at 900-1,100 repositories per hour. The campaign confirmed 187 memory-safety findings; by worst-case CVSS v3.1, 12 are critical, 148 high, 23 medium and 4 low. The decision step runs at 4.4 decisions per second on one GB10 and 9.8 on a consumer RTX 4090 gaming PC, with matching scores. A small decision model supports vulnerability discovery through prioritization, while deterministic analysis and verification remain essential. All confirmed findings are being disclosed to maintainers under coordinated disclosure before publication.

papers.title: Tricritical Dynamics Reveal Black Hole Interior Geometry
papers.abstract: We reconstruct the interior Kasner exponents of a scalarized black-hole equilibrium from the growth rate of a radial perturbation outside the horizon. The equal-entropy coexistence line of Reissner--Nordström and scalarized phases ends at a tricritical point. We follow the intermediate equilibrium separating the two phases along the coexistence line. The radial growth rate $Ω_u$ is proportional to the magnitude of the entropy-potential curvature. As the tricritical point is approached, the curvature vanishes as the fourth power of the horizon scalar amplitude. The interior logarithmic scalar gradient grows inversely with the horizon amplitude. Eliminating the amplitude connects exterior dynamics to interior geometry, giving the angular Kasner exponent $p\sim2\sqrt{Ω_u/C}$. The static source expansion and the critical Reissner--Nordström zero mode fix $C$ before the scalarized interior is integrated. We compute the growth rate from linear radial perturbations on asymptotically flat and anti-de Sitter black-hole backgrounds. At the sampled equilibria closest to tricriticality, the reconstructed angular exponent agrees with the result of independent inward integration at about the $0.5\%$ level.

papers.title: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions
papers.abstract: Qudits, which generalize qubits to $d$ levels, store more information per circuit element than qubits. As with qubits, however, their sensitivity to noise must be overcome before they can be used for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Here we show that, by exploiting the second harmonic of the current--phase relation, a superconducting loop of three Josephson junctions can host qutrits strongly protected against relaxation, while dephasing limits their coherence. When the second harmonic is positive, a simple loop with a small asymmetry between the junctions provides a tunable, symmetry-protected qutrit. When it is negative, a protected qutrit can be realized by adding a small symmetry-breaking term, such as a weak Josephson diode effect. The two designs involve different trade-offs: the first has an exact charge selection rule, whereas the second is nearly insensitive to charge noise and its quasiparticle errors can be corrected. The preferable choice therefore depends on the materials used. Both require a sizable second harmonic to begin with, and we identify altermagnetic Josephson junctions as a candidate platform. Finally, microscopic calculations show that a gate voltage selects the sign of the second harmonic in these junctions, although gate-voltage noise then becomes the leading source of dephasing. These findings establish the sign of the second harmonic as a design principle for protected superconducting qudits.

papers.title: The Regular Cover Problem is NP-complete
papers.abstract: The regular cover problem is the following question: given a finite language $L$ and a $k\geq 0$, is there an acyclic regular grammar $G$ with at most $k$ productions that covers $L$, i.e., that satisfies $L(G) \supseteq L$. The study of this problem is motivated by applications in proof theory and automated deduction. The regular cover problem is known to be in NP. In this paper we show that it is NP-complete by reducing the vertex cover problem for graphs with maximum degree three to it.

papers.title: SPARC: Accurate Photonic Matrix Multiplication via Representative Vectors
papers.abstract: Photonic neural network accelerators have emerged as a promising solution for reducing the power consumption of deep neural network (DNN) inference by executing matrix multiplication on analog photonic hardware. However, their inference accuracy is limited by low-bit quantization required for photonic processing and by analog photonic noise. This paper proposes an approach for improving inference accuracy by exploiting the high similarity among activation vectors in DNNs. Specifically, our approach constructs a representative vector for each group of similar activation vectors, computes its inner product digitally with high precision, and offloads the residual inner products to the photonic accelerator. Since the activation vectors within each group are highly similar, the residual vectors have much smaller norms, thereby reducing the effects of quantization errors and analog photonic noise. Furthermore, our approach preserves the photonic inner-product computation pipeline, allowing seamless integration into existing and future photonic accelerators without hardware modification. Experimental results on six representative DNN models demonstrate that the proposed approach can improve inference accuracy across diverse network architectures and application domains.

papers.title: When and How SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Functional Scaling Law Perspective
papers.abstract: We study how the sign operator interacts with gradient noise to shape the learning dynamics and scaling behavior of sign-based optimizers. In power-law kernel regression with diagonal features, we establish a functional scaling law (FSL) for SignSGD under general learning rate schedules. The FSL describes the learning dynamics through two processes: signal learning and noise forgetting. The key mechanism is noise-induced preconditioning: gradient noise smooths the sign operator, inducing an effective preconditioned SGD. Noise-curvature alignment enables this preconditioning to transform the effective Hessian from $\mathbf{H}$ to $\mathbf{H}^{1/2}$. The resulting dynamics exhibit faster signal learning but slower noise forgetting than SGD. This tradeoff yields a regime-dependent comparison with SGD: (i) SignSGD achieves improved data efficiency in the hard-task regime; (ii) both optimizers achieve the same data efficiency in the easy-task regime, but SignSGD maintains this efficiency at larger batch sizes, requiring fewer optimization steps for a fixed data budget. Power-law kernel regression experiments support the proposed mechanism and predicted scaling behavior. LLM pre-training experiments further suggest that the SignSGD FSL better captures the batch-size dependence of loss dynamics for sign-based optimizers than the original SGD FSL.

papers.title: Inverse Confounding Analysis: Part 2. Applications to Real- World Observational Data
papers.abstract: Unmeasured confounding factors in observational data may lead to biased estimates of the effect of an exposure on an outcome. Consequently, a central problem in causal inference based on observational data is sensitivity analysis with respect to unmeasured confounding. Existing sensitivity-analysis methods generally focus on worst-case bounds. We propose an exact method for quantifying the significance of confounding, defined here in terms of the complete range of analytical values of the stratification-based Risk Ratio over the set of all joint distributions compatible with the observed characteristics. We refer to the proposed method as Inverse Confounding Analysis (ICA) - it is described in [1]. This paper presents examples of applying ICA to several real-world statistical datasets and examines an important issue that has attracted criticism of the method: the practical feasibility of obtaining the input data required for its application. The results are compared with those of two other methods for confounding analysis, the E-value and the method proposed by Pena.

papers.title: Delta-Iterations: A General-Purpose Linear Regression Solver for Huber's Penalty, $ε$-Insensitive Loss, and Other Moreau Envelope-Based Loss Functions
papers.abstract: A general-purpose linear regression solver for a class of smooth loss functions is presented. The method applies to loss functions of the Moreau envelope type, which are continuously differentiable and have Lipschitz-continuous first derivatives. This class includes piecewise-defined cost functions consisting of constant, linear and quadratic segments, such as Huber's loss, insensitive least squares, one-sided least squares. The convergence guarantee provided by the associated proximal operator, the simplicity of the method and its versatility in handling various cost functions within a unified framework are its main advantages. MATLAB code for reproducing the numerical results presented in this article is provided.

papers.title: Game-Theoretic Analysis of RIS-Assisted Challenge-Response PLA - Part I: Perfect Channel Knowledge
papers.abstract: We consider a physical layer authentication scenario in which a legitimate user (Alice) communicates with an authen- ticator (Bob) through a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), controlled by Bob. An attacker (Trudy) aims to impersonate Alice by suitably precoding her messages and still transmitting them through the RIS. This two-part study analyzes this attack-defense interaction between Bob and Trudy under perfect (Part I) and partial (Part II) channel knowledge by all the agents. Part I formulates the joint RIS selection and precoder design under perfect channel knowledge as a finite zero-sum game, establishing exact channel subspace conditions for attack indistinguishability alongside equilibrium mixed strategies. Part II extends the defense to incomplete channel information, where each agent observes only its own channel, by formulating a finite-action Bayesian game and characterizing the resulting Bayesian Nash equilibrium. Simulations in geometric and 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi-NLOS channels reveal that authentication performance is governed by available spatial degrees of freedom, channel correlation, and operating signal-to-noise ratio. The proposed equilibrium strategies effectively balance communication rate and security, outperforming conventional benchmark policies.

papers.title: Localizing Mean Shifts in High-Dimensional Vector Autoregressive Models
papers.abstract: We study the localization of mean changes in high-dimensional vector autoregressions (VARs) when the autoregressive dynamics remain common across regimes. We develop a three-step procedure that first obtains preliminary change-point estimates from the raw series ignoring the dependence structure, then estimates a common sparse VAR using observations away from the estimated changes, and finally filters the series to refine the change point locations. For a single change point, we show that the preliminary localization rate depends directly on the strength of temporal dependence, whereas filtering removes this dependence penalty from the oracle rate. With an estimated filter, the refined rate additionally reflects the error in estimating the VAR dynamics and the relation between the change in the stationary mean and the corresponding change in the VAR intercept. We characterize these rates explicitly and establish conditions under which filtering improves localization. Because filtering near a change point uses lags from adjacent regimes, it also creates a short-lived distortion in the filtered mean; we characterize when this boundary effect is innocuous and develop a transition-corrected alternative. We extend the procedure to an unknown number of change points. Overlapping local windows are used to generate candidate locations, an information criterion removes redundant and spurious candidates and estimates the number of changes, and the retained locations are subsequently refined using the estimated VAR filter. We establish consistency for the estimated number of changes and simultaneous localization rates for their locations. Numerical experiments corroborate the localization gains and show robustness to moderate departures from common VAR dynamics. An application to a large panel of U.S. macroeconomic indicators identifies economically interpretable changes.

papers.title: Similarity-Guided Optimization Strategies for Approximate Network Symmetry Detection
papers.abstract: Symmetry in complex networks is a structural property with broad implications for network function, dynamics, and robustness. While classical approaches rely on exact automorphisms and thus remain highly sensitive to small perturbations, recent work of Liu has introduced approximate formulations that relax the strict invariance condition and recast symmetry detection as an optimization problem over permutations. We investigate how node-level similarity information can be used to bias the search toward structurally plausible vertex correspondences, with network centralities serving as one interpretable instance. Building on this perspective, we adapt simulated annealing, genetic algorithms, tabu search, particle swarm optimization, differential evolution and the quadratic symmetry approximator to this problem, add similarity guidance to each, and introduce Bilinear Approximate Symmetry Inference (BASIN), which learns a soft assignment matrix via bilinear embeddings. Using a unified evaluation pipeline, we compare their guided and unguided variants, BASIN and a random baseline on four synthetic graph families, structural brain connectomes, and three empirical networks with known automorphism groups. Node-similarity guidance is decisive where a planted orbit exists that the unguided search misses, and algorithm-dependent elsewhere, on synthetic and empirical networks alike. Overall, tabu search achieves the strongest performance; its guided variant (SGTS) has the lowest median score among the guided variants in all 44 synthetic conditions, while BASIN is the better of the continuous relaxations on rewired lateral graphs. The effect of node-similarity guidance is therefore regime-dependent rather than uniformly positive.

papers.title: The asymptotic number of $BCK(p)$-terms
papers.abstract: A $BCK(p)$-term is a closed lambda-term in which each abstraction binds at most $p$ variables; for $p=1$ these terms are related to the axiom system BCK of combinatory logic. We determine the number of $BCK(p)$-terms of size $n$, up to a constant multiplicative factor, for every $p\ge2$. For $p=2$ the result is fully explicit: \[ f\_n\sim A\,n^{2n/5}2^{n/5}e^{-2n/5}n^{-3/5}e^{P(n^{1/5})}, \] where $P$ is an explicit polynomial of degree $4$. In general the asymptotic formula involves $n^{pn/(2p+1)}$ and an exponential of a polynomial in $n^{1/(2p+1)}$. The proof combines a linearization of the defining functional equation, the analysis of the Borel transform of the linearized generating function, which satisfies a linear differential equation with an irregular singularity at infinity, the saddle point method for Hayman-admissible functions, and positivity arguments comparing the original and the linearized sequences. For $p=1$ this comparison fails: the quadratic term then also changes the polynomial factor.

papers.title: Inelastic Scalar Dark Matter in a Gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ Model and its LZ Phenomenology
papers.abstract: We study inelastic scalar dark matter (DM) in a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ model motivated by the high-energy recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ). The model introduces two complex scalars, $Φ$ and $S$, charged under $U(1)_{B-L}$. The scalar $S$ is responsible for spontaneous symmetry breaking, while the two real components of $Φ$, $ϕ_1$ and $ϕ_2$, serve as DM. This two-component DM framework accommodates both exothermic and endothermic scenarios. In the exothermic scenario, the lifetime of the heavier state $ϕ_1$ exceeds the age of the Universe, and both states contribute to the present-day DM abundance. In the endothermic scenario, the abundance comes almost entirely from the lighter state $ϕ_2$. We investigate the thermal history of the dark sector and find that the two scalars have approximately equal abundances at freeze-out. We identify parameter regions that reproduce the observed relic abundance. We calculate the nuclear recoil spectra, perform a three-bin likelihood analysis, and obtain the best-fit points interpreting the LZ signal in both scenarios.

papers.title: Progress on the MALTA CMOS Sensor: Edge-TCT Measurements for Parametric Pixel Simulation
papers.abstract: MALTA2 is a monolithic active pixel sensor, developed in the 180 nm CMOS imaging technology for radiation-hard applications in high-rate environments. This contribution summarizes recent developments in the characterization and simulation of MALTA2. The charge collection of a sensor on epitaxial silicon is studied with the Edge Transient Current Technique (Edge-TCT), using a digital readout, where the charge is reconstructed solely from binary hit data. In previous works, only specially designed analog output pixels at the matrix periphery were investigated. In contrast, the digital readout gives access to the full edge of the pixel matrix. Laser scans across neighboring pixels enable a two-dimensional parameterization of the charge collection. This parameterization serves as input to a parametric pixel simulation, which has been developed for chip design optimization and system-level studies. The simulation results are validated with test beam data.

papers.title: Hardness, Approximation, and Parameterized Algorithms for Asynchronous Border Minimization
papers.abstract: In the Asynchronous Border Minimization Problem (BMP), a set of DNA probe strings is placed on a grid and synthesized using a common sequence of nucleotide-deposition steps. At each step, every cell may accept or skip the offered nucleotide. The cost is the total number of disagreements between neighboring cells over all steps. We study both free placement, where the probes may be rearranged, and fixed placement, where their positions are given. We show that free-placement BMP on a square grid is NP-complete over three symbols. For one-dimensional BMP, we prove APX-hardness over a binary alphabet, and NP-completeness even when every probe has length two. We also obtain an $8/7$-approximation for the latter restriction. For square grids, we give a randomized $O(n^{1/4}\log n)$-approximation, improving the earlier $O(n^{1/4}\log^2 n)$ guarantee. Both free- and fixed-placement BMP on rectangular grids are fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized only by the allowed border cost.

papers.title: Central limit theorems for Frobenius, Hecke and Kloosterman angles
papers.abstract: The Frobenius angles of non-CM elliptic curves and the Hecke angles of non-CM newforms are equidistributed with respect to the Sato--Tate measure, while for Kloosterman angles, this is known on average over natural families. We study the fluctuations around these laws in large families, for smooth test functions. We prove an unconditional central limit theorem for Frobenius angles of elliptic curves for a much larger class of test functions than previously considered; earlier results assumed the Riemann hypothesis for $L$-functions of Hecke eigenforms of full level. This result follows from a general framework, developed here, which yields Gaussian moments for statistics of sequences in $[0,1]$ varying over families. In this framework, independence is replaced by two quantitative conditions: approximate independence at distinct indices, and convergence of the family averages to the Weyl limits at a suitable rate. As further applications, we extend central limit theorems for Kloosterman angles and for Hecke angles of newforms to larger classes of test functions, the latter with the weight and the level varying simultaneously. We also treat the dilated angles $αθ$ for integers $α\geq2$, whose limiting distribution is uniform. Finally, we discuss sharp statistics, obtaining a central limit theorem for Hecke angles and explaining the obstruction for the other two families.

papers.title: Direct estimation of the lunar-solar precession with geodetic very long baseline interferometry
papers.abstract: Geodetic very long baseline interferometry (VLBI) is capable of measuring the Earth's instantaneous rotation pole (IRP) components (hereafter, $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$) with sufficient accuracy using the VLBI delay rate. The least-squares fit of the $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$ polynomial expansion coefficients produces the precession model parameters independently of planetary motion theories. Our aim was to estimate the precession parameters using VLBI delay rate observations as well as the nutation coefficients in order to produce a full transformation matrix from the IRP to the Geocentric Celestial Reference System (GCRS). Then, the goal was to incorporate the free core nutation (FCN) effect from the VLBI group delay to form a complete and simple analytical model. We obtained an empirical model of the transformation from International Terrestrial Reference System (ITRS) to Geocentric Celestial Reference System (GCRS) based on observational results. Similar to the IAU2006 theory, the new model produces time series of $X_{IRP}$ and $Y_{IRP}$ angles, but these two angles now point out the direction of the IRP rather than the celestial intermediate pole (CIP). A simple analytical model defines the IRP location for any epoch during the interval of observations. Therefore, the non-rotation origin concept is not required for the transformation matrix construction. The estimate of the lunar-solar precessional parameter based on analysis of VLBI delay rate is $ψ_{A}= 5038.500\pm 0.019"$/cy (referred to the observational epoch 2000.0), which is close to the adopted IAU2006 precessional parameter value $ψ_{A}= 5038.4815"$/cy.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Spacecraft performance in the L2 environment
papers.abstract: The Euclid mission was designed around the need for thermo-optical and mechanical stability, stray-light suppression, low outgassing, and precise guiding. After three years in space, a wealth of data is available to assess the performance in these areas. We review the L2 halo-orbit design and consumables budget. Solar stray-light gradually increases by 14\% per year and is consistent with meteoroid puncturing, but remains low overall. Data loss from high solar activity has declined notably since the maximum of the 25th Solar cycle passed. The thermodynamical response of the optical elements to a thermal step impulse follows sigmoidal growth curves, entering the asymptotic equilibration regime after 21--46 hours. Water-ice contamination has affected data from both instruments and requires continued monitoring; we review detection and decontamination methods, and Euclid's contamination history. High-precision measurements of the zodiacal background reveal, at eight sigma significance, the subtle modulation caused by the changing perspective on the dust distribution due to the L2 halo-orbit libration. These data also show that conservative pre-launch estimates overestimated the out-of-field stray-light by factors of 4 (H band) to 27 (I band). Telemetry data demonstrate excellent guiding, and enable highly significant detections of solar radiation pressure and of thermal-emission recoil from Euclid's unilluminated dark sides. Lastly, we present a list of 34 meteoroid impacts, discuss their mechanical and optical signatures, and derive a minimum detectable impactor mass of 5e-7 g.

papers.title: Polynomial eigenfunctions and recurrences of fixed length
papers.abstract: This paper solves the fixed-length recurrence problem posed by Horozov, Shapiro and Tater. For the rational Darboux transformations specified here, it also resolves the order and classification questions raised by their two conjectures. It classifies monic polynomial sequences whose members are eigenpolynomials of one fixed nonscalar differential operator of arbitrary finite order with polynomial coefficients and for which multiplication by the variable involves a fixed number of consecutive polynomials. Orthogonality is not assumed, and only sufficiently large degrees need be prescribed. If the lowest recurrence index is $n-m+1$, with $m\ge3$, the differential order equals $m$ times the degree of the eigenvalue as a polynomial in $n$. After translating the variable, every such sequence is a finite rational Darboux transform of an explicit family with differential order $m$ and eigenvalue $n$. Necessary and sufficient conditions on the factors determine all polynomial differential eigenoperators of the resulting family. For families that cannot be obtained by these transformations from families of smaller minimum differential order, the minimum differential and recurrence orders coincide. All such families are classified in minimum differential orders at least three, including additional families in composite orders.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Calibration strategy and observations
papers.abstract: This paper reviews how Euclid's top-level calibration requirements were translated into a calibration plan, how this plan is implemented and maintained during the survey, and how it performs in the current DR1 release. We show that DR1 already meets or exceeds most end-of-mission spectrophotometric calibration requirements. The construction of spectroscopically complete and pure samples relies on ongoing data acquisition for the Euclid Deep Survey, while point-spread-function modelling and shear calibration are still converging to their stringent accuracy requirements. With all DR1 data reprocessed with the DR1 pipeline configuration, more subtle effects have been detected and characterised, and correction strategies have been developed for DR2. These include improved absolute flux calibration, astrometry, charge-persistence correction, shutter effects, wavelength calibration, and spectrophotometric corrections for water-ice contamination. Finally, synthetic photometric transformations between Euclid and each of Roman, the James Webb Space Telescope, and the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope, are presented.

papers.title: A perturbative construction of a modular $S_3$ model for quarks
papers.abstract: We present a modular-invariant supersymmetric model of flavour for quark masses and mixing, based on the group $Γ_2\cong S_3$. Hierarchies in the quark sector follow from the symmetric structure of the model, as they are generated by modular forms of different weights in the mass matrices, and no severe tuning of free superpotential coefficients is needed. Moreover, no flavons are employed besides the modulus $τ$ which is, given the gCP symmetry imposed on the model, the only source of CP violation. 8 dimensionless observables (4 mass ratios and 4 CKM parameters) are reproduced by making use of 10 free model parameters (including real and imaginary part of the modulus) within the $1σ$ range making our model, to the best of our knowledge, the $S_3$ modular model for quarks with the fewest free parameters.

papers.title: Matching lattice and continuum chiral determinants at finite volume
papers.abstract: Recent formulations of lattice chiral gauge theories define a complex fermion weight either through Craig's gauge-invariant overlap measure or, following Hsu and Witten, through a continuum Weyl determinant on a reconstructed gauge connection, with its phase fixed by the five-dimensional $η$-invariant. For one $SU(5)$ generation on a flat four-torus, we prove that their relative weights agree in the continuum limit along smooth gapped paths, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang-Mills counterterm, whose coefficient we determine. On bounded smooth families a uniform Dirac gap suffices: the vacuum expansion need not converge. We obtain explicit uniform convergence rates for the logarithmic variations and, for Craig's interpolation, prove the reconstruction bounds that the matching requires, extending Hsu's small-field comparison to finite amplitude. For Hsu's reflection-positive reconstruction with flat collars, the phase variations still match, while the logarithmic coefficient of the quadratic counterterm is enhanced by a calculable, profile-dependent factor. In a hypercharge background on which the vacuum expansion diverges, numerical comparisons at the input gauge field support quadratic convergence of the phase, whereas the modulus acquires a logarithmic correction to quadratic scaling, whose coefficient follows analytically from the free overlap vacuum polarization.

papers.title: To Race or Not to Race? Exploiting Performance Variability in Mixed-Integer Programming via Root-Gated Resource Allocation
papers.abstract: Mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver runtimes vary substantially across random seeds. Parallel replication exploits this variability but can waste computational resources when applied indiscriminately. We investigate whether information from an ordinary solve can guide this allocation decision. We formulate replication under a finite deadline, establish an exact relationship between runtime dispersion and the value of independent searches, and analyze delayed replication and imperfect allocation decisions. Using 101,615 seeded SCIP runs, we examine the association between root-LP dual degeneracy and replication value. We then introduce a non-invasive root-gated policy that preserves the original solver trajectory and launches three additional seeded processes when a root dual-degeneracy indicator reaches a fixed threshold. In a prospective two-hour experiment on 130 paired instances, root-gated racing proves optimality on 77 instances (59.23%), versus 73 (56.15%) for both Single and unconditional Race-4, while reducing active worker-process occupancy by 43.00% relative to unconditional racing. These findings demonstrate the promise of selective parallel resource allocation without solver-source modifications.

papers.title: Single-spike superradiant free-electron lasers
papers.abstract: Free-electron lasers (FELs) deliver high-brilliance radiation from the infrared to X-rays, enabling atomic-scale studies on femtosecond-to-attosecond timescales. Yet conventional facilities rely on large, costly radio-frequency accelerators. Laser wakefield accelerators (LWFAs), combining high accelerating gradients with ultra-high peak currents, offer a compact alternative and open up new prospects for advanced FEL operation. Here, we demonstrate a tabletop superradiant FEL driven by single-spike, pre-bunched electron beams from a LWFA. By manipulating the energy chirp during acceleration and compressing the bunch to sub-wavelength duration, we obtain coherent radiation extending into the vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) regime within a remarkably compact 3-metre beamline--from gas target to radiator. Under optimized conditions, the measured photon yield reaches 2.8x10^10 per pulse after transmission through a 500-um slit, with a reproducibility of approximately 70%. This approach uniquely exploits the energy chirp and high-current characteristics inherent to LWFA beams without recourse to exponential gain, substantially minimizing device length while obviating the need for external synchronization and offering enhanced tolerance to jitter--thereby establishing a practical route toward efficient, compact FELs suitable for applications in academic, industrial, and clinical settings.

papers.title: A Finite Markov Chain Analysis of the Simplified Swarm Optimisation Update Rule
papers.abstract: Simplified swarm optimisation (SSO) updates each variable by one draw that copies the global or personal best, keeps the current value or redraws uniformly, with probabilities $c_g$, $c_p$, $c_w$ and $c_r$. As a finite Markov chain under frozen memory, its coordinate kernel $c_w I + (1 - c_w)Π$ has an explicit stationary law and exact convergence rate $c_w^t$. The elitist chain has a geometric hitting-time bound, from a non-optimal start a fixed $c_r$ needs at least $\exp(nc_r/2)$ expected evaluations to reach a unique optimum, and a coupling under changing memories gives $O(n\log n)$ and $O(n^2)$ expected generations on OneMax and LeadingOnes for every population size with redraw share of order $1/n$ and no inertia, and within a $\log n$ factor for fixed inertia. With a frozen memory, inertia cannot speed up first entry into any set from stationary positions, though it can from others. Where the three reference values agree, only $c_r$ acts; where they disagree, copy branches recombine the memories, forcing a redraw only where no active branch holds the target value. Branch logging and checkpoint replay show inertia slowed the tested OneMax and LeadingOnes runs and suggest memory-mediated gains on wider gaps. On Jump functions SSO needed 3.8--8.9 times fewer evaluations than the (1+1) evolutionary algorithm with rate $1/n$, but no consistent advantage over rate-adjusted mutation or a $(μ+1)$ genetic algorithm with uniform crossover was established. The analytical redraw rule improved six of eight benchmark--setting pairs and redundancy allocation, but was slower than $c_r = 0.1$ on Jump$_2$.

papers.title: Dynamic Scenario-Based Portfolio Optimization for Multi-Asset ETFs
papers.abstract: Portfolio outcomes may depend as much on trading restrictions as on how returns are modeled. We compared historical moving-window returns with conditional scenarios from ARMA--GARCH models and a Student-$t$ copula for 30 U.S.-listed exchange-traded funds. Matched mean--variance and conditional value-at-risk portfolios were evaluated under long-only and limited long--short bounds over 946 sessions. Historical portfolios had higher observed reward--risk ratios in most comparisons, but no paired difference remained significant after multiple-testing adjustment. Conditional scenarios did not consistently reduce realized downside risk. We distinguished changes in target weights from trades required to rebalance holdings after market movements. Relaxing the target-adjustment limit changed exposures, turnover, and some returns more than varying scenario count or seed in the examined tests. These findings suggest that assessments of conditional return inputs should consider portfolio constraints and trading requirements.

papers.title: Self-Organizing Maps for the Exploration and Classification of X-Ray Sources in the Chandra Source Catalog
papers.abstract: In this work, we apply Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to the Chandra Source Catalog (CSC) to investigate the distribution of observation-level detections in the feature space defined by their spectral and variability properties. SOMs are neural-network-based models that project points in high-dimensional space onto a two-dimensional latent space while preserving their local topological structure. From CSC 2.1.1 we extract a sample of 36,904 ACIS-only, observation-level, high statistical significance detections, belonging to 17,927 unique sources. Among these detections, 25,192 (10,078 sources) are associated with a label from SIMBAD via a 1" cross-match that provides information about their astrophysical nature. Training a 40x40 hexagonal SOM reveals structured regions in the U-Matrix and activation response map, and feature-projection maps trace coherent patterns in spectral shape and variability. Overlaying SIMBAD classes shows that labeled populations occupy distinct, partially adjacent regions of the map and that generic categories can be interpreted via their SOM locations. We then retrain the SOM for classification using a source-grouped train/validation/test split and introduce SOMClassifier. When applied to 11,712 detections without SIMBAD labels, it assigns valid (non-abstained) labels to 6,225 detections (coverage ~53%). Furthermore, we release the trained models and visualization/classification workflows through a public web application built on the most up-to-date CSC release.

papers.title: Pl@ntNet machine-to-machine identification service with Pl@ntNet API: enabling automated biodiversity monitoring through large-scale plant identification
papers.abstract: 1. Monitoring plant biodiversity requires identifying large numbers of plants across space and time. Although artificial intelligence (AI) can now identify plant species from images with high accuracy, most existing systems rely on users manually submitting images. As ecological monitoring increasingly generates large image collections from cameras, drones, robots and online platforms, there is a growing need for plant identification services that can be directly integrated into automated data-processing workflows. 2. Here, we present Pl@ntNet's machine-to-machine AI plant identification service. This service uses an application programming interface (API) to provide programmatic access to Pl@ntNet's plant recognition models and the associated taxonomic processing. This service enables the implementation of automated identification workflows without human intervention and can thus directly link large image collections and automated observation systems to an AI-based plant identification system. 3. We establish that this service, which covers 85,000 species from around the world, (1) has a species prediction accuracy of 0.89, (2) process images up to 666 times faster than workflows requiring human intervention, (3) and has processed over 84 million identification requests since its launch, including more than 40 million in 2025 alone. We demonstrate how it has already enabled the implementation of a new generation of ecological workflows: identifying plants from images of insects to reconstruct the plant-pollinator interactions, analysing geolocated images from social media to study plant distribution, detecting invasive plants using images taken at the roadside, and identifying weeds using agricultural robots. Finally, we illustrate its application using a reproducible example: identifying plants from insect photos on iNaturalist. In approximately 30 min on a standard laptop, 2,424 images were processed to generate a dataset of 708 plant-pollinator interactions, with a weighted precision of 0.98 for flower detection and an accuracy of 0.88 for genus plant identification. 4. In conclusion, this machine-to-machine species identification is already operating on a considerable scale and meets a genuine need. All of this paves the way for a new paradigm in biodiversity monitoring, in which automated sensors and image collections can be directly connected to AI-based identification services.

papers.title: Incremental Model Predictive Control for Reference Tracking of Nonlinear Anesthesia Dynamics
papers.abstract: Anesthesia dynamics are commonly described by Wiener models, consisting of linear dynamics followed by a static nonlinearity. This nonlinear output complicates the derivation of theoretical guarantees on closed-loop stability and convergence. Model Predictive Control (MPC) is particularly suitable for anesthesia control, as it explicitly accounts for constraints in the control design. In this paper, we propose an incremental MPC formulation for tracking a desired reference. The proposed approach exploits the structure of the nonlinear output equation to reformulate the control problem within a linear framework. An incremental model is then employed to avoid the explicit computation of steady states and inputs, which may be inaccurate in the presence of model uncertainties. The proposed controller is evaluated through simulations involving 1000 virtual patients and compared with a benchmark MPC formulation. Results show improved steady-state reference tracking while maintaining satisfactory disturbance rejection.

papers.title: The Evertse-Ferretti interval result for a set of weights, and the exponent $1/2$ in three complexity bounds
papers.abstract: The interval result of Evertse and Ferretti (2013) concerns a tuple $L$ of linear forms and one tuple $c$ of weights. It says that the parameters $Q$ for which the twisted height $H_{L,c,Q}$ has a small value outside an exceptional subspace $T(L,c)$ lie in $O(δ^{-2}\logδ^{-1})$ intervals $[Q_i,Q_i^ω)$. We prove this for a whole set $\mathcal{C}$ of weights with the same forms. At most $J$ subspaces $T(L,c)$ occur, where $J$ depends only on the dimension and on the number of places, and one family of $O(δ^{-2}\logδ^{-1})$ intervals serves every $c\in\mathcal{C}$ at once. Neither count depends on $\mathcal{C}$. In applications of Bugeaud-Evertse type the solutions are sorted into about $\varepsilon^{-1}$ classes with the same forms and different weights, and one application now serves all classes. We deduce three complexity bounds. For a real algebraic irrational number $ξ$, the number $p(n,ξ,b)$ of blocks of length $n$ in its base-$b$ expansion satisfies $\limsup p(n,ξ,b)/(n(\log n)^η)=\infty$ for every $η<1/2$; Bugeaud and Evertse proved this for $η<1/11$. The same holds for the continued fraction expansion of an algebraic number of degree at least three, and for the steering word of $(3/2)^n$. We explain why $1/2$ is the limit of the method. All results are machine-verified in Lean~4.

papers.title: Bulk CMSX-4 Single-Crystal Builds via Laser-Directed Energy Deposition: Epitaxial Stability and Microstructure Evolution
papers.abstract: Single-crystal processing of Ni-based superalloys using laser-directed energy deposition (L-DED) is extremely challenging, given the interplay of a number of processing parameters. In this work, we develop strategies to maintain single-crystal growth in long cylindrical rod geometries by combining dynamic adjustment of laser power, informed by in-situ infrared thermal feedback, with a simulation-guided external cooling system. This combined approach ensures optimal heat extraction during additive manufacturing, maintaining near-steady-state conditions at the solidification interface and extending continuous epitaxial growth to nearly twice the build height achievable through process control alone. The developed strategy results in continuous single-crystal growth, as validated by electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). The steady-state nature of solidification is revealed through the near-constant primary dendritic arm spacing. Further, the heat-treatment is optimized by reducing the solutionizing time (by 47\%), resulting in faster eutectic dissolution. Comparison of the aged microstructures reveals a similar distribution of precipitates between the classical Bridgman- and L-DED-processed samples.

papers.title: Context-Predictive Low-Rank Adaptation for Face Presentation Attack Detection
papers.abstract: Face presentation attack detection requires representations that distinguish physical spoofing cues across changes in acquisition devices, subjects, and attack media. Large visual encoders offer transferable representations, but conventional binary fine-tuning supervises their final decisions without explicitly constraining how local facial evidence is represented under partial observation. We present CP-JEPA, a context-predictive adaptation framework that combines low-rank tuning of a pretrained CLIP image encoder with a joint-embedding predictive objective. A student predicts complete-image teacher features at masked spatial locations, while unmasked classification, masked classification, and prediction consistency retain the connection to the live/spoof task. An exponential-moving-average teacher supplies evolving latent targets. The auxiliary components are used only during training; inference requires only the LoRA-adapted CLIP visual encoder and binary classifier. {We evaluate CP-JEPA under single-source and multi-source OCIM transfer, additional CelebA-Spoof training, transfer to CelebA-Spoof, two-source training, and unseen-attack evaluation on SiW-Mv2.} On the standard OCIM benchmark, CP-JEPA achieves 3.74\% mean HTER and 98.73\% mean AUC. {Single-source evaluation achieves 11.36\% mean HTER across twelve source--target combinations.} With CelebA-Spoof added to the three OCIM training sources, CP-JEPA reduces mean HTER from 3.45\% to 2.35\% and increases mean AUC from 98.68\% to 99.32\%. On SiW-Mv2, it achieves 3.36\% mean HTER across the held-out attack categories. Controlled loss ablations examine the contributions of latent prediction, masked classification, and prediction consistency. The results show that context-predictive adaptation can improve cross-dataset PAD performance, although the gains vary with the training sources and evaluation setting.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Colouring Euclid with external ground-based imaging data
papers.abstract: Accurate photometric-redshift estimation and calibration of the weak-lensing point-spread function (PSF) for Euclid require complementary ground-based optical imaging with high photometric precision and spatial homogeneity. The Organisation Unit for External Data (OU-EXT) integrates heterogeneous ground-based surveys into the Euclid Science Ground Segment (SGS), delivering uniformly calibrated, co-added images, and associated PSF models. To minimise systematics in spectral energy distribution (SED) reconstruction and photometric-redshift estimation, these data must achieve relative photometric stability at the $\sim$10 mmag level on Euclid-tile scales. We present the ground-based imaging component of Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), comprising $\sim2500$ deg$^2$ across the wide, deep, and auxiliary fields. We summarise the OU-EXT production workflow and validation framework, and quantify the achieved data quality of the co-added products in terms of depth, photometric zero-point stability, and spatial colour homogeneity. In the Euclid Wide Survey (EWS), the point-source $10σ$ depths in the $griz$ bands reach 24.8/24.3/24.0/23.0 AB mag, with the deep fields extending 1--2 magnitudes deeper. Most EWS DR1 tiles meet the 10 mmag relative photometric requirement, with 1.1% and 1.5% showing offsets exceeding 50 mmag in the northern and southern hemispheres, respectively. Spatial colour variations remain typically below 5--10 mmag across the southern EWS footprint, while larger residual structures of 10--25 mmag appear in some northern regions. These results demonstrate that the EXT production chain provides a largely homogeneous framework for integrating ground-based datasets into Euclid, while identifying calibration and co-addition limitations that have to be addressed in DR2 to meet the mission's most stringent cosmological requirements. (Abridged)

papers.title: Thermal and dynamical behaviors of the spin-nematic phases in a spin-1 triangular lattice
papers.abstract: The triangular lattice compound Na$_2$BaNi(PO$_4$)$_2$ has been recently established as a strong candidate for realizing the spin-nematic physics. In this theoretical work, we study the finite-temperature properties and the dynamics of a spin-1 triangular lattice model, which reproduces the spin-nematic physics and provides insights relevant to the compound. We show that a small biquadratic interaction can be used for stabilizing the SN phases in the semiclassical approach with SU(3) coherent states, which allows for a mathematical parameterization of the spin-nematic wave functions. With a semiclassical Monte Carlo calculation, the finite temperature transitions into the spin-nematic phases are shown to be related to BKT transitions associated with the proliferation of half vortices in the original spin-1 model. Using quantum Monte Carlo calculations with a low-energy effective model, the phase boundaries are determined and found to agree qualitatively with the semiclassical analysis. Within the spin wave approach, the low-energy spin dynamics can be captured equally well by either the spin-1 model with a small biquadratic term, or the effective spin-$1/2$ model. The accidental degeneracy of the semiclassical approach at zero field is revealed by explicit analytical parameterization, and is shown to be associated with the pseudo-Goldstone mode observed in the spin dynamics.

papers.title: On the Adams spectral sequence of $eo_2(C_4)$
papers.abstract: We calculate the mod $2$-homology of the fixed points of the $C_4$-equivariant Hill--Hopkins--Ravenel theory $BP^{((C_4))}\langle 1\rangle$, as an $\mathcal{A}_*$-comodule algebra. $2$-locally these fixed points are $tmf_0(5)$ by a theorem of Quinn. We deduce that $tmf_0(5)$ is an indecomposable $tmf$-module that is an extension of two $tmf$-modules of the form $tmf\otimes K$ for a finite spectrum $K$. The $K(2)$-localization of $tmf_0(5)$ is $32$-periodic, and we compute the Adams spectral sequence of $tmf_0(5)$ through the $32$-stem.

papers.title: New measurement of BR$(K^+\rightarrowπ^+ν\barν)$ at the NA62 experiment
authors: Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration
papers.abstract: The decay $K^+\rightarrowπ^+ν\barν$ with a very precisely predicted branching ratio of less than $10^{-10}$ is one of the best candidates to reveal indirect effects of new physics at the highest mass scales. The NA62 experiment at the CERN SPS is designed to measure the branching ratio of the $K^+\rightarrowπ^+ν\barν$ decay. A new measurement of its branching ratio based on the 20230-2024 dataset is presented. This doubles the total dataset, leading to a 5$σ$ expected sensitivity for the Standard Model process.

papers.title: Characterizations of products of projective spaces and quadrics
papers.abstract: We characterize products of projective spaces and smooth quadrics using Schur functors and positivity of vector bundles. First, we obtain characterizations of projective spaces and smooth quadrics using positivity of arbitrary Schur functors of extensions of a unipotent bundle by the tangent bundle, generalizing several existing results. We then prove that almost nef regular foliations whose direct sum is a subbundle of the tangent bundle determine a product decomposition, if the corresponding Schur functors admit suitable positive Schur submodules. For smooth weak Fano varieties similar results are obtained by replacing almost nefness and individual integrability of the foliations by the integrability of their total image. As special cases, we obtain product analogues of well-known characterizations of projective spaces and quadrics.

papers.title: Edge-scaling softening of a universal machine-learned potential: point-defect formation energies in a coronene graphene quantum dot
papers.abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are increasingly used as computationally efficient surrogates for density functional theory (DFT) in high-throughput nanomaterials screening. Systematic softening has been reported for several universal MLIPs when high-energy and far-from-equilibrium configurations are underrepresented in training data. We examine how this behavior appears at under-coordinated edge sites in graphene quantum dots (GQDs), where a vacancy can have pronounced molecular-radical character. Using coronene (C$_{24}$H$_{12}$), a hexagonal GQD with $D_{6h}$ symmetry and three carbon classes, we benchmark SevenNet (7net-omni-i12) against spin-polarized PBE DFT (GPAW) for monovacancy, divacancy, and Stone-Wales defects. Beyond the full site- and bond-resolved landscapes, we perform a controlled matched-reconstruction comparison in which 28 vacancy and divacancy configurations are scored by both engines using self-consistent chemical-potential reservoirs. In this dataset, SevenNet underestimates all 28 vacancy and divacancy formation energies, and the mean deficit increases with under-coordination within each defect family: 0.30-0.74 eV for monovacancies and 0.65-1.11 eV for divacancies as the number of broken edge C-H bonds increases. By contrast, the mean Stone-Wales energies differ by only 0.013 eV. SevenNet also preserves the ordering of three hydrogen-dependent reconstruction basins and reproduces $D_{6h}$-equivalent sites to within a few meV. The within-class symmetry spread therefore provides a practical diagnostic of basin-sensitive relaxations. Within the present coronene benchmark, these results support MLIP-based structure screening and preliminary ranking, while absolute vacancy energies and multi-basin edge configurations still require DFT validation.

papers.title: AI has its own style in mathematical proving
papers.abstract: As large language models increasingly generate mathematical proofs, whether they develop a proving style distinct from that of human mathematicians remains an open question. This question is particularly pressing as mathematicians increasingly voice concerns that proofs generated by large language models are difficult to interpret. Here we ask three large language models to independently reprove all 465 propositions of Euclid's \textit{Elements} and compare their citation choices against the human-proof baseline through Jaccard similarity and complex network analysis. We find that AI-generated proofs differ from human proofs, and this difference is stable and reproducible: mean pairwise Jaccard similarity among AI runs (~0.68) is nearly twice that between AI and human proofs (~0.37), and cross-run classification consistency is also high. By examining citation structure in detail, we identify the concrete signature of this difference: approximately 40% of AI citations point to foundational elements (definitions, common notions, and postulates), compared with only 13\% in human proofs; even among theorem-to-theorem citations, AI tends to cite more distant results.
