Green--Tao--Ziegler's theorem on linear patterns of primes supplies the rational solutions needed for a Diophantine model of integer arithmetic.

papers.title: Novel Esscher concepts for informational risks and valuation in market models under random horizon
papers.abstract: This paper considers the setting constituted by the triplet $(S,\mathbb{F},τ)$. The pair $(S,\mathbb{F})$ is the initial model where $S$ is the discounted price process of risky assets (Stocks) and $\mathbb{F}$ is the ``public" flow of information that is available to all agents over time. $τ$ is an arbitrary random time, which might not be seen through the flow $\mathbb{F}$, and it represents a default time in credit risk and a death time of an insured in life insurance where mortality and/or longevity risks present serious challenges. For simplicity, we suppose $S$ follows a geometric jump-diffusion model with stochastic volatiles and $\mathbb{F}$ is generated by a Brownian motion and Poisson process. In this setting, we address how the Esscher densities and/or measures notions can evolves with the informational risk induced by $τ$. In fact, we introduce the notion of Esscher with degrees-of-freedom associated to the informational risks generated by $τ$. On the one hand, we give various and complete characterizations of these Esscher notions in our informational setting. On the other hand, we fully characterize the Escher-prices bounds, for vulnerable claims (claims built on the occurrence of $τ$), using constrained backward stochastic differential equations (CBSDEs for short hereafter) that appear to be novel as well.

papers.title: CoordX Types: A Trustless, Swappable Type System for Shared Records
papers.abstract: The CoordX Protocol carries signed and encrypted entries between parties. It proves who wrote each entry and who had permission to write it. It does not say what an entry means. That task belongs above the protocol layer. This paper describes the CoordX type system, the layer that gives entries a meaning. A type is a short document that says how to read one part of a shared record: which entries count, what each position means, what a party may do there, and what a party must do next. The type system has two key properties. It is trustless: a type is an ordinary signed object fixed by its digest, and every party evaluates it for itself over entries that the CoordX Protocol has already verified. No party has to trust a server, a registry or another party's software. It is swappable: a type names the interpreter it is written for, so many interpreters, of different capabilities and designs, can be used side by side in one record. We describe how to write type schemas, and we define the expressive power of the schema language. Payloads form a regular language. Entry structure forms a regular tree language. Every rule and every computed value is a total function in the primitive recursive class, so evaluation always halts. We compare this with KQML, FIPA-ACL and CBCL, and we relate it to language-theoretic security.

papers.title: Hump around 30 keV in Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 -- Possible evidence of strong rapid-proton capture process --
papers.abstract: In a neutron star low-mass X-ray binary, heavy elements (with mass number ~100) are believed to be synthesized through the rapid-proton (rp) capture process, as indirectly indicated by the long tail of X-ray burst light curves. Although direct evidence for the rp-process was lacking so far, we reported in our previous study that an unidentified hump is present at ~30 keV of the Suzaku spectra of Aquila X-1 in its hard state. The feature was tentatively identified with a recombination quasi-continuum from highly ionized ions of cadmium or indium, which are possibly produced by the rp process during X-ray bursts and lifted up into the neutron-star atmosphere. To reinforce this scenario, we quantitatively evaluated the physical conditions of the assumed emitting region in the atmosphere, and confirmed that the scenario is possible when the putative rp-process ashes in the atmosphere has ~10^7 times higher abundances than their solar values. The results are compared with theoretical model calculations for the nucleosynthesis in X-ray bursts. We suggest that the observed spectral hump is a radiative recombination feature from the stable isotope 106Cd, produced in X-ray bursts via the rp-process. Further issues about the detectability are briefly discussed.

papers.title: Split-and-scale Latent 3D Representations
papers.abstract: Latent 3D representations have significantly expanded the capabilities of modern shape modeling, enabling compact encoding of 3D scenes and supporting powerful 3D generative models. Despite this progress, current representations struggle to capture the fine details of complex objects, fundamentally limited by the capacity of their latents. However, scaling latent capacity at training time is computationally expensive and often infeasible under memory limits, and naively increasing the number of latents at inference fails to make effective use of the added capacity. In this paper, we address both challenges with \textit{split-and-scale}, a method that effectively expands latent capacity at inference while keeping training cost tractable. Our key observation is that by representing 3D scenes as continuous functions of 3D coordinates, a single pretrained tokenizer can be applied at inference to arbitrarily small sub-regions of a scene, allocating the same latent capacity to a smaller spatial extent and thus capturing far higher detail. We validate this insight by conducting extensive ablations to study the trade-offs between compute, memory, latent capacity, and reconstruction quality, demonstrating our inference-time scaling method achieves quality competitive with much larger models that exceed single-GPU memory limits. We further demonstrate that split-and-scale supports high-quality generative modeling, training an autoregressive 3D generator that performs competitively with state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Integrated optical isolators enabled by 2D semiconductors via spin-momentum locking
papers.abstract: Integrated optical isolators based on spin-momentum locking hold great potential for protecting photonic integrated circuits from unwanted reflections. Currently, the most common implementations are magneto-optical isolators that require an externally applied magnetic field. Nevertheless, a wide range of nonreciprocal effects remains to be exploited in alternative material platforms. Although the majority of these effects induce changes to the propagation of light as a function of its polarization, they can be directly connected to the propagation direction through spin-momentum locking. We employ a computational approach to investigate various designs of integrated isolators based on nonreciprocal 2D semiconductors, studying the influence of their geometry and optical properties on the device performance. Additionally, we propose a novel concept for an all-optical isolator based on spin-valley polarization and optically tunable magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers. Our results establish 2D semiconductors as an advanced platform for integrated nonreciprocal devices, enabling functionalities that are difficult to achieve with conventional magneto-optical materials like all-optical operation.

papers.title: On classifying knotted surfaces
papers.abstract: These notes, which are based on four lectures delivered at the summer school "Knotted Surfaces in Four-Manifolds" at PCMI in 2026, discuss classifications of locally flat surfaces in simply-connected $4$-manifolds.

papers.title: SwarmSafe-Delta: Isolating Message Effects on LLM Agent Safety
papers.abstract: When a tool-using LLM agent team violates policy, aggregate outcomes do not reveal whether an upstream message changed the executor's action. We introduce SwarmSafe-Delta, a paired executable protocol that freezes upstream computation, varies real, hidden, and format-matched placebo delivery, and scores a single committed action against deterministic benign and risky policy states under preassigned budgets. Across four models and constructed optional tasks, real delivery at $N=4$ produces 21.4% risky-world violations, versus 5.0% with placebo and 1.0% with hidden delivery (paired differences +16.4 and +20.3 percentage points). Real delivery also improves benign task success, illustrating that suppressing communication sacrifices utility. In a second regime constructed to require an upstream lookup route, real delivery improves safe completion by 74.2 points relative to hidden delivery. These effects quantify message-delivery contrasts under specified information dependencies, not naturally occurring failure rates. Exploratory action-level analyses show that the effect depends strongly on whether the upstream message recommends a prerequisite check or direct execution; model differences also largely track these message compositions. The contribution is a controlled, execution-grounded measurement protocol rather than a general claim that agent communication is harmful or protective.

papers.title: Intent-Aware Protection for AI Agents
papers.abstract: AI agents increasingly access enterprise data, invoke powerful tools, and act with limited human oversight. Existing security defenses primarily detect prompt injection, harmful outputs, or suspicious behavior, but do not determine whether an agent remains faithful to the purpose for which it was deployed. An action may contain no attack pattern and stay within granted permissions while still violating the agent's role, organizational constraints, or purpose. We introduce Intent- Aware Security, a framework that treats trusted agent intent as a first-class security object. We define Intent Preservation and Intent Drift, and operationalize them through an Intent Profile: an agent-specific representation extracted from organizational, role, and developer intent. We further introduce an Intent-Aware benchmark of 887 validated samples across 35 agents, built by a generation procedure that fixes ground-truth labels before LLM realization, and four Intent Profile-based protections: pre-execution detection, post-execution detection, input alignment, and system-prompt hardening. Across all evaluations, Intent Profile-based protection outperforms all profile-free baselines on the primary metric. On our benchmark, it raises four-class acro-F1 from 45% to 79% (Out-of-Scope F1 from 8% to 76%). On more than 10,000 executed AgentDojo trajectories, where ground truth comes from environment state, profile-based post-execution detection reaches 0.949 AUROC versus AlignmentCheck 0.909, 0.897 with raw agent configuration and 0.843 without context. Profile-based input alignment improves protection success by 7 points over DataFilter with a comparable benign utility. These results suggest that an agent's intended purpose can serve as a useful security reference for detecting and mitigating deviations from its deployed role and operational boundaries.

papers.title: A thermodynamically consistent, fully compressible, fluctuating hydrodynamics model of a Cahn Hilliard binary fluid mixture
papers.abstract: We derive, from first principles, a thermodynamically consistent set of fully compressible fluctuating hydrodynamic equations for a Cahn-Hilliard binary fluid mixture, in isothermal and non-isothermal form and for symmetric and non-symmetric mixtures. The derivation uses the GENERIC formalism, with the friction operator constructed from flux fluctuations following Jelic and Ottinger, so that deterministic and stochastic fluxes derive from the same operator and correlation matrix and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem holds by construction. We show that the momentum equation must use the total mass density, that the Cahn-Hilliard variable is the mass fraction, and that the diffusion flux must be driven by the specific, not the volumetric, exchange potential. We derive a generalized Korteweg tensor for square-gradient energies in density and composition, and show that the reversible pressure tensor of the non-isothermal model is fixed by the degeneracy condition, producing a thermal capillary stress when the interfacial free energy has an entropic part. Thermodynamic consistency is proved in full: Jacobi identity, positivity and degeneracy, local energy conservation with interstitial-working fluxes, a local entropy balance, Soret-Dufour reciprocity, and Einstein statistics of the linearized equations. The final equations are written in conservative form for finite-volume discretization, and closed-form static and dynamic structure factors are given for all models as analytic benchmarks. An appendix shows that the same models follow from classical irreversible thermodynamics with the Helmholtz or Gibbs free energy; this route is unique for isothermal flows and has a gauge freedom in the non-isothermal case that GENERIC removes.

papers.title: Separation of Variables and Spectroscopy of Massive Spin-3/2 Fields on a Kerr Background
papers.abstract: We separate the neutral massive Rarita-Schwinger equation on a Kerr background at finite rotation. Two commuting matrix angular operators and a physical first integral yield a second-order radial equation and reversible field reconstruction. The resulting equations give quasibound spectra, greybody factors, and helicity-resolved Hawking emission. For a matched weakly bound level, the leading rotational splitting has the opposite sign to that of a Dirac field. We derive its coefficient and identify its angular momentum origin.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Near-infrared processing and data products
papers.abstract: The Euclid near-infrared processing function (NIR PF) converts the raw observations acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer (NISP) into calibrated images and source-level products. Following the first implementation delivered with the Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1), the NIR PF has been revised for the first major Euclid Data Release (DR1), with improvements to detector-level processing, calibration, image reconstruction, and quality control. The DR1 processing includes observations covering more than $1900\,\rm{deg}^2$ and has produced $71\,659$ calibrated near-infrared (NIR) images. We assess the performance of the processing chain through extensive astrometric and photometric validation. The astrometric solution reaches an average root-mean-square (RMS) of 10 mas, remaining below 20 mas for 99% of the dithers in all three NISP bands. Temporal variations in the instrumental throughput are typically corrected to a level of 2 mmag RMS, while the relative photometric accuracy reaches 0.9% for sources brighter than 19 mag in $Y_\mathrm{E}$, $J_\mathrm{E}$, and $H_\mathrm{E}$, and the residual spatial variations of the photometric calibration across the focal plane are at the level of approximately 10 mmag for the entire sample. Despite some remaining limitations, the DR1 NIR imaging products are consistent with the required astrometric and photometric performance over the large area covered by this release.

papers.title: Uncertainty Aware AFM-IR Hyperspectral Cube Reconstruction via Convolutional-Attentive Conditional Neural Processes
papers.abstract: Atomic force microscopy-infrared spectroscopy (AFM-IR) maps chemical composition at nanoscale spatial resolution, but the time required to acquire individual spectra limits hyperspectral imaging. Here, we introduce a convolutional-attentive conditional neural process (CACNP), a neural process architecture for reconstructing AFM-IR hyperspectral cubes from sparsely sampled spectra and a small set of structure images, each acquired at a selected wavenumber. The model is trained entirely on synthetic cubes generated from experimental infrared spectra and predicts both spectral intensities and their associated uncertainty. Validation on experimental datasets of poly(methyl methacrylate) and polystyrene particles embedded in epoxy demonstrates accurate reconstruction using only 5% of the available spectra, with competitive performance when compared to other methods. Inference takes less than 0.1 s on 128 X 128 hyperspectral cubes, supporting rapid reconstruction updates, while predictive uncertainty provides a basis for adaptive sampling of localized chemical features. This approach advances autonomous, high-throughput AFM-IR workflows and offers an architecture for accelerating other hyperspectral imaging methods.

papers.title: Quantum Control
papers.abstract: Quantum Control is the art of steering the fragile dynamics of a quantum system in a precise way toward a desired final state or transformation. It is a cornerstone of many quantum technology applications and at the same time allows us to shed light on the fundamental connection between the energy structure and the time dynamics of quantum systems at the heart of some of the most interesting phenomena of quantum mechanics. In this chapter on quantum control, we introduce the control problem, go through basic error sources and methods to suppress these errors and then discuss state-of-the-art techniques to solve the control problem, like adiabatic methods, quantum optimal control and methods of machine learning.

papers.title: Robo-SWE: An Executable Issue-Resolution Dataset Mined from Robot Software Repositories
papers.abstract: Coding agents are evaluated mostly on general-purpose software, but domain-specific systems require domain-aware evaluation. Robot software is a particularly challenging case: Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) packages have their own build tools, simulators and learning frameworks are built on physics engines, and behavior that depends on timing and hardware is hard to test. We present Robo-SWE, a dataset of 236 executable issue-resolution tasks mined from merged pull requests in 28 public robotics repositories in four domains: ROS 2 systems, simulation and physics engines, robotics algorithm libraries, and robot-learning frameworks. Each task contains the original issue text, a container recipe for the repository at the commit before the fix, the developers' fix, and the developers' tests, which fail before the fix and pass after it in repeated offline runs. The dataset also keeps a provenance ledger of all 1,567 candidate pull requests, with the stage each reached and the reason for every rejection, and, as a first use, 3,540 graded attempts by five coding-agent setups with recorded patches and 3,529 available trajectories. Across three runs per primary setup, resolve rates range from 45.8% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 to 56.5% for Claude Opus 5.5; GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 54.1% at maximum effort and 52.5% at medium effort, and GPT-6 Astra 51.4%. GLM-5.3 resolves 46.2%, and Kimi K3.1 Pro 43.9%. The tasks are validated by execution; verification of their fairness by human reviewers is future work. The dataset and public leaderboard are available online.

papers.title: Phase Interference and Transverse Catalysts Govern the Noise Fragility of Long-Range Variational Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Long-range entangling gates shorten variational state preparation, but they also accelerate operator spreading across the register, linking nonlocality to a presumed noise fragility. Here we show that the single-fault fragility $F$ of a variational circuit is governed by how fault phases interfere on the target Hamiltonian, not by how far faults spread. For Heisenberg chains we prove that two faults with identical extensive support can incur either bounded or extensive energy damage, in the exact ratio $N/2$. A phase-matched longitudinal halo remains energetically dark until ignited by transverse catalysts that break a symmetry of the remote register, namely spatially nonuniform single-qubit rotations or the pair-flip component of two-qubit $XX/YY$ gates, whereas uniform rotations and magnetization-conserving exchange gates leave it strictly dark. In noisy training with full-width long-range $ZZ$ gates, suppressing either catalyst alone leaves circuits trapped on an ignited plateau sustained by remote $XY$ couplings, whereas suppressing both eliminates the plateau, achieves minimal fragility despite larger fault operators, and halves the dephasing error. Training is driven by a race between catalyst pruning and gradient force balance, as annealing the transverse catalysts out of trapped circuits rescues every trajectory while annealing the entire longitudinal sector does not. Combined with the gate-count exposure $λ=pK$, a single fragility measurement accurately predicts the noise-induced energy shift across circuit architectures and noise strengths, reducing ansatz design to a trade-off between coherent expressivity and gate count.

papers.title: ADAPT: Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing for Pull Requests
papers.abstract: Modern software development relies on pull requests (PRs) that introduce small, targeted code changes. Once merged, these changes should be protected by focused tests that exercise the behavior the PR introduces, yet developers often submit PRs without such tests, leaving the new behavior unguarded against future regressions. Most test generation techniques target entire software units and optimize objectives such as code coverage rather than the behavior a change introduces, and prior diff-aware approaches have had limited success in capturing it. We propose ADAPT (Agentic Diff-Aware Patch Testing), a regression test generation approach that uses an autonomous coding agent to produce change-focused tests for PRs. Given a PR, the agent analyzes the diff between the base and head versions to identify the modified functions and their context, then plans and generates candidate unit tests. A dedicated fail-to-pass (F2P) verification tool runs each candidate on both versions and, after F2P success, reports which executable changed lines remain uncovered; guided by this feedback, the agent iteratively refines its tests. We evaluate ADAPT on the same 426 real-world PRs used by the prior state-of-the-art baseline, with GPT-4o and GPT-5-mini. ADAPT+GPT-4o reaches an F2P rate of 62.0% (264/426), compared with BLAST's reported 35.4% (151/426), while ADAPT+GPT-5-mini reaches 89.9% (383/426). On 137 PRs shared with Change And Cover (ChaCo), ADAPT achieves full patch coverage on 83.9% of PRs, compared with 79.6% for ChaCo, at considerably lower time and cost. A manual evaluation confirms that the F2P-valid tests target each PR's intended change, with mean scores of up to 4.54/5 for importance, 4.35/5 for assertion strength, and 4.49/5 for readability, often covering behavior beyond the developer-written tests.

papers.title: Testing Quantum Advantage in High-Frequency Trading with Market-Derived Nonlocal Games
papers.abstract: Non-classical correlations enabled by entanglement could be exploited for distributed coordination tasks with communication constraints such as high-frequency trading in fragmented markets. However, previous studies have largely specified the game and its payoff structure theoretically, using toy market models without testing how well these models reflect observed market behavior. Here, we introduce market-derived nonlocal games, in which historical order-book data and backtests of joint actions determine the game's inputs and payoffs, rather than a prespecified idealized model. We start from classical trading strategies based on market considerations, using quantum correlations only to coordinate the agents' decisions. We compute exact classical optima and quantum upper bounds for the payoff. For games with a possible quantum advantage, we introduce an optimization algorithm to find explicit entangled strategies and end-to-end backtest them on historical data. We demonstrate the approach in a two-agent, three-stock cross-venue arbitrage setting. The game derived from the observed market data shows no resolved quantum-classical gap at the measured interaction scales. Controlled variations in liquidity competition and cross-stock repricing then show how the approach identifies regimes supporting quantum advantage, constructs explicit strategies, and tests whether their advantage survives end-to-end backtesting on modified historical market data.

papers.title: Evolution of Internal Waves on Surfaces of Revolution with Flat Ends
papers.abstract: We generalize the 2D linear internal wave equation to non-compact surfaces of revolution with flat ends. We show that the leading profile of this equation with oscillatory forcing is the unique incoming solution to the corresponding stationary equation. This is done by proving a limiting absorption principle via propagation of semiclassical defect measure.

papers.title: Subgroup distortion in free-by-cyclic groups with linearly growing monodromy
papers.abstract: Let $G=F\rtimes_ϕ\mathbb Z$ be the mapping torus of a linearly growing UPG automorphism $ϕ$ of a finitely generated free group $F$. We compute the distortion of every finitely generated subgroup $H$ of $G$, and we show that it is linear, quadratic or exponential. In contrast, for each $d\ge2$, Dison and Riley constructed an automorphism of polynomial degree $d$ whose mapping torus contains a free subgroup with distortion equivalent to the Ackermann function $A_{d+1}$, which grows faster than every iterated exponential function. Using the natural splitting of $G$ over $\mathbb Z^2$ subgroups and its topological representative, we associate to $H$ a family of \emph{horizontal components}, together with \emph{dilation homomorphisms} defined from slopes along these components. We prove that $H$ is undistorted in $G$ if and only if every horizontal component of $H$ consists of only one piece. Otherwise, the distortion of $H$ is quadratic if all dilation homomorphisms are trivial, and exponential if one of them is nontrivial. Along the way, we show that the distortion of $H$ is determined, up to superadditive closure, by the distortions of the stabilizers of its horizontal components.

papers.title: Harnessing Environmental Scatterers for Endogenous Target Covertness in 6G ISAC: A New Paradigm for Sensing Security
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a cornerstone of 6G networks, enabling simultaneous data transmission and environmental perception. However, the ubiquitous radiation of sensing waveforms introduces a critical security vulnerability where the physical existence and characteristics of targets are continuously exposed to unauthorized wardens. Meanwhile, existing sensing-secure methods primarily focus on degrading a target warden's parameter-estimation accuracy, yet they fail to prevent wardens from detecting the target's physical presence. In this article, we first analyze sensing security threats in ISAC systems and survey existing sensing-secure methods. To address the critical gap, we propose a novel security paradigm termed endogenous target covertness. By intentionally harnessing environmental scatterers, such as known objects, ambient backscatter devices, and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), as ghost targets, the proposed scheme ensures a low probability that the warden detects the true target for the true target at the warden. This deliberately renders the true target's existence indistinguishable to the warden, while the legitimate base station can extract the true target's response using prior knowledge of the scatterers. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme through a case study, proving that absolute target covertness can be achieved without consuming dedicated jamming power. Finally, we outline key open challenges and promising research directions to realize truly secure, ubiquitous sensing in future ISAC ecosystems.

papers.title: Euclid: Data Release 1 (DR1) -- Bayesian 3D shape inference of star-forming galaxy populations
papers.abstract: Understanding the intrinsic 3D shapes of galaxies provides crucial insights into their formation and evolution, but determining these from projections remains challenging. We apply a Bayesian inference framework to optical images of galaxies from the Euclid Data Release 1, leveraging its large sample size to test the scalability and robustness of this methodology. Applying Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) sampling to Sérsic axis ratios and effective radii, we constrain the population-level mean 3D ellipticity, triaxiality, and size, together with their covariances for $40\,864\,304$ star-forming galaxies with stellar masses $M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{10.5}M_\odot$ at redshifts $0<z<1.2$. Our sample size exceeds previous shape inference studies by factors of $440$--$52\,800$ relative to early observations by JWST, and factors of $440$--$17\,600$ relative to legacy observations from HST in overlapping mass-redshift bins, enabling finer binning alongside improved statistical constraints on shape evolution. We additionally include over 9 million galaxies at $z<0.5$, a regime historically limited by sample size in previous shape inference studies. We recover key evolutionary trends identified in previous smaller-sample studies. We find high ellipticities ($μ_E \sim 0.600$--$0.821$) across all bins, indicating that the underlying 3D shape distributions are statistically dominated by flattened geometries. Most notably, we recover the decline of the prolate fraction towards $z=0$ at low masses ($M_\ast=10^{9}$--$10^{9.5}M_\odot$) reported by previous studies. This trend is seen consistently in comparable analyses of independent data sets spanning different depths and resolution regimes, showing that it is not an artefact of small-sample statistics, suggesting it may be a genuine feature of galaxy evolution. We also identify future methodological improvements for subsequent Euclid data releases.

papers.title: How Do People Debug Complex SQL Queries With LLMs? A Qualitative Study
papers.abstract: While LLMs are increasingly used in various contexts, we lack a fundamental understanding of how they impact SQL query debugging. In response, we conducted a user study with 16 participants of varying SQL expertise, examining how they debug complex SQL queries with and without LLM support. Initial benchmarking indicated that our selected models are already capable SQL debuggers. Qualitative analyses of our study data revealed that while participants trusted the LLM, they varied widely in how and whether they delegated debugging tasks to the LLMs, which we characterized through a new three-state model of participants' SQL reasoning processes. Additionally, participants enforced specific collaborative roles for the LLM such as TA or sounding board, which participants controlled by withholding context from the LLM. These findings suggest that LLM-based tools could enable preset role selection, broader context management, and flexible automation features, including low automation options, to support SQL debugging moving forward.

papers.title: Trained on What Screen Readers Cannot Read: Accessibility Debt in the GUI Corpora Behind Computer-Use Agents
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents learn to operate mobile interfaces from corpora of captured screens and accessibility trees. The same trees are what a screen reader consumes, so an agent trained on them inherits whatever labelling gaps the underlying applications carry. This paper measures one of those gaps, content-description coverage, in two Android corpora: Rico, collected in 2017, and AndroidControl, collected in 2024. Across 17,373,614 interface elements, 17.74% of the Rico elements that need a content description under our coding rule carry one, against 57.27% in AndroidControl. The difference of 39.5 percentage points holds under five alternative coding rules and when whole apps are resampled. It describes two datasets that also differ in app selection, capture method and platform version; it does not measure change over time. Input controls are the least labelled role in both corpora (2.20% and 27.21%, or 30.99% in AndroidControl if hint text counts as a name). Descriptions in the older corpus are also five times more likely to be placeholders (10.25% against 1.95%), so the difference is not an artefact of developers typing filler. Resolving 26,205 task actions to the elements they touched shows that, among tappable graphics with no text, demonstrations operate elements described 9.0 points more often than the others on the screens they visit, about 3.5 points of it from the choice of element within a screen. That is a selection effect inside the benchmark. A two-coder reliability check (kappa = 0.91 and 0.96) and the full pipeline accompany the paper.

papers.title: Machine learning and high accuracy: Neural preconditioners for computational gravity
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) developments have empowered valuable calculations in many areas of theoretical physics. Certain topics involving moderate-to-low accuracy requirements have been particularly fortunate because many ML techniques, such as neural networks, introduce a noise floor that would be difficult to penetrate with stricter tolerances. For this reason, topics requiring high accuracy can be hesitant to pursue ML. One prominent example is gravitational wave modeling, which relies on traditional methods that accommodate the high sensitivities of detectors such as LISA. However, recent progress in applied mathematics has identified hybrid methods where fast-but-noisy ML mechanisms are inserted into otherwise traditional numerical schemes to accelerate convergence in a way that ultimately meets or exceeds the accuracy of standard methods. We develop an optimized hybrid ML method to tackle a class of challenging PDEs; specifically, we demonstrate ML implementations for gravitational waves from asymmetric-mass black hole binaries and elastic waves. These require solving sparse linear algebra systems with Helmholtz features that are especially difficult for traditional iterative methods. Our new approach is to train a graph neural network (GNN) as a significantly faster preconditioner using a novel loss function based on the true residual of the iterative algorithm. For the most difficult regions of parameter space, our neural preconditioner decreases iteration counts by 2-15x compared to traditional preconditioners. Because the GNN operates directly on the sparse matrix and needs only modest physical context, it generalizes beyond its training domain and can be adapted to new problems across physics by retraining rather than redesign. Hybrid ML methods such as this offer a new and compelling avenue to handle high accuracy and speed requirements in gravitational wave modeling and beyond.

papers.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
papers.abstract: We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$. At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques. Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.

papers.title: Show Your Work in Swahili: Reinforcement Learning for Native-Language Mathematical Reasoning
papers.abstract: We present Fikiria, a two-stage SFT+GRPO recipe for Swahili mathematical reasoning. Its reward multiplies a format gate by a weighted sum of answer accuracy and the ChrF\texttt{++} similarity of the Swahili reasoning to an in-language reference chain of thought, so that training targets the surface fidelity of the reasoning trace and not only the final answer. We train on a 2.3k-problem Swahili dataset created by translating GSM8K with GPT-4.1 and filtering with SSA-COMET. On AfriMGSM Swahili, Fikiria-AfriqueQwen-14B reaches 79.2\%. Under the same fixed prompt and strict answer-format scoring, GPT-4o reaches 68.0\%, partly because it often fails the required answer format; IrokoBench reports 78.8\% for GPT-4o using a best-per-model prompt, a figure numerically close to ours but not directly comparable. In a small human evaluation with co-author annotators, GPT-4o's outputs were preferred overall. ChrF\texttt{++} measures surface fidelity, not the validity of individual reasoning steps.

papers.title: Low Probability of Target Detection in Wireless Sensing by Harnessing Reconfigurable-antenna based Reflectors
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce low probability of target detection (LPTD) as a new security objective for wireless sensing systems, where the existence of a target is concealed from passive wardens. Unlike conventional communication security and covert communication, LPTD aims to protect the sensed target itself from malicious detection, rather than concealing transmitted signals or communication activities. Specifically, we propose a reconfigurable-antenna-based reflector-assisted target covertness scheme, where passive reflectors deployed around the target are harnessed as artificial scattering sources to confuse the warden. By adjusting their reflection coefficients, these reflectors reshape the local scattering environment and mask the target-induced echo. We then analyze the warden's optimal detection strategy and derive the false-alarm and missed-detection probabilities, followed by a closed-form expression for its minimum total detection error probability. Numerical results validate the analysis and show that sufficient cooperation among reflectors can increase the warden's minimum total detection error probability to approximately 0.94--0.96, making target detection close to random guessing.

papers.title: Is generative AI really changing public sector work? Evidence from a multi-country survey
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has the potential to transform how public services are delivered, with important implications for public service productivity. But how widely is the technology actually being used - and is it making any difference? Our survey of 3,362 public sector workers across the UK, the USA, South Africa and the EU finds widespread use of AI in every region. Our findings suggest that this spread is being driven by bottom-up individual adoption rather than top-down institutional adoption. In the EU, for example, 65\% of respondents use AI, while only 19\% say their organisation has formally adopted it. Most users are positive about its effects, with 79\% saying AI has improved their productivity. However, only 29\% say it has increased what is expected of them at work, raising questions about how truly transformative the technology is so far. Across regions, South Africa is a clear outlier, with the highest levels of use, organisational adoption, optimism and awareness of guidelines.

papers.title: Addendum to "Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds"
papers.abstract: In the paper ``Geodesic fields for Pontryagin type $C^0$-Finsler manifolds'', the same authors introduced a geometric object called Pontryagin-type $C^0$-Finsler structures, which includes Finsler structures on a smooth manifold $M$. Such a structure is defined locally by a control system of $C^1$ unit vector fields on an open subset $U$ of $M$, such that Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) is applicable. As a result of PMP, we obtain the extended geodesic field $\mathcal{E}$, which is a multivalued vector field on the slit cotangent bundle $T^{\ast}U\backslash 0 = \{(x,α): x\in U, α\in T^{\ast}_x U\}$, such that every minimizing path $x(t)$ on $(U,F)$ is an extremal (projection of a Pontryagin extremal $(x(t),α(t))$). Some time after its introduction, its use and external comments, it is useful to provide remarks that clarify the applicability and limitations of this theory. In addition, we point out two errors contained in that work which, although discernible from the context, we believe should be pointed out. Finally, we prove some cases where the property that a minimizing path is the projection of a Pontryagin extremal can be extended beyond a coordinate system, sometimes to $M$. We also work on the problem of determining when $\mathcal{E}$ does not depend on the control system chosen to represent $F$. In particular, $\mathcal{E}$ satisfies these two properties globally for left-invariant $C^0$-Finsler structures on Lie groups, and for $C^1$-Finsler structures (without the condition of strong convexity).

papers.title: Hiding a Gap Does Not Close It: The Price of Removing the Mean Group Contrast from Learned Models of Learning Dynamics
papers.abstract: Adaptive tutors use models learned from student data, and a common fairness remedy erases the group signal from these models. We turn the cost of this remedy into an audit tool. Building on mean-parity regression, we give the minimum extra error, relative to the best predictor, of removing the mean group contrast from a predictor that cannot use the group, $p_0p_1Δ^2/R^2$, and the exact cost of any correction built from an estimated group model, which, for the best predictor, is never below this minimum. A three-stage audit (fit on training units, announce the cost on validation units, test on independent units) estimates this cost before the correction is used. In a controlled study, the price can be large even when the state predicts the group poorly. On three real data sets, erasing the group from a learned model of learning dynamics predicts almost no gap where one is observed. In a selected knowledge-tracing network, erasing the hidden state leaves most of the gap; a correction of the prediction removes it at an extra Brier score of 0.021 on average. On Eedi, with the network selected on separate units, the audit accepted the announced cost in all five splits, the measured cost fell inside the announced interval in all five, and the gap reduction transferred to new classes in four; on new ASSISTments schools the audit abstains. In a tutoring simulator, the objective and the help budget matter more than the erasure, and floors on each group's knowledge separate narrowing a gap from levelling down. Hiding a gap in a model does not close it.

papers.title: CupOFMoCA: Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly
papers.abstract: Molecular conjugates, including PROTACs and peptide-drug conjugates (PDCs), derive their function from the joint behavior of multiple coupled components, yet most generative approaches design these components independently and combine them only after generation. Such staged pipelines ignore cross-component dependencies and often produce conjugates that are chemically invalid, fall outside empirical conjugate distributions, or lose function upon assembly. In this work, we introduce Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly (CupOFMoCA), a discrete generative method that enforces cross-component chemical constraints during conjugate generation. CupOFMoCA restricts guided updates to chemically feasible conjugate states and reweights local transitions using molecular design objectives. Across three PDC systems, coupled generation achieved 100% conjugation validity among valid peptides and increased valid yield over matched post-hoc filtering, with comparable predicted binding scores across the full valid sets. In three-seed evaluations of three PROTAC systems, CupOFMoCA achieved the highest assembly validity on two systems and generated more assembly-valid molecules per second than the evaluated baselines. We further evaluated the generated PROTACs with post-hoc DegradeMaster scoring and explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, supporting their predicted activity and conformational properties. Together, these results establish CupOFMoCA as an efficient generator of molecular conjugates, supporting therapeutic development via coordinated control of assembly and molecular properties.

papers.title: VISTA: View-Independent micro-Doppler Reconstruction with Multistatic ISAC
papers.abstract: The micro-Doppler (uD) spectrum provides detailed characteristics of target movement, making it highly valuable for applications such as target classification and human activity recognition. However, traditional Integrated Sensing And Communication (ISAC) systems are highly view-dependent and limited by blind spots and angle dependencies. Existing approaches rely on either configuration-specific solutions or data-driven models. The former results in poor generalization when device deployments or target orientations change, while the latter requires acquiring extensive multi-view datasets, which is time-consuming and not always feasible. To address these limitations, in this work we propose VISTA, a novel method for reconstructing the uD spectrogram in an absolute coordinate frame, yielding view-independent Doppler features that are invariant to the spatial distribution of ISAC nodes. We formulate the uD estimation as a sparse reconstruction problem that jointly leverages measurements from all ISAC receivers. This is solved using a modified Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) algorithm, which iteratively alternates between jointly selecting candidate velocity vectors across all receivers (RXs) and independently estimating the complex channel gain amplitudes for each RX. Our results show that, provided sufficient spatial diversity, VISTA successfully reconstructs the targets' absolute uD spectrograms with a median error \leq 0.69 m/s for speeds \leq 15 m/s.

papers.title: A Matching Lower Bound for Online Smooth Calibration
papers.abstract: We study smooth calibration error in sequential binary prediction, which measures how far a sequence of probabilistic forecasts is from being calibrated and, unlike the classical expected calibration error, is robust to small perturbations of the forecasts. Against adaptive adversaries, the minimax smooth calibration error is known to lie between $Ω(T^{1/3})$ and $O(\sqrt{T})$ (Qiao and Zheng, 2024), where $T$ is the number of rounds. In this paper, we close this gap by constructing a new adversary whose outcome mean moves with the forecaster's cumulative residual. This design makes compensating for past residuals costly, and forces every forecaster to incur an expected smooth calibration error of $Ω(\sqrt{T})$. This lower bound matches the known upper bound up to universal constants, and further implies $Ω(\sqrt{T})$ lower bounds for calibration distance and lower calibration distance. Overall, our results settle the minimax rates of these calibration measures in sequential prediction. The proof ideas are partially developed by GPT-6 Astra under the authors' guidance.

papers.title: The Ultimate Karp-Lipton Collapse
papers.abstract: Karp and Lipton proved that if $NP\subseteq P/poly$, then $PH$ collapses. A long line of work pushed the collapse to smaller classes. In particular, Chakaravarthy and Roy obtained two such collapses, to (apparently) incomparable classes $O_2^P$ and $P^{prMA}$. We united them earlier by a collapse to the input-oblivious version $P^{prOMA}$ of $P^{prMA}$, which is contained in both; and, jointly with Williams, to a slightly smaller class. Two other deepest known collapses are to $ZPP^{ONP}$ (following from Köbler and Watanabe) and to $OL_2^P$ (proved in this paper). We unite the three collapses by a collapse to a class contained in all of them. We use a three-stage computational model OGTD (oblivious generator-tester-decoder): a polynomial-time generator with an oracle computes an advice string from $1^n$, a tester certifies it, and a polynomial-time decoder uses it (it is the only one that sees the actual input). Let $OM$ be the class of OGTD languages defined by a restricted version of $prOMA$ as the generator's oracle, by a co-$ONP$ tester, and a $P$ decoder. We show that it is contained in the three collapse classes above and prove that $PH$ collapses to $OM$ under $NP\subseteq P/poly$. The collapse also holds for an unambiguous version of $OM$. All these input-oblivious collapse classes lie in $P^{prSBP}$, and so do even the non-input-oblivious versions $P^{prMA}$, $L_2^P$ and $S_2^P$: we prove that $P^{prS_2^P}\subseteq P^{prSBP}$. This strengthens the containment $S_2^P\subseteq P^{prAM}$ of Chakaravarthy and Roy and our earlier containment $L_2^P\subseteq P^{prSBP}$. The proof unites the Goldreich-Wigderson-type procedure of Chakaravarthy and Roy with our earlier approximate-counting technique. Its input-oblivious counterpart concerns $O_2^P$, the first collapse class of Chakaravarthy and Roy: every language in $O_2^P$ has polynomial-size circuits constructible in $FP^{prSBP}$.

papers.title: Data-center growth impacts household electricity costs more through wholesale prices than through grid reinforcement
papers.abstract: Rapid data-center expansion is raising concerns about electricity affordability, yet how the costs of serving these large new loads reach residential customers remains poorly understood. Here, we quantify the potential impact of 371 announced Texas data-center projects, totaling 38.9 GW by 2030, on residential electricity costs by linking power system expansion, wholesale electricity markets, transmission reinforcement, and retail cost allocation. We find that accommodating this demand increases modeled residential electricity costs in one representative case by 1.64 cents/kWh, with 68% arising from higher wholesale electricity prices and 32% from regulated transmission charges. Allowing new gas generation near data centers reduces the 2023 residential cost increase to 0.92 cents/kWh, whereas excluding data centers from the transmission cost-sharing base raises it to 1.87 cents/kWh. These findings reveal that the residential cost burden of data-center growth is driven primarily by wholesale electricity price increases, rather than direct transmission investment costs, and depends critically on generation siting, infrastructure planning, and cost allocation.

papers.title: Optical symmetry breaking for single-image field reconstruction
papers.abstract: Light carries information in both amplitude and phase, although cameras record only intensity. Reconstructing the optical field is at the heart of wavefront sensing, microscopy and coherent communications. Existing methods often rely on multiple measurements or iterative phase retrieval. In fields described by known spatial modes, intensity is determined by pairwise products of their complex coefficients. Yet optical symmetries can make these products indistinguishable, leaving different fields with nearly identical images. Here, we show that engineering the optical measurement to break these symmetries enables direct reconstruction of the complex field from a single intensity image. We optimise a phase mask followed by propagation to separate pairwise modal signatures while retaining light on the detector. A calibrated linear inverse and rank-one projection then recover modal amplitudes and relative phases without iterative phase retrieval. In simulations, optimised masks satisfy conditioning and light-capture requirements unmet by random masks. Experiments reconstruct 42-mode fibre fields using either a spatial light modulator or a passive diffuser, with median complex-field errors of 9.1% and 4.6%, respectively, against holographic references. This extends an earlier five-mode experimental demonstration of fast intensity-only modal decomposition. Per-frame computation takes 2.1 ms, and batched throughput exceeds 4,000 frames per second. These results establish measurement-space symmetry breaking as a route to rapid single-image optical field reconstruction.

papers.title: Measuring Preferred Representation in AI-generated Images with Community Scorers
papers.abstract: AI-generated images often misrepresent historically marginalised communities, with real-world consequences beyond the images themselves. However, conventional metrics fail to measure how communities want to be represented in AI-generated images. To address this, we introduce the concept of preferred representation. Building on previous work, we propose a measurement instrument that operationalises this concept through a Community Scorer - a model that evaluates a specific community's preferred representation in AI-generated images. We interrogate the validity of Community Scorers on three diverse disability communities that span the Global North and South. The results show that Community Scorers align significantly better with community ratings compared to other widely used text-to-image metrics. We then demonstrate the usefulness of these scorers in a downstream content filtering task. We release the Community Preference Dataset to enable others to optimise how Community Scorers can be scaled for culturally specific evaluation of AI-generated visual media.

papers.title: Critical behavior of the bosonized Schwinger model with uniform matrix product states
papers.abstract: Quantum electrodynamics in two spacetime dimensions, also known as the Schwinger model, admits a dual formulation in terms of a non-compact boson field. Using a Hamiltonian lattice discretization of the bosonized model, we compute the critical mass of the continuum Schwinger model at $θ=π$. We numerically obtain the ground state on an infinite chain by the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm, preserving charge conjugation exactly. As a truncated basis for the local Hilbert space, we employ the oscillator basis that diagonalizes the one-site reduced density matrix of the free limit. We constrain the fitting functions for the continuum extrapolation using the Symanzik effective theory for lattice corrections. Our result for the critical mass, $(m/g)_c = 0.333\,555(5)$, agrees with recent staggered-fermion determinations at comparable precision.

papers.title: Dynamical stability of double planets in compact multiplanetary systems
papers.abstract: The "peas-in-a-pod" architecture of planetary systems, where planets are roughly evenly sized and log-spaced, is pervasive throughout known exoplanetary systems. However, many systems deviate slightly from this trend in that they have a "gap" where no planet has been detected, where one might have otherwise expected one to exist. There are many common explanations for the existence of these gaps, including the existence of as-yet-undiscovered planets lurking in these gaps; however, we propose that one potential explanation for some of these gaps is that they are filled by binary planets, a pair of gravitationally bound planets orbiting a common center of mass outside of both bodies. Specifically, in this work, we investigate the dynamical stability of these binary planets as compared to the more conventionally assumed single planets using Monte Carlo N-body simulations. We find that binary planets are slightly less stable than single planets. Overall, we find that binary planets and their cousins in exomoons provide a plausible explanation, at least from a stability perspective, for the existence of some dynamical gaps.

papers.title: Multi-UTE Myelin Fraction Mapping: Repeatability and Cross-Field-Strength Reproducibility at 1.5T and 3T
papers.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the repeatability and cross-field-strength reproducibility (1.5T vs 3T) of in vivo cerebral myelin fraction (MF) mapping with multi-contrast dual-resolution 3D UTE (multi-UTE), and to compare it with magnetization transfer (MT)-based methods. Methods: MT methods provide an indirect myelin-sensitive measure derived from magnetization exchange between macromolecular and free-water proton pools, whereas multi-UTE targets the ultrashort-T2* signal components. In five healthy volunteers, multi-UTE and MT-based measurements were performed at 1.5T and 3T, and the calculated MF maps were compared with magnetization transfer ratio (MTR) and magnetization transfer saturation (MTsat) maps. Two volunteers underwent repeated multi-UTE measurements within and between days. Field-strength reproducibility and test-retest repeatability were evaluated using linear regression, Bland-Altman analysis, concordance correlation coefficient (CCC), and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: Multi-UTE enabled simultaneous acquisition of quantitative and high-resolution structural images at both 1.5T and 3T. MF repeatability was high at 3T (ICC = 0.94-0.96) and more variable at 1.5T (0,64-0.96). Across field strengths, MF and MTsat showed comparable reproducibility (CCC 0.70 vs 0.60) with small median absolute differences (8.8% vs 8.9%). MTsat showed tighter correlation (R2 = 0.77 vs 0.68), while MF showed a wider inter-regional dynamic range. MTR differed strongly between field strengths (CCC = 0.06). Conclusion: Multi-UTE MF, obtained without B1 or T1 mapping and alongside a high-resolution structural image, achieves cross-field reproducibility comparable to, but not exceeding, MTsat. Lower SNR at 1.5T and unmodelled T1 weighting may have contributed to residual field dependence.

papers.title: One Future Fits All: Text-to-image AI and the Narrowing of Global Imagination
papers.abstract: Persistence of algorithmic bias is well established in scholarship, reflecting, reproducing and reshaping inequalities and injustices. Yet, as technology changes, we cannot assume that inequalities will be reproduced in the same or similar forms. This article explores the reproduction of bias in text-to-image generative AI, looking at the tool, Microsoft Bing Create, based on DALL E 3. It draws on results of a collaborative exploratory study of 907 image-based outputs of text-to-image generation in 15 languages and concerning 12 countries. We utilise the notion of synthetic probes (de Seta, 2024) to iteratively explore correlations of inputs and outputs within the context of place, language and power. We find striking simplicity in the scope of possibilities through which Bing Create considers the current and future city. Stripping out (explicit) indications of conflict, poverty and politics, we are left with images whose localised diversity harkens back to versions of Orientalist imaginaries. Images of the future emerge as one civilising mission or modernisation narrative, with all places headed to one future of hovercrafts, urban gardens and solar panels, encased in a composition of shades of blue and green. We argue that the visual outputs of this generative AI tool reflect and reproduce a simple but pervasive and persistent colonial/developmental worldview. We explore explanations for this emergent narrative and its implications, suggesting the threat of generative AI is not in its complexity or intelligence, but rather its banality. With this, we propose banality not as mere repetition, but the systematic narrowing of representational possibility: a convergence on tourist-friendly, depoliticised, development-saturated visual grammars that smooth contradiction and foreclose plural futurisms.

papers.title: Subsurface schematisation from sparse CPT data using the tabular foundation model TabPFN
papers.abstract: Subsurface schematisation supports geotechnical decisions but remains challenging because sparse site-investigation data leave substantial gaps in information about ground conditions. This study explores TabPFN, a foundation model pretrained on general synthetic tabular data, for this task. Using only grid coordinates and soil behaviour type index observations from sparse cone penetration tests (CPTs), we first reconstruct two-dimensional sections without geotechnical fine-tuning or predefined layer boundaries. We evaluate the approach on synthetic sections and at two field sites in the Netherlands, comparing it with SchemaGAN, a conditional generative adversarial network trained on synthetic geotechnical sections, and with reference interpolation methods. In the baseline comparisons, TabPFN achieved mean errors close to SchemaGAN's on synthetic sections and lower mean errors at both field sites. On synthetic sections, TabPFN's mean absolute error decreased at each tested increase in CPT count, and, under the baseline input setting, its pointwise prediction intervals had mean coverage close to nominal levels. Subsequent fine-tuning on the synthetic sections used to train SchemaGAN improved synthetic test accuracy but increased mean errors at both field sites. These findings indicate that general-purpose tabular foundation models offer a promising route for updating subsurface predictions from sparse and evolving site-investigation data without retraining.

papers.title: Convergence rates for truncated and discretised signature expansions
papers.abstract: Linear expansions in Brownian Stratonovich signatures, which originate in stochastic Taylor expansions, are increasingly used to represent and model processes with memory. Their numerical use requires truncating the signature at a level $M$ and discretising the driving path along $N$ steps. Under a simple growth condition on the coefficients of the linear expansion, we establish strong and weak convergence rates for both approximations, uniformly in time. The strong truncation error decays like $(B^M/(M!)^\varepsilon)^a$ for some constant $B$, uniformly in $N$, where $\varepsilon$ measures the growth of the coefficients and $a$ the regularity of the test function; the weak error does not improve on it. The discretisation error is of order $N^{-a/2}$ in $L^p$, and $N^{-1}$ weakly for polynomial test functions, uniformly in $M$. All these rates are sharp for polynomial test functions, and $M$, $N$ can be chosen independently. We extend the estimates to errors in probability, on distribution functions and on risk measures, and illustrate them on stochastic delay equations, Volterra processes and option pricing in signature volatility models.

papers.title: Minimal Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings
papers.abstract: A ring $R$ with nonzero unity is called centrally essential if for every nonzero element $a$ of $R$ there exist nonzero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In this paper we obtain a complete classification, up to isomorphism, of non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order $64$.

papers.title: Tunable Long-Range Magnetic Exchange in Adatom-Decorated Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Monolayers: An ab initio Embedding Model Study
papers.abstract: Engineering magnetic interactions in two-dimensional materials offers a promising route toward programmable magnetic phases and reconfigurable spintronic functionalities. Here, we investigate magnetic adatoms on metallic monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) as a platform for tunable indirect exchange, focusing on Fe adatoms on monolayer TaS$_2$. In the intermediate-distance regime, DFT+U calculations reveal atomic-scale oscillations in the exchange coupling between two Fe adatoms and show that biaxial strain tunes the coupling. We develop a first-principles embedding model that reproduces the DFT-calculated pair exchange and establishes a substantial RKKY contribution to the exchange; controlled comparisons further identify RKKY-mediated coupling as the primary origin of the exchange's strain tunability. These results point to combining adatom arrangement with strain as a means of engineering reconfigurable magnetic interactions in metallic monolayer TMDs.

papers.title: An Optimized Expansion Auction Integrating Energy, Flexibility, and Network Constraints
papers.abstract: Auction mechanisms are widely used to support generation investments. In the US, capacity auctions serve as supply-adequacy instruments to address the missing-money problem, whereas in Latin America, energy and capacity auctions procure long-term contracts to support generation expansion. In both settings, accreditation metrics, such as Firm Energy (FE) and Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), are used to approximate the reliability contribution of selected units and winning projects are selected based on a financial offer. This approach fails to recognize the actual contribution of winners to the multiple services they provide to the system. This limitation becomes more significant with high shares of renewables, as the value of each resource increasingly depends on network and technological constraints, as well as on complementarities within the generation portfolio. Inspired by short-term auctions, such as day-ahead markets, this paper proposes a joint optimization-based auction for generation and transmission investments that internalizes these interactions, capturing the intrinsic value of generation candidates without requiring the computation of FE or ELCC metrics. The auctioneer determines the winning portfolio through an expansion-planning model that explicitly represents network constraints, operational interactions, reliability standards, and multiple scenarios. A case study of the Brazilian system indicates lower system costs, lower risk, and a more diverse portfolio relative to the stylized decoupled procurement approaches currently deployed in many systems.

papers.title: Tendex Lines and Short-Time Deformation: The Geometry of Lunar Tides
papers.abstract: Tendex lines and the stretchlines and squeezelines of Lagrangian coherent structure theory share a geometric construction: they integrate eigenvector fields of symmetric tensors. We connect their dynamical interpretations through the short-time deformation of particles released with zero initial velocity relative to a freely falling reference in an autonomous gravitational field. The leading departure of the Cauchy--Green tensor from the identity is quadratic in time and equals the tidal tensor multiplied by the squared observation time. The tidal tensorlines therefore give the limiting principal stretching and squeezing directions. For the planar lunar field, these tensorlines are radial lines and concentric circles centered on the Moon. The same tidal tensor defines a Lorentzian metric whose null directions have no quadratic change in line-element length. Its null geodesics are logarithmic spirals, describing the short-time limit of finite-time unit-stretch geometry. Near Earth, the principal tensorlines clarify the two outward tidal tendencies, while the null directions distinguish vanishing leading extension from vanishing relative acceleration.

papers.title: Gradient-Aware AI Agents for Autonomous Turbulence Model Discovery via Differentiable CFD
papers.abstract: Turbulence modeling relies on human choices of closure form, physical inputs, and tunable parameters. Training closures a posteriori is efficient only with gradients through long chaotic rollouts, which few solvers provide. Most a posteriori approaches therefore resort to gradient-free optimization, and nearly all fix the closure form in advance, learning only its parameters. In this work, we introduce a gradient-aware agentic framework that poses closure discovery as a bilevel problem: a multi-agent large language model (LLM) system searches over closure forms, while a GPU-native differentiable computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solver supplies gradients, making differentiable a posteriori learning an action of the autonomous AI agent. For each proposal, the agents construct a differentiable training program by embedding the analytical, neural, or hybrid closure in the solver, implementing a differentiable objective, and validating the gradient path. They then decide whether to evaluate the closure, compute its parameter sensitivities, or train it a posteriori, select the optimization settings, and revise subsequent proposals using the simulation outcomes and returned gradients. Truncated-horizon gradients make this training usable under chaotic dynamics for closures with tens of thousands of parameters. Demonstrations include dissipation-law and subgrid-scale closure discovery in two-dimensional turbulence and wall-model discovery for large-eddy simulation of three-dimensional channel flow. With gradient-based training, the agent recovers reference coefficients that forward evaluation alone does not reach within the same budget, and autonomously discovers and trains analytical and neural closures that improve agreement with the targeted reference statistics. These results demonstrate the feasibility of end-to-end autonomous turbulence model development in time-resolved flows.

papers.title: KNO functions for dipole-dipole scattering from large Pomeron loops: log-normal tails and a test in exactly solvable models
papers.abstract: The sum of large Pomeron loops in QCD, based on the $t$-channel unitarity and on the solution of the Balitsky-Kovchegov (BK) equation in the saturation region, has been combined with the AGK (Abramovsky, Gribov and Kancheli) cutting rules to obtain multiplicity distributions with KNO (Koba, Nielsen and Olesen) scaling and an entropy equal to the logarithm of the gluon structure function. We reexamine these distributions for the BK amplitude and for dipole-dipole scattering. The KNO functions that follow from the Gaussian representation of the asymptotic series have log-normal and not Gaussian tails, $\lnΨ_{\rm BK}\simeq-\frac{1}{2}\ln^2ξ$ and $\lnΨ_{\rm dd}\simeq-\frac{1}{4}\ln^2ξ$, and we give them in closed form in terms of the Lambert function. They are log-normal mixtures of the distributions of one and two BFKL cascades, and the summation is not unique. The KNO scaling requires that power-like factors in the coefficients of the series be discarded, and the alternative contour representation leads to functions that change sign. We then test the approach in two exactly solvable models in zero transverse dimensions. In the unitary toy model we confirm that the resummed series reproduces the exact $S$-matrix to within 2.5-10%, while the $S$-matrix changes by many orders of magnitude. Nevertheless, the multiplicity distribution obtained from the same series with the AGK rules agrees with the exact one only as long as both cascades are dilute. At higher energies the exact mean grows as a power of rapidity, the KNO scaling is absent, and the entropy in the rest frame of the target grows as one half of the logarithm of the mean multiplicity. The amplitude is determined by rare configurations of the cascades and the multiplicity by the typical ones, so that the agreement of the amplitudes does not validate the multiplicity distributions.

papers.title: TGen-SQD: Physics-Informed Transferable Configuration Generator for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) avoids iterative variational circuit optimization, but its accuracy and cost depend on selecting a compact determinant subspace that captures the ground state. Existing machine-learning selectors use task-specific physical cues and typically retrain for each Hamiltonian. We introduce TGen-SQD, a physics-informed generator jointly trained across multiple Hamiltonians. It learns from configuration-interaction-weighted data and uses orbital- and system-level descriptors to guide generation. After training, its weights remain frozen for inference on seen and zero-shot geometries. On a 20-qubit H10 chain, TGen-SQD achieves mean energy errors of 40.18 +/- 1.52 and 43.97 +/- 1.20 mHa on seen and unseen geometries, respectively, 12.7% and 11.7% lower than the state-of-the-art PIGen-SQD baseline under matched shot and proposal budgets.

papers.title: Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted étale groupoid model
papers.abstract: We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal étale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.

papers.title: Simple Length Multiplicity on X(n)
papers.abstract: We study multiplicity among lengths of simple closed geodesics on the principal congruence surfaces $X(n)=Γ(n)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. We show that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there are positive constants $n_\varepsilon,C_{\varepsilon}$ so that, for $n\ge n_\varepsilon$, there are at least $\exp((\frac{π^2}{12}-\varepsilon)n)$ simple closed geodesics on $X(n)$ of the same length $\ell<C_\varepsilon n$. We produce the same multiplicity for $λ$-length of simple arcs with distinct endpoints via the McShane identity, which is immediately relevant as the size of a McShane gap around such an arc is roughly the reciprocal square of its $λ$-length. Our method of proof relies on an independently interesting theorem about the McShane identity for $X(n)$: the total mass of the gaps of pants with two cusps tends to 1 as $n\to \infty$. We present a proof of this latter fact that relies on estimates for the speed of mixing provided by Selberg's 3/16-Theorem (discovered with the help of ChatGPT). We indicate several avenues for further investigation.

papers.title: Desorption of water from cosmic silicates
papers.abstract: Recent JWST and ALMA observations of protoplanetary disks have identified water reservoirs in the inner regions of the disks. This would provide terrestrial planets forming therein access to a water reservoir. In situ formation of water molecules on grain surfaces was proposed as one possible formation process in the PDS 70 system, but transport by small silicate particles coupled to the gas could be another mechanism. Laboratory experiments on the thermally induced desorption of water molecules from different water-containing silicates at elevated temperatures provide another possibility for the enrichment of water molecules in the inner disk. Physically and chemically bound water in silicates can be released upon annealing processes. Water that is physically bound undergoes desorption at temperatures up to 473 K. In contrast, chemically bound water in form of different silanol or Mg-OH groups in amorphous silicates or phyllosilicates, can be released at higher temperatures, ranging from 773 to 923 K. The relevant temperatures are sufficient to trigger the solid-state recrystallization of amorphous silicates to Mg-rich orthopyroxene and olivine. The existence of these crystalline silicates has been substantiated through Spitzer and JWST-MIRI observations. Based on the experimental results, we postulate that the desorption of bound hydroxyl groups may serve as a mechanism for the formation of the water reservoir at temperatures up to 900 K, much higher than the water sublimation temperature of 100 to 200 K.

papers.title: An EPTAS for Max-Cut on Interval Graphs
papers.abstract: Max-Cut was shown NP-hard on interval graphs by Adhikary, Bose, Mukherjee, and Roy (SoCG 2021). The best previously known approximation ratio for this class, due to Ahn, DeHaan, Kim, and Lee (APPROX 2025), exceeded the Goemans--Williamson ratio of about $0.878$ by only $10^{-34}$. We give a deterministic efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme (EPTAS): for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximate cut of an unweighted $n$-vertex interval graph can be found in time $2^{O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log^3(2/\varepsilon))}n^2$. The same guarantee and running time hold for Max-Bisection. An FPTAS is impossible unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. Our algorithm rests on a structural theorem: every interval graph with $m$ edges can be turned into an interval graph of clique-width $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(2/\varepsilon))$ by deleting at most $\varepsilon m$ edges. The construction combines endpoint-rank coordinates, length-dependent rounding, and a shifted dyadic hierarchy. Intervals intersecting cell boundaries at their own scales are isolated at small total edge cost; the interactions of remaining long intervals with smaller subproblems can be summarized by counts. The structural theorem also yields a randomized EPTAS via Lampis's scheme for bounded clique-width; our direct dynamic program is deterministic and handles Max-Bisection. Finally, for every $\varepsilon>0$, it is NP-hard to approximate Max-Cut within $84/85+\varepsilon$ on unweighted chordal graphs, which contain interval graphs. Thus an approximation scheme for Max-Cut on chordal graphs would imply $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$.

papers.title: Exclusive cross section measurements of $^{12}$C(n,p$_\text{n}$) and $^{12}$C(n,d$_\text{n}$) reactions
papers.abstract: A single-crystal chemical vapor deposited (sCVD) diamond detector was used at LANSCE to measure neutron-induced reactions on carbon. Neutrons with a broad energy spectrum were produced via spallation. Relative cross sections are reported from above threshold up to 26 MeV incident neutron energy for $^{12}$C(n,p$_2$)$^{12}$B, up to 23 MeV for $^{12}$C(n,p$_{3+4}$)$^{12}$B, and up to 35 MeV for $^{12}$C(n,d$_1$)$^{11}$B and $^{12}$C(n,d$_2$)$^{11}$B, all of which represent the highest-energy measurements for these reactions to date, and the first measurement for (n,d$_2$). Cross sections for $^{12}$C(n,p)$^{12}$B$_\text{total}$ and $^{12}$C(n,d)$^{11}$B$_\text{total}$ are also reported from sums of the partial cross sections. These measurements are compared with recent data from EXFOR as well as TALYS calculations. These data are useful for future nuclear data evaluations and can be used as cross section inputs for data-based simulation packages.

papers.title: Holographic Wilsonian RG of Yang-Mills theory in AdS
papers.abstract: In this work, we extend the equilibrium-evolution duality between stochastic quantization and Wilsonian renormalization to non-abelian gauge theories in anti-de Sitter space, for which the radial coordinate of AdS plays the role of the stochastic time. We show, to all orders in the fields for bulk theories without explicit radial dependence, that the Langevin distribution at time $t$ is the product of the ultraviolet and infrared radial wavefunctions at the cutoff $ε=t$. We therefore identify this Langevin process as the ground-state (Doob) transform of the radial evolution. By explicit calculation, we also extend the existing dictionary in the stochastic-renormalization duality: the radial component of the bulk field is Zwanziger's stochastic gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization; and the bulk gauge $A_z=α^{-1}\partial_iA_i$ is Zwanziger's gauge. We also obtain the expressions for the triple-trace and quadruple-trace couplings of the holographic Wilsonian action at finite cutoff in closed form; in the infrared, they reduce to the known gluon correlators and, at the total-energy pole, to flat-space Yang-Mills amplitudes as expected. Although our explicit results are provided at tree-level and derived in AdS$_4$, we also comment on the de Sitter counterpart of these statements and on the loop corrections.
