PA-XAI therefore turns structured domain assumptions into explicit, testable controls for explanation auditing; support modeling, raw-flow reconstruction, and adaptive explanation attacks provide complementary validation layers.

papers.title: On the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures: disjointness of the cohomology groups
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is to start proving the Broué--Digne--Michel conjectures concerning the cohomology of Deligne--Lusztig varieties attached to roots of the full twist. The main result establishes that the $\mathrm{Ext}$-algebras of the cohomology complexes attached to roots of the full twist are concentrated in degree $0$. The main idea is to reduce the problem to a calculation in the Hecke category. The resulting argument is essentially topological and applies to all realizations of the Hecke category.

papers.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
papers.abstract: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

papers.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
papers.abstract: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.

papers.title: Generic unipotent representations of finite reductive groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a generic reductive group in the sense of Broué--Malle--Michel. We construct a category over $\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}]$ which interpolates between the various categories of unipotent representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ as we specialize $t$ to $q$. We use this category to show two properties of the unipotent decomposition matrix of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ mod $\ell$ (not dividing $q$): that, uniformly in $(q,\ell)$, there are finitely many such matrices and that for $\ell$ large enough, depending only on $\mathbb{G}$, this decomposition matrix depends only on the root of unity corresponding to $q$ mod $\ell$. We also prove that for $q$ and $q'$ two prime powers that are $\ell$-adically close enough, the categories of unipotent mod $\ell$ representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(q')$ are equivalent.

papers.title: Runtime Analysis of Cartesian Genetic Programming on Max: A Proven Exponential Speedup
papers.abstract: Genetic Programming (GP) is a search paradigm inspired from natural evolution for the automated discovery of expressions, functions, and computer programs. Cartesian GP (CGP) is a flavor of GP that uses a graph-based model to encode candidate programs, as contrasted to the conventional Tree-based GP (TGP). Since its inception two decades ago, CGP has predominantly been analyzed empirically, thus little is known regarding its theoretical performance guarantees. This paper analyzes CGP for the Max problem, which has been only rigorously studied for TGP with a proven expected runtime superlinear in the optimal program length $n$. We prove that the expected time for the ($1$+$1$)~CGP employing common mutation operators to evolve an equivalent optimal of the same output is polylogarithmic in $n$, specifically at most $O(\log^9{n})$. This is remarkable, as it shows an exponential speedup by switching to CGP. Our results shed light on the benefit and the compactness of the graph-based representation for programs, and on how CGP can navigate its search and fitness spaces efficiently. This is a first proven performance guarantee for CGP on an established benchmark problem. Experiments complement our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Topology-Aware 4D Gaussian Splatting for Egocentric Videos
papers.abstract: Reconstructing dynamic scenes and objects from monocular egocentric video is crucial for embodied AI, yet existing 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) approaches struggle with everyday interactions involving topological changes, such as cutting, assembly, opening, or closing. Since 4DGS methods rely on deforming a fixed representation, events that split, merge, or reveal surfaces cause severe visual artifacts. To address this challenge, we introduce TopoEgo, the first benchmark dedicated to topological changes in egocentric video (covering fission, fusion, open, and close), alongside Topo-4DGS, a topology-aware reconstruction method. Topo4DGS jointly models part-level motion and time-varying surface support by assigning independent rigid transformations to interacting parts and dynamically activating or deactivating Gaussians as surfaces appear, disappear, or separate. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Topo-4DGS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art 4DGS approaches across topological changes, especially on post-event frames. Code and data will be made publicly available.

papers.title: Zero detection via Cox random measures
papers.abstract: Using point process theory we propose and investigate a probabilistic identification of zeros of a deterministic real valued function. We construct a random atomic driving measure for a Cox point process whose mass at a candidate location depends explicitly on the value of the function at that location. We study the properties of the constructed random measure, including its exact asymptotic properties, its Laplace functional and related random processes. We also give an important application involving zero detection for Riemann's ξ function.

papers.title: Iris-Z: Scaling One Generative Model Past Specialist Geometry Models
papers.abstract: Language moved from many task-specific models to one unified model: a single generative model with a single generative training task that handles all of them within the same backbone, and keeps improving with data, parameters and compute. We believe the bitter lesson applies just as much to computer vision, 3D and spatial understanding, in the end to visual intelligence: the effort should go into general architectures that solve all these tasks in a unified way, and into scaling them, rather than into task-specific designs. We test this on monocular geometry, a task that has belonged to specialised architectures for years. Iris-Z is a general image generator that produces appearance and geometry together. A single backbone denoises, reasons about and understands the image and its depth at the same time, and one set of weights generates images with their depth, estimates depth from photographs and paints images onto a given depth. At enough scale it surpasses state-of-the-art specialists on established depth benchmarks while keeping the generative abilities of the backbone it started from without specialized layers. We release two models for the community.

papers.title: JustRUA: A Controlled Study of GPT-6 Robot-Use Agents
papers.abstract: GPT-6 Astra can drive a robot arm directly through a fixed harness, and scores of such robot-use agents on RoboDojo have risen quickly since. Reported systems differ in harness and test subset and often change several designs at once, so it is hard to tell which choices produce the gains. We take these designs apart and test them in one framework, along the harness around the model, the action interface, the reuse of experience and the scene geometry given to the model. A lean harness that keeps the full episode history and stops each motion early goes a long way. Reusing experience changes how the model acts but is not a free lunch, and scene geometry helps most, even when depth is predicted from RGB alone. JustRUA starts from the official L3 harness and keeps only what matters most. Even with no learned policy, self-improvement loop or task-specific tuning, this simple harness raises the score on the RoboDojo simulation benchmark substantially, from 29.7 to 50.3.

papers.title: Invariant random compacts for $\times p, \times q$ on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove that for multiplicatively independent natural numbers $p,q \ge 2$, if $μ$ is a Borel probability measure on the space $\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{T})$ of nonempty compact subsets of the circle $\mathbb{T}$ which is invariant under the induced actions of both multiplication by $p$ and $q$, and $μ$-a.e. $Y$ has positive Hausdorff dimension, then $μ$-a.e. $Y$ is equal to $\mathbb{T}$.

papers.title: Sharp constants and martingale proofs for two-weight Hardy inequalities with general measures
papers.abstract: We study the least constant $C_*$ in the two-weight Hardy inequality from $L^p(σ)$ to $L^q(ω)$ for the operator $H_σg(x)=\int_{(0,x]}g\,dσ$, where $σ$ is a Borel measure on the half-line that is finite on each interval $(0,x]$ and $ω$ is a $σ$-finite Borel measure there, atoms allowed. Let $\mathcal A$ be the Maz'ya--Rozin functional and let $1<p<\infty$. For $0<q<p$ we find the best factor $κ_{p,q}$ in $C_*\leκ_{p,q}\mathcal A$. For $1\le q<p$ we prove $C_*\ge\mathcal B\ge\mathcal A$, where $\mathcal B$ is a Lebesgue--Stieltjes form of $\mathcal A$. The factor $1$ is best possible. For $0<q<1$ we give a lower factor valid for all such measures and an upper bound for the best lower factor. This bound comes from atoms of $ω$. It is smaller than the lower factor proved by Sinnamon (1991) for weights. A two-atom example shows that the bound is not always sharp. The proofs use a reverse martingale with Doob's inequality, a special function of Osękowski (2015), a quantile coupling and a splitting of atoms. The same tools recover the theorem of Li and Mao (2020) for $1<p\le q$, in the closed-interval form of Klaassen and Wellner (2021). They also recover the two-sided estimate of Sinnamon and Stepanov (1996) for $0<q<p$, which goes back to Maz'ya (1979) for $q\ge1$ and to Sinnamon (1991) for $q<1$. We also treat the case $p=1$ and a discrete criterion.

papers.title: A flash before dawn: 21 cm signatures of transient reionization from supermassive Pop III stars
papers.abstract: Recent data from cosmological galaxy surveys combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) data give a preference for a departure from $Λ$CDM, favoring a model with an evolving dark energy equation of state or a small neutrino mass. However, recent works have shown that the electron scattering optical depth to the CMB ($τ$) can reduce this preference if $τ\sim0.09$, larger than that preferred by CMB low-$\ell$ E-mode polarization data. With standard monotonic hydrogen reionization histories, such a high value of $τ$ is in strong tension with spectroscopic galaxy data constraining the end of reionization. Thus, high-$τ$ models are restricted to non-standard reionization scenarios, where astrophysical sources inject an appreciable amount of ionizing photons at early times. One recently studied model for this is a supermassive population III star scenario, where radiative feedback from a self-annihilating dark matter particle enables a pathway to form $M\sim10^5 M_\odot$ stars that, upon collapse, photoionize a surrounding volume large enough to source appreciable contributions to $τ$ as a population. Here we present the first self-consistent treatment of the feedback from these supermassive population III stars within a large semi-numerical cosmological simulation, accounting for their ionizing, Lyman-Werner, and X-ray feedback on the intergalactic medium. We use it to predict the distinct signatures on the large-scale 21 cm signal at Cosmic Dawn, and forecast its detectability. We find that the 21 cm power spectrum probed by future radio survey arrays like the Square Kilometre Array could detect signatures of these supermassive population III at high significance and set model-dependent constraints on $τ$ that approach $σ_τ\sim0.012$, enough to distinguish our fiducial $τ\sim0.097$ scenario from current Planck values at $>3σ$.

papers.title: Transient early reionization allows for a high optical depth while remaining consistent with kSZ measurements
papers.abstract: Recent works have shown that a CMB optical depth of $τ\approx0.09$, above the Planck low-$\ell$ polarization value of 0.054, would weaken the preference of DESI data for dynamical dark energy and for a low neutrino mass. Apart from the low-$\ell$ CMB, another probe that prefers a $τ\sim0.055$ is the kinetic Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (kSZ) effect when combined with the end of hydrogen reionization as measured by the Ly$α$ forest. In this work we use a new self-consistent model of supermassive Population~III stars, which partially ionize the intergalactic medium at high redshifts ($z\approx20$--$25$), to predict the kSZ signal. We show that such an early, transient reionization phase can raise $τ$ to $\approx0.09$ while remaining consistent with current kSZ and Ly-$α$ forest constraints. We forecast that the Simons Observatory, combined with Ly-$α$ forest and UV luminosity function data, can constrain the optical depth accumulated above $z=12$ to $\pm0.008$ in our fiducial supermassive Pop~III scenario.

papers.title: Blow-up rate for 1-d semilinear wave equations without scaling invariance at characteristic points
papers.abstract: We investigate the blow-up behavior of solutions to the semilinear wave equation $$ \partial_t^2 u - \partial_x^2 u = |u|^{p-1}u \ln^a(u^2+2), \quad (x,t)\in \mathbb{R} \times [0,T), $$ with $p > 1$ and $a<0$. While the blow-up rate at non-characteristic points was determined for all $a \in \mathbb{R}$ in previous work, the analysis at characteristic points has remained an open problem. The main obstruction is that known constructions of a Lyapunov functional in similarity variables require several steps and rely on a covering argument, which is not available at characteristic points. Focusing on the regime $a < 0$, we construct a Lyapunov functional directly, without any covering argument. This yields uniform bounds on the solution in similarity variables, and hence the blow-up rate at every point, including characteristic ones. To our knowledge, this is the first work to determine the blow-up rate at characteristic points for an equation without scaling invariance.

papers.title: Fit-LRP: Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes for Neural Network Verification over Non-Convex Regions
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art neural network verifiers evaluate linear relaxations over axis-aligned bounding boxes. However, verification domains in cyber-physical systems are rarely boxes. Reachability specifications, obstacle-avoidance constraints, and neural Lyapunov certificates typically yield oblique or non-convex polyhedral regions, over which box-based bounds become extremely loose. This paper proposes Fit-LRP (Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes), a framework the implements exact optimization of affine bounds over non-convex domains (represented by unions of polytopes) by solving a sequence of small, low-dimensional linear programs. Our approach seamlessly enhances the final optimization step of LiRPA and $α,\! β$-CROWN branch-and-bound (BaB) algorithms. In BaB verification, approximating oblique constraints with axis-aligned splits causes severe combinatorial blowup and risks non-termination. By optimizing the final affine bound of a nonlinear function over the exact polyhedral state-space constraints our method eliminates box-induced over-approximations, enabling earlier search-tree pruning. On ARCH-COMP and neural Lyapunov benchmarks, Fit-LRP reduces branching on the hardest region by $47\times$, cuts worst-case verification time by $15\times$, and with region-wise partitioning, verifies on a single CPU $6.1\times$ faster than $α,\! β$-CROWN on a GPU.

papers.title: On the algebraic Mackey deformation
papers.abstract: This paper provides a conceptual understanding of the Mackey bijection from the admissible dual of a real reductive group $G$ into the admissible dual of its Cartan motion group $G_0$, by studying the primitive spectrum of a Hecke algebra over $\mathbb{C}[t]$ arising from the contraction of $G$ to $G_0$. If $K$ denotes a maximal compact subgroup of $G$, our approach leads to the following two results: the admissible Mackey bijection is a piecewise homeomorphism, each piece being defined by the length of the lowest $K$-types; the Hecke algebras of $G$ and $G_0$ have, up to $K$-types not exceeding a certain length, the same periodic cyclic homology.

papers.title: A Proper Random Walk Spline Model for Bayesian Smoothing
papers.abstract: We introduce the Proper Random Walk (PRW) family of spline models with a particular focus on the Second-Order Proper Random Walk (PRW2), a proper stationary alternative to the standard random walk of order 2 (RW2) spline. The PRW2 retains the computational strengths and spline-like smoothing of the RW2 while providing uniform marginal variance and stable uncertainty behavior. The PRW2 model is governed by a range parameter that controls correlation decay: in the infinite-range limit, it recovers RW2. In addition to its discrete representation, we show that the PRW2 model admits a continuous-time formulation as the critically damped Matérn model with smoothness $ν=3/2$, which provides an interpretable parameterization and enables construction through a Galerkin finite-element approximation on general grids. To mitigate edge distortions on bounded domains, we propose a local boundary correction that enforces the stationary joint law while preserving sparsity and $O(n)$ factorization. Finally, we develop penalized complexity priors for the model hyperparameters, enabling principled shrinkage toward the RW2 limit. The model is applied to simulated and real data to illustrate its properties and advantages.

papers.title: Predicting the Needle in a Petabyte Scale Haystack: Open-Vocabulary Event Anticipation in Satellite Imagery
papers.abstract: Satellite constellations now image the Earth daily, capturing the lifecycle of events from deforestation to urban construction. Anticipating these events before completion enables timely intervention, yet existing systems cannot jointly identify where a change occurs, what it will become, and when it will finish across an open vocabulary. Building such a model requires diverse event data, but events are like needles in a haystack, making manual annotation at global scale infeasible. We address this problem by representing change as the vector difference between vision-language model embeddings at distinct time points. This arithmetic approach allows us to search for semantic transformations directly in the latent space, enabling (1) an automated data engine for global event discovery without manual annotation and (2) the largest global satellite event dataset to our knowledge, comprising 21,000+ locations across 64+ event types with ~2M images from PlanetScope and Sentinel-2 spanning six continents, to train (3) a novel global-scale event anticipation model. Our model detects change with a 93.5% max F1 score, outperforms baselines 3.6x on predicted event retrieval, and forecasts completion dates with a 3-day median error, even nine months before completion. Code: https://github.com/ShreelekhaR/predicting-the-needle

papers.title: Recurrence and Transience in Monotone Environments: Increasing Conductances and Growing Domains
papers.abstract: We study discrete-time random walks on a locally finite graph whose conductances are non-decreasing in time and bounded on each edge. We compare their hitting probabilities with those of the time-homogeneous walk obtained by fixing the conductances at the starting time. These estimates give proofs of two results established in greater generality by Li and Park: if the upper network is recurrent, every vertex is visited infinitely often almost surely; if the initial network is transient, the expected number of visits to each vertex is finite. In a finite domain, the difference between the two exit probabilities is bounded by the square root of the product of a capacity increment and a dual energy. We obtain a corresponding infinite-volume estimate for the probability of never hitting a given vertex. To prove these estimates, we compare two Dirichlet forms and use a contraction property of the killed transition operators. We also consider walks on increasing finite sets. On each prescribed time interval, called a plateau, the transition operator is fixed. A lower bound on transition probabilities after mixing and an upper bound on the expected number of returns give a sufficient condition for every vertex to be visited infinitely often almost surely. For uniformly elliptic lazy walks on boxes of radius $R_n$ in $\mathbb Z^d$, $d\geq3$, it is enough that $\sum_n(L_n-b_n)_+/R_n^d$ diverges, where $L_n$ is the duration of the $n$th plateau and $b_n=\lceil aR_n^2\rceil$.

papers.title: PSR J1807-2459B in NGC 6544: A Unique Relativistic Binary in a Dense Cluster
papers.abstract: The globular cluster NGC 6544 is a high-density, dynamically evolved system located in the direction of the Galactic Center, known for hosting the eccentric binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1807-2459B. We present a new timing solution for this pulsar, based on more than 26 years of observations with the Parkes, Green Bank and MeerKAT radio telescopes. We measure for the first time the variation of the orbital period, which is dominated by the acceleration of the binary in the cluster potential: this places the pulsar in front of the cluster center and reveals its intrinsic spin-down, typical of a fully recycled millisecond pulsar. We also improve the measurements of the rate of advance of periastron and of the Einstein delay, the latter by a factor of four, and include the previously neglected contributions of the proper motion, which makes these parameters and the derived masses of the pulsar and its companion, $1.3636^{+0.0017}_{-0.0021}\,M_\odot$ and $1.2071^{+0.0021}_{-0.0017}\,M_\odot$, more realistic. Together with the Shapiro delay, these measurements allow two independent tests of general relativity, both passed. Our results show that precise post-Keplerian parameters of a binary pulsar in a dense cluster can probe both the cluster gravitational field and general relativity, provided that kinematic effects are carefully taken into account.

papers.title: What Can Next Generation Ultrafast Light Sources Tell Us About Quantum Materials?
papers.abstract: Ultrafast spectroscopy of quantum materials has emerged as a principle application of modern ultrafast optical sources. Measurements made with ultrashort pulses allow the normally strongly coupled internal degrees of freedom inside these systems to be de-coupled in the time-domain, revealing the key interactions for the different orders that lead to dramatic emergent phenomena. This has naturally motivated a wide range of experiments, and quantum materials have now been studied with ultrafast sources spanning from the hard X-ray to the THz, with fields intense enough to create non-equilibrium states, and using pulses down to the attosecond duration. As the optical spectroscopist's toolbox becomes increasingly complete, it is worth pausing and reflecting on what are the capabilities that we currently lack for examining quantum materials, and what are the problems that require the next generation of ultrafast sources now coming on-line or being designed. Here I will offer an overview of the remaining missing capabilities in ultrafast optical sources as required for studying quantum materials, and identify some outstanding problems where I believe these new sources can provide decisive impact in our understanding of quantum and strongly-correlated materials.

papers.title: The Levitt--Yoccoz gasket: dynamics, Hausdorff dimension and norm exponent
papers.abstract: In S.P.~Novikov's problem on plane sections of 3ply periodic surfaces, the author and I.\,A.~Dynnikov showed that, for the $μ$-cube, the directions lying in no stability zone form the union of a fractal set $N$, the Levitt--Yoccoz gasket (projectively equivalent to the Rauzy gasket), and of its images under the sign changes of the coordinates. $N$ is the limit set of a parabolic projective iterated function system $PΓ_N$ generated by a semigroup $Γ_N\subset SL_3(\mathbb Z)$, and each zone is labelled by a primitive integer vector, its soul. We show that $N$ is the global attractor of $PΓ_N$ and that the chain graphs of $PΓ_N$ and its Hutchinson map consist of a single node. Building on the theorem of Jiao--Li--Pan--Xu and Jurga that $\dim_H N$ equals the affinity exponent of $Γ_N$, we prove $1.6853<\dim_HN=\dim_BN<1.6854$. For some class of cut-out gaskets $K$, we bound $\overline{\dim}_B K$ from both sides by the norm exponent $s_N(Γ)$. The norm exponent $s_N$ of $G_N$, the counting exponent of the souls, is Baragar's exponent of the Markoff--Hurwitz equation $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2+x_4^2=ax_1x_2x_3x_4$. We prove $2.4411\le s_N\le2.4465$, improving Baragar's bounds, and $\frac23 s_N\le\dim_H N\le\frac12(1+s_N)$, which proves a conjecture by Gamburd, Magee and Ronan; and we show that the exponent of the equation in six variables exceeds $3$, answering a question of Baragar. For the three-dimensional Levitt--Yoccoz gasket $G\subset\mathbb RP^3$ we prove $2.74\le s_N(Γ_G)\le2.777$ and $\dim_H G\le2.3885$. Finally, for the renormalization flow of Avila, Hubert and Skripchenko, we show that the invariant measure they introduce is the Gibbs measure at the parameter $s_N$ and that $s_N$ is the maximal entropy per unit time of the return map, attained only by this measure. So, the diffusion exponent of their chaotic plane sections is less than 0.7766.

papers.title: Communication inequalities: robust quantum advantage, measurement testing and dimension witnessing with minimal setups
papers.abstract: Communication scenarios (CS) are arguably the simplest setting in which quantum behaviors can be observed. Yet, in contrast to Bell scenarios or prepare-measure scenarios with shared randomness, no general method is known to separate classical and quantum statistics. Here we close this gap by deriving dimensional inequalities to separate classical and quantum statistics in CS. These depend only on four parameters of the input-output statistics, corresponding to correlated and anticorrelated events. Under dimensional assumptions, saturating one of the inequalities certifies SIC-POVMs with analytical noise robustness. The inequalities also yield a dimension witness for both correlated and anti-correlated statistics, without the need of measurement incompatibility.

papers.title: Path Components of Almost Doubly Commuting Fredholm Tuples
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that the Fredholm index classifies the norm-path components of almost doubly commuting Fredholm n-tuples on a separable infinite dimensional Hilbert space. Using Kasparov's technical theorem, we join each tuple to an essentially normal one by a straight-line Fredholm path and applying the Douglas-Curto theorem.

papers.title: Self-Force and Bremsstrahlung in Finite Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study the self-force and the accompanying Bremsstrahlung for a moving point charge in nonlinear electrodynamics with finite self-field and self-energy. The self-force in the Maxwell theory has been the subject of many studies, often by renowned physicists. After reviewing Coleman's lucid treatise for Maxwell among them, we wish to explore the same question in the Born--Infeld theory, our prototype. We independently compute the local self-force and the global radiative dissipation, and show how the two are mutually consistent. Despite the nonlinearity turning off for the asymptotic radiative field, its residual effect survives via the effective multipole moments of a moving charge, allowing deviation from Maxwell. We close with a detailed discussion about two different manifestations of the self-force in the literature and how these enter our computation. One of the appendices explores Born--Infeld ModMax as a generalization.

papers.title: The multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier
papers.abstract: We prove that the multiplicative complexity of the three-bit low-half multiplier is six, giving a structural, enumeration-free lower-bound proof valid against unrestricted nonlinear reuse in Boolean XOR-AND circuits. The value was previously established by SAT searches of the second author. An explicit six-AND circuit supplies the upper bound. The lower bound combines derivatives, quadratic products, complementary minors, and extraction modulo a Boolean ideal. Independent finite checks accompany the arguments. $\mathrm{MC}(M_3)=6$ is fully formalized in Lean 4. The kernel-checked proof uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

papers.title: Adaptive Distance Detection and Adaptive Instance Segmentation
papers.abstract: This paper is about object detection model and semantic segmentation model in an FPS game Counter Strike: Condition Zero to detect enemies. Semantic segmentation is pixel-wise detection algorithm. We customized the architecture for semantic segmentation. We used YOLOv5s to train object detection model. After training, the inference time of semantic segmentation was compared to object detection. It was observed that object detection was slightly faster and semantic segmentation is slower but better at detecting the exact shape of the object. However, we found out that this slight difference of inference can grow exponentially if the both models get more complex. To solve this, we propose a novel approach called Adaptive distance detection which combines both algorithms. We will also introduce Adaptive instance segmentation to combine semantic segmentation and panoptic segmentation.

papers.title: Characterizing the Edge of Stability in Variational Training Without Priors
papers.abstract: Variational approaches in deep learning promise to deliver improved uncertainty quantification and out-of-distribution generalization by inferring a distribution over weights, regularized by a divergence to a chosen prior. However, prior elicitation presents a significant challenge in deep learning, resulting in the common practice of significantly downweighting the regularization term in the variational objective. Recently, it was proposed to train solely via the expected loss by relying on implicit regularization from the optimizer, rather than explicit regularization from the divergence to the prior. While this approach largely sidesteps the issue of prior elicitation, current theory lacks an understanding of how key optimization hyperparameters impact the implicit regularization. Here, we theoretically and empirically demonstrate that larger learning rates and fewer parameter samples lead to flatter minima of the loss landscape, which are known to generalize better. We show that training on the expected loss operates at a modified edge of stability, characterized by the signal-to-noise ratio of the gradient estimates and the number of Monte Carlo samples. Experiments on out-of-distribution benchmark datasets confirm the practical significance of the theoretical results.

papers.title: What Roles Do System Prompts Really Assign? Validating and Steering Occupational Role Vectors in LLMs
papers.abstract: Applications built on large language models assign the model a role through its system prompt, intending to shape how it responds for their use case. We introduce a validation framework for extracting and injecting occupational role vectors, activation-level directions that capture how someone in a given occupational role would distinctively respond to a task or question. We validate these vectors through two complementary lenses, on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. The interpretability lens asks whether each vector is a stable, separable, domain-consistent representation of its role: extracted vectors are highly reproducible across repeated runs and sampling temperatures, remain separable even for very similar roles, and agree more with themselves across in-domain and out-of-domain questions than with other roles' signal. The control lens asks whether injecting a role vector during generation makes the model express the role, and sustain it over a conversation, as well as a role prompt does. On Qwen, injecting the vector alone makes the model express the intended role substantially more often than unsteered, but at best matches a role prompt; on both models, adding the vector to the prompt strengthens the role in single answers but did not slow the role's decline over 30 turns. Together, the two lenses show why both are needed: out of domain the role is expressed only subtly, yet the activations still encode it; and a vector that is stable and separable can still barely steer the model's behavior.

papers.title: Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
papers.abstract: Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. Working in dimension $n \ge 2$ throughout the paper, we prove that for symmetric uniformly elliptic operators with bounded measurable coefficients, every bounded open set satisfying the mean value inequality for all integrable subsolutions defined on that set (what we call ``strong mean value sets'') agrees almost everywhere with the canonical set from Caffarelli's construction which has the same center and volume. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ``mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume as this weak mean value ball has a hole of positive measure.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): Photometric-redshift pipeline overview and validation
papers.abstract: We present the pipeline design of the photometric redshift processing function for Data Release 1 (DR1) of the $Euclid$ mission, and the validation and performance of our cosmology-related products that are released as part of DR1-Foundation. The $Euclid$ mission aims to constrain the equation-of-state parameter of dark energy, $w$, to percent-level accuracy through the measurement of large-scale structure via weak gravitational lensing and galaxy clustering. As part of DR1-Foundation we release determinations of photometric redshifts (photo-$z$), corrected photometry, and object classes that are used to form the basis of the cosmological samples. The release furthermore includes estimates of the spectral energy distributions of stars and galaxies for the careful modelling of the point-spread function for weak-lensing measurement. We estimate the performance of the photo-$z$ point estimates and probability distribution functions using overlapping spectroscopic redshifts, which are weighted to match different flux-limited target samples. We find that the current performance is somewhat below mission design requirements ($40\%$ in scatter and a factor of 2 in outlier fraction) at the nominal survey depth ($I_{\rm E}<24.5$), but closely matching requirements at slightly brighter magnitudes ($I_{\rm E}<24$), consistent with pre-launch analyses and the slightly shallower external data (up to $0.3\,\mathrm{mag}$) with respect to end-of-mission expectations. Data from Rubin-LSST will help alleviate this issue by the time of the final cosmology analyses. The other cosmology-related outputs are tested to the extent that is possible with currently available comparison data. This paper is partnered by an article describing the measurement of the physical properties of galaxies for the purpose of non-cosmological science.

papers.title: K3 surfaces and BHK Mirror symmetry: A counterexample
papers.abstract: For K3 surfaces of BHK type, there are two versions of mirror symmetry that might be applied, namely BHK mirror symmetry and LPK3 mirror symmetry of Dolgachev, which involved choosing a polarizing lattice. It has been conjectured that for a pair of BHK mirror K3 surfaces, one can choose a polarizing lattice as the invariant lattice of some nonsymplectic diagonal symmetry. We provide a counterexample, showing that LPK3 mirror symmetry cannot be realized by polarizing surfaces by the invariant lattice of a diagonal symmetry. However, in our example the polarizing lattice can be realized as the invariant lattice of a permutation symmetry.

papers.title: Three-body streaming forces lower the axial binding threshold of a held transverse three-sphere chain
papers.abstract: Particles in oscillatory liquids can form chains perpendicular to the drive. We ask whether the forces between isolated pairs predict when three spheres can bind at a finite spacing. We first hold the spheres fixed during small-amplitude oscillation and calculate the cycle-averaged force on an end sphere. The three-body contribution lowers the critical Stokes number from 4.283 for the pair-additive model to 3.534 for the full chain, a reduction of 17.5 percent. An independent finite-element calculation reproduces the shift. The three-body attraction also draws the spheres close enough for the nearest-neighbour pair forces to become repulsive. This compression accounts for most of the tendency to bend out of the plane containing the drive and the chain. For freely translating and rotating spheres at a particle-to-liquid density ratio of 2.2, the multipole calculation predicts initial growth of this bend at five sampled equilibria. A point-singularity calculation confirms the sign at two of those spacings.

papers.title: Elastic tricriticality at the collapse of magnetic order in a valence fluctuating Eu-based compound
papers.abstract: Spin and charge fluctuations are key for understanding the properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons, but their coupling to the atomic crystal lattice is often assumed to be weak and perturbative. In this work, we demonstrate that at tricritical points (TCPs), that are associated with electronic correlations, a coupling to crystal elasticity is generically non-perturbative. It will modify the tricritical universality class leading to elastic tricriticality, characterized by a compressibility that diverges in a universal manner with the correlation length. To test this scenario experimentally, we use single crystals of EuPd$_2$(Si$_{1-x}$Ge$_x$)$_2$, where, depending on $x$ and pressure, magnetic order collapses due to strong valence fluctuations. First, we confirm the presence of a TCP for $x \approx 0.1$ by using complementary probes, in particular, measurements of relative length changes under control of temperature and He-gas pressure. Second, by studying the elastic response, we uncover clear signatures of elastic tricriticality, notably a drastically enhanced compressibility.

papers.title: TRACE: Trajectory Synchronization for Training-Free Resolution Extension in Video Generation
papers.abstract: More text-to-video models are available, but many remain limited to low resolutions. Training them for higher resolutions is costly, while existing training-free methods still struggle with fine detail, scene structure, and efficiency. We propose TRACE, a training-free method that synchronizes low- and high-resolution generation trajectories. During early denoising, TRACE aligns predicted scene content at corresponding noise levels. It computes high-resolution updates from low-resolution predictions and the current high-resolution state, without high-resolution model inference. The high-resolution trajectory retains fine-grained variation for generating new details. Local window attention then refines fine details in a shared high-resolution latent state. TRACE checks suspected duplicate subjects against the corresponding low-resolution layout and corrects selected regions and their solver history while preserving detail elsewhere. Experiments across all kinds of video generation backbones and resolutions show improved perceptual quality and text-video alignment over FreeSwim, a state-of-the-art training-free method, with 2.0-2.9x end-to-end speedups. Our code and models will be released at https://github.com/libozhu03/TRACE.

papers.title: Analysis of TraceFEM for the Surface Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard Model
papers.abstract: We analyze a trace finite element method (TraceFEM) for a surface fluid with a stabilization term that filters out Killing vector fields, and use it to discretize the surface Stokes-Cahn-Hilliard problem in space only. Assuming no geometric error, we show that the discrete inf-sup condition that our method requires is equivalent to the usual condition found in the literature and known to hold for trace Taylor-Hood pairs of arbitrary order in intrinsic dimension two. Inspired by a continuous dependence estimate at the PDE level, we derive error estimates for our scheme in the energy norms, which in turn lead to estimates in $L^2$-norms and, for two-dimensional surfaces, $L^\infty$-norm for the phase variable. To that end, we introduce a $p$-dependent scaling for the normal derivative volume stabilization, and use it to prove new approximation and inverse estimates in the $L^p$- and $W^{1,p}$-based setting ($p \in [1,\infty]$ for approximation and $p \in [2,\infty]$ for inverse estimates). Finally, we corroborate the analysis with numerical experiments.

papers.title: DexRemo: A Force-Sensing Hand Platform and Task Suite for Contact-Rich Removal Manipulation
papers.abstract: Many manipulation tasks require separating adhered, embedded, contaminated, or mechanically constrained targets. We study this setting as removal manipulation, where progress depends on evolving contact states that are only partially observable from vision and kinematics. We introduce DexRemo, a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation, modular fingertips, and three-axis fingertip force sensing, together with a nine-scenario real-robot task suite spanning adhesive detachment, surface cleaning and self-cleaning, and occluded retrieval. To make multi-finger force observations easier to fuse, we express fingertip forces in a shared wrist-centered frame, giving force components consistent geometric meaning across fingers and time. Using an Action Chunking Transformer backbone, policies fuse multi-view vision, proprioception, fingertip pose, and force observations to predict closed-loop action chunks from demonstrations. Evaluation uses six core benchmark tasks for controlled fingertip-input and force-frame ablations, plus three extension scenarios for additional held-out coverage. Across these evaluations, the learned policies achieve consistent removal performance, and ablations show that wrist-frame forces, especially with fingertip pose, improve stability and generalization over local-frame force inputs and no-force baselines. Project website: https://dexremo.github.io

papers.title: Data-driven Correction Reduced-Order Stochastic Collocation Method for the Time-Dependent Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: We develop two hybrid data-driven Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) Reduced-Order Models (ROMs) for the non-stationary incompressible Navier--Stokes Equations (NSEs) with random viscosity. The proposed framework combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) ROMs, spatial filtering, data-driven closure modeling, and the Stochastic Collocation Method (SCM). A key feature is the approximation of the realization-dependent closure term by the closure associated with the expected viscosity. Consequently, a single data-driven closure model constructed from the full-order solution corresponding to the expected viscosity can be reused across all realizations, thereby avoiding the expensive construction of realization-specific closure models. This leads to the Data-Driven Correction UQ ROM (DDC-UQ-ROM) and its physically constrained variant, the Constrained DDC-UQ-ROM (CDDC-UQ-ROM), in which physical constraints are imposed on the data-driven correction model. The proposed methods are evaluated for a two-dimensional (2D) flow past a circular cylinder problem with a 5D random viscosity field, considering mean Reynolds numbers $Re=100$ and $Re=500$, different correlation lengths, and both in-sample and out-of-sample parameter settings. Numerical results show that the DDC-UQ-ROM generally improves upon the standard Galerkin ROM (G-ROM), while the CDDC-UQ-ROM exhibits the most accurate and robust approximation of the benchmark energy evolution across the cases considered. The robustness and accuracy of the CDDC-UQ-ROM are further assessed through statistical error analyses of the first- and second-order energy moments, reduced-training-data experiments, and an indicative comparison of wall-clock computational costs with the full-order UQ calculations.

papers.title: Matching 2HDM to HEFT in triple Higgs boson production from WBF
papers.abstract: In this work we compare the Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT) predictions with the Two Higgs Doublet Model (2HDM) predictions for triple Higgs production via $WW \rightarrow hhh$ scattering, under the hypothesis of very heavy Higgs bosons $H$, $A$, and $H^\pm$, and assuming the lightest one $h$ has the observed mass in the experiments, $m_h \simeq 125$ GeV. By requiring the matching of the two corresponding scattering amplitudes for this $WW \rightarrow hhh$ process in the limit of very heavy mass for these bosons, we find the solutions for the leading order HEFT coefficients. Concretely, we determine the coefficients $a$, $b$, $c$, $κ_3$ and $κ_4$ defining the effective interactions $WWh$, $WWhh$, $WWhhh$, $hhh$ and $hhhh$, respectively, in terms of the 2HDM input parameters, $c_{β-α}$, $\tan β$ and $m_{12}$. We will also compare these solutions with the corresponding solutions found for the case of double Higgs production. The solutions presented here for the matched coefficients summarize the non-decoupling effects from the heavy modes, $H$, $A$ and $H^\pm$ in the scattering process $WW \rightarrow hhh$ and provide the most relevant contributions to the cross section $σ(WW \rightarrow hhh)$ that do not decrease as inverse powers of the heavy masses. In the last part, we will also discuss the numerical predictions of the cross section $σ(WW \rightarrow hhh)$ in terms of the HEFT-matched coefficients. The focus of this discussion is set on the big gap between the HEFT-matched prediction and the SM prediction due to the non-decoupling behaviour occurring whenever misalignment is assumed in the 2HDM, i.e. for $c_{β-α} \neq 0$. This big gap could serve as potential signals of the 2HDM heavy modes, $H$, $A$ and $H^\pm$, at future high energy colliders, even if they are too heavy and cannot be produced at these colliders.

papers.title: Tests of Covariate Effects and Model Selection in Finite Mixture Regression Model
papers.abstract: Finite mixture regression models are widely used to capture the heterogeneous effects of covariates on a response variable. Our study, motivated by the analysis of Chiroptera, explores the dynamic effects of various environmental, biological, and human-related covariates on the evolutionary development of bat forearm using finite Gaussian mixture regression (GMR) models. In this paper, we address two key questions: (1) which covariates are associated with the variation in forearm length; and (2) whether the associated covariates have the same effect across all subpopulations. To answer these questions, we propose two stepwise procedures within the finite GMR framework based on the weighted significance test (WEST): (1) a stepwise variable selection procedure to identify relevant influential covariates, and (2) a stepwise effect-type determination procedure to determine each relevant covariate as having either a homogeneous or heterogeneous effect across subpopulations. Based on these procedures, we introduce a stepwise model selection procedure for finite mixture regression, illustrated through finite GMR models. Simulation studies are conducted to assess the performances of our proposed procedures. The proposed procedure will be applied to the Chiroptera dataset.

papers.title: Quantum geometric bounds and uncertainty relations for velocity variance and spread of Wannier function
papers.abstract: By utilizing the derivation of quantum Cramér-Rao bound and an argument put forward by Efimov and Dodonov, we derive several uncertainty relations for mixed states that constrain the diagonal product, trace, and each diagonal element of the covariance matrix of multiple observables. By choosing the observables to be the symmetric logarithmic derivative, the uncertainty relations imply various geometric bounds on quantum Fisher information matrix caused by mean Uhlmann curvature, which in pure states become geometric bounds on quantum metric caused by Berry curvature. Our formalism reveals optical sum rules for velocity variance and spread of valence band Wannier functions, and how they are bounded by the Berry curvature and commutator of velocity operators. Canonical ensembles of spins, topological materials, common semiconductors, and transition metal dichalcogenides are used to verify these geometric bounds and uncertainty relations.

papers.title: Finiteness properties of Bestvina-Brady kernels for graph products with torsion
papers.abstract: We study Bestvina-Brady kernels associated to graph products whose vertex groups are either infinite cyclic or finite. Using a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ cubical complex constructed by Ruane and Witzel, on which the graph product with defining graph $Γ$ acts, together with an equivariant Morse function, we establish sufficient conditions for homological finiteness properties in terms of the topology of the flag complex $Γ^\blacktriangle$, the subcomplex $Γ^\blacktriangle_\infty$ spanned by the infinite vertices, and the ascending and descending links of certain vertices. We also prove a partial converse, showing that, under additional vanishing hypotheses on homology in the next degree, non-vanishing homology of these complexes obstructs higher finiteness properties of the Bestvina-Brady kernel. The main new features are the presence of finite stabilizers and the resulting additional link conditions, which are expressed in terms of the flag complex of $Γ$. When the finite vertex groups are abelian, we characterize when the kernel has finitely many conjugacy classes of finite subgroups, describe the normalizers of its finite subgroups as Bestvina-Brady kernels of smaller graph products, and obtain a criterion for the kernel to be of Bredon type $\underline{\mathrm{FP}}_n$.

papers.title: Towards Unified File Management for Data Lakehouse Systems
papers.abstract: Data lakehouse systems have garnered widespread adoption, yet their metadata management systems face a fundamental architectural dilemma. File-based OTFs (Open Table Formats) scale well, but suffer from metadata bloat, high commit latencies, the absence of multi-table transactions, and unsafe garbage collection. On the other hand, catalogs relying entirely on a transactional database incur severe scalability bottlenecks due to analytic file-level metadata. To reconcile this tension, we present Raven, an operational catalog that stores transactional metadata within a database while offloading analytical metadata to underlying OTF structures. Based on this hybrid architecture, Raven introduces an extended Merge-on-Read (MoR) mechanism to reduce commit latency and mitigate metadata bloat, alongside multi-table transactions under snapshot isolation. Furthermore, Raven unifies core data lakehouse semantics including versioning and reference tracking under an extensible ER (Entity-Relationship) metadata model, enabling safe global garbage collection across diverse types of assets. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that Raven substantially reduces commit latency and metadata bloat when integrated with Apache Iceberg and Delta Lake, maintains a catalog storage footprint orders of magnitude smaller than database-only systems like DuckLake, and achieves scalable garbage collection with minimal disruption.

papers.title: Video-Action Models for Data-Efficient Industrial Manipulation
papers.abstract: Industrial manipulation requires precise alignment and controlled handling of rigid, deformable, and flexible components. Yet, the benefits of pretrained visuomotor policies remain underexplored in settings where limited access to specialized hardware, components, and fixtures constrains demonstration collection and evaluation. Understanding task-specific data requirements is important for assessing their scalability across diverse processes on the factory floor. We investigate whether video pretraining can support reliable industrial manipulation with limited action data. We propose FLUX-mimic, a video-action model, motivated by the potential of video pretraining to capture motion and interaction patterns that enable sample-efficient training. FLUX-mimic is built on a backbone pretrained on large-scale web and industrial task data, and an action expert to generate robot trajectories. We train our policy by joint video-action training. Across four automotive manufacturing benchmark tasks and two bimanual robot platforms, FLUX-mimic outperforms all considered baselines on the dexterous robot platform and matches pi_{0.5}'s average success rate on the gripper-based robot platform. On a deformable part kitting task, FLUX-mimic reaches 77.5% success with as little as two hours of task-specific action-labeled demonstrations.

papers.title: Observation of the $η$ $\to$ $μ^+μ^-π^+π^-$ decay and an improved measurement of the $η$ $\to$ $μ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$ branching fraction
papers.abstract: An observation of the rare decay $η$ $\to$ $μ^+μ^-π^+π^-$ is reported from proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13.6 TeV, collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC in 2022 and 2023, and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.6 fb$^{-1}$. In addition, the branching fraction ratio of $η$ $\to$ $μ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$ relative to $η$ $\to$ $μ^+μ^-$ is measured with a precision improved by 44% compared with the previous measurement. The measured branching fraction ratios are $\mathcal{B}(η\toμ^+μ^-π^+π^-)/\mathcal{B}(η\toμ^+μ^-)$ = [2.89 $\pm$ 0.48 (stat) $^{+0.42}_{-0.29}$ (syst)]$\times$ 10$^{-3}$ and $\mathcal{B}(η\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-)/\mathcal{B}(η\toμ^+μ^-)$ = [0.86 $\pm$ 0.06 (stat) $^{+0.09}_{-0.08}$ (syst)]$\times$10$^{-3}$.

papers.title: Pointwise Convergence and Approximation of Matrix-Transform Means of Vilenkin--Fourier Series
papers.abstract: We study convergence, divergence, and approximation of matrix-transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series. For bounded groups, we prove convergence along ${M_n}$ at Vilenkin--Lebesgue points without additional diagonal conditions. For arbitrary bounded or unbounded groups, every regular matrix-transform method admits divergence on any prescribed null set along any increasing sequence. We also obtain $L_p(G_m)$ approximation estimates in terms of the modulus of continuity.

papers.title: Better Boundary Prediction Does Not Guarantee Better Structural Representation
papers.abstract: Punctuation marks often mark phrase boundaries, carrying linguistic information. Therefore, punctuation marks' abundance and feasibility as proxies of linguistic structure has led to suggestions that using punctuation marks to optimise on phrasal structure may help language models (LMs) improve their representations of argument, semantic, and syntactic structures. In this paper, we test the above claim in English across three primary LM architectures: decoder-only, encoder-only, and encoder-decoder LMs, by complementing traditional token prediction with punctuation restoration (PR). Our evidence, collected at the <1B parameter scale, suggests that optimising for boundary prediction does not necessarily guarantee higher-quality structural representation in decoder-only, encoder-decoder, and encoder-only LMs, failing to improve performance on downstream tasks that require understanding structure in linguistic input.

papers.title: $L^p$ Integrability and Spectral Complexity of Manifolds with Higher Codimension
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between the $L^p$ integrability of functions and the curvature geometry of their Fourier support. We prove that if $M\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a $C^n$ manifold of dimension $d$ and $n>2d$, then every $u\in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\widehat u\subseteq M$ vanishes whenever \[ 2\le p\le\frac{6n-4}{3d-1}. \] This strictly improves the classical threshold $2n/d$ throughout the range $n>2d$. More generally, we obtain a family of dimension-dependent improvements in higher codimension. As a consequence, we obtain a strict quantitative improvement in the necessary conditions for Fourier restriction when $n>2d$, resolving a conjecture of Mockenhaupt \cite{Mockenhaupt96}. This further establishes the nonexistence of quadratic manifolds satisfying the Christ--Mockenhaupt condition when $n>2d$. For quadratic manifolds, we obtain spectral synthesis bounds from joint sublevel estimates for the eigenvalues of the normal Hessian pencil. In codimension two, we determine the exact critical exponent from the ranks and eigenvalue vanishing orders, including nonexistence at the critical endpoint. We also obtain integrability bounds for manifolds with constant relative nullity, extending Guo's hypersurface results \cite{Guo93} to higher codimension. Finally, we use the Fourier ratio as a measure of the geometric complexity of individual strata of the characteristic set to establish $L^p$ uniqueness criteria for homogeneous constant-coefficient PDEs.

papers.title: A New High $γ$-$γ'$ Fraction Polycrystalline Co/Ni Superalloy
papers.abstract: An ingot-processable Co/Ni-based $γ/γ'$ superalloy has been developed for wrought parts in aircraft engines. An 8.5 kg VIM ingot was homogenised and hot rolled to a true strain of 1. A heat treatment was then developed to produce 50% $γ'$ and a grain size of 142 $μ$m. High-temperature tensile testing showed yield strengths of 820 MPa at 700 $^\circ$C, 785 MPa at 800 $^\circ$C and 783 MPa at 850 $^\circ$C. Creep tests at 750 $^\circ$C/600 MPa and 800 $^\circ$C/300 MPa demonstrated reduced minimum creep rates and extended rupture lives relative to current wrought Ni-base alloys. Oxidation at 800 $^\circ$C for 100 h formed a 1 $μ$m dual chromia/alumina scale with minimal subsurface degradation. Long-term exposure at 800 $^\circ$C for 8000 h showed limited $γ'$ coarsening and no deleterious intermetallic or grain boundary phases. The alloy therefore offers a promising balance of processability, strength and oxidation resistance for high-temperature static and rotating components.or grain boundary phases. The alloy therefore offers a promising balance of processability, strength and oxidation resistance for high-temperature static and rotating components.

papers.title: DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces
papers.abstract: Learning from paired modalities is commonly equated with aligning them: two encoders are trained until the embeddings of a pair coincide in a shared space. We study whether cross-modal retrieval and classification can instead be obtained while the two encoders' own embedding spaces remain directly unaligned. DuoJEPA trains one encoder per modality with the self-supervised LeJEPA objective and appends to each encoder a single transformer layer that translates its embedding into the other encoder's space, supervised by a contrastive objective computed entirely within that target space. No loss term compares the two own spaces directly, although the encoders are optimised jointly through the translation objective. In our experiments, the translator's residual connections determine where the cross-modal pressure is absorbed: with a residual translator the two encoders become directly aligned, whereas with a skipless (residual-free) translator a paired-cosine test detects no alignment in the final models, and at most a weak one in the ablations, at comparable cross-modal performance. The learned class-token translation is well approximated by a single scaled rotation of the source space. We evaluate DuoJEPA on two modality pairs that differ in nearly every respect. On chest radiographs and reports from CheXpert Plus, it attains a zero-shot AUC of 86.6 and a cross-modal retrieval score of 78.5, compared with 60.0 and 64.2 for our reimplementation of LeVLJEPA with the same encoders and data. On Sentinel-2 optical and Sentinel-1 radar imagery, the frozen encoders fall within the range of published Sentinel foundation models under our reproduction of the Copernicus-Bench linear-probe protocol, the translator retrieves the paired image of the other sensor among 4,000 candidates in 77-79% of cases, and a patch-level extension transfers the within-image similarity structure of the scene.

papers.title: Comprehensive quantum electrodynamics of fast electrons interacting with dissipative nanostructures and quantum light
papers.abstract: Theoretical descriptions of the quantum electrodynamical interaction between fast electrons and nanostructures conventionally rely on standard macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (MQED), which, when applied to bounded objects in vacuum, formally requires an asymptotic limiting procedure to account for free-space radiation modes. To explicitly incorporate these modes from the outset, we employ the modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF), which independently quantizes both the asymptotic scattering modes and the electromagnetic field generated by dissipative material sources. Utilizing an exact second-order Magnus expansion, we derive a closed-form, nonperturbative master formula for the transverse-momentum-resolved energy exchange probability. In the unilluminated regime, we demonstrate that at finite nanostructure temperatures, the vacuum scattering and thermal material fluctuations do not mathematically recombine into the total imaginary part of the dyadic Green's function. This breakdown does not violate the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem, because the explicit zero-temperature scattering field acts as an independent dynamical system that maintains the configuration out of global thermodynamic equilibrium. This fundamental separation reveals an intrinsic Stokes--Anti-Stokes asymmetry, yielding distinct transverse diffraction patterns for energy loss and thermal energy gain, and establishing a generalized detailed-balance relation that governs the radiative reduction of the apparent temperature in nanoscale electron thermometry. In the illuminated regime, our framework rigorously incorporates quantum-optical states into macroscopic dissipative electrodynamics, demonstrating that...

papers.title: Subject-Held-Out Evaluation of Deep Ground Reaction Force Estimators Across Two Laboratories: Leakage and Cross-Laboratory Transfer
papers.abstract: Deep networks that estimate ground reaction forces and centers of pressure from motion-capture markers are validated within one laboratory, in a seldom-stated coordinate frame, and sometimes with trial-level splits that put the same person in the training and the test set. We measured what each practice costs, and whether such models transfer between laboratories. Three sequence models (convolutional, convolutional-recurrent, and convolutional-transformer) were evaluated on two independent datasets, locomotion (6 subjects) and occupational patient handling (10 subjects), under one pipeline, one tuning procedure, three seeds, and four protocols: trial-level split, leave-one-subject-out, pooled two-laboratory training with matched held-out subjects, and cross-laboratory transfer. At a fixed configuration, trial-level splits overstated the subject-held-out coefficient of determination by +0.040 to +0.194; on occupational data the overstatement exceeded every difference between architectures. With subjects held out, the three models reached values between 0.583 and 0.804; the leader differed between datasets, and gaps lay within subject-to-subject variability. Pooling the laboratories changed neither dataset on matched subjects. Transfer between laboratories was below chance in both directions, including the vertical force, which no in-plane rotation can affect. Leaving force targets in the plate frame while inputs were heading-aligned cost 0.57 of locomotion anteroposterior-force explained variance, enough to make that force look hardest; a Newton's-law correlation detected the mismatch before training. Split protocol and target frame changed reported accuracy more than architecture did. Learned force estimators should be validated with subjects held out, checked for frame consistency before training, and tested across laboratories before deployment claims are made.

papers.title: PhysICL: In-Context Learning of Physical Fields on Unstructured Meshes from Procedural Priors
papers.abstract: Engineering design studies produce a few tens to a few hundred simulations of one problem, each on its own mesh, and their surrogates are retrained for every study. Tabular foundation models instead infer a new task from its examples in one forward pass, after pretraining on synthetic tasks. We demonstrate the feasibility of in-context learning for physical field prediction on unstructured meshes. A single model, PhysICL, pretrained solely on procedural tasks, predicts fields, with quantiles, directly on each query mesh from labeled simulations, without updating its weights. The same checkpoint accepts variable numbers of context examples, scalar inputs and input fields, and any number of output fields, while mesh size and connectivity can vary within a task. Its procedural prior draws generic laws and boundary-element physical models on morphed 2D and 3D template meshes, evaluated only at the points the model samples, fast enough that tasks generated on the fly by CPU workers keep the GPUs busy throughout pretraining. On five PLAID datasets never seen in pretraining, its field error decreases as the context grows and, from $K = 32$, is below that of the nearest context simulation on every dataset and context draw. It is on par with per-dataset reduced-order models on two of them, behind them where the fields are low-rank. On AhmedML surfaces with a median of 1.1 million nodes, twenty times the largest pretraining mesh, its fixed spatial budgets keep the peak GPU memory at $K = 64$ at 4.27 GiB, against 4.07 GiB on the 6,000-node meshes of 2D\_MSHE. Finally, on 2D\_MSHE, far from the prior, fine-tuning on procedural tasks that reproduce its geometry and loads, without any of its outputs, at a tenth of the pretraining cost, divides the stress error by 2.7.

papers.title: COMBS: Concealed Object Multi-modal Bayesian Search
papers.abstract: This work addresses the problem of finding a concealed object in an environment by unifying formalisms for partially observable environments with multi-modal priors drawn from a mix of ontologies, semantic networks, LLMs, and VLMs. We propose a concealment-adaptive mixed-observability MDP (CA-MOMDP), a Bayes-adaptive setting where uncertainty is over both object locations and which nodes can conceal them, held as a hypothesis with a bounded ontology prior and resolved only by interaction. We define a hierarchical transition system (HTS) to abstract the environment into room and object nodes that can be planned over via our CA-MOMDP. We further propose a COMBS-score: a multi-modal fusion of a human informed semantic network, LLM, and VLM, to initialize the belief over object locations, which grounds our abstractions and reduces reliance on a single model. Belief is maintained via Bayes' rule, which never lets a look rule out a closed container. We prove a present target is found in a bounded number of searches under exact perception and that its location is never ruled out given missed detection under noisy perception. We ablate each component to demonstrate their significance. Across five simulator configurations, from a gridworld to Matterport3D with a real detector, COMBS finds 92-100% of in-distribution and 92-100% of out-of-distribution targets, matches or beats the baselines in processing speed, significantly outperforms a per-step LLM policy at lower cost on the larger scenes, recovers more out-of-distribution placements than a TidyBot ranking, and matches an LLM-only prior at a fraction of its per-decision latency. COMBS is the only standalone method that can declare a target absent at a stated error level, and the per-step LLM policy offered a termination action abandons 12-22% of targets that were present, against 1.6-3.2% for COMBS on the same episodes.

papers.title: WELP : Weighted Ensemble in the LooP for committor learning
papers.abstract: Understanding how complex molecular systems transition between metastable states is a central challenge in computational chemistry and biophysics. A key tool for characterizing these transitions is the committor function: the probability that a trajectory initiated from a given configuration reaches one state before another. Because the committor encodes both the progress and the mechanism of a transition, it is an ideal collective variable (CV). Learning it, however, requires sampling the rare transitions it describes. We address this circular dependency with a ``WE-in-the-loop'' framework that couples committor learning with weighted ensemble (WE), an enhanced sampling method that uses a CV to drive transition dynamics. Our framework alternates between the two: WE simulation generates transition data for training a neural network committor with a self-consistent loss, and the learned committor then serves as an improved CV for subsequent WE simulation. Across a two-channel 2D system, alanine dipeptide, and chignolin, our framework consistently outperforms greedy baselines, highlighting the importance of principled exploration. We also curate a public benchmark of empirically determined committor values for alanine dipeptide. Together, the framework and benchmark provide a new method for studying rare transitions in high-dimensional molecular systems and a standard for evaluating committor learning methods.

papers.title: Affine Springer Fibers and Slodowy varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the geometry of certain affine Springer fibers. In particular, we generalize the construction of Lusztig in "Remarks on affine Springer fibres" to identify a locally closed subvariety in terms of some Lagrangian in the resolution of the nilpotent Slodowy slice. We use this description to prove some geometric properties of these affine Springer fibers, including existence of affine pavings and equidimensionality of affine Spaltenstein varieties.

papers.title: Is Spoken Hungarian Low-resource?: A Quantitative Survey of Hungarian Speech Data Sets
papers.abstract: Even though various speech data sets are available in Hungarian, there is a lack of a general overview about their types and sizes. To fill in this gap, we provide a survey of available data sets in spoken Hungarian in five categories (e.g., monolingual, Hungarian part of multilingual, pathological, child-related and dialectal collections). In total, the estimated size of available data is about 2800 hours (across 7500 speakers) and it represents a rich spoken language diversity. However, the distribution of the data and its alignment to real-life (e.g. speech recognition) tasks is far from optimal indicating the need for additional larger-scale natural language speech data sets. Our survey presents an overview of available data sets for Hungarian explaining their strengths and weaknesses which is useful for researchers working on Hungarian across disciplines. In addition, our survey serves as a starting point towards a unified foundational speech model specific to Hungarian.

papers.title: A pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot--Poisson--Nernst--Planck system
papers.abstract: We develop a pseudostress-based fully mixed finite element method for the stationary Biot-Poisson-Nernst-Planck system describing ionic transport in a charged, saturated, and deformable porous medium. The mechanical equations are reformulated in terms of a non-symmetric pseudostress and the solid displacement, while mixed formulations are retained for the Darcy, electrostatic, and ionic equations. The nonlinear electrostatic and advective couplings are treated in a Banach space setting. The formulation provides direct approximations of the pseudostress, fluxes, and concentration gradients, and permits algebraic reconstruction of the displacement gradient and Cauchy stress. Under block-stability and small-data assumptions, we establish continuous and discrete well-posedness, with poroelastic stability bounds uniform with respect to the first Lame parameter. A conforming Raviart-Thomas discretization, completed by discontinuous polynomials, yields a priori error estimates and convergence rates. For the coupled scheme in two dimensions, we construct a residual-based a posteriori error estimator and establish its reliability under an additional smallness condition on the prescribed data. Local efficiency is proved for polynomial boundary data, with boundary-data oscillation included for general traces. We also describe the estimator modifications for nonhomogeneous displacement and normal-flux data under corresponding stability and solvability hypotheses. Numerical experiments examine convergence of the mixed and reconstructed fields, robustness in the nearly incompressible regime, adaptive refinement, and ionic polarization in a charged porous medium.

papers.title: OGLE Pre-discovery Observations of the Dwarf Planet Candidate 2026 ED138
papers.abstract: The newly discovered trans-Neptunian object, 2026 ED138, is a strong dwarf planet candidate detected by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Despite its high intrinsic brightness, it evaded detection by previous sky surveys as it hid near crowded Galactic disk fields. Here, we present an analysis of precovery observations of 2026 ED138 in archival data from the Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment (OGLE). We identify 102 reliable detections of the object as it moved across the dense regions of the Galactic plane and bulge between 2011 and 2024. We provide precise astrometric and photometric measurements of the object. Modeling its phase curve yields absolute magnitudes of H_I = 2.224 +/- 0.034 mag and H_V = 3.154 +/- 0.035 mag. Period analysis of the phase-angle-corrected light curve reveals a candidate rotation period of 1.18077 days and its 1-day alias 0.54066 days, although a low signal-to-noise ratio renders these periodicities tentative.

papers.title: DUFT: Device-Unique Feedback Traversal for Entropy-Estimated Response Extraction and Mutual Authentication using SRAM PUFs
papers.abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) are a promising technology in the realm of random number generation for key generation, but for PUF-based authentication, they have been sidelined due to their limited challenge space as a reservoir of Challenge-Response Pairs (CRPs). In this paper, we develop a seed-based, round-iterated feedback mechanism, which we name Device-Unique Feedback Traversal (DUFT). The feedback chain is driven by the device's unstable and stable bit positions in its stability mask against the address to create a unique traversal. Additionally, a device-key hashed from the unique SRAM-PUF array is also included in calculating the next round of the chain to keep it secret. By estimating the physical SRAM source's entropy and error rate empirically, or by having a source with established metrics in both, DUFT estimates the number of rounds of feedback in the traversal to be performed to achieve a certain amount of min-entropy. We reach 128 bits of estimated min-entropy on our reference hardware under stated assumptions and experimental estimates. The number of rounds in the traversal scales directly with measured source-entropy, allowing security to be increased for weaker sources at the cost of running time. Using this feedback-traversal wrapper over SRAM-PUFs to obtain a measured-response, we propose an extremely lightweight authentication and key-encapsulation protocol for resource-constrained embedded devices. We realize and evaluate DUFT end-to-end on physical IoT/embedded hardware: a discrete-SRAM node pair running the complete mechanism and end-to-end protocol, and an embedded-SRAM microcontroller for the mechanism alone.

papers.title: The Curious Case of Anapole Dark Matter at LZ: Minimal, Elastic and Testable
papers.abstract: Majorana fermions can carry neither charge nor dipole moments, leaving the anapole moment as their leading electromagnetic interaction. A stable Majorana fermion is therefore a minimal realization of electromagnetically interacting dark matter. The momentum dependence of the anapole interaction produces a harder recoil spectrum than standard momentum-independent interactions. We show that this makes elastically scattering anapole dark matter a viable interpretation of the single high-energy nuclear-recoil event recorded by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, in a region where almost no background is expected.
