While large deviations for stochastic nematic liquid crystal models have been studied earlier, the central limit and moderate deviation regimes have not been considered. We first prove a central limit theorem in the natural energy space and show that the rescaled fluctuations converge, in every $L^p$-norm and with rate $\sqrt{\eps}$, to the solution of a linear stochastic system. The limiting process is centred Gaussian. We then establish a moderate deviation principle with a quadratic rate function determined by the corresponding linearised skeleton equation, which coincides with the Cameron--Martin form of the Gaussian limit. We also show that the moderate deviation principle holds uniformly over bounded sets of initial data. The main arguments use a cancellation between the coupling terms, a one-sided estimate for the polynomial potential, and energy estimates with deterministic Gronwall coefficients, thereby avoiding exponential moment estimates.

papers.title: Semi-log canonical minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of certain steps of the minimal model program for projective morphisms between complex analytic spaces in the semi-log canonical case, generalizing results of Ambro and Kollár. This is obtained by providing a sufficient criterion for the finite generation of the relative log canonical algebra. As a consequence, we prove demi-normal analogues of results of Hacon--Xu and Birkar. As a further application, we derive the existence of crepant semi-dlt modifications of analytic slc pairs whose irreducible components are normal in codimension 1, extending a result of Hashizume. The methods are new even in the algebraic case, providing streamlined proofs of the algebraic counterparts to the statements proved in this work, without relying on Kollár's gluing techniques.

papers.title: Superradiant photon bunching in nanolasers: from a polarization-order hierarchy of the master equation to Dicke Markov chains
papers.abstract: In nanolasers, a few to a few hundred quantum emitters share a single mode of light. Coupled identically to the mode, the emitters do not radiate independently but form collective bright and dark states, producing superradiant bursts and strongly bunched photon statistics below the laser threshold. We investigate to what extent this behavior can be understood as random jumps between collective Dicke states. From the laser master equation, we derive a hierarchy of models defined by the polarization order, i.e., the number of photons involved in the coherence between the emitters and the light, and include the coherence to various orders. With all of the coherences eliminated, we obtain a Dicke Markov chain, a stochastic jump process over the photon number and the Dicke states, in which collective effects enter only through enhanced or suppressed transition rates. It predicts superthermal bunching and a strong even--odd dependence on the emitter number. It recovers about 80\% of the bunching in the most coherent regime, where conventional rate equations predict no superthermal bunching. Keeping the first polarization order, i.e., the optical polarization, and eliminating the second order, i.e., the two-photon coherences, yields a population-polarization model, which recovers the bunching of the full master equation almost perfectly. This hierarchy of polarization orders is an alternative to the cumulant expansion and, unlike it, recovers the master equation at the highest order. As a numerically exact reference, a symmetry-reduced master equation extends the simulation range all the way to 34 (24) emitters below (above) threshold. The Dicke Markov chain can be solved directly for hundreds of emitters and sampled for thousands of emitters, further extending the range of numerical methods. We compare the numerical performance of the methods in detail to guide the choice of technique.

papers.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward heavy-flavor correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
papers.abstract: We investigate heavy-flavor azimuthal correlations as probes of gluon saturation in high-energy $p$+$p$ and $p$+Pb collisions within the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. Heavy flavor has several advantages: heavy-quark production is especially sensitive to the small-$x$ gluon distribution of the target, while the quark mass suppresses collinear radiation. Further, the heavy meson carries a large fraction of the momentum of its parent quark, so that the meson pair follows the partonic kinematics more closely than for light hadrons. We present the first calculation of heavy-meson pair correlations over the full azimuthal range that combines small-$x$ evolution from an initial condition constrained by HERA data with Sudakov resummation near the back-to-back limit. It provides a good description of the $D$-$\bar D$ and $b$-hadron pair correlations measured by LHCb. In contrast to the light-flavor case, we predict, in addition to a suppression of the away-side yield in $p$+Pb relative to $p$+$p$ collisions by about $15\%$, a broadening of the peak by approximately $10\%$ to $25\%$ for Gaussian fits near $ΔΦ=π$, which makes heavy-flavor correlations a promising observable in the search for gluon saturation.

papers.title: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
papers.abstract: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model provides an analytically controlled setting for strongly interacting quantum dynamics and holography, but its fermionic formulation leads to nonlocal encoding overheads on qubit-based quantum processors. We study a U(1)-symmetric spin analogue of the complex SYK model, constructed from random charge-conserving $q$-spin interactions that are native to a qubit Hilbert space. In the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, the model reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK under the identification of chemical potential with magnetic field and charge density with magnetization. We investigate the finite-$N$, finite-$q$ regime using exact diagonalization. A U(1)-invariant ordering susceptibility increases with system size for $q = 2, 4$ but decreases for $q = 6$, while bulk-spectrum level statistics are consistent with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble at half filling and the Gaussian unitary ensemble in the adjacent magnetization sector. We further construct coupled-cluster chains and obtain domain-wall dynamics consistent with diffusive magnetization transport in a small-cluster regime accessible to matrix-product-state simulations. These results establish analytical benchmarks and finite-size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos, and magnetization transport in U(1)-symmetric spin-SYK models, and they motivate quantum simulation of the low-temperature, large-system regime, which remains difficult for classical methods.

papers.title: Your Hypergradient is Skewed: Antithetic Neumann Estimation for Bilevel Optimization
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization is a core tool in practical machine learning workflows, including hyperparameter tuning, data reweighting, robust learning, reinforcement learning, and imbalanced classification. Hypergradient computation requires the inverse of the inner Hessian, typically estimated via a truncated Neumann series. While existing analyses focus on bias and variance, we show that the product structure of the Neumann series introduces a third source of error: skewness. We identify that, unlike ordinary gradients, whose asymmetry is suppressed by mini-batch averaging, the Neumann estimator amplifies skewness across factors, with the third-moment error growing, under weak contraction, with truncation depth, inner condition number, and per-factor noise asymmetry. This arises in many practical settings such as corrupted labels, outliers, heterogeneous or class-imbalanced datasets. To address this, we introduce the Antithetic Neumann Estimator (ANE), which pairs each Hessian sample with a mirrored counterpart around a reference Hessian and averages the resulting inverse-Hessian estimates. With an exact reference, the antithetic product retains only even-order noise, eliminating all odd-order perturbation terms; with an approximate reference, the residual odd-order contribution is bounded linearly in the reference error. ANE requires only a modification of the Hessian vector step and combines with existing stochastic or variance-reduced bilevel methods. We instantiate ANE-SGD and ANE-VR, the latter adding recursive variance reduction. Across robust regression, data cleaning, offline reinforcement learning, and imbalanced classification, ANE-based methods improve on stochastic and variance-reduced baselines on every task (20 seeds each), lowering loss by 4 to 25% relative to the best baseline; the largest gains, on robust regression, are a 25% lower test loss and a 54% higher test r-squared.

papers.title: Strangeness in the Chiral Mean Field model phase diagram
papers.abstract: We explore the phase diagram of the Chiral Mean Field model in the space of temperature and baryon, charge, and strangeness chemical potentials, focusing on the role of the strangeness direction. At low density, a negative $μ_S$ leads to finite strangeness in the nuclear liquid--gas transition and rotates the order parameter away from the purely baryonic direction. The critical mode remains baryon dominated over the $μ_S$ range considered, while the critical locus develops a strong parametrization dependence once multistrange baryons appear. At higher density, a separate first-order transition toward strangeness-rich hadronic matter appears only for one of the two parametrizations considered, emphasizing its interaction dependence. The high density transition reorganizes octet-dominated matter into decuplet-dominated matter: $Δ$ baryons provide most of the baryon-density discontinuity, while $Ξ^*(1530)$ baryons provide the largest contribution to the strangeness-density discontinuity. Its order parameter is dominated by the strangeness density, and its normalized direction in the $BQS$ space changes little with temperature even as the discontinuity vanishes at the critical point. The critical baryon chemical potential changes by almost $1$~GeV over $μ_S\in [-300, 300]$~MeV. We characterize both transitions using the fixed-temperature $BQS$ susceptibility matrix, the density discontinuity between the coexisting phases, and a generalized Clausius--Clapeyron relation. This work also accompanies the release of \cmfpp{} \texttt{v2.0.0} as part of the MUSES framework. The extension of the initial release includes, among other features, finite-temperature thermodynamics, new interactions and parametrizations, and susceptibility calculations based on a Jacobian method.

papers.title: Chains of Vector-like Leptons at Colliders
papers.abstract: Vector-like leptons (VLLs) are predicted in the chain flavor models, which possess characteristic features to explain the mass hierarchy and mixing of the fermions in the Standard Model (SM). We investigate the production and decay of the VLL chains and quantify the discovery potential at the LHC, FCC-hh, and lepton colliders. The resonant mass sets the new physics scale responsible for the fermion mass generation. The observation of the VLL multiplets associated with each lepton flavor yields the chain structure. The mass difference among the VLL multiplets determines the hopping parameter that gives the power-law pattern for the observed SM fermion masses. The single VLL production via vector boson-lepton fusion directly measures the partial width, equivalently the new Yukawa coupling and the VLL mass hopping parameter. At hadron colliders, the leading production mechanism is pair production via their gauge interaction. We find that HL-LHC may have the sensitivity to reach the chain scale of $800-900\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and FCC-hh reaches $>2.5\,\mathrm{TeV}$. In $e^+e^-$ and $μ^+μ^-$ colliders, VLL pair production is a clear discovery channel once the threshold is reached. Single production via $Z$-lepton fusion becomes more accessible owing to a lower mass threshold and extends signal discovery to the collider kinematic limit.

papers.title: New line-driven mass-loss rate predictions for central stars of planetary nebulae: Luminosity dependence when approaching the Eddington limit
papers.abstract: After expelling most of their envelopes, asymptotic giant branch stars turn bluewards in the Hertzsprung-Russel diagram and become hot objects. These objects ionise the surrounding material, possibly creating a planetary nebula. Because they are hot and rather luminous, they are able to launch a line-driven wind. The luminosity dependence of these winds has not yet been studied in detail using global wind models that consistently consider the interaction of the photosphere and the wind. We provide line-driven wind models of the central stars of planetary nebulae focusing on the dependence of these winds on luminosity. While the mass-loss rate is strongly sensitive to stellar luminosity, the terminal velocity increases with effective temperature and only weakly depends on luminosity. The predicted values agree reasonably well with observations, except that observational mass-loss rates show a rather large scatter, and the predicted terminal velocities are slightly lower than observational values. We provide ionising fluxes and show that for stars cooler than approximately 40 kK, the ionising fluxes computed from plane-parallel models are inadequate. The wind efficiency stays rather weak, which implies that the Wolf-Rayet type of central stars is connected with objects with an elevated mass fraction of heavy elements.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). NISP spectroscopy of gravitational arcs and multiple images
papers.abstract: Applications of strong gravitational lensing in astrophysics and cosmology critically depend on building reliable strong lensing models, which require accurate measurements of on-sky positions of multiple images and of the redshifts of the background sources from which they originate. In this context, Euclid is a unique facility, as it simultaneously provides high-resolution multi-band photometric imaging and slitless spectroscopy for an unprecedentedly large sample of gravitational lenses, most of which are newly discovered. In this work, we exploit Euclid slitless spectroscopic data to determine the redshifts of four spatially extended lensed sources, and to reconstruct emission-line images. Specifically, two of the target sources are lensed into giant arcs by the massive galaxy clusters SPT-CLJ0411$-$4819 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.424$, where "d" denotes the lensing deflector) and Abell 2280 ($z_\mathrm{d}=0.326$). The third system is a quadruply imaged active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidate strongly lensed by a massive galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.68$, while the fourth is a galaxy-scale Einstein ring produced by a lens galaxy at $z_\mathrm{d}=0.235$. This work represents a proof of concept for the exploitation of Euclid slitless spectroscopic data in the study of strong gravitational lensing, providing one of the first determinations of spectroscopic redshifts for strongly lensed features from NISP spectra. These results demonstrate the feasibility of applying the same methodology to the very large sample of gravitational lenses that Euclid has started to discover and is expected to identify over the course of the mission.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): VIS processing and data products
papers.abstract: This paper describes the characteristics of the Euclid visible imager (VIS) data delivered as part of the Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). This data set contains 42092 calibrated frames. Validated nominal exposures cover 2092 deg$^2$ of sky. We outline the minor changes made to the VIS processing function (PF) since previous releases. For the wide survey, the photometric and astrometric accuracy of the reference stellar sample $(18.5 < I_{\rm E} < 19.8)$ is excellent. The internal and external astrometric dispersions are 0.08 and 0.18 mas, respectively, at the quadrant level, and 3.4 and 5.6 mas at the source level. The corresponding internal and external photometric dispersions are 0.76 and 1.4 mmag at the quadrant level, and 11 and 25 mmag at the source level. We characterise remaining astrometric and photometric systematic effects: focal-plane-dependent variations; time-dependent photometric offsets; and colour-dependent centroid shifts. The noise floor in the deepest VIS images appears to be set by the extended diffuse light of faint galaxies. Globally, the DR1 VIS data meet pre-launch mission requirements and the 42092 images it contains provide our first substantial look at the sky as seen by VIS.

papers.title: Gray-body factors: Method matters II, WKB vs GrayHawk
papers.abstract: We present a systematic comparison between two independent approaches for the computation of gray-body factors. A fully numerical integration of the radial scattering equation, as implemented in GrayHawk, and one based on the WKB approximation. We consider four black hole geometries and scalar, fermionic, and vector perturbations, comparing the corresponding gray-body factors, primary Hawking emission spectra, and Page evaporation factors. As expected for high-frequency and large $l$ regimes, the two methods provide excellent agreement. At low frequencies, however, systematic discrepancies emerge and become particularly pronounced for nearly-extremal black holes. Systematic discrepancies are also met when considering effective geometric potentials characterized by the presence of more than one peak. A significant difference between the two approaches is also found in their computational cost, highlighting their complementary nature.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) C: Lens modelling pipeline overview
papers.abstract: Galaxy-scale strong lenses provide precise measurements of galaxy mass distributions, magnified views of distant galaxies, and a competitive cosmological probe. Historically, such studies have been limited to hundreds of lenses, with automated modelling methods proving difficult to scale. We present automated lens modelling of 15 072 strong-lens candidates from Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), over an order of magnitude larger than any previously modelled sample. Using PyAutoLens-JAX, we perform three fits with multi-Gaussian expansion (MGE), pixelised, and Sérsic representations of the source, adopting an isothermal ellipsoid mass model with external shear. These fits provide foreground lens-light subtraction, adaptive Delaunay source reconstructions, and deblended photometry. More than 20 expert inspectors visually assess the resulting models, and each model is assigned the classification on which at least 75% of its inspectors agree. Of the 6073 grade A (secure) lens candidates, inspectors classify 4098 (67.5%) as successfully modelled, 580 (9.6%) as failures, 317 (5.2%) as multi-galaxy lenses, 15 (0.2%) as double-source-plane lenses, and 7 (0.1%) as unsure if lens, while 1032 (17.0%) reach no consensus and 24 (0.4%) have incomplete models. For the 8999 grade B (probable) candidates, the modelling success rate falls to 43.1%, primarily reflecting an increase in cases without consensus (37.6%), rather than a comparable increase in agreed failures (12.9%). Successfully modelled grade A and B systems have a median effective Einstein radius of 0.85 arcsec and a median total $I_E$-band source magnification of 8.1. We publicly release the successful lens models, their inferred properties, and magnified-source reconstructions through the ECLIPSE catalogue, demonstrating automated modelling at Euclid sample sizes and enabling population-level strong-lensing science.

papers.title: Subsystem Flow: Quantum Error Correction, Petz Recovery, and Ergodic Inclusions
papers.abstract: In quantum error correction (QEC), the goal is to engineer an encoding that protects logical information against the erasure of a physical subsystem. In local many-body quantum systems, by contrast, nature provides a subsystem inclusion $\mN\subset \mM$ in a fixed reference state $\ketΩ$. Asking whether the inclusion admits a reference-preserving code that protects subsystem $\mN$ against erasure of the complement is equivalent to asking whether $\mN$ is preserved under the modular dynamics of $\mM$ in this state (modular autonomy). We define the subsystem flow, which measures the departure from this error correction regime. Away from autonomy, the infinitesimal flow quantifies relative-entropy loss, while the history algebra and persistent core describe which observables the modular orbit generates and retains. We call an inclusion ergodic when modular orbits generate everything and retain nothing. Analytic continuation of subsystem flow yields Petz recovery maps and a family of positive inclusion parent Hamiltonians. We show that, in general, evolving with these parent Hamiltonians allows $\mN$ to leave $\mM$, and in some cases, it can generate the entire $\mM\vee\mM'$. Inclusions with a common cyclic and separating vector generate everything, and standard inclusions of factors, such as those of nested subregions in QFT, are ergodic. Moreover, the $L^2$-nuclearity property implies that the spectrum of parent Hamiltonians is discrete. We define a dissipative semigroup by repeating the Petz recovery map, whose fixed-point algebra is the modular persistent core and whose spectrum is gapped under the assumption of $L^2$-nuclearity. We conjecture that the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of inclusion parent Hamiltonians can be used to define local spectral measures of quantum chaos.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) B: Discovery pipeline overview
papers.abstract: We present the method used to identify the $15\,000$ high-grade galaxy-galaxy strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Given that lenses are intrinsically rare systems and the DR1 data set is vast, this lens search was conducted in a number of stages: a catalogue-level cut; a machine-learning and ensemble search; a two-stage citizen-science search, and finally grading of lens candidates by strong lens researchers. In this paper, we describe each search stage and their respective results. This search was enabled by the automated classification of over 68 million objects by neural networks, more than 4.5 million classifications of $300\,000$ objects by citizen-scientist volunteers, and the inspection of over $30\,000$ objects by strong lens researchers. We find this multi-stage approach helps maximise the number of lenses identified, while minimising inspection requirements of both citizen scientists and strong lens researchers. We measure a completeness in our comprehensive search of $0.73_{-0.15}^{+0.08}$ to grade A ('definite') systems and $0.34_{-0.06}^{+0.05}$ to grade A+B ('definite' + 'probable') systems. Our search therefore identifies the majority of the definitive strong lens systems in the DR1 area with the remainder likely to be fainter or more ambiguous cases. We find that researcher grading remains subjective; in this work we implement calibration to account for biases of individual inspectors and highlight the benefit of lens modelling (ECLIPSE-C) in determining the nature of a lens candidate. This paper forms part of the ECLIPSE series, here focussing on the discovery pipeline used to identify lens candidates in Euclid DR1; an overview of the lenses discovered is presented in ECLIPSE-A.

papers.title: Reward-Driven Collider Physics Challenges for Self-Improving Agentic AI via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Recent advances in agentic AI have demonstrated the potential to automate complex high-energy physics (HEP) workflows. We focus on the regime of HEP tasks where frontier models still struggle to provide correct and complete solutions, and introduce an open-ended optimization task format with continuous, automatically evaluated rewards. Unlike conventional benchmarks focused on task completion, these tasks target reinforcement learning (RL) environments to generate agentic improvement on state- of-the-art HEP challenges. We benchmark frontier reasoning models on several HEP tasks and demonstrate an initial proof of concept in which a small language model improves through RL using automated feedback without human intervention. By connecting challenging HEP problems with verifiable scientific rewards and RL, we aim to advance agentic AI from reproducing established workflows to autonomously discovering better scientific solutions, paving the way toward self-improving scientific agents.

papers.title: A statistical study of ionized outflows in low-mass galaxies from DESI DR1
papers.abstract: We present a statistical analysis of ionized gas outflows in a large sample of low-mass ($\mathrm{log(M_{*}/M_{\odot})\lesssim10}$) galaxies at $z<0.45$ from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). Using [OIII] and H$α$ emission lines, we identify $\sim5800$ dwarf galaxies with robust signatures of ionized outflows. Most are star-forming systems above the star-forming main sequence, with a smaller fraction of composites and AGN hosts. The derived mass-loading factors span $η=0.001-1$, with a median $η\sim0.01$, consistent with previous studies at similar stellar masses. These values are $1$--$2$ dex lower than predicted by cosmological simulations, suggesting that the ionized phase traces only a minor fraction of the total outflow mass. Outflow velocities are sufficient to enrich the circumgalactic medium in $\gtrsim80\%$ of cases, while escape into the intergalactic medium appears efficient mainly in composite and AGN hosts. We find that mass-loading factors decrease with stellar mass, broadly reproducing simulated trends despite the normalization offset. Comparing individual detections with stacked spectra of the general low-mass star-forming population, we find systematically lower mass-loading factors in the stacks, although the difference decreases toward larger offsets above the star-forming main sequence. Together with a positive correlation between mass-loading factor and specific star-formation rate, this suggests that enhanced star formation and burstiness regulate feedback efficiency and shape galactic winds. Our results highlight the role of ionized outflows in the baryon cycle of low-mass galaxies and the need for multiphase studies to fully understand feedback in galaxy evolution.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) A: Strong lens catalogue overview
papers.abstract: We present 15 072 high-confidence strong lens candidates in Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1), spanning 2000 deg$^2$. These comprise 6073 grade A ('sure lens') and 8999 grade B ('probable lens') systems, which we publish alongside a further 9010 grade C ('possible lens') candidates. With more high-confidence candidates than all previous catalogues combined, this sample establishes a large, homogeneous data set of galaxy-scale strong lenses with high-resolution imaging, transforming strong lensing from a field of rare discoveries to a robust statistical tool for astrophysics and cosmology. Of the roughly 900 million sources in DR1, we searched the 68 million passing our catalogue selection using a bespoke discovery pipeline that synthesises scores from five machine-learning models with visual classifications from around 7000 citizen scientists and 67 strong lensing experts. Beyond classical Einstein rings, our catalogue includes 84 candidate double-source-plane lenses and over 1000 candidate disc lenses, two exotic classes with few previously known examples, as well as several hundred candidate lensed AGN and quasars. We deliver automated lens models for the combined grade A+B systems, and photometric redshifts and stellar population properties for the deflector galaxies, providing immediate science-ready data products. We find that the majority of the deflector galaxies are massive and quiescent, with stellar masses of $\log_{10}(M_\ast /M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$ (Salpeter initial mass function; 16th-84th percentile range). The deflector galaxies span a range of photometric redshifts ($z=0.68 ^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$), extending to higher redshifts than previous ground-based lens samples, and the lenses have a typical Einstein radius of $0.85 ^{+0.44}_{-0.24}$ arcsec. Extrapolating by area, we expect over 100 000 high-confidence strong lens candidates in the Euclid Wide Survey.

papers.title: Automated identification of dipole mixed-modes in red-giant stars
papers.abstract: Dipole mixed modes probe the internal structure of red giants by carrying information from both the convective envelope and the radiative core. Hence, identifying these modes allows for the determination of evolutionary states and stellar interior conditions. This identification typically relies on comparing observed frequencies with theoretical ones derived from the mixed-mode asymptotic relation. However, the process is challenging due to parameter-space degeneracies, stellar rotation, as well as missing modes and spurious peaks in the power density spectrum. In this work, we aim to develop an automated method for identifying dipole mixed modes, suitable for large-scale asteroseismic analyses. We introduce a metric that measures the overlap between observed and asymptotic dipole frequencies, represented as spike trains convolved with Gaussian kernels. After optimising this metric with a genetic algorithm, we use the best-fit parameters to perform a global assignment of the oscillation modes. We then validated the method using synthetic frequencies of RGB and CHeB stars perturbed by stellar rotation, and further tested it on four benchmark stars. Validation using perturbed synthetic frequencies shows that our method recovers over 95% of the dipole mixed modes across different evolutionary states, and this performance remains robust to spurious peaks and missing modes. For the benchmark stars, our dipole mode identification is consistent with previously published results, with mixed-mode parameter estimates typically agreeing within 1% for $ΔΠ$1 and 10% for $δν$rot and $q$. Our analysis demonstrates that the proposed method effectively addresses the challenges associated with the complex dipole mode spectrum. Thus, it enables automated identification of dipole mixed modes, supporting homogeneous, large-scale asteroseismic analyses of evolved stars.

papers.title: Measuring the growth index in the $w_0w_a$CDM background
papers.abstract: We produce a measurement of the growth index, $γ$, which is used to parametrize the scale-independent growth of linear matter perturbations on sub-horizon scales, for the $w_0w_a$CDM background model. In 2023, assuming the $Λ$CDM background, the value $γ=0.633^{+0.025}_{-0.024}$ was obtained, excluding the General Relativity value of $γ=0.55$ at $3.7σ$ statistical significance. In 2025, an analysis of baryon acoustic oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopy Instrument (DESI) demonstrated a preference for a dynamical dark energy over the cosmological constant model, $Λ$, ranging from $2.8-4.2σ$, depending on the external datasets used. Therefore it is important to determine how the $γ$ measurement is modified in the context of dynamical dark energy and verify whether the tension with the expected theoretical value persists. Considering data from Planck cosmic microwave background anisotropies, $fσ_{8}$, baryon acoustic oscillation from DESI and supernova Ia luminosity distances from Phanteon+, we find $γ_{w_0w_a}=0.633\pm0.024$, essentially the same value found for the $Λ$CDM background. This result excludes the General Relativity value for the $w_0w_a$CDM background evolution at $3.4σ$ level. We also show that the $γ$ posteriors across many datasets combinations are consistent with each other and that main driver of the "$γ$ tension" is the $fσ_{8}$ dataset.

papers.title: Identification of extragalactic radio sources in the VISTA survey of the Magellanic Clouds using an unsupervised machine learning algorithm
papers.abstract: The Magellanic Clouds benefit from a wealth of data across the electromagnetic spectrum, but extracting extragalactic sources from these crowded fields is a less than straightforward endeavour. We used an unsupervised machine learning algorithm (t-distributed stochastic neighbourhood embedding; t-SNE) to classify 6,652 and 1,356 sources in the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, respectively, that were detected in the VISTA Survey of the Magellanic Clouds (VMC) and the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) survey with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). Multi-wavelength photometry and colours from optical to radio were used as features to cluster similar sources together in 2D space on a t-SNE map. We used previously classified sources to separate the clusters into five classes: AGN, low-redshift galaxies, blazars, dusty stellar objects (e.g. young stellar objects, planetary nebulæ etc) and high proper-motion stars. Previous photometric classifications from the literature match with specific clusters identified, as well as provide insight on areas of the t-SNE map for which there are no previous classifications. This work shows that the combination of unsupervised machine learning with photometry from optical to radio has proven adept at separating the stellar from the extragalactic, and the AGN from the galaxies. Our associated new spectroscopy with SALT includes new discoveries of AGN up to redshift 3.3 and Magellanic emission-line objects.

papers.title: Self-Regulated Cosmic-Ray Electron Acceleration in High-Mach-Number MHD-PIC Shocks
papers.abstract: Shock waves in supernova remnants are thought to accelerate cosmic rays (CRs) via diffusive shock acceleration (DSA). If acceleration is efficient, CR-modified shock models and nonlinear DSA predict smoothly decelerated precursors and concave spectra that harden with energy. These predictions are in tension with observations, which favor spectra closer to the test-particle form, $4 πf(p) p^{4} = {\rm const}$ or steeper. We use one- and two-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic-particle-in-cell simulations to follow the long-term nonlinear coupling of the thermal plasma and CR electrons in non-relativistic quasi-parallel, high-Mach-number shocks. We choose electrons over ions for their larger charge per unit mass, probing the limits of current-driven feedback. We vary the supplied CR-electron mass fraction to measure the shock's response. Our injection model determines the effective injection and acceleration from particle trajectories through the evolving upstream turbulence, rather than a prescribed shock injection fraction. The reflected CR-electron current excites Bell-type non-resonant turbulence. The resulting magnetic structures scatter and isotropize the current-carrying particles, limiting the coherent upstream current and suppressing the formation of a spatially extended CR-pressure precursor. Across the CR-electron mass supply explored, the saturated upstream magnetic energy and far-upstream CR current converge to similar levels. In 1D, the downstream high-energy spectrum approaches the test-particle DSA shape across the resolved momentum range, with nonthermal pressure reaching a few tens of percent of the upstream ram pressure. These results suggest that, once injection is sufficient to sustain strong current-driven turbulence, supernova-remnant shocks can approach a common regulated state largely insensitive to the details of CR injection.

papers.title: Dark Matter Velocimetry with Quantum Networks
papers.abstract: Quantum sensor networks can use the spatial phase coherence of wavelike dark matter to probe not only particle properties but also the motion and structure of the Galactic halo. We explore this idea for the minimal two-node network, in which a nonlocal exchange measurement samples the characteristic function of the velocity distribution. We compare the Standard Halo Model (SHM) with a Gaia-inspired radially anisotropic component and their mixture (SHM++), taking into account daily and annual modulation, postselection, depolarizing events, and a flat instrumental offset. We show that annual modulation at one fixed local sidereal time has the same phase waveform for the centered SHM and Gaia-inspired SHM++ models, leaving them degenerate when the overall signal amplitude is unknown. Earth's rotation breaks this degeneracy by scanning the baseline through Galactic directions and exposing the direction-dependent coherence of an anisotropic population. Distinguishing these velocity distributions would test whether the local halo is smooth and nearly isotropic or contains a radially biased accreted component, turning a quantum-network detection into a probe of Milky Way structure. Our likelihood analysis shows how modulation and signal-odd controls separate this information from flat backgrounds and provides a path from model discrimination toward measurement of the local velocity distribution.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) D: Photometric redshifts and the first census of strong lenses in the galaxy evolution framework
papers.abstract: The Euclid mission is revolutionising the study of strong gravitational lenses by providing high-resolution imaging over an unprecedented survey area, increasing the number of known lenses by two orders of magnitude compared to previous surveys. Characterising this sample of lens-galaxies requires accurate measurements of their physical properties. However, standard catalogue photometry often blends the light from the foreground lens and the lensed background source, limiting the reliability of derived galaxy parameters. We present a homogeneous catalogue of photometric redshifts and physical properties for 9538 galaxy-scale strong lenses identified in Euclid's DR1 strong-lens sample. We use deblended multiwavelength photometry obtained from the lens modelling of Euclid and ground-based images with PyAutoLens. The photometric redshifts of the lens galaxies are estimated using the template-fitting code Phosphoros. The stellar masses, SFRs, stellar ages, and metallicities are inferred through SED fitting with Prospector, adopting a flexible non-parametric SFH and a Salpeter IMF. The robustness of the inferred parameters is assessed through comparisons with spectroscopic redshifts and external galaxy surveys. The sample of lenses spans a broad redshift range of $0.13\lesssim z_{\rm phot} \lesssim 1.98$, with a median $z_{\rm phot} = 0.68^{+0.33}_{-0.29}$. The sample is dominated by massive quiescent galaxies with a $M_\ast$ range $[10^{10},\,10^{12.1}]\,M_\odot$ and a median $\log_{10}(M_\ast/M_\odot) = 11.39^{+0.29}_{-0.33}$. This catalogue represents one of the first large-scale characterisations of strong-lens galaxies in the Euclid era. By combining deblended photometry with homogeneous photometric redshift and SED-fitting analyses, it provides a foundation for studies of galaxy evolution, lens-galaxy scaling relations, and the connection between stellar and total mass in strong lenses.

papers.title: Cubic Curvature Deformations to the Kerr Black Hole Shadow
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. Starting from a perturbatively corrected Kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. Using a Hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. We find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the Kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. In particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. We validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical Kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. Our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.

papers.title: Rebrightening in the Radio: Secondary Flares from Tidal Disruption Events AT2019ehz and AT2019eve
papers.abstract: We present the discovery of new secondary delayed radio flares from two tidal disruption events (TDEs), AT2019ehz and AT2019eve from observations ranging 1-18 GHz using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array. For AT2019ehz, we find a secondary flare in radio emission began at 1545 days post-disruption, 770 days after the first radio flare detected at 775 days post-disruption, and for AT2019eve the secondary flare was detected at 1594 days post-disruption, 825 days after its initial radio detection at 769 days post-disruption. Through spectral modeling of the multi-frequency observations, we extract physical parameters of the new flares to constrain the origin of the rebrightening. We find the secondary flare of AT2019ehz is likely produced by a second outflow launched at roughly 1000 days. For AT2019eve, the secondary flare reveals unexpected spectral evolution with a self-absorbed peak increasing from 1325 to 2173 days post-disruption, which is not well explained with most models of expanding outflows and instead suggests a more complex physical geometry. This inconclusive origin of AT2019eve highlights the need for more complex models to explain observed TDE radio evolution.

papers.title: Dual-species atom interferometry for axion dark matter
papers.abstract: Atom interferometers are sensitive to oscillations of the masses and transition frequencies of atoms, which can be induced by axion dark matter. The main limitation is the sensitivity to gravity gradient noise (GGN). We propose a dual-species atom interferometry sequence that provides a suppression of GGN by up to three orders of magnitude and a sensitivity enhancement via the mass difference of the two atoms. We show that, under realistic experimental assumptions, a 10m-baseline dual-species atom interferometer is more sensitive to the axion gluon coupling than a 100m single-species gradiometer. Including a comprehensive noise analysis, we demonstrate that the Very Long Baseline Atom Interferometer (VLBAI) in Hannover with a baseline of 10m can probe the axion decay constant at levels almost competitive with leading laboratory constraints. The proposed 100m-baseline Atom Interferometer CERN Experiment (AICE) can extend this sensitivity by up to two orders of magnitude, surpassing laboratory constraints for axion masses of $10^{-19}\;\text{eV}/c^2 \lesssim m_a \lesssim 3\times10^{-15}\;\text{eV}/c^2$.

papers.title: Scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia: do they bind?
papers.abstract: We investigate the existence of molecular two-glueball bound states, so-called glueballonia, in pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory. We mainly concentrate on the scalar and pseudoscalar channels, thus studying scalar-scalar and scalar-pseudoscalar bound states, respectively. Near the onset of binding, when a bound state first appears just below threshold, a nonrelativistic framework is justified. We employ an attractive scalar-exchange Yukawa potential together with a smeared contact term contribution and determine the critical attraction required for binding. For two scalar glueballs, we use the scalar dilaton effective theory to determine the parameters of the non-relativistic potential: the Yukawa interaction is generated by t- and u-channels involving the exchange of one scalar glueball, while the repulsion emerges by the s-channel annihilation and contact interaction. Using lattice-YM input to fix the dilaton parameters, we find that the attraction is strong enough: the scalar glueballonium binds, and the result is quite robust with respect to parameter variations. In a minimal scalar-pseudoscalar extension, the Yukawa attraction is again given by the t-channel scalar glueball, while the crossed u-channel pseudoscalar exchange induces an attractive local contribution, making the pseudoscalar glueballonium also bind in pure gauge. Importantly, both the scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia are stable in the YM vacuum. Next, we briefly comment on the pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar, scalar-tensor, and tensor-tensor channels: all these channels are attractive too and could form bound states, which, however, would be unstable in pure YM due to decay into two lighter glueballs. Finally, as a cross-check, our formalism confirms that Higgs-Higgs bound state does not form.

papers.title: Band geometry, Anderson's theorem, and vortex nucleation in unconventional 2D superconductors
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent discovery of chiral superconductors in 2d materials, we study the effects of disorder on superconductivity in materials with non-trivial band geometry. First, we show how Anderson's theorem and the conventional Abrikosov-Gorkov description of disorder-induced pair breaking are modified by the structure of the normal-state Bloch functions. We apply these results to twisted MoTe2 and show that a BCS pairing mechanism for the observed superconductor is in tension with the measured normal state residual resistivity. Second, we study whether random potential disorder can nucleate superconducting vortices in a chiral time- reversal-breaking superconductor. We show that, for a superconductor stabilized by the usual BCS mechanism, weak disorder does not induce a vortex glass phase, in contrast to superconductivity formed from an anyon fluid.

papers.title: Revealing Bell Nonlocality Does Not Require the Same Physical Measurement to be Performed Twice
papers.abstract: Bell inequality violations, or Bell nonlocality for short, is not only central to testing the foundations of quantum physics but have also become an essential ingredient of numerous quantum information protocols, from quantum key distribution to the device-independent certification of randomness and secure communication. Existing analyses of Bell nonlocality assume that a small set of predefined measurement directions can be reproduced exactly. But what if these directions cannot be reproduced at all? This may happen for fundamental or technical reasons, such as variations in the measurement apparatus. Here we show that the violation of a Bell inequality remains possible and that it also retains its operational significance, even when the measurement directions never repeat. We experimentally confirm these results using polarization-entangled photons, detecting only one particle pair per randomly chosen analyzer direction. Our results establish the robustness of Bell inequality violations against imperfect measurement repeatability and further connect Bell tests with the broader framework of randomized measurements. Moreover, they extend quantum information protocols to settings with limited measurement control, including quantum device certification, communication complexity, and quantum cryptography.

papers.title: Cosmological Dressing Rules for Massive Scalars
papers.abstract: The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation of de Sitter correlation functions comes in different guises including harmonic analysis and dressed flat space correlators. We observe that these are equivalent spectral representations of the same Sturm-Liouville problem. Starting from the latter we derive dressing rules for scalar fields of arbitrary mass with auxiliary propagators in the form of Euler integrals that are accessible to flat space diagrammatic tools.

papers.title: Discovering new physics with semitauonic $b$-hadron decays
papers.abstract: Anomalous lepton flavor universality violation (LFUV) observed in semileptonic decays of beauty hadrons may be the first signal of new physics (NP) beyond the Standard Model. We review the essential theoretical concepts and experimental considerations required for self-consistent and unbiased NP interpretations of these LFUV anomalies. We examine the status of present-day analyses, and assess the core challenges to the future precision studies that will be required to conclusively establish or reject an NP signal, as well as promising strategies to resolve them.

papers.title: Cosmological correlators and kinematic flow on complex Hartle-Hawking saddles
papers.abstract: The Lorentzian gravitational path integral over homogeneous and isotropic metrics in a closed universe with positive cosmological constant is dominated by complex saddle points, such as the Hartle-Hawking saddles. We ask how to compute cosmological correlators on such complex backgrounds, and how they respond to the shifts of the kinematic variables---the kinematic flow---without tracking the bulk time evolution explicitly. We, specifically, study a conformally coupled scalar test field with a cubic interaction around these saddles. We find that the wave function coefficients can be written as discrete spectral sums with the summands containing the corresponding coefficients in the Einstein static universe, which are obtainable in analogy with the polytopes program for flat spacetime. Whereas the wave function coefficients of the flat FLRW case are given by integrals over shifted kinematics, the discrete spectrum on the three-sphere for Hartle-Hawking saddles produces sums. We identify the coefficients, which depend on the final hypersurface through a phase fixed by its size, with Srivastava-Daoust multi-variable hypergeometric functions. They satisfy recursion relations for any number of sites, under which the sums collapse into rational functions. For the one- and two-site Feynman-Witten tree diagrams, we derive difference equations in the kinematic variables which close on a finite set of sums, giving a discrete kinematic flow. The transformation matrices are upper triangular with rational elements, and satisfy a consistency condition which makes the flow path independent. We then obtain the two-, three- and four-point cosmological correlators. At the late-time conformal boundary, we derive an explicit difference equation for the four-point function.

papers.title: Ensemble Learning with Unsupervised and Semi-Supervised Models for New Physics Searches at Colliders
papers.abstract: New physics beyond the Standard Model is widely believed to exist motivated by key limitations of the current theory. However, in the absence of undisputed experimental signals, there is little guidance on what type of extended physics model should be built. To address the challenge of training machine learning classifiers to spot unknown phenomena, many algorithms have been applied to the task of either identifying anomalous events relative to background expectations or cluster collision events together in classes of similarity. However, as in the supervised case, the no free lunch theorem assures that the performance of unsupervised models depends on the specific signal hypothesis and their inductive biases, and the successful identification of a given signal by a particular algorithm does not guarantee comparable performance for other signals. In this study, we take a step toward a more model-independent unsupervised and semi-supervised search strategy by combining classifiers into ensembles. Our goal is addressing two complementary aspects of unsupervised ensemble learning - overall performance and robustness of the classification task from a thorough assessment of ensemble models. We show that, despite sacrificing some performance relative to the best individual model in the majority of cases, the ensembles provide robust and reliable classification predictions across several signal hypotheses, increasing confidence that genuinely unknown new physics will not pass unnoticed.

papers.title: oMEGACat. XI. Kinematic Characterization of Omega Centauri's Subpopulations: A Flattened Primordial Component
papers.abstract: Omega Centauri ($ω$ Cen; NGC 5139), the likely stripped nucleus of a dwarf galaxy accreted by the Milky Way, is one of the few galactic nuclei resolvable into individual stars. Because of its long relaxation time, the kinematics of its stars may still retain memory of how this nucleus formed. We combine HST proper motions and MUSE line-of-sight velocities from the oMEGACat survey to compare populations defined by abundance variations (the chromosome map), metallicity, and age within the half-light radius. The chromosome-map division separates two dynamically distinct components. The primordial stars have a flattened dispersion field, with kinematic ellipticity $ε\approx 0.7$ ($σ_{\rm minor} / σ_{\rm major} \approx 0.8$), which we recover independently in the line-of-sight velocities and the proper motions. The enriched stars are consistent with $ε=0$ in the line-of-sight velocities and are no more flattened than the full sample in the proper motions, and the two components show no strong difference in rotation. Metallicity bins show no comparable structure, because each bin mixes stars from both components, and the age-metallicity sample covers only the cluster core, where it cannot test for the flattening. The present-day central concentration of the most enriched (P2) stars suggests that they formed more centrally concentrated than the primordial stars, independent of assembly scenario. These results favor a picture in which the primordial stars retain the flattened orbital structure of the progenitor, while the enriched stars fell inward as dense clumps or formed in compact, centrally concentrated starbursts.

papers.title: Toward the minimal set of states in axion superradiance
papers.abstract: Observational searches for black hole superradiance require predicting the growth and evolution of quasi-bound states on astrophysical timescales. For axions (and most light spin-0 particles), self-interactions efficiently redistribute energy and angular momentum from the fastest-growing superradiant states into higher-order, more weakly bound states, and do so on short timescales. This has made it difficult to compute even the most mundane of observables across large regions of parameter space. In this work we extend the study of self-interacting systems, following the evolution of nearly 300 coupled quasi-bound states. We evolve a $10\,M_\odot$ black hole over a Salpeter timescale, and $10^4$ and $10^8\,M_\odot$ black holes over a Gyr, identifying for each axion mass the minimal set of states required to describe the evolution of the black hole and the shape of the superradiant cloud. In most cases the evolution converges as increasingly weakly bound states are added; we identify no less than 203 distinct quasi-bound states that play a role in establishing this convergence. In small regions of parameter space, however, we find no converged solution, and show that broad resonant features and nearly degenerate scattering rates redistribute mass to bound states with principal quantum numbers $n \gtrsim 45$. We further show that the cloud can extend to radii orders of magnitude larger than usually assumed, that gravitational-wave level transitions can prevent the growth of superradiant states, and that both the gravitational-wave spectrum and the interaction with the environment are far richer than previously appreciated.

papers.title: Frequency-dependent time delays in Sgr A* from a broadband VLA observation
papers.abstract: Frequency-dependent radio time delays have been measured in Sgr A* light curves, with higher-frequency emission generally leading lower-frequency emission. These lags have been interpreted in terms of an organized jet-like outflow, expanding plasma components, or magnetic-flux eruptions, although their origin and recurrence remain uncertain. We aim to search for and quantify frequency-dependent radio time delays in a new high-cadence Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observation of Sgr A*. Using the improved broad 12-37 GHz frequency coverage, we measured the timing of the dominant variability feature and compared the resulting lag-wavelength slope with previous measurements. Sgr A* was observed with the VLA on 28 May 2022 in the Ku, K, and Ka bands over a 6-hour track. We extracted both band-averaged and 2 GHz subband light curves and measured the delays using a peak-time method and a locally normalized cross-correlation function. The light curves show one broad variability feature, with the maximum occurring progressively later at lower observing frequencies. Both timing methods recover a positive lag-wavelength relation, with a slope of order 40 min/cm. This value agrees with time lag results reported over more than 15 years from the first VLA observations at 22-43 GHz to later multifrequency VLA and ALMA campaigns. The sign and magnitude of the estimated delay are consistent with outward propagation through an optically thick synchrotron-emitting region. The recurrence of comparable delays over almost two decades suggests that frequency-dependent radio lags are a persistent feature of Sgr A* variability. Broadband, multi-epoch VLA monitoring of Sgr A* provides a useful probe of its radio variability, but robust lag measurements require high cadence and improved (u,v) coverage of both Sgr A* and the surrounding extended emission such as by combining different VLA configurations.

papers.title: Non-Bloch Topology of Frustrated Non-Hermitian Flat Bands
papers.abstract: Frustrated lattices with exactly flat bands and compact localized states provide an ideal setting to uncover the topology of flat bands, leading to intriguing physics in two dimensions. Extending from Hermitian to non-Hermitian systems, however, band structures are drastically changed by the non-Hermitian skin effect, which is less well understood beyond one dimension. Here, we construct a broad class of two-dimensional frustrated non-Hermitian lattice models with exactly flat bands which can be naturally described in a non-Bloch band theory. Using non-Hermitian breathing Kagome and checkerboard models as illustrations, we reveal how flat bands acquire a basis-independent skin effect induced by the other bands; in the breathing Kagome model it appears exactly when the flat band enters the area spanned by the periodic-boundary spectra of the dispersive bands. A flat band becomes singular when its eigenvectors hold immovable discontinuities at band crossings. Such singularity in non-Hermitian systems is sensitive to boundary conditions and unprotected by band flatness. Non-Bloch topology underlying is uncovered in a bulk-boundary correspondence with the formation of a singular band touching in the bulk and a robust flat band skin mode on the boundary. We present a geometric approach to construct this boundary skin mode from a macroscopic sum of compact localized skin modes and trace its topological origin to two linearly independent noncontractible loop states on a non-Bloch torus. To characterize the correspondence, an invariant is proposed based on biorthogonal polarization of the zero-energy corner mode. Breaking exact flatness, we further realize nearly flat non-Bloch Chern bands.

papers.title: $α'^2$-corrections to the bosonic string from an action-level double copy map
papers.abstract: The low-energy effective action of the bosonic string contains higher-derivative corrections of the form Riem$^2$ and Riem$^3$ to the Einstein--Hilbert action, together with the associated Kalb--Ramond couplings. We construct an action-level double copy description of these corrections up to cubic order in the fields. Two ingredients are required: a higher-derivative gauge-theory Lagrangian, which up to field redefinitions is controlled by a single $F^3$ coupling, and a deformation of the color-to-kinematics replacement of the structure constants by the corresponding three-momentum tensor. We show that no higher-derivative gauge-theory operator can produce the Riem$^3$ vertex with the standard replacement rule, and that the matching conditions for the gauge-theory coupling and the deformation of the map admit a unique solution, a double root, which renders the cubic action left--right symmetric, of the form $(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)\otimes(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)$. Without further input, the resulting map reproduces the cubic $\mathrm{Riem}\,H^2$ coupling of the bosonic string at order $α'$, the absence of six-derivative cubic Kalb--Ramond couplings at order $α'^2$, and the absence of interactions odd in the Kalb--Ramond field. The comparison is performed in transverse-traceless gauge, up to field redefinitions.

papers.title: A Scattering Phase Space Primer
papers.abstract: The kinematic phase space is fundamental to all particle scattering processes across experiments - from lepton and hadron colliders to dark matter searches. While $2 \to 2$ scatterings are well understood, the simplest non-trivial case of three-body final states presents major analytic challenges that are typically circumvented by numerical methods. This paper provides the first comprehensive analytic treatment of $2 \to 3$ phase space and cross section distributions that uses a non-constant matrix element and keeps all particle masses non-zero. This is fundamental for an accurate description of crucial configurations for Beyond Standard Model searches, e.g. Vector Boson Fusion. Using Gram Determinants as our primary language for Lorentz-invariant kinematics, we derive exact, closed-form expressions for differential cross section distributions and explicitly construct the complete physical phase space boundaries. This paper serves as both a pedagogical introduction and a practical reference for the analytic computation of realistic $2 \to 3$ processes, showing how the $m\neq0, |{\cal M}|\neq 1$ problem is computationally tractable through proper kinematic methods. The results apply universally across all $2 \to 3$ scatterings regardless of center-of-mass energy, particle masses, or interaction type.

papers.title: Cosmological Signals from Finite-Lifetime Domain Wall Networks
papers.abstract: We study cosmological perturbations sourced by metastable domain wall (DW) networks. Using the unconnected segment model, we derive analytic expressions for the scalar and tensor power spectra in the long-wavelength regime, finding a fixed ratio between their amplitudes during the scaling regime. These spectra grow as the network evolves, driven by the increasing correlation length and slower redshifting of the wall energy density relative to radiation, and peak at a scale set by the network's collapse time. Comparing the scalar spectrum with observational constraints, we derive bounds on the DW energy density at collapse, which we apply to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and axion models. When these bounds are saturated, the resulting CMB $B$-mode signal can be comparable to or larger than the inflationary signal for a tensor-to-scalar ratio $r \sim 0.03$, potentially bringing it within reach of future CMB polarization experiments.

papers.title: Learning Quantum Hamiltonians from the Dynamical Structure Factor
papers.abstract: Identifying the microscopic interactions governing a quantum system is essential for developing predictive theories of materials and validating quantum technologies. Despite considerable progress, learning Hamiltonians from realistic experimental data remains a challenge. Motivated by neutron scattering and quantum simulations, we study the problem of learning a quantum Hamiltonian from the dynamical structure factor (DSF), which captures two-point correlation data in quantum magnets. We show that the DSF encodes sufficient information to efficiently reconstruct broad classes of quantum Hamiltonians. Our approach exploits simple relations between low-order spectral moments of the DSF and microscopic couplings, giving rise to three complementary Hamiltonian tomography protocols based on the high-temperature expansion, strong-field polarization, and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, respectively. The framework we introduce establishes practical and robust Hamiltonian learning from common experimental data, with potentially immediate application to neutron scattering experiments.

papers.title: Cosmic Ray Heating of the Early IGM: Realistic Galaxy Populations, Reduced Efficiency, and 21-cm Signatures
papers.abstract: Cosmic rays (CRs) accelerated by the first supernovae could heat the intergalactic medium (IGM) before reionization. Previous 21-cm simulations, assuming a kinetic-energy power-law spectrum and simplified galaxy populations, found that CR heating can rival X-ray heating from high-mass X-ray binaries, imprint a distinct signature on the 21-cm power spectrum, and flatten the absorption trough of the global 21-cm signal. Here we model CR heating in 21cmFAST with: (i) the momentum power-law spectrum predicted by diffusive shock acceleration; (ii) Coulomb losses off free electrons; and (iii) injection from data-informed populations of atomic-cooling and molecularly cooled galaxies. We find that CR heating is about an order of magnitude weaker than previously estimated because a momentum power law places little energy in the sub-relativistic protons ($\lesssim 40$ MeV) that supply 99% of the heat. For our fiducial spectral slope, at the hard end of those inferred for Galactic supernova remnants, and for matched efficiency, this reduces the heating by a factor of $\approx 12$, and together with a more realistic galaxy model, by a factor of $\approx 28$ at $z = 15$. At the efficiencies that supernovae can supply, CR heating is weaker than standard X-ray heating, and the global signal alone cannot tell the two apart. Distinguishing CR from X-ray heating with the 21-cm power spectrum requires CR efficiencies a few times higher than those expected from local observations. At such efficiencies, CR heating yields up to $\approx 55\%$ more power than X-ray heating at matched global signal (median over scales), compared with only 3-6% at a locally motivated efficiency. A flattened absorption trough, like the one claimed by EDGES, requires efficiencies over two orders of magnitude above the local ones, beyond plausible Population III supernova budgets.

papers.title: Crystalline Equivalence Principle for Anomalies
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic characterization of crystalline symmetry anomalies in bosonic lattice systems in (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions with a combination of crystalline and finite unitary internal symmetry. We construct anomaly indices of symmetry operators and derive their cocycle conditions and coboundary ambiguities. For generalized crystalline symmetries combining permutations of onsite Hilbert spaces with quantum cellular automata, anomaly indices take values in $H^3(B\widetilde Γ,U(1)_r)$ and $H^4(B\widetilde Γ,U(1)_r)$ respectively, where $\widetilde Γ$ is the total group of crystalline and internal symmetries, and the coefficient twist $r$ accounts for spatial orientation reversal. When crystalline symmetries act solely by permuting onsite Hilbert spaces, the anomaly classes restrict trivially to the spatial subgroup. These results establish a crystalline equivalence principle for bosonic anomalies at the microscopic level, without assuming a continuum description or emergent Lorentz invariance. We prove that a nontrivial total anomaly index obstructs any symmetric invertible phase. The framework incorporates modulated symmetries where spatial symmetries permute internal symmetries. Our results reproduce LSM and SPT--LSM constraints, with the latter illustrating how spectral-sequence differentials can trivialize candidate LSM anomaly indices.

papers.title: Beyond the Standard Model EFT: Stress Testing the Electroweak Phase Transition in the Real Singlet Model
papers.abstract: The real singlet scalar extension of the Standard Model is a much studied benchmark model for a strong first order electroweak phase transition (EWPT) and its role in electroweak baryogenesis. However, this model is not sufficient to generate the baryon asymmetry of the Universe, since it does not introduce any additional sources of CP violation. That is, additional new physics is still expected in the TeV range. In this paper we use effective field theory (EFT) methods to study the effects of new physics on the EWPT in the real singlet model with no $Z_2$. Effective operators up to dimension six with a cutoff scale of $Λ=1$ TeV are included in the scalar potential. We study the correlations between a strong first order EWPT, the Higgs trilinear coupling, resonant di-Higgs production, and gravitational wave signals in the EFT. We find that in the real singlet model with a strong first order EWPT the allowed region of the Higgs trilinear coupling is sensitive to TeV scale new physics, while the predictions of the gravitational wave signal and maximum resonant di-Higgs rate (with no additional production mechanisms) are robust against additional weakly coupled physics at or above the TeV scale.

papers.title: Dynamical evolution of the stellar mass function in multiple-population globular clusters
papers.abstract: The dynamical evolution of globular clusters is significantly influenced by the multiscale structure introduced by the presence of multiple stellar populations. In this study, we investigate the long-term dynamical evolution of the stellar mass function (MF) within globular clusters hosting two stellar populations using a suite of Monte Carlo simulations run with the MOCCA code. Dynamical processes including two-body relaxation, mass segregation, and tidal stripping result in distinct radial profiles describing the variation with distance from the cluster's center of the stellar MF slope within the first population (P1), the second population (P2), and the cluster as a whole. We show that these radial profiles are well described by a broken power law with a knee located slightly interior to the half-mass radius, a feature partially driven by the multiscale structure of the multiple populations. In both 3D and 2D projected coordinates, we explore several characteristic clustercentric distances within the profile, including those where the local MF slope matches the global value of the present-day MF slope and the initial mass function (IMF) slope, and we examine how these positions evolve with the cluster's dynamical age. Our results highlight how the initially more centrally concentrated P2 drives a steeper radial gradient and a steeper MF slope in the outer regions, which subsequently affects the global cluster values. Motivated by recent observational studies suggesting that a bottom-light IMF may better describe massive globular clusters, as well as measurements of a flatter P2 MF slope in the outer regions of 47 Tucanae, we additionally explore a three-parameter bottom-light IMF and a simulation in which the P1 IMF differs from the P2 IMF, with the P2 IMF flatter than that of the P1 in the lower mass range.

papers.title: Swing Surfaces in AdS/CFT
papers.abstract: We study holographic entanglement entropy in the flat limit of AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, and clarify the relation between Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces and the swing surfaces proposed for flat-space holography. We show that the ordinary RT formula does not admit a well-defined flat-space limit and connect this to subtleties of the state-operator map in the flat limit. We then construct an AdS$_3$ uplift of the swing prescription and develop its corresponding information-theoretic interpretation through two complementary approaches. First, we show that the swing surface length computes the mutual information between suitably chosen nearly null boundary intervals in a special class of pure CFT states. The gravity interpretation of this result involves scattering processes which take place deep inside of the AdS$_3$ bulk. Second, we reduce the problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation for swing surfaces to the more general problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation of black hole inner horizons in holography.

papers.title: Einstein Reconstruction Scheme: Metric Reconstruction by Direct Inversion of the Einstein Operator
papers.abstract: We propose a metric reconstruction scheme that computes the metric directly from the linearized Einstein equations for noncompact sources. Working in a traceful radiation gauge, we hierarchically solve four Einstein transport equations, with the remaining six enforced by suitable homogeneous data. Unlike previous Newman-Penrose approaches, we show how the homogeneous data are fixed, thereby closing the full set of Einstein equations. We conclude by relating our scheme to existing sourced reconstruction methods, thus establishing a connection between the Newman-Penrose and Hertz-potential approaches.

papers.title: The Dark Side of the Periodic Table: Theory and Signatures of Nuclear Atomic Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We study the theory and signatures of a Mirror Twin Higgs (MTH) scenario in which stable twin neutrons constitute most of the dark matter (DM), while a subdominant component of twin elements survives as nuclear atomic dark matter (naDM). This framework offers a solution to the $matter~coincidence~problem$ ($Ω_{\rm DM}\simeq5Ω_b$), as the twin $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry can correlate the visible and DM mass scales and their number densities. We analyze twin nucleon freeze-out and the onset of twin Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) to estimate the total naDM abundance, and determine which elements in the dark periodic table could be populated. An appreciable but subdominant naDM component generally requires a fractional nucleon mass splitting near the percent level, with twin-BBN creating heavy elements up to twin carbon. Strong twin neutron-proton scattering allows nearly all of the dark matter, not only the atomic sub-component, to participate in $dark~acoustic~oscillations$ (DAO) at early times, giving rise to a characteristic two-stage DAO signature that may be detected with future cosmological probes. Interactions between the twin and visible sectors, including the irreducible Higgs portal, make this scenario a well-motivated target for future directional direct-detection searches, and the naDM sub-component is expected to exhibit highly exotic astrophysics. We outline a supersymmetric twin Froggatt-Nielsen realization in which spontaneous $\mathbb{Z}_2$ breaking in the flavon sector can generate the required fermion spectrum and Higgs potential.

papers.title: Universal Theory of Strange and Bad Metals from Spatially Random Interactions with Underdamped Quantum-Critical Bosons
papers.abstract: One of the most important challenges in condensed matter physics is understanding the macroscopic properties of strange metals, particularly why their resistivity remains linear in temperature over several decades. We propose that a (2+1)d theory of fermions coupled to underdamped quantum-critical bosons through a spatially disordered interaction provides this long-sought-after theoretical explanation. The key novelty of our work is to establish the appropriate separation of scales so that the bosons are underdamped. Using this framework, we obtain two distinct forms for the fermionic self-energy: a conformal-limit solution, $Σ\sim\sqrtω$, and a marginal Fermi-liquid solution, $Σ\simω\log(1/ω)$, corresponding to regimes above and below the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit, respectively. These solutions produce Planckian scattering, exhibit exact $T$-linear resistivity, $ω/T$ scaling in the optical conductivity, as well as $\sim T\log(1/T)$ heat capacity at low temperatures. Moreover, our theory naturally unifies strange- and bad-metal phenomena within a single framework, suggesting that we are now approaching a new epoch in understanding the physics of strongly correlated matter.

papers.title: Exploring a Correlation Between AGN Black Hole Mass and X-ray Luminosity
papers.abstract: The traditional method to measure Type-1 Active Galactic Nuclei central black hole masses ($M_{BH}$) is the reverberation mapping (RM) technique. Motivated by the desire to find a less observationally expensive method (than RM) to estimate $M_{BH}$, we have explored a purported correlation between X-ray luminosity and $M_{BH}$. For this we have compiled a sample of 35 AGN with RM $M_{BH}$ estimates that were detected in the eROSITA All-Sky Survey public data release. Using a sample that is larger than that of J. A. Mayers et al. 2018 and has a cleaner selection function, we confirm their XMM-Newton based result of a positive correlation. However, the scatter on the scaling relation remains too high ($σ_\mathrm{int}=0.50^{+0.08}_{-0.06}$) to make this a practical method to predict $M_{BH}$ for a given X-ray detected Type-1 AGN. That said, our findings can be used to improve mock X-ray skies generated from large volume hydrodynamical cosmological simulations. Such mocks are a necessary ingredient for cluster cosmology and preparation for future missions such as NewAthena.

papers.title: Sharp Lower Bounds for Parallel Log-Concave Sampling
papers.abstract: How many rounds of parallel queries are needed to sample from a smooth, strongly log-concave distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$? For every fixed condition number $κ\in (1, \infty)$, we prove that any sampler making polynomially many queries per round requires $Ω_κ(\log d)$ rounds to achieve constant total variation error in the worst case. The lower bound holds even if queries return derivatives of all orders. Together with the first-order parallel Picard algorithm of \cite{zhou2025parallel}, this establishes a depth complexity of $Θ_κ(\log d)$ for parallel log-concave sampling with $\operatorname{poly}(d)$ width. We then study centered Gaussian targets to understand how much width is needed at a given depth. From \cite{chewi2023query,zhou2026complexitygaussiansampling}, it is known that either one round of width $d$ or $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtκ \log d)$ rounds of constant width suffice for first-order Gaussian sampling. At fixed $κ$ we characterize the depth-width tradeoff interpolating between these regimes: when using $ \lceil c \log d\rceil$ rounds, if $0 < c < c_\star(κ)$ then the optimal width at constant TV error is $\widetildeΘ(d^{1-c/c_\star(κ)})$, while if $c \geq c_\star(κ)$ then it is $Θ_κ(1)$. Here, $c_\star(κ)$ is an explicit constant with $c_\star(κ) \sim \sqrtκ / 8$ as $κ\to \infty$.

papers.title: Directed Wada cascade in systems with discrete scale invariance
papers.abstract: Dissipative systems whose equations are unchanged by a dilation can host an infinite ladder of attractors, each shell an exact magnified copy of the one before. Since such dynamics cannot tell a magnification from its inverse, the natural expectation is that these basins are maximally entangled, with every boundary point lying on the boundary of all of them, following the Wada property. We find that this expectation fails, and fails in a precise way. Dilation covariance and a single trapping region together bound which basin boundaries a point can lie on, and the bound depends only on its distance to the origin. No point lies on the boundary of all of them.
