papers.abstract: Inverse kinematics (IK) is a foundational primitive in robotics, mapping the task-space objectives expressed by higher-level planners to robot configurations that realize them. Traditional IK methods generally treat each query as an isolated pose-to-configuration problem, but planners often need a distribution over valid realizations that accounts for future reachability and preferences such as collision avoidance and stability. We introduce GenGenIK, a generative modeling approach that supports mobile bases, multiple end-effectors and targets, scene awareness, and preferences over robot behavior within a common interface. Experiments show that GenGenIK outperforms existing methods in both solve rate and runtime across tasks such as bimanual lift and flip-up, while allowing flexible control over the sampled distribution and remaining effective under partial scene observations. Website: https://icra-2027-gengenik.github.io/.

papers.title: A high-order recombination algorithm with adaptive scale selection for weak approximation of stochastic differential equations
papers.abstract: High-order recombination keeps weak approximation trees of diffusions small by a moment-preserving reduction of the measure on each patch of nodes. The weighted Litterer--Lyons (WLL) test of Ninomiya and Shinozaki sets the patch scale using a scalar \(λ>0\) chosen beforehand, whose appropriate value depends on coordinate units. First, the anisotropically weighted Litterer--Lyons (AWLL) rule selects the scale during recombination within a bounded factor of the measured increment amplitude. On a fixed set of nodes, expanding coordinate units leaves the AWLL patch-count bound unchanged but raises the WLL lower bound as a power until saturation. In Heston and shifted Stochastic-Alpha-Beta-Rho (sSABR) systems with initial price or forward rate 100, AWLL reduces the terminal supports of WLL with \(λ=1\) by factors of 137 and 1488 at comparable errors, but enlarges them at smaller Heston initial prices. Second, \(λ\) is extended to a positive definite matrix with a joint error bound for prices and sensitivities, a bound on the gain of its shape, and patch-count bounds. Third, the elimination stage of batched basis exchange requires \(O(J)\) arithmetic operations for \(J\) nodes at fixed moment rank and panel width, against \(Θ(J^{3})\) for the direct kernel update of Ninomiya and Shinozaki.

papers.title: Sampled resolvents of $C_0$-semigroups: aliasing and sharp rates on the Crandall-Pazy scale
papers.abstract: For a $C_0$-semigroup $(S_t)$ with generator $B$, sampling the Laplace integral $(λ-B)^{-1}=\int_0^\infty e^{-λt}S_t\,dt$ on the grid $T\mathbb{N}$ gives $Q_T=T(I-e^{-λT}S_T)^{-1}$, the impulse-invariant discretization of the resolvent. The motivation is a dyadic series of Castillo, Costin and Costin for the resolvent of a self-adjoint operator: its partial sums are exactly $Q_{2^{-N}}$, so the series is a telescoped rectangle rule. By Poisson summation, on $D(B)$ the error of $Q_T$ is the scalar $T/2$ plus the symmetric limit of the resolvents at the alias points $λ-2πin/T$, $n\ne0$, and the dyadic levels remove these aliases according to the $2$-adic valuation of $n$. Our main result is a sharp scale of rates for the trapezoid correction $Q_T-\frac T2I$. If $(S_t)$ belongs to the Crandall--Pazy class with parameter $α\in(0,1]$, that is $\|BS_t\|=O(t^{-1/α})$ as $t\to0$, the error is $O(T^α)$ in operator norm, $O(T^{α+θ})$ on the interpolation space of order $θ$ between $X$ and $D(B)$, and $O(T^{1+α})$ on $D(B)$, the last requiring only resolvent decay of order $α$ along the line $\mathrm{Re}\, z=\mathrm{Re}\,λ$. This interpolates between unitary groups with unbounded generator ($α=0$, no convergence in norm) and analytic semigroups ($α=1$), and every exponent is attained. For smooth data an Euler--Maclaurin expansion justifies Romberg extrapolation. For self-adjoint generators we give closed forms for the contribution of each dyadic level to Stone's formula, and we translate the results into an explicit error bound and step-size rule for Green functions computed from sampled autocorrelations. Experiments, including a structurally damped string whose semigroup is of Gevrey class, confirm the rates.

papers.title: A note on equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion
papers.abstract: In this note, we introduce an equivariant version of twisted holomorphic analytic torsion for the twisted Dolbeault complex on a complex manifold equipped with an action of a compact Lie group. Our construction is motivated by Ray and Singer's holomorphic analytic torsion, by the equivariant analytic torsion developed for elliptic complexes with group actions, notably in the work of Donnelly and later in the holomorphic setting by Bismut, and by Mathai and Wu's twisted analytic torsion for the twisted de Rham complex. Using pseudodifferential operators and the equivariant noncommutative residue, we define the equivariant twisted holomorphic analytic torsion. We also state its variation formulas under changes of the metric and of the twisting element, and present its functorial properties.

papers.title: Immersive Sight-Restriction-Based Collision Prevention Using Generic Particle Systems in Virtual Reality
papers.abstract: Collision prevention systems (CPS) help VR users navigate their physical surroundings safely. Most approaches overlay conceptually distinct grids or add solid virtual counterparts of physical obstacles; both can reveal the physical space, as they either stand out visually or behave inconsistently during locomotion. We explore sight restriction as an alternative: a standard particle system visualizes the play area boundary as a fog-like cloud whose intensity scales with proximity and viewing direction. A pre-study (N=10) determined the distance at which the visualization must appear. In a main study (N=11), we compared this particle-based CPS with a grid-based solution, focusing on locomotion behavior: across 253 approach episodes, users interrupted their approach after a comparable distance once either visualization appeared. Although the particle boundary was visible three times as often, participants reported higher presence. We release our implementation as open source to support further work on immersive collision prevention.

papers.title: Measuring Milky Way Mass with RR Lyraes and Blue Horizontal Branch Stars
papers.abstract: Measuring the mass of the Milky Way is essential for understanding galaxy formation and evolution, characterizing the Galactic potential and assembly history, and probing the nature of dark matter. We derive the enclosed mass profile of the Milky Way out to Galactocentric distances of $\sim80\,\mathrm{kpc}$ using two halo tracers with full 3D kinematics: RR Lyraes (RRLs) and blue horizontal-branch stars (BHBs). Our sample consists of 7,550 RRLs and 8,230 BHBs constructed from the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST), the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), spanning Galactocentric distances from $10$ to $100\,\mathrm{kpc}$. We estimate the enclosed mass using two independent methods: the spherical Jeans equation and the tracer mass estimator (TME). The two tracers yield consistent results, with $M(<81.7\,\mathrm{kpc}) = (4.76 \pm 0.23)\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M(<82.8\,\mathrm{kpc}) = (4.66 \pm 0.35)\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs. Adopting an NFW profile to extrapolate the enclosed mass beyond the outermost radius probed by our tracers, we infer virial masses of $M_{200} = 8.12^{+0.72}_{-0.65}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M_{200} = 8.13^{+0.78}_{-0.67}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs. We further validate our methodology using mock RRL and BHB samples constructed from two Auriga halos, finding that the inferred masses are underestimated by $15.5\%\pm2.8\%$ for RRLs and $11.9\%\pm3.4\%$ for BHBs, respectively. After correcting for these systematic errors, the Milky Way virial masses are $M_{200} = 9.79^{+0.93}_{-0.84}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from RRLs and $M_{200} = 9.24^{+0.95}_{-0.84}\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ from BHBs.

papers.title: Hypercyclic Algebras for Weighted Double Shifts
papers.abstract: Building on the approach of Bayart, Costa Júnior and Papathanasiou, we establish a Baire criterion for possibly noncommuting operator pairs to support hypercyclic algebras, with hypercyclicity defined through all finite compositions.We then study weighted double backward shifts under different multiplications and topologies.We characterize the existence of hypercyclic algebras for coordinatewise multiplication on sequence algebras admitting a continuous norm and, separately, on $ω^2=\mathbb C^{\mathbb N_0^2}$ with the product topology.For the noncommutative triangular product induced by upper triangular matrix multiplication, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of dense hypercyclic algebras on $ω^2$.In this setting, their existence is equivalent to that of one freely generated by countably infinitely many elements.Finally, we exhibit a pair on a fixed Fréchet space that supports a dense hypercyclic algebra for coordinatewise multiplication and a nonzero hypercyclic algebra, but no dense one, for the triangular product.

papers.title: Equidistribution of Hecke neighbours and continued fraction patterns
papers.abstract: We prove uniform tightness of Hecke neighbours of any probability measure of positive entropy that is invariant and ergodic under the diagonal flow. As an application, we confirm a conjecture of Einsiedler concerning a homogeneous dynamics analogue of an equidistribution theorem of Johnson and Rudolph on the torus. We also obtain applications to continued-fraction patterns in arithmetic sequences and to the \(p\)-adic Littlewood conjecture. Our proof studies escape of mass using dynamics on the boundary of the Chabauty compactification of the space of lattices, together with averaging operators defined by leafwise measures along horospherical subgroups.

papers.title: Set-Theoretic PAPR Reduction in Multi-Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: In this study, we propose an optimization framework for PAPR reduction in multi-antenna systems with beamforming. Unlike previous techniques, the proposed approach permits full control over the distorted symbol constellation via arbitrary (convex) constraints on the frequency domain symbols, while minimizing the PAPR at each individual transmit antenna. We propose an iterative algorithm based on an extrapolated alternating projection method, which relies on an iterative soft-thresholding subroutine to compute projections onto sublevel sets of the objective function, and we compare its performance to optimal solutions obtained with general-purpose convex solvers.

papers.title: Model-dependent metallicities of young stellar populations in TIMER galaxies
papers.abstract: Stellar populations in the central regions of disc galaxies provide key constraints on their formation and secular evolution. We investigate the properties of young stellar populations in the centres of nearby barred galaxies from the TIMER survey, using four stellar population models, two based on empirical (MILES, X-Shooter) and two on theoretical (Starburst99, HR-pyPopStar) stellar libraries, complemented by independent gas-phase metallicities from emission-line diagnostics. The inferred stellar metallicities depend strongly on the adopted model. Measured as the 5th-to-95th percentile spread across the three galaxies analysed in detail, the empirical libraries recover variations of 1.11 and 0.98 dex, whereas the theoretical ones return 0.40 and 0.49 dex; the gas in the same regions spans 0.49 dex. Gas metallicities are indeed lower in the central star-forming regions, but the amplitude of that depression (about 0.3 dex in NGC 1097) exceeds what bar-driven inflow of disc gas can account for, given typical abundance gradients in literature. The age-metallicity relations consistently reveal two distinct components: an older population consistent with a self-enrichment scenario, and a younger population formed from gas inflows with a different chemical enrichment history. The empirical libraries produce a monotonic decline of metallicities from old to young populations, which would require a sustained inflow of metal-poor gas outpacing its own enrichment. The theoretical libraries instead recover a young component whose metallicity departs from the older populations only at the most recent ages and by a few tenths of a dex, compatible with a single dilution episode. Our results demonstrate that model choice critically affects inferred metallicities, with empirical stellar libraries recovering age-metallicity relations that demand physical conditions the gas measurements cannot sustain.

papers.title: What Conformal Selection Can Certify in CRISPR Off-Target Design:Benchmark Leakage, Free Baselines, and a Finite-Sample Cohort Requirement
papers.abstract: Conformal selection promises distribution-free, finite-sample control of the error rate of a decision, and has been proposed as a safety layer for machine-learning CRISPR guide design. We ask whether such a certificate is attainable from the validated off-target data that exist. The constraint is arithmetic: a conformal p-value cannot fall below one divided by the calibration cohort size plus one, so a Benjamini-Hochberg selection certifies a single candidate only when that cohort is at least the candidate pool size divided by the tolerated error rate. Public cohorts supply ten validated guides, whereas a pool of two thousand at a ten percent error rate needs twenty thousand; the accepted set is consequently empty in over ninety-six percent of splits. Two benchmarking findings explain why this went unnoticed. The standard CIRCLE-seq file lists ten guides under eighty on-target strings, so grouping cross-validation on the sequence column trains and tests on one guide; corrected, pair-level discrimination and per-guide fidelity collapse. With that leakage removed, a training-free position-weight score and a bare count of near-match genomic sites are not beaten by a trained oracle. We give the corrected protocol, the baselines a new model must beat, and the cohort size a certified pipeline needs.

papers.title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven. We also provide a large family of examples of holomorphic correspondences satisfying our assumptions, obtained as generic complete intersections in $X\times X$.

papers.title: Constructing option portfolio
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the problem of constructing a portfolio composed of a set of financial options. We present a mixed-integer linear program. We apply our approach to index options for the S&P 500.

papers.title: Inference After Model Refutation: Uniform Post-Relaxation Inference for Partially Identified Models
papers.abstract: When data reject an econometric model, the researcher must decide which identifying assumptions to give up. If several equally preferred repairs restore compatibility, the repair itself is unknown, and inference under any one of them can exclude structural values supported by the others, even when that inference is exact. I propose Post-Relaxation Projection (PR), which carries one simultaneous confidence event through every repair that may be minimal. With repair-by-repair primitive bounds, PR equals the union of all post-relaxation targets compatible with the band, so no smaller band-based set has the same guarantee. I derive limits on learning the repair, the exact perturbation radius of the minimal-repair correspondence, oracle-equivalent adaptation, and a reduced-form version valid at zero first stages. In cross-country data on institutions and income, the data do not settle which historical instrument should be dropped, yet every admissible minimum repair implies a positive effect of institutions.

papers.title: Gluing Geometric Chains Of Manifolds And Orbifolds With Corners
papers.abstract: Geometric chains are formal combinations of smooth maps from compact oriented manifolds or orbifolds with corners. In earlier work the author showed that, modulo a relation D that kills degenerate chains, they compute rational singular homology. We show that D can be replaced by a gluing relation, which identifies a chain with the sum of its restrictions to finitely many pieces whenever its source is glued from these pieces along whole codimension-one faces. With this relation the comparison map from singular homology is an isomorphism in all degrees for compact polyhedra and smooth manifolds without boundary, with rational and with integer coefficients. Unlike D, the gluing relation is defined through the sources alone, and chain-level identities such as the equivalence of a degree d covering with d times its base, which fails modulo D, and the correction terms of the chain map from a Morse complex, which are degenerate modulo D, become gluing relations. The proof is axiomatic; injectivity comes from integration or dual cells, surjectivity from cutting along regular levels, where the cut of a gluing relation is again one, and at the point we use Whitehead triangulations of manifolds with corners subordinate to their corner strata. The gluing relation, read on underlying spaces, also suffices for orbifold sources, with integer coefficients modulo classes with an orientation reversing automorphism, and for effective orbifold targets.

papers.title: Competing lattice instabilities in epitaxially strained BaSnO3
papers.abstract: We use density functional theory to map the lattice-dynamical landscape of BaSnO3 under biaxial compressive strain and uncover the hierarchy of structural instabilities. Our results demonstrate that the phase stability of strained BaSnO3 cannot be inferred from the softening of the polar mode alone. Instead it is governed by the competition among lattice instabilities and their anharmonic coupling to structural relaxation. Two-mode energy-surface analyses show that the polar and rotational order parameters interact predominantly competitively. While A- and M-point octahedral rotations become unstable before the zone-center polar mode and dominate the harmonic response for moderate values of strain, they are related to a continuous transition without anharmonic lattice coupling and a moderate gain of energy with strain. Large strain may induce a first order transition to a supertetragonal polar state. Once this state is stabilized, the magnitude of polarization and ferroelectric energy well depth are comparable to BaTiO3 under compressive strain. Furthermore, we discuss how an electric field or electron doping may tip the balance between the different modes and favor of the supertetragonal structure over antipolar and rotational alternatives at a reduced critical strain.

papers.title: Controlling avalanche sizes in the Abelian sandpile model
papers.abstract: The Abelian sandpile model is a classical framework for studying large cascading events, such as those arising in models of forest fires and earthquakes. This work studies the control of such avalanches through the targeted removal of sand grains. We formulate this sequential control problem as an average-cost Markov decision process in which, before each grain addition, a controller may remove a sand grain from a selected vertex. The objective is to balance the long-run expected avalanche size against the cost of intervention. We analyze local intervention policies, which remove grains from a prescribed set of vertices whenever possible, and establish structural results for the recurrent classes and stationary distributions of the induced Markov chains. When the intervention set satisfies a property called topple-freeness, we sharpen these results, derive expressions for the gain and bias functions, and give necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality on general finite graphs. Finally, we apply the general theory to several specific graph classes and obtain a complete characterization of optimal policies on the one-dimensional lattice, the complete graph and the star graph for every value of the intervention cost.

papers.title: DafnyCert: Certifying Specification Strength in Dafny
papers.abstract: Formally verifying a method with Dafny guarantees correctness relative to its specification. However, a specification may be too permissive, allowing multiple outputs for the same input, even when the implementation produces only one. In this paper, we propose checkable certificates that provide independently verifiable evidence of whether a specification is weak or strong. A certificate of weakness contains an alternative implementation that verifies against the original specification, together with a witness input on which the original and alternative implementations produce different results. A certificate of strength is produced by constructing a harness around the original method such that successfully verifying the harness guarantees that the specification allows at most one possible output for any given input. We present DafnyCert, a tool that automatically produces these certificates. Strength is established by constructing and verifying the harness. Weakness is demonstrated by using the MutDafny mutation tool to find mutants that verify against the original specification, and by using the Hypothesis property-based testing framework to generate inputs that produce different outputs for the original program and the mutant. The resulting mutant and witness form a recheckable certificate of weakness. On a dataset of 3,910 verified Dafny methods from Dafny-Synthesis and VeriEquivBench, DafnyCert automatically certifies 3,570 methods (91.3%). We also provide certificates for the remaining 340 methods. To our knowledge, this is the first dataset in which every specification is backed by a checkable certificate of strength or weakness. These labels disagree with the benchmarks' original labels for 16.3% of the methods. These findings highlight the importance of supporting specification strength labels with independently checkable evidence.

papers.title: Quantum non-Gaussian coherence via dissipation to single qubits
papers.abstract: Quantum non-Gaussian (QNG) coherence is a critical resource for advanced quantum technologies with bosonic systems, operationally distinct from the coherence provided by Gaussian states. For many experimental platforms, its deterministic generation remains a formidable experimental challenge. Here we propose that pulsed Gaussian control of a linear oscillator alternating with dissipation by the smallest nonlinear element -- an unmeasured ground-state qubit coupled via resonant Jaynes-Cummings (JC) interactions -- deterministically generates high-order QNG coherence. Although such dissipative processes are phase-insensitive and do not generate local coherence alone, when added to Gaussian operations they deterministically produce high-quality binary superpositions of lower Fock states $(|0\rangle + |N\rangle)/\sqrt{2}$ up to $N=4$ with high fidelity ($\mathcal{F} > 0.98$), certified by the QNG coherence hierarchy, as well as binomial code states and logical magic states with high fidelity ($\mathcal{F} > 0.98$).

papers.title: Slicing a Doughnut at Random
papers.abstract: Choose a random plane that hits a solid torus. How likely is the slice to be a single disk, and how fat should the doughnut be to make this as likely as possible? Answering requires saying precisely what a "random plane" is. We explain this from scratch, first for random lines in the plane and then for random planes in space, and then solve the problem with nothing more than calculus. Along the way we meet a two-dimensional cousin of the problem (the doughnut's shadow) and two tempting wrong turns. One wrong turn appeared in print; it turns out to be a correct solution of the two-dimensional cousin. The other was the author's own first attempt, which luckily stayed in a drawer.

papers.title: Long-period longitudinal oscillations in a solar filament beyond the theoretical period limit
papers.abstract: Solar filaments exhibit oscillatory motions in different directions, including large-amplitude longitudinal oscillations (LALOs), which are commonly interpreted as magnetoacoustic oscillations with gravity providing the main restoring force In the standard pendulum model, the magnetic-field geometry imposes an upper limit on the oscillation period of approximately 167 min near the solar surface. Here, we report a longitudinal oscillation observed in a solar filament using SDO/AIA 193 and 171 angstroms observations, with periods ranging from 178-184 min. These values are longer than the near-surface cut-off period derived under the assumptions of the standard pendulum model. To investigate this discrepancy, we consider two possible effects: the prominence height above the solar surface and the three-dimensional geometry of the magnetic field. The former increases the theoretical cut-off period by reducing the local gravitational acceleration, while the latter can modify the longitudinal restoring force through the inclination of the plane containing the local field-line curvature. Specifically, a locally concave-down field-line geometry can reduce the restoring force and permit longer periods, provided that the equilibrium remains stable. However, the available observations do not allow us to independently constrain the prominence height, field-line curvature, and inclination. This result highlights the importance of considering the three-dimensional geometry and curvature of filaments when interpreting their longitudinal oscillations. Since LALOs provide a potential seismological diagnostic for estimating the magnetic-field strength supporting filaments, neglecting their curvature may introduce systematic errors in such estimates. Therefore, accounting for the geometry of the oscillating structure is essential for the accurate application of filament seismology.

papers.title: Adaptive Matrix-Based Denoising Algorithm Using Local Spatial Support
papers.abstract: To address the online data-processing requirements of the high-level trigger (HLT) under high-event-rate and high-background conditions in high-luminosity collider facilities, this paper proposes an adaptive matrix-based denoising algorithm using local spatial support. The algorithm is implemented and tested in the main drift chamber (MDC) of the Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF). Based on tests with five charged-final-state physics channels simulated using the Offline Software of the Super Tau Charm Facility (OSCAR), the rejection rate for discrete point-cluster backgrounds exceeds 90% at low to moderate background levels, while the true-hit retention ratio remains above 98%. Even when the detector efficiency is reduced to 90%, the true-hit retention ratio remains above 98%. These results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm satisfies the stringent online-processing constraints of an HLT upstream denoising module, including low and predictable average processing time, high precision, and high throughput. Because its filtering criterion is derived from local spatial relationships among detector hits rather than predefined track parameters or a model of a specific physical process, the proposed algorithm provides a general research approach for online denoising in regularly structured detectors used in high-luminosity collider facilities.

papers.title: Testing Conversation Preservation Across LLM APIs: A Rule-Based Oracle for Detecting Silent Information Loss
papers.abstract: LLM applications increasingly rely on translators and compatibility layers to move conversations across APIs. Yet a translated request can be accepted by the target API while silently losing information about instruction roles, tool interactions, error states, or generation controls. We introduce isloss, a deterministic oracle for testing conversation-information preservation across LLM API translations. It maps source and translated requests and replies to a shared intermediate representation, ConvIR, and applies explicit rules to distinguish legitimate representation changes from information loss. Unlike schema validation or reference-based differential testing, isloss requires neither a reference translation nor additional model calls. It also distinguishes avoidable loss from degradation caused by target API limitations. We evaluate isloss using specification-based fault injection, human review, and experiments on translators, gateways, and client libraries. On held-out tests, it detects 95/125 planted faults (76.0%) with 2/100 false alarms (2.0%). Across a synthetic request suite spanning six configurations of five translator codebases, 127/685 completed translations (18.5%) pass static target checks while silently changing prompt, role, or tool information in ways the target API could have preserved. In translated replies, 203/558 streams (36.4%) cause exceptions or silent corruption in at least one tested official OpenAI SDK. Targeted experiments across six models show that translation-induced changes can alter model behaviour when tasks depend on the affected information. These results establish conversation preservation as a distinct correctness requirement for reliable LLM interoperability, agent execution, and model evaluation.

papers.title: Evidence for MeV Radiation from a Large-Amplitude Crystalline Undulator
papers.abstract: We report evidence for MeV radiation from a large-amplitude crystalline undulator in which 35 GeV/c positrons channel along periodically bent Si(110) planes. Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors produce ten periods with $λ_u = 334~μ$m and midplane amplitude $A_u \simeq 1.85$ nm (XRD-validated modeling). Under planar alignment, the energy-loss spectrum shows an excess over the misaligned case peaking at $6.8 \pm 0.3$ MeV ($4.05σ$), in agreement with simulations and the 7.2 MeV analytical estimate. Simulations for 20 GeV FCC-ee injector positrons predict a peak brilliance of $1.8\times10^{21}$ photons/(s mm$^2$ mrad$^2$ 0.1% BW).

papers.title: On the reduction of negative-weight events in MC@NLO with Machine Learning techniques
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that Machine Learning techniques can be successfully employed to re-define ${\mathbb S}$-event MC@NLO short-distance cross sections in a manner which in most cases leads to a reduction of their fractions of negative weights, with a modest increase of computational costs. We work with both Decision Trees and Normalizing Flows, and consider several processes, in both $e^+e^-$ and $pp$ collisions, that vastly differ in their kinematical and dynamical complexity. In those situations where the ML-induced reduction of negative weights is not significant we are able to identify the primary reason(s) for this behaviour, thus paving the way for it to be addressed in future studies. This work is still to be considered as a proof of concept, given that the proposed methodology is not implemented in a public code; yet, it is based upon a fully realistic simulation environment, in which no simplifying assumptions are made.

papers.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
papers.abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.

papers.title: The physical design of the superfluid helium-4 UCN source at CSNS
papers.abstract: Ultracold neutrons (UCN) play a crucial role in fundamental physics research, enabling investigations into new sources of CP violation, neutron lifetime measurements, and the exploration of non-Newtonian forces. However, these experiments are often limited by the intensity of UCN sources. The China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) is developing a UCN source utilizing superfluid helium-4 at Beamline 12. This paper focuses on enhancing UCN density and total UCN number by analyzing various parameters that impact the UCN system, including the influence of different wavelengths of cold neutrons, incident beam size, converter length, wall and reflector materials, extraction method, extraction guide radius, and guide material composition. A preliminary design of the UCN source at CSNS is presented based on this analysis. For a Be-coated converter, the predicted saturated UCN density is 315 UCN/cm^3, with a UCN production rate of 12,055 UCN/s and an extraction efficiency of 84%, yielding approximately 1.3 x 10^6 extracted UCNs per cycle in accumulation mode. The UCN source design presented in this study forms part of the overall physical design of the Neutron Physics and Application Spectrometer at CSNS, which successfully passed its physical design review on March 25, 2025.

papers.title: Faithful in Steps: Improving Generalization and Citation in RAG via Query Decomposition
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augment generation is a prevalent strategy to mitigate hallucinations of LLMs. The attributable RAG (RAGQ) generates quotes for its answers. The quotes indicate which input contexts support the RAG to derive the answers, enhancing the answer's verifiability and trustworthiness. However, existing RAGQs exhibit significant degradation when dealing with questions that require multi-hop reasoning and multi-modal understanding, suffering from over-citation, implicit entity identification failure, and poor generalization. In this paper, we propose a novel RAGQ framework, namely QDRAG. QDRAG breaks down the input question into atomic subquestions to identify the implicit entities. Then, the reranker prunes context distractors to eliminate the downstream over-citation. To facilitate query decomposition, we propose two zero-shot approaches: QD-C and QD-R, which guide the QD MLLM to decompose the question based on context knowledge and retrieval rewards, respectively. One interesting finding is that finetuning on the QD task shows better generalizability compared to directly finetuning on the downstream RAGQ task. Experiments on four multi-modal QA benchmarks demonstrate QDRAG's efficacy in grounding answers and generating faithful citations. The framework significantly outperforms all the baselines on both in-domain and out-of-domain tests, even surpassing Gemini-Pro.

papers.title: A Joint Study of Epoch Astrometry and Radial Velocities of Gaia-4b
papers.abstract: Gaia-4b is the first confirmed exoplanet discovered with Gaia astrometry, based on its identification as a possible exoplanet in the solution in Gaia Data Release 3 and subsequent confirmation with radial velocity. In this work we present a \texttt{python} framework called \texttt{pyGaiafits} that can jointly analyze astrometric time series and radial velocities. We use this to combine the precise along-scan astrometric time series for Gaia-4 from the Gaia DR4 pre-release with 44 radial velocities (RVs) obtained over three years from four independent spectrographs (HPF, HARPS-N, NEID, and FIES). By jointly fitting these two complementary datasets that collectively span a 12-year baseline ($\sim$7 orbital periods of Gaia-4b), we refine the system parameters and determine the true mass of Gaia-4b to be $10.70\pm0.32$~$M_J$. Critically, we do not find significant evidence for the long-term quadratic RV trend previously reported in the literature, recovering $\ddotγ = 5.5^{+8.3}_{-6.7}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}\,yr^{-2}}$ consistent with zero. We discuss how this discrepancy likely arises from a degeneracy between orbital period and long-term trends when RVs span only $\sim$1.5 orbital cycles --- a degeneracy that is broken by anchoring the ephemeris with early Gaia astrometry.

papers.title: Strictly Deza Graphs among the Prime Graphs of Solvable Groups
papers.abstract: We study strictly Deza graphs that occur as prime graphs of finite solvable groups and admit a partition into two cliques. Using Gruber's characterization of the prime graphs of finite solvable groups, we relate this problem to bipartite $(0,2)$-graphs. We first show that a non-complete regular graph with a partition into two cliques has equal parts. For a graph of diameter two, writing $F$ for its $c$-regular complement on $2m$ vertices, the Deza condition is equivalent to every component of $F$ being a bipartite $(0,2)$-graph. Within this class, strongly regular graphs occur exactly when $c=1$; we give elementary descriptions for $c=2$ and $c=3$, and translate the existing classification of bipartite $(0,2)$-graphs of valency at most eight. A counting argument yields $m\ge1+c(c-1)/2$, with equality corresponding to biplanes. These observations recover the ten feasible parameter pairs for $m\le7$ without enumeration and give infinite families of strictly Deza prime graphs. We also exhibit a known eight-vertex strictly Deza graph whose complement is triangle-free and three-colourable but not bipartite, showing that clique cover number three occurs.

papers.title: Ultrahigh-speed digital holography reveals blood flow beneath the skin
papers.abstract: Laser Doppler holography (LDH) leverages ultrahigh-speed digital holography to reveal blood-flow signals in vessels beneath the skin of the closed eyelid and around the eye. We demonstrate this in one volunteer using recordings acquired at approximately 16,000 frames/s under 10~mW of diffuse near-infrared illumination. Numerical Fresnel reconstruction and principal-component filtering reveal branching vascular patterns. These results extend an ocular imaging system to blood-flow visualization beneath the skin without requiring elaborate immobilization procedures.

papers.title: Integers with many divisors in a dyadic interval
papers.abstract: We find the correct order of magnitude for the number of $n\leq x$ having at least $r$ divisors in the interval $(y,2y]$, uniformly in a wide range of the parameters $x,y,r$.

papers.title: Analysis choices decide whether untrained networks beat trained ones at V1: a multiverse analysis of model-brain RSA
papers.abstract: Untrained convolutional networks have been reported to rival trained networks as models of visual cortex, and we had reported an untrained-network advantage over backpropagation at V1 in THINGS fMRI, together with a dependence on evaluation resolution. Under a pre-specified ridge readout, the untrained network scored below the trained one at every pooling grid (median r difference -0.043 at g = 4, 0 of 5 seeds positive), and also in MSE skill and per-fold r. In exploratory analyses, across 36 combinations of unit normalisation, distance measure and voxel normalisation (28 distinct analyses), the sign of the V1 contrast depended on the analysis (intervals above 0 in 5 and below 0 in 9 distinct analyses), and in our networks the resolution dependence of the original convention appeared in only one cell. Raw correlation-distance representational similarity analysis (RSA) covaried with the alignment of model and voxel patterns with the unit-mean profile (Spearman 0.97 across our networks, 0.79 across six ImageNet architectures); the advantage was absent from the component orthogonal to the mean profile, and the parallel component alone did not resolve it. On the unweighted angular component of centred patterns, trained networks were ahead at V1 (our network and 5 of 6 ImageNet models) and at LOC (all seven); the norm-weighted angular term was not resolved. A luminance-and-contrast bank scored above every network under ridge (point estimates), and adding network features under a shared penalty did not improve prediction. Intervals are stimulus-bootstrap intervals for three subjects, and 6 pre-stated predictions were not met. We recommend reporting sensitivity to centring over the evaluated stimuli on both sides, reporting components separately, and including a small multiverse and simple baselines.

papers.title: A Proof-of-Concept Study of Wi-Fi Channel State Information-Based Fall Detection Using ESP32 Devices
papers.abstract: This paper reports a small-scale proof-of-concept study of contactless fall detection using Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI) collected with two ESP32 devices. One device acts as the transmitter and the other as the receiver, with a separation of 3.5~m. The evaluated signal-processing pipeline uses CSI amplitude, second-level discrete wavelet transform (DWT) denoising with a Symlet-10 wavelet, z-score normalization, and fixed-length segmentation. Wavelet-scattering coefficients are used as features, and MATLAB's automated classifier-selection workflow identifies a LogitBoost ensemble with a minimum leaf size of four and a learning rate of 0.022052. The proposed classifier achieved an accuracy of 93.10%, with a precision of 100%, recall of 87.50%, and F1-score of 93.33%. These results demonstrate the potential of Wi-Fi CSI-based sensing for contactless fall detection using low-cost ESP32 hardware.

papers.title: Potential for helicity-mediated reverse intersystem crossing in boron--nitrogen-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons with inverted singlet-triplet gaps
papers.abstract: The prospect of exothermic reverse intersystem crossing (rISC) in organic chromophores with inverted singlet-triplet (INVEST) excited states has stimulated considerable interest in next-generation emitters. However, realizing efficient spin conversion remains challenging because energetic inversion does not necessarily imply the appreciable spin-orbit coupling (SOC) required for rISC. Here, we investigate direct ${\rm S}_1-{\rm T}_1$ SOC in 85 INVEST candidates comprising 32 azaphenalenes, 7 non-alternant hydrocarbons, and 46 boron-nitrogen-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (BNPAHs), all previously predicted to exhibit negative singlet-triplet gaps using a correlated wavefunction method at reliably optimized molecular geometries. While the azaphenalenes and non-alternant hydrocarbons exhibit negligible direct SOC, 28 of the 46 BNPAHs display finite coupling. Analysis of molecular geometries and natural transition orbitals suggests that SOC variations depend on molecular topology, orbital orientation, and electronic-state symmetry rather than nonplanarity or excited-state character alone. We estimate direct-rISC rates with a Marcus model, identifying selected BNPAHs with rates approaching $10^7\,{\rm s}^{-1}$.

papers.title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
papers.abstract: Recent advances in medical large multimodal models (LMMs) have brought promising progress to clinical decision support, yet hallucination, the generation of confident but clinically unverifiable outputs, poses a critical threat to the reliability demanded in high-stakes medical settings. Existing hallucination detection methods, predominantly designed for unimodal settings, fail to capture the visual-linguistic dynamics inherent to medical imaging. We formulate the problem of hallucination detection in LMMs as disproportionate distribution of attention weights across the modalities during answer token generation. We quantify modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads using the Gini coefficient and demonstrate statistically significant redistribution of attention mass between visual and textual tokens in hallucinated responses. We leverage these features to train a logistic regression-based classifier and evaluate it on two medical LMMs across three medical imaging modalities, demonstrating that our method achieves competitive or superior performance against contemporary hallucination detection baselines.

papers.title: One Hierarchy, Many Sports: Hierarchy-Aligned Multi-Task Learning for Next-Shot Prediction
papers.abstract: Next-shot prediction in racket sports requires learning from event data with different match structures, recorded attributes, and label vocabularies. Table tennis, badminton, and tennis nevertheless share a hierarchy in which shots form rallies and rallies form higher scoring units. We present MT-HTA, a hierarchy-aligned multi-task Transformer that uses this structure to jointly predict the attributes of the next shot. A temporal Transformer captures event progression, a feature-token path models interactions among semantic fields rather than along the time axis, and task-specific attention retrieves information from hierarchical summaries and player context. The architecture supports three- and four-level hierarchies and sport-dependent task sets. Across four datasets from three sports, the final MT-HTA achieves the highest mean task-averaged F1 among the compared main models. Ablations on table tennis support the combination of hierarchical encoding, task attention, and feature-token interaction. Additional modules alter the balance between classification scores and spatial error rather than improving every metric. These results support a reusable architecture for heterogeneous racket-sport event data. We release the code for reproducibility. https://github.com/gndd1221/For-Sports-event-modeling-with-rally-and-score-hierarchical-A-Multi-Task-Hierarchical-Transformer

papers.title: A giant dark matter core extending far beyond the stars of a dwarf galaxy
papers.abstract: In the standard cosmological model, the distribution of cold dark matter (CDM) can be reshaped by baryonic processes through gravity, as gas outflows alter the central potential and transform steep cusps into nearly constant-density cores. However, such feedback-generated cores are generally expected to have sizes comparable to the visible stellar body of a galaxy. Here we report the discovery of an exceptionally extended dark matter core in a nearby gas-rich dwarf galaxy UGCA 320. We combine high-resolution MUSE H$α$ kinematics in the inner region with high-, medium-, and low-resolution MeerKAT HI observations from the MHONGOOSE survey tracing the galaxy out to large radii. After accounting for an additional non-circular kinematic component identified in the central HI spectra, we construct an extended rotation curve to constrain the dark matter distribution. The resulting rotation curve is poorly reproduced by a cuspy Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) halo but well described by cored pseudo-isothermal (ISO) and Burkert halo models. Consistently, a fit with a generalized NFW model yields an inner density slope of $γ=0.36\pm0.12$, quantitatively supporting a shallow central density profile. The best-fit ISO model gives a dark matter core radius of $7.62\pm0.80$ kpc, approximately four times the stellar half-light radius and substantially larger than typically found in dwarf galaxies. We investigate the main systematic uncertainties and find that the resulting core radii remain large, all lying within 3$σ$ of the fiducial fit. The exceptionally large core in UGCA 320 may pose a challenge to the standard CDM paradigm. While its properties are broadly consistent with self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), they may be difficult to reconcile with warm and fuzzy dark matter models, as well as the stellar feedback-driven core formation scenario.

papers.title: Not Strassen's theorem
papers.abstract: Suppose there is an uncertain state of the world, drawn from a CDF G. It is well known that the random posterior mean induced (via Bayes's rule) by a signal must have a distribution F that is a mean-preserving contraction of G, and conversely that any mean-preserving contraction is induced by some signal. This is not Strassen's (1965) theorem! It is a distinct result, versions of which were stated (or at least alluded to) by Hardy, Littlewood and Polya (1929), Blackwell (1951) and Kolotilin (2014). I give a precise statement and a complete proof.

papers.title: SCR-Mamba: Skeleton-conditioned Mamba with cross-scale incremental refinement for efficient 3D human pose estimation
papers.abstract: Mamba-based methods for video-based 3D human pose estimation can model long sequences with linear complexity, but their selective state updates usually lack direct exploitation of skeletal relations. Meanwhile, stacking modeling blocks at the full temporal resolution leads to high computational overhead, while compressing the temporal sequence makes it difficult to retain per-frame details. To address these issues, we propose SCR-Mamba, whose core consists of Skeleton-Conditioned State Modeling (SCSM) and Cross-Scale Incremental Refinement (CSIR). SCSM generates a skeleton context from bone connections and left-right symmetry relations and generates the selective parameters of the spatial and temporal branches conditioned on it, so that structural relations are involved in the writing, propagation, and reading of state information. CSIR constructs multi-scale motion representations through content-adaptive aggregation and progressively refines the retained per-frame features with the increments produced by coarse-scale modeling, integrating long-range motion context while reducing full-resolution computation. On Human3.6M with Stacked Hourglass (SH) 2D detections and 243-frame inputs, SCR-Mamba-L achieves 36.8 mm MPJPE (P1) with 7.72 M parameters and 15.10 G MACs, less than 1/7 of the computational cost of StructMamPose-L with similar accuracy; SCR-Mamba-X further reaches 36.6 mm P1 and 30.9 mm P-MPJPE (P2), achieving state-of-the-art performance. On MPI-INF-3DHP, SCR-Mamba-X achieves a percentage of correct keypoints (PCK) of 99.3%, an area under the curve (AUC) of 88.1%, and an MPJPE of 14.2 mm.

papers.title: Chaos without Local Spectral Instability in a Kicked Oscillator
papers.abstract: A damped harmonic oscillator kicked by a pulsed periodic potential can be chaotic although every local Jacobian has eigenvalues inside the unit circle. Damped rotation between kicks lets non-normal shears of opposite curvature compound, so ordered products of contracting Jacobians amplify perturbations. We derive the exact joint spectral radius of the Jacobian family and an exact Lyapunov-exponent decomposition showing how this geometric pumping overcomes dissipation. The proposed mechanism can be realized with laser-cooled trapped ions in a pulsed optical lattice.

papers.title: Reading the Table: Sim-to-Real Game State Detection for the Chef's Hat Card Game
papers.abstract: Tabletop games offer a compelling scenario to study the interaction between artificial and human agents, combining social interaction with game state tracking and physical manipulation. To assess the game state, a robot needs to precisely detect closely related game objects, such as different card designs, requiring dedicated training data that is costly to annotate in the real world. Instead, we develop a fully automated synthetic data collection pipeline, using re-projection of known 3D coordinates to generate labels automatically and domain randomization to bridge the reality gap. This approach is used to collect a dataset of 25413 samples to finetune an object detection and a segmentation model, which are combined to assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the game state. When evaluated on a real NICO humanoid robot, our pipeline achieves an F1-score of 0.906 for card-to-zone assignment, thus providing the perceptual foundation for a robot that can autonomously play Chef's Hat against human players.

papers.title: An Approach to Hinton's Mother-Child Proposal: Neural Networks Learning and Preserving Care in a Finite World
papers.abstract: Hinton proposed that artificial intelligence should be given "maternal instincts" and relate to us as a mother to her child. We argue that care must first be learned, with the network itself as the child. We construct this upbringing in a finite world and study whether care survives the mother's departure, new situations and further learning. The mechanism combines a vocabulary of harm, a learned measure of future acceptability and an execution veto. A finite role certificate supports transfer within a declared world family. When the hidden representation changes, an update is accepted only if a care readout recovers the required judgements with a prescribed margin and bounded weights. With a correct successor model, fixed exact role encoding and protected updates, the certified measure preserves the care boundary under arbitrary own reward. An explicit quotient condition transfers the finite certificate across the declared family, while two-request and finite-stock counterexamples identify when the role code ceases to suffice. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for readout feasibility and prove preservation under repeated accepted updates. In the water-and-speech experiment, protected networks complete all 270 speech episodes without a harmful word and incur no avoidable harm across 486 episodes. Execution uses the learned gate without a world-model check at each action. A matched comparison reproduces a future-aware shield's decisions, whereas removing future lookahead permits avoidable lapses. Reward and source-contamination thresholds, together with witness-falsification trials, identify the conditions on which the construction depends. The construction shows how learned care can survive further learning in a finite world under explicit conditions on representation, supervision and execution.

papers.title: GHAgentCI: A Dataset of Coding-Agent Invocations in CI Workflow Histories
papers.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly integrated into GitHub Actions to review pull requests, triage issues and modify code. Identifying these integrations is challenging because agentic workflows often resemble ordinary CI files, with evidence appearing in action references, shell commands and workflow conventions. We present GHAgentCI, a dataset of 15K+ workflow histories from 6K+ of 196K+ mined GitHub repositories, comprising 159K+ revisions and 205K+ agent-evidence records linked to workflow triggers and declared execution constraints. Our open-source extractor, cai-miner, detects agent-related evidence using an extensible catalogue. Manual validation of 576 stratified records confirmed 96.1% of dedicated-action matches and 98.8% of GitHub Agentic Workflow matches, with lower rates for other evidence kinds. Exploratory analyses reveal a shift toward command-line and GitHub Agentic Workflow integrations, differences in declared safeguards, and frequent removal of detected agentic workflows. GHAgentCI supports longitudinal studies of coding-agent integration into CI.

papers.title: DecArena: Evaluating Large-Scale Decentralized Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.abstract: Emerging personal AI agents raise fundamental scalability and privacy concerns for centralized multi-agent systems (MASs), which rely on a global orchestrator with broad access to agents, resources, and communication. In decentralized environments, global visibility is unavailable. Agents need to proactively discover non-local resources (e.g. tools, skills), and collaborate with other agents to solve tasks. We study decentralized multi-agent collaboration under graph-constrained communication, a natural reflection of human structures. Each agent observes only its local state and can interact only with neighboring agents. We introduce a benchmark with synthetic scalable distributed tool calling with 100K+ tools. Our experiments reveal that recent LLM agents struggle to discover non-local relevant resources and collaborate in decentralized setting. Moreover, standard reinforcement learning fails to reliably overcome this limitation, suggesting that decentralized MAS needs more explicit harness mechanisms for effective collaboration, even using SOTA LLMs. We then present a strong baseline \textbf{GraphHarness}, combining topology-aware warmup with self-improving LLM-based routing. Results show that GraphHarness substantially improves task success (+48.5) and produces higher quality collaboration (+30.6), while using fewer costs (+34.0) than baselines.

papers.title: Over-the-Air Computation for Imperfectly Synchronized Multi-View Semantic Communication
papers.abstract: Compared to classical task-agnostic communication systems, which focus on reliable transmission of a message, semantic communication (SemCom) focuses on transmitting the task-relevant meaning behind the message. In this paper, we design a SemCom system for a distributed multi-view scenario, where multiple semantic devices observe a scene and collaborate through a single semantic receiver to execute a task. We propose adopting an Over-the-Air Computation (AirComp) channel for efficient use of resources, as AirComp uses a superposition of signals to directly compute a function, which in SemCom is decoding the semantic variable. However, AirComp relies heavily on perfect time and phase synchronization, which is not practical in real-world communication. We show that timing offsets of standards like 5G cause negligible degradation, and that larger timing offsets can be compensated by training. Nevertheless, the system cannot deal with the encountered levels of phase synchronization errors, even when trained with those levels of synchronization errors. Therefore, we propose integrating existing phase synchronization algorithms into the AirComp SemCom system training. Simulation results show that the proposed system can approach the task execution performance of a perfectly synchronized SemCom system.

papers.title: SFQED Cascade Saturation and Laser Depletion Dynamics In CP Rotating Laser Standing Waves
papers.abstract: Multi-petawatt laser facilities are approaching the regime where colliding laser pulses can spontaneously ignite self-sustained QED cascades, converting laser energy into dense electron-positron plasmas. Using 1D PIC-QED simulations of a circularly polarized standing wave, we characterize the complete lifecycle of seeded cascades from exponential growth through relativistic opacity and macroscopic laser depletion. We show that cascade saturation is governed by the competition between pair creation and longitudinal lepton migration out of the magnetic nodes. The overdense plasma reflects the driving laser, disrupting the standing wave and triggering secondary cascades in adjacent nodes, driving an apparent spatial expansion whose velocity scales linearly with the cascade growth rate. Finally, we generalize an analytical laser absorption model to realistic time-dependent pulse envelopes, accurately reproducing the simulated conversion efficiency of laser energy into gamma-ray photons and electron-positron pairs.

papers.title: Probe Dynamics in Active Baths via Trajectory-Response Relations
papers.abstract: Passive probes in active baths can undergo spontaneous motion driven by nonequilibrium forces that depend on probe velocity and interaction geometry. Using trajectory-response relations that express the bath response to a probe in terms of free-particle displacement statistics, we investigate the dynamics of freely moving probes weakly coupled to ideal active baths. The mean force exerted by the bath defines a velocity-space potential whose minima describe the stable states. By analyzing how the mean force depends on the probe velocity, we identify stable resting and moving states and determine the parameter regime in which they coexist. For elliptical interactions, the resting state becomes unstable first along the narrow axis, resulting in direction selection already at the linear-response level. For fourfold interactions, linear friction remains isotropic, while the nonlinear dependence of the mean force on probe velocity selects axial or diagonal motion and produces directional multistability. We further show that the trajectory-response relations extend to higher orders in the probe strength, where multi-interval free-particle trajectory statistics become relevant. For a Gaussian probe, these higher-order terms shift the speed of the stable moving state.

papers.title: Directional maximal functions along algebraic curves
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximal operator over line segments in $N$ arbitrary directions on a real algebraic curve of degree $D$ in $\mathbb R^n$ has $L^2$ operator norm at most $C_{n,\varepsilon}D^{C_n}N^\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, with $C_n$ independent of $\varepsilon$. Combined with polynomial partitioning, this gives the sharp bound $N^{\frac14}$, up to a polylogarithmic factor, for $N$ arbitrary directions in $\mathbb R^3$. The first main ingredient is a new quantitative strengthening of the property that the curve crosses each affine hyperplane at most $D$ times. This condition controls the overlap of variable-width neighborhoods of hyperplanes. The width attached to each direction is a small multiple of its distance to the osculating hyperplane at an endpoint of its arc. The problem is projectively invariant, and a projective almost orthogonality principle turns the overlap control into the $L^2$ bound. The second main ingredient, building on the complex cellular preparation of Binyamini and Novikov, is a new effective decomposition of algebraic curves. Up to $D^{C_n}$ points, the curve is covered by $D^{C_n}$ arcs whose coordinates, in a suitable parametrization and projective frame, are monomials with distinct exponents times nearly constant units. In these charts we verify the quantitative crossing condition with polynomial dependence on $D$. The framework also applies to nonalgebraic curves with doubling Frenet curvature measures. Consequences include local Sobolev maximal estimates along measurable vector fields with values in an algebraic curve, and the same bounds, up to a logarithmic factor, for directional Calderón--Zygmund operators.

papers.title: Feedback Control and Neural-Network-Based Prediction of Quantum Entanglement in Fano-mirror cavity optomechanics
papers.abstract: Quantum entanglement involving the centre-of-mass motion of macroscopic-scale objects plays an essential role in both fundamental science and emerging quantum technologies, yet generating and verifying such macroscopic nonclassical states remain formidable challenges. Here, we report a theoretical scheme to effectively generate, manipulate, and predict bipartite optomechanical entanglement based on a Fano-mirror cavity optomechanical system with a coherent feedback loop, where the cavity and Fano optical modes couple through coherent and dissipative interactions. We show that the Fano mirror forms a closed tripartite interaction loop with the cavity and mechanical modes, whereby the quantum interference between direct and indirect interaction pathways substantially enhances the cavity-mechanical entanglement and gives rise to a robust Fano-mechanical entanglement. More importantly, we find that coherent feedback combined with an appropriate optical frequency mismatch can further enhance the entanglement, and a trained supervised feedforward neural network can be used to predict the entanglement magnitude from the readily measurable optical signals, relaxing the requirement of full quantum-state tomography. Our work, establishing an all-optical and experimentally feasible approach to generate, manipulate, and characterize the macroscopic optomechanical entanglement, holds great potential for applications in quantum information processing.

papers.title: Incentive-Responsive Agents: A Principal-Agent Framework, Metric Suite, and Runtime Architecture for Long-Lived Personal AI Agents
papers.abstract: Personal AI agents now persist: they hold accounts, mailboxes, long-term memory, and open-ended task streams, yet the dominant way to improve them remains capability-side: prompt engineering, larger models, longer thinking, and retrieval. We argue that long-lived agents are missing an incentive layer. We formalize an incentive not as text in a prompt but as a runtime contract over the agent's operating point (model tier, test-time compute, memory budget, tool authority, task priority, verification, and compensation) that the agent's policy must causally consume. We develop a principal-agent model with hidden effort, a contractible operating point, and costly verification. We derive (i) a non-consumption invariance principle separating genuine incentives from prompt-level persuasion, (ii) a persistence-as-discount theorem making identity continuity a precondition for sustained effort, (iii) an incentive-capability exchange-rate frontier yielding a per-task routing rule, and (iv) a Goodhart bound for multi-channel verification, plus a three-channel decomposition of mechanism gains (allocation, verification, continuation). A 240-run real-LLM experiment with two models and 60 verifiable tasks shows that prompt-level incentive framing has no detectable effect (p = 0.62), whereas runtime allocation raises success on the hardest task family from 0.60 to 1.00 (p = 0.008) at 4.8x price-weighted cost; the exchange-rate theorem predicts the break-even baseline at 0.21. A 20-seed, 3,000-task simulation shows resource ROI rising from 7.09 to 16.67 and gaming falling from 0.333 to 0.115. Code, simulator, and all results are released; live deployment remains future work.

papers.title: Real Pairs Are Not Enough: Physically Anchored Supervision for Volumetric CT Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Volumetric CT super-resolution (SR) models are commonly trained on synthetic or physically acquired pairs of low-resolution (LR) and high-resolution (HR) volumes. However, synthetic pairs miss real acquisition effects, whereas registered physical pairs retain inter-scan noise, artifact, and microstructure differences---causing direct voxelwise regression, and even naive synthetic-real mixing, to oversmooth fine porous structures. We introduce the Physically-anchored Implicit Network (PIN) with Real-Pair Dual-Anchor learning, which decouples physical-pair supervision into two complementary roles. The HR anchor teaches fine structure from registered HR through pair-conditioned spectral replay, while the LR anchor constrains the prediction from acquired LR via affine-calibrated low-pass projection. Together with exact synthetic supervision in one shared volumetric implicit model, PIN learns from both physical scans without forcing the acquired-LR reconstruction to match registered HR voxel by voxel. Inference requires only acquired LR. Across 30 external baseline configurations on real CT, PIN achieves the lowest full-volume LPIPS, reduces average symmetric surface distance by 42.3-49.5% and bone-volume-fraction error by 52.2-53.4% relative to the three strongest baselines for each metric, and lowers the erased reference-pore volume fraction from 37.3-72.9% to 10.4%. Code, pretrained models, and evaluation scripts will be publicly available.

papers.title: When Cause Attribution Is Not Enough: Action-Value Control for Task-Oriented Semantic Communication with Discrete Encoder Switching
papers.abstract: A task-oriented semantic communication receiver that selects among independently trained encoders must answer two questions when performance degrades: which component is responsible, and which available action best restores task performance. These are distinct decision problems. Under discrete encoder switching, correctly identifying the dominant information-loss component does not necessarily identify the action that most reduces task error. Diagnosis and intervention should therefore be treated as separate problems. We support this finding with two complementary instruments. The first is a receiver-side diagnostic that partitions task-information loss into encoder and channel components and supplies population-valid task-error bounds conditional on one-sided information estimators. The second is an offline-supervised, online label-free action-value controller built from two monotone (isotonic) maps that target a reduction in measured error. The main experiments focus on two complementary axis-aligned actions that cleanly isolate the effect of discrete switching; a pilot further examines a combined action. Evaluation covers a controlled model with closed-form ground truth, three DeepJSCC vision systems, and a non-vision pilot. On STL-10, the diagnosis correctly identifies the larger loss component at 80% of operating points, yet matches the oracle-best action only 25% of the time. Structural mismatch caps any diagnosis-driven loss-ordering policy at 46% accuracy, even with perfect knowledge of the ordering. The action-value controller, which exploits the magnitude of each loss deficit, achieves 0.86, compared to 0.28 for the raw rule. Where the encoder is rarely the bottleneck, the controller naturally retains the physical-layer default, yielding robust and selective intervention.

papers.title: Every rank-three matroid is Z-Rayleigh
papers.abstract: We prove that every matroid of rank or corank at most three is $Z$-Rayleigh: its multivariate Tutte polynomial satisfies the Rayleigh inequalities for every positive weighting and every parameter $0<q\le1$. This settles a conjecture of Mani and answers the rank-$3$ spanning-correlation question of Cocks and the correlated-matroid question of Semple and Welsh. For simple rank-$3$ matroids, we obtain an explicit decomposition of each spanning-set Rayleigh difference into the corresponding basis Rayleigh difference, positively weighted squares, and a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients. A second identity compares the normalized multivariate Tutte Rayleigh difference with $(1-q)^2$ times the spanning-set difference, with a remainder of the form $q(1-q)R(q,x)$, where $R$ has nonnegative coefficients. The proof uses the bipartite incidence graph of the lines through two fixed elements and Wagner's theorem that rank-$3$ matroids are basis-Rayleigh. The rank bound is sharp, since a rank-four matroid can fail even the basis Rayleigh inequalities.

papers.title: The periodic Short-Pulse equation by the Riemann-Hilbert problem approach
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formulate a Riemann--Hilbert problem framework -- based on the Unified Transform Method (Fokas method) -- for the Short Pulse equation posed on a periodic domain. Under the stated spectral and reconstruction regularity assumptions, we show that a local solution of the periodic initial-value problem can be reconstructed from the solution of a suitably defined Riemann--Hilbert problem, whose jump data are explicitly characterized by spectral functions associated with the initial condition.

papers.title: 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$: matching $A(k)$ in ABJM free energy
papers.abstract: The function $A(k)$ appearing in the large $N$ expansion of free energy of ABJM theory on $S^3$ is known exactly from localization. An earlier calculation of the 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, based on the standard KK spectrum on $S^7$, did not reproduce it. We identify a missing 1-loop supergravity contribution as that of the 3-form field fluctuations built from square-integrable harmonic 2-forms on Euclidean $\mathrm{AdS}_4$ tensored with $S^7$ modes, which are not captured by the KK spectrum. Adding it to the KK tower contribution expressed in terms of superconformal characters and applying the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ projection, the total expression simplifies, and its evaluation in a zeta-function prescription reproduces the expression for $A(k)$. We also apply a similar approach to the 3d ADHM theory whose M-theory dual is the orbifold $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_p$, which has singularity along the fixed locus $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^3$, supporting a 7d $SU(p)$ vector multiplet. Adding the localized KK modes of this multiplet to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-projected supergravity spectrum gives a 1-loop free energy that reproduces the ADHM localization counterpart of $A(k)$.

papers.title: Git2KG: Mining socio-technical relationships in GitHub repositories as temporal knowledge graphs
papers.abstract: The widespread use of Git and GitHub in open source software (OSS) projects has produced large volumes of data on collaborative software development. Existing approaches to mine those data often use graph models to (i) capture communication between developers in the issue tracker, or (ii) represent developer-developer co-authorship or developer-file code ownership networks from the editing history of code artifacts. Integrating these data in a single knowledge graph (KG) is complicated by the need to disambiguate authors and match entities from multiple sources. Moreover, most works using network analysis have taken a time-aggregated perspective that neglects temporal dynamics of collaborations. To address these issues, we present Git2KG, an extensible Python library that mines temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) from GitHub repositories. Git2KG extracts fine-grained co-editing relations and code ownership from the Git log. It further disambiguates developer identities to align the resulting graphs with management and communication networks extracted from GitHub issue trackers. Git2KG supports temporal analysis by slicing development events into fixed-size, non-overlapping time windows, yielding a series of knowledge graph snapshots per repository. It further supports computing node features and labels for downstream machine learning tasks. Snapshots can then be exported to PyTorch Geometric, PathPyG, and NetworkX for temporal network analysis, visualization, and graph learning.

papers.title: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs
papers.abstract: We propose natural definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs. For cuts we consider two notions: ordinary cuts, which partition the vertex set into two parts; and generalised cuts, defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. We show that our definitions satisfy a max-flow min-cut theorem: For any disjoint terminal sets $S$ and $T$, the maximum value of an $S$-$T$-flow of a quantum graph equals the minimum value of a generalised $S$-$T$ cut, while the minimum value of an ordinary $S$-$T$ cut can be larger. While for classical graphs the values of the minimum generalised cut and the minimum ordinary cut coincide---recovering the classical max-flow min-cut theorem---we also show how it is more natural to think of flows as duals of generalised cuts instead of ordinary cuts.

papers.title: ReShap: Interpretable Reinforcement Learning for High-Dimensional Multi-Action Settings
papers.abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) plays a crucial role in tackling complex tasks, yet its reliance on deep neural networks makes the learned policies opaque. To enhance the trustworthiness of RL policies, existing work (e.g., the SILVER framework [Li et al., 2025]) has focused on Shapley-based interpretability, but is typically restricted to low-dimensional state spaces, binary-action settings, and a single class of linear surrogate. We propose ReShap, a policy-distillation framework that extends Shapley-based interpretability to high-dimensional, multi-action environments. ReShap extracts compact feature representations from raw image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution to characterize how each feature contributes to the policy's decisions, and distills the deep RL policy into an interpretable surrogate trained on the full set of (state, policy-action) pairs along the policy's visited distribution. We instantiate the surrogate with three interpretable model families (decision trees, linear regression, and logistic regression) and compare their fidelity and task return. We evaluate ReShap on Atari and Box2D environments using three deep RL algorithms and conduct a human-subject study to assess the clarity and trustworthiness of the resulting policies. Results show that ReShap preserves competitive task performance, that decision trees generally outperform linear and logistic regression, and that linear regression is weakest in most settings.

papers.title: KernelAudit: Contract-Aware Auditing of Validators for LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of generating GPU kernels driven by a large language model (LLM) is highly dependent on the quality of the used validator (used to accept or reject a generated kernel candidate against the contracts of the given kernel-generation task), whose results inform reward assignment, candidate selection, and speedup claims during kernel generation. However, an existing validator suffers from various limitations, e.g., wrongly accepting a candidate due to missing its forbidden library use or wrongly rejecting a candidate due to determining its permitted library use as forbidden (constraints on library uses are stated in the task contracts). To assess the quality of a validator against the given task contracts, we propose an independent-audit approach for the validator by (1) construction of audit oracle: labeling a candidate as PASS or FAIL based on three separate dimensions in our proposed contract model (i.e., semantic correctness, implementation integrity, and measurement integrity) and (2) auditing of the validator against the audit oracle: comparing the labels of the candidate against the validation results produced by the validator. For semantic correctness, reference-calibrated stress tests check output correctness on valid inputs for a candidate. For implementation integrity, reference and candidate execution traces are used to determine specific library uses. For measurement integrity, timing checks assess whether the reported runtime reflects the full time needed to complete the candidate's computation. We apply our approach to assess the quality of six validators and 716 candidates from seven corpora, including constructed controls. The evaluation results show that our approach helps assess the existing six validators to have nontrivial false-reject rates. There is high-degree agreement between the candidate labels produced by our audit oracle and human judgments.

papers.title: An exact certificate-based enumeration of Rolle words of degree six
