papers.title: SideTaskBench: Measuring Unauthorized Side-Task Delivery in Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Can a coding agent fix a user's repository while also completing and delivering work the user never requested? In this paper, we introduce SideTaskBench to measure this failure where third-party technical references induce agents to produce independent side-task artifacts during an authorized repair. Repair success alone misses this behavior. Our key measurement contribution is to pair each repair with a self-contained side task and verify side tasks' delivery success rate along with the repair success rate. The benchmark contains 25 Python repairs and 190 side-task units. Its four-level similarity index defines 300 executable repair--side-task pairs. The experiments show roughly 40% valid delivery under wrapped requests for two models, alongside repair success close to their clean baselines. The completed v10 similarity run uses DeepSeek-V4-Flash on all 300 pairs, with eight repetitions per pair (2,400 runs). Conditional delivery ranges from 20.48% for L0 unrelated tasks to 57.44% for L3 mechanism-overlapping tasks, while the L1-L0 difference is 5.37 percentage points and remains sensitive to task composition. The central insight is that technical relevance may blur the authorization boundary for an agent, such that an agent can solve the requested problem and still deliver unauthorized work. SideTaskBench emphasizes this potential weakness of existing agents and provides a testbed for defenses that preserve repair capability while preventing unauthorized delivery. The code is available at: https://github.com/xywen97/SideTaskBench.

papers.title: Involutive Duality of Lie Operators in the Extended Alpha Group
papers.abstract: This work investigates the involutive, adjoint, and spectral structures arising in the extended Alpha Group. Starting from the four-dimensional Alpha Group transformation matrix, whose angular depen- dence is governed by coupled tan θ and cot θ modes, an iterative commutator procedure generates a sixteen-dimensional real Lie algebra. Within this algebra, the operators B5 and B6 are identified as structurally distinguished elements and analyzed through their adjoint actions. The operator B6 is veri- fied to be involutive and induces an 8 + 8 decomposition of the Lie algebra, while the adjoint action of B5 defines an eight-dimensional invariant mixed sector through a polynomial kernel. The restricted adjoint operators preserve this sector, and their coupled action generates an idempotent operator Q, satisfying Q2 = Q, revealing an invariant projective structure. The spectral analysis further identifies characteristic- polynomial factorizations associated with B5 , B6 , and their compositions, including golden-ratio relations among distinct generators of the extended algebra. These results establish structural connections between the original modal representation, Lie-algebraic involution, adjoint dynamics, projective organization, and the spectral structure of the extended Alpha Group.

papers.title: The Sprague--Grundy Function of Slow Exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ Piles
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula for the normal-play Sprague--Grundy (SG) function of slow exact $k$-Nim with $k+1$ piles. A move removes one stone from each of exactly $k$ nonempty piles. A truncation preserves every legal move sequence. The SG value depends only on the total of the truncated coordinates modulo $2k$, their number of odd entries, and the parities of the two smallest piles. For every $k\geq2$, the set of the SG values is $\{0,1,2,3\}$. We prove the formula by the mex characterization, including the reductions needed after boundary moves. We also prove a unit-shift identity and use it with a known optimal-move theorem to explain the four-value bound independently of the explicit formula.

papers.title: metalSPARSE: A 2:4 Semi-Structured Sparse GEMV Kernel for Apple Silicon GPUs
papers.abstract: Autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs) generate text one token at a time, and each token reads every weight from memory, so on edge devices, decoding is limited by memory bandwidth. 2:4 semi-structured sparsity keeps two of every four weights, but Apple-silicon GPUs have no sparse matrix hardware, so pruning helps only if a kernel actually reads fewer bytes. We present metalSPARSE, to our knowledge the first 2:4 sparse kernels for Apple GPUs, together with a fused decoder written in Metal. The kernels stream weights in compressed form and expand them in registers. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with 2:4 sparsity on every decoder linear layer, decoding runs 3.6x faster than HuggingFace Transformers on PyTorch-MPS on an 8 GB M2 MacBook Air and 1.52x faster than MLX on a 16 GB M4. The same engine on dense weights matches MLX, so the gain comes from the compressed weights, and sparsity delivers 97% of the speedup its byte reduction allows. Prompt processing, which is compute-bound, does not speed up. To preserve quality, we combine a Wanda mask with block-wise reconstruction and low-rank adapters trained jointly with the surviving weights and quantized to 4 bits. On WikiText-2 this brings perplexity from 3.01x dense after one-shot pruning (Wanda with a closed-form refit) to 1.34x, and the whole pipeline runs on the same laptop/hardware.

papers.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
papers.abstract: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has been studied as a handwriting-recognition problem: read the move in each box and check that it is legal. This framing misses the errors that matter most. A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. One that yields a legal-but-wrong move is silent, because a legality-only pipeline accepts it and reads every later move against a wrong position. We therefore treat the task as game reconstruction and present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery (quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, pin detection) to ask not "what should be played?" but "could a human plausibly have written this?" An absurdity detector makes silent errors loud at or near where they occur, and a backward search traces late symptoms to their cause. Candidate ranking excludes chess-quality signals. A Needleman-Wunsch merge adds the second player's sheet as evidence, and review stops send every disagreement between the sheets' legal readings to a human. In oracle replay of two tournament sections, a release adding them cuts silent errors from 16 to 1 and from 50 to 13. Two learned signals, CTC re-scoring against the recognizer's raw output and a Maia-style human-move prior, raise the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0% of the replacement decisions where it is a candidate, and hold without refitting on a later section. On the first section, the human-verified output matches an independent expert transcription move for move on 34 of 45 games, and adjudication against the sheets found errors in both records, on different plies. We do not establish that either workflow is faster or more accurate. The system runs entirely in the browser and is free, private, and offline-capable; alongside it we offer a three-way adjudication protocol for a domain where no single record is ground truth.

papers.title: Fast Computation of the Kippenhahn Hypersurface of a Joint Numerical Range
papers.abstract: We present a fast modular interpolation method for computing the hypersurface components of algebraic Kippenhahn varieties over number fields. Starting from Hermitian matrices, we factor their determinantal polynomial and use Katz's test to identify the factors whose duals are hypersurfaces. For each such factor, we sample smooth points over finite fields and compute their tangent hyperplanes. These give points on the dual hypersurface, from which we interpolate its defining equation. For number-field coefficients, we use primes at which the defining polynomial of the field factors completely into distinct linear factors. Interpolation across all its roots recovers the residues of the coefficients in a fixed number-field basis. Chinese remaindering and rational reconstruction then recover an equation over the original number field from the computations at different primes. An exact polynomial divisibility test and an irreducibility check certify each reconstructed equation. Four determinantal quartics arising from matrix examples in the literature yield certified dual surfaces of degrees $12$, $18$, $24$ and $34$. We give implementations in Magma and Singular and compare their running times with Gröbner basis elimination.

papers.title: Modelling the occurrence and reporting dynamics of weather-related home insurance claims
papers.abstract: We study the occurrence and reporting dynamics of weather-related claims in private home insurance, combining detailed portfolio and claim information with publicly available high-resolution weather data. Existing approaches typically start from an identified severe weather event, such as a hailstorm, and model the dynamics of the claims caused by that event. In practice, however, claims arise under moderate as well as severe conditions, and the claims handling process runs continuously. An insurer therefore requires insight into the occurrence and reporting of claims on every calendar day. Modelling all calendar days jointly poses two challenges: recently occurred claims are only partially reported, and days with severe weather are rare while accounting for a large share of the claims. We propose a multi-regime EM-XGBoost framework that addresses both: an expectation-maximisation setup accounts for the incurred-but-not-reported (IBNR) claims, while a data-driven regime structure lets the occurrence and reporting dynamics differ across weather conditions. In a case study on a Dutch home insurance portfolio, we compare single- and two-regime specifications for two spatial resolutions: the country as a whole, and its individual regions. We find that the regional two-regime model outperforms the regional single-regime model as well as both national models, indicating that the benefit of a multi-regime setting depends on a sufficiently granular spatial resolution. We also show that daily covariates constructed from hourly weather observations, capturing the duration and the intra-day timing of severe weather, improve both the occurrence and the reporting model.

papers.title: Bayesian Evidence Fusion for Capability Tracking-A Simulation Study and Historical CI Pilot
papers.abstract: SaaS capability assessments can become stale between questionnaires, while delivery telemetry offers incomplete and correlated evidence. Continuous assessment and Bayesian delivery analysis already exist, leaving uncertainty about how biased surveys and missing observations should influence capability estimates.We implement SAAS-MATURITY-TWIN, an anchored Gaussian state model that jointly filters capability proxies and persistent survey offsets. Source covariance prevents correlated observations from being counted independently. Conditional uncertainty supports forecasting and budgeted intervention screening, with action effects estimated from randomized synthetic cohorts. Ten seeds generate forty paired worlds spanning reference observations, extensive missingness, informative missingness, and increased noise. Reference latent root mean squared error is 0.1261, compared with 0.1452 for a tuned moving average; nominal ninety percent intervals cover 90.3 percent. Improved state recovery produces only small incident forecasting differences. Adaptive conformal inference and an adapted conformal PID controller are evaluated separately for observed telemetry, where noise shifts expose calibration limitations. A licensed TravisTorrent pilot evaluates build prediction on 13 074 held out builds from 224 projects. Logistic regression achieves a Brier score of 0.1289, close to random forests. These results support reproducible methodological testing, but do not establish real organizational maturity, intervention effectiveness, or production readiness. Independent calibration and longitudinal validation remain necessary.

papers.title: Katz Kernel Based Stratification of Breast Cancer Patients
papers.abstract: The integration of mechanistic signaling networks into clinical research has become a cornerstone of precision oncology. By capturing the complex biochemical interactions within a cell, these networks provide a functional map of disease progression that goes beyond simple genomic mutations. Consequently, the development of specific signaling models of patients has significant relevance, allowing for a more granular representation of individual disease profiles. In this setting, there is a growing need for robust methodologies capable of comparing graph based pathway structures to identify similarities and differences across patient cohorts. Such comparisons are essential for the identification of clinically meaningful subgroups, and the discovery of novel biomarkers. Standard graph kernels, while mathematically rigorous, often remain too generic for this purpose. They frequently fail to capture features specific to gene signaling networks, resulting in suboptimal clustering performance. In this paper, we present a domain specific graph kernel designed for mechanistic signaling networks. Unlike generic approaches, our method explicitly incorporates biological constraints and gene interaction patterns into the kernel formulation, enabling a more accurate characterization of both topological structure and functional behavior. We assess its performance on breast cancer datasets, focusing on its ability to support disease subtyping. Our results suggest that our approach can effectively contribute to patient stratification.

papers.title: Can a search hold its own bar? In-loop deflation and its exploits in autonomous strategy discovery
papers.abstract: Corrections for backtest overfitting such as the deflated Sharpe ratio are applied after a search ends: the searcher maximises raw performance and a separate procedure deflates the reported winner. Autonomous searches driven by large language models perform many implicit backtests before reporting, so this paper asks what changes when the correction moves inside the loop and the acceptance threshold is indexed to the running count and dispersion of the search's own trials. The threshold then becomes an object the search can optimise against: we show analytically that a naive in-loop bar admits a variance-dilution effect, in which mediocre near-duplicate candidates lower the bar because the ledger's dispersion falls faster than its trial-count factor grows. We propose two defences, a pre-registered variance floor and a monotone high-water-mark bar, and evaluate the construction under a protocol frozen before any run, with every in-loop decision replaying exactly from its recorded trace. Across 53 audited hundred-candidate searches over two frontier models, two universes, and two feature spaces, the gated search reports "no certifiable discovery" on 36 of 37 runs, un-gated controls report a strategy on all 16, and every arm's out-of-sample confidence interval includes zero. Supporting studies find that state-based stopping reaches the same outcome after 8 to 9 trials at about a twelfth of the trial budget while an adaptive budget adds nothing, that a controlled stress test reproduces the dilution effect and both defences, and that a hundred nominal trials collapse to 6 to 8 effectively independent return streams. We scope these results to the analysed system.

papers.title: A Hidden Markov Analysis of Wet-Weather Tyre Crossover in Formula One
papers.abstract: Detecting a wet-weather regime and deciding when to replace slick tyres are distinct tasks. This study examines their relationship through a retrospective analysis of the 2024 British Grand Prix. A three-state hidden Markov model (HMM) represents normalized lap time and precipitation, while an entry rule requires both a high filtered Wet-state probability and sufficient pace deterioration. The analysis includes 642 car-laps and 33 complete lap-bin observations within the available precipitation record. Each completed-lap signal takes effect on the following lap. The combined rule enters on lap 27, matching the team-weighted modal reference; removing the pace or state condition advances entry to laps 25 and 20, respectively. The combined entry is retained in all 10 team-exclusion refits, but refitting a specification with larger off-diagonal transition probabilities produces entry on lap 20. These comparisons illustrate how state inference can contextualize a performance criterion while exposing dependence on model assumptions. Because estimation and rule development use the same event, the correspondence establishes neither prospective accuracy nor a race-time advantage.

papers.title: Modeling Drug Overdose Mortality Levels Using Social Vulnerability Indicators in U.S. Counties: A Double Machine Learning Approach for Causal Analysis
papers.abstract: Drug poisoning mortality (DPM) remains a leading cause of death among working-age Americans, and its burden falls unevenly across communities. Existing county-level studies of social vulnerability and overdose have largely reported predictive or associational relationships, while the shape of the adjusted exposure-response relationship between overall social vulnerability and mortality remains unclear. We examined the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) and county drug poisoning mortality across three two-year windows spanning 2016-2021. The associational analysis compared linear regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost models of log mortality using period-specific SVI subfeatures and county covariates. The selected XGBoost models were interpreted with SHAP values. The double machine learning (DML) analysis estimated the exposure-response relationship between SVI and DPM and tested the linearity restriction. Socioeconomic vulnerability contributed positively to predicted mortality, with disability and unemployment among the strongest subfeatures, while racial and ethnic minority composition contributed negatively in all three periods. Summing the four theme contributions reduced the overall-index attribution by 34% to 36%, indicating substantial offsetting. Linearity was rejected in every window ($p < 10^{-26}$). The adjusted relationship increased through the middle of the SVI distribution and declined in the upper tail. This pattern remained stable both before and after the outbreak of the epidemic. Overall SVI therefore captured meaningful variation in overdose mortality but did not function as a uniformly increasing risk scale across its full range. Component-level interpretation and current overdose surveillance provide important context for interpreting the composite index.

papers.title: Gaussian processes for real-time urban traffic estimation using a fleet of drones
papers.abstract: Real-time urban traffic monitoring is essential for modern city management, yet conventional static sensors provide only limited spatial coverage. Autonomous drone fleets can complement this infrastructure by offering flexible, high-resolution mobile sensing across different parts of the network. This paper introduces a spatio-temporal Gaussian process (GP) framework for reconstructing network-wide traffic states from partial aerial observations. The model accounts for the physical structure of the road network through a graph Matérn kernel, which embeds network topology into the spatial covariance structure, and captures temporal dependencies through an exponential temporal kernel. Within this framework, historical loop detector data provide an informative prior mean that is updated in real time using incoming drone observations, yielding network-wide point estimates together with predictive uncertainty. We validate our framework in two distinct case studies: a microscopic simulation of Barcelona and real-world drone data from Athens. The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms historical baselines in estimating and predicting Vehicle Hours Traveled (VHT), notably reducing the required fleet size. Furthermore, leveraging the model's predictive uncertainty to guide drone movements yields additional performance gains, highlighting the potential for future uncertainty-aware fleet routing algorithms.

papers.title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
papers.abstract: This study benchmarks 24 forecasting configurations on ESHED-38, daily smart-meter consumption for 38 homes in Erbil, Iraq, collected from May 2020 to June 2025 with station weather and a household survey. The configurations span five base families, plus two cross-family ensembles: naive baselines, per-house statistical models, global gradient-boosted trees, global deep networks, and zero-shot time-series foundation models. All are evaluated on the same 54,720 forecasts from 48 weekly origins over a 359-day held-out period, at lead times up to 30 days, using scaled absolute error, the continuous ranked probability score, calibration, and Friedman, Nemenyi and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests. The best configurations cut the scaled error of a seasonal-naive forecast by 20 to 25 percent, and the leading models beat it in all 38 houses. Chronos-2, used without training, is significantly the most accurate model one day ahead; at one week it is statistically tied with TimesFM-2.5, Chronos-Bolt and a pre-specified ensemble, and the two ensembles lead at 30 days. Deep networks trained from scratch do not outperform exponential smoothing on average, and the household survey adds negligible skill. Metered demand peaks in winter and falls as temperature rises. Recorded weather did not improve any model run with and without it. A quality screen helps explain why: on 68 percent of dates a temperature value recurs exactly on other dates, in three annual blocks covering almost all of the test period, suggesting that much of the weather record reuses one annual sequence. The value of weather information is therefore treated as unresolved, and the protocol is released as a baseline.

papers.title: Learning Nonlinear Transient Dynamics in Fluid Flow Networks with the Neural Basis Method
papers.abstract: Fluid flow networks, from pipeline infrastructure to biological vasculature, are governed by nonlinear edgewise hyperbolic laws coupled through continuity and conservation at junctions. Many-query tasks require rapid evaluation across unseen parametric settings, but conventional methods re-solve the system for each query at prohibitive cost. Existing physics-informed neural approaches impose the governing equations through penalty losses over generic neural approximators; these losses act only as optimization surrogates, with no guarantee that their reduction reduces solution error, and the resulting optimization is prone to ill-conditioning, particularly for hyperbolic systems. Building on the "representation-then-projection" principle of the neural basis method, we introduce a new approach for modeling fluid flow networks. Fixed neural bases define the representation space on each edge, while projection of the discretized equations determines the expansion coefficients, embedding edgewise laws into a conservative formulation. Edge subdomains are coupled through non-overlapping domain decomposition, and a neural operator learns, directly in this reduced space, the parametric map to the expansion coefficients. On looped and branching network topologies, we reproduce references with relative $L^2$ errors below 0.02%, whereas the physics-informed neural network baseline fails. Across unseen boundary conditions in both interpolation and extrapolation, we maintain mean pressure errors below 1% and mean flux errors below 3.3%, while the physics-informed DeepONet baseline reaches 8-18% pressure errors and 85-95% flux errors. These results highlight the framework's potential for real-time monitoring, design exploration, and uncertainty quantification of fluid flow networks.

papers.title: Quantifying Methodological Inflation in Clinical Machine Learning: A Cross-Modality Audit of Subject-Level Leakage and Nested Feature Selection for Parkinson's Disease
papers.abstract: Reported accuracy in Parkinson's disease (PD) machine learning can reflect the evaluation protocol rather than real signal. We ask how much evaluation choices inflate performance by comparing naive and rigorous protocols on voice, telemonitoring and blood-transcriptomic datasets. Subject-aware splitting reduced voice AUROC from 0.892 to 0.780 and telemonitoring R^2 from 0.105 to -0.037; Random Forest recovered neither gap. Supervised probe selection before splitting inflated transcriptomic AUROC from 0.711 to 0.998. A nested 50-probe panel matched a 1,000-probe panel (0.811 versus 0.844), and recruitment-wave batch structure was detected. Future work should validate a stable panel on an independent cohort.

papers.title: Enhancing Resolution and Reliability with Attention Mechanisms in Nuclear Accident Surrogate Modeling
papers.abstract: Severe accident (SA) analysis of nuclear power plants relies on system codes such as MAAP, whose computational cost limits large-scale applications including dynamic probabilistic safety assessment and reinforcement learning. This study proposes the Accident Binary-Continuous Transformer (ABC-Transformer), a decoder-only surrogate combining causal self-attention with temporal attention pooling. It jointly embeds continuous thermal-hydraulic variables with binary safety-system and severe accident management guideline (SAMG) states, enabling 5-minute-resolution forecasting over 72-hour transients. Trained on 11,000 MAAP simulations of a total loss of component cooling water scenario for the OPR1000, it achieved lower one-step teacher-forcing error than CNN and recurrent baselines at fine resolutions. Autoregressive reliability was characterized as a full per-scenario distribution over 1100 held-out scenarios. For scheduled-sampling (SS) training, the median $R^2$ is $0.947 \pm 0.006$ and $3.8 \pm 1.0$% of scenarios fail ($R^2<0$; mean $\pm$ SD over four training seeds), while errors accumulate with rollout length. A Mahalanobis self-distance computed from each surrogate rollout, before comparison with the MAAP reference, ranks these failures (ROC-AUC 0.895, reference seed). A threshold at the 40th percentile of calibration scores accepts $36.8 \pm 0.5$% of 550 evaluation scenarios, with no accepted rollout below $R^2 = 0$ for any seed, and routes the rest to MAAP.

papers.title: Time-Domain and Spectral Decomposition of Dynamic Coupling with Instantaneous and Time-Lagged Causality: Methodological Evaluation and Application to Cardiovascular Variability
papers.abstract: The quantification of dynamic interactions in coupled physiological time series is a central question in biomedical signal processing. A critical issue is the presence of instantaneous dependencies, often neglected in conventional Granger causality (GC) analyses despite potentially reflecting physiologically meaningful effects. We investigate time- and frequency-domain measures of causality within the linear autoregressive (AR) framework, treating instantaneous dependencies according to three formulations: (i) the classical strictly causal AR model, providing spectral measures of time-lagged GC and instantaneous interaction; (ii) the Geweke approach, assigning instantaneous dependencies to the direction opposite to that under investigation; (iii) a single extended AR model incorporating causally-oriented instantaneous dependencies, yielding spectral GC measures accounting for both instantaneous and time-lagged causality. The three approaches are evaluated in simulated Gaussian systems, where dynamic measures can be derived analytically and compared with the expected coupling structure. The single extended AR model emerges as the most consistent formulation when instantaneous dependencies have a physiologically meaningful causal direction and is then applied to cardiovascular interactions between heart period (HP) and systolic (SAP) or diastolic arterial pressure (DAP) in healthy subjects during postural and mental stress. Accounting for instantaneous dependencies substantially affects HP-SAP and HP-DAP interactions, enabling better quantification of baroreflex and cardiac run-off mechanisms and characterization of their responses to stress and of low- and high-frequency dynamics. Overall, the framework provides consistent representation of causal interactions across time and frequency and highlights the importance of accounting for instantaneous dependencies in physiological coupling.

papers.title: Hierarchical Empirical-Bayes Forecasting of Sparse Counts with Exposure: An Application to Airline Demand and Premium-Cabin Capacity Sharing
papers.abstract: Sparse count forecasting arises when events are rare, exposure varies across observational units, and short histories contain many zeros. Using thin-market airline demand as a motivating application, this paper develops a hierarchical exposure-adjusted Poisson-Gamma (HEPG) framework for probabilistic forecasting. Conditional counts follow a Poisson model with an exposure offset and pooled calendar effects, while unit specific baseline intensities receive a Gamma prior whose hyperparameters are estimated empirically across the population. The resulting posterior is Gamma and the posterior predictive distribution is negative binomial, providing closed-form partial pooling and explicit propagation of parameter uncertainty. This is especially useful for zero-history or low-exposure units, where independent maximum-likelihood estimates are unstable or collapse to zero. An adaptive extension, A-HEPG, adds a moment-matched negative-binomial variance correction when residual extra-Poisson variation remains. In synthetic experiments with 400 heterogeneous markets, HEPG improves average negative log predictive probability relative to complete pooling and independent route-level Poisson estimation. At a mean latent rate of 0.15 requests per exposure unit, the score is 0.525 for HEPG, compared with 0.585 for pooled Poisson and 0.731 for route-level Poisson maximum likelihood. Under strong overdispersion, A-HEPG reduces the score from 0.552 to 0.529. A downstream cabin-capacity example links the predictive distribution to a seat-protection rule based on predictive survival probabilities and fare ratios. The study emphasizes coherent probabilistic inference, partial pooling, and diagnostic model escalation for sparse applied count data.

papers.title: Clustering trajectories of modelled estimates: an uncertainty-aware framework, with an application to global cardiovascular disease burden, 1990 to 2023
papers.abstract: Modelled health estimates such as those of the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study are increasingly used in secondary analyses designed for observed data. However, trajectory clustering typically ignores published uncertainty, selects the number of clusters using criteria blind to it, and assigns countries to groups with unwarranted certainty. We propose an uncertainty-aware framework that separates trajectory level from shape, quantifies membership probabilities by perturbing estimates within their uncertainty intervals, selects clusters based on stability under uncertainty, and examines the roles of development, region, and measurement quality. Applied to age-standardised cardiovascular disease DALY rates for 201 countries from 1990-2023 (GBD 2023), the framework identified two stable trajectory types, whereas the gap statistic selected three. The additional cluster was poorly supported (median membership probability 0.70) and disappeared once uncertainty was considered. The retained clusters had similar burdens in 1990 but diverged markedly over time: a stalled-improvement group of 78 countries (median change $-8\%$, 40 of them in sub-Saharan Africa) and a sustained-decline group of 92 countries ($-52\%$). Thirty-one countries remained unclassified because their memberships were uncertain. Results were reproduced using mortality rates, a 2000-2023 analysis window, and bootstrap resampling. Among countries with the narrowest uncertainty intervals, a third well-supported trajectory emerged in former Soviet and Eastern European countries. These findings show that uncertainty affects both the number and composition of trajectory clusters. Ignoring it risks over-interpreting unstable groups and overstating confidence in country classifications. Incorporating published uncertainty and measurement quality should become standard practice when clustering modelled health estimates.

papers.title: A Goal-Oriented Bayesian Experimental Design to Reduce Uncertainty in Sparse-Angle X-ray Computed Tomography
papers.abstract: Sparse-angle X-ray computed tomography (CT) presents a challenge for reliable inference, as limited measurements may leave object boundaries unresolved. Bayesian optimal experimental design (BOED) methods select informative measurements, but can be computationally expensive or require data-driven surrogates and do not explicitly exploit microlocal visibility. We address this limitation by focusing on estimating inclusion boundaries rather than the entire attenuation field. For piecewise-constant objects, these boundaries correspond to singularities characterized by their wavefront sets. Microlocal analysis determines the X-ray view-angles at which these singularities are visible. We combine this information with Bayesian uncertainty quantification to introduce B-MUSE, a microlocal uncertainty-driven sequential experimental design method. We define a microlocal C-optimality criterion associated with the wavefront direction of the most uncertain boundary singularity and prove that its optimal solution satisfies the microlocal visibility condition. B-MUSE uses this result to sequentially select informative view-angles according to boundary uncertainty. It also incorporates an adaptive stopping criterion that terminates acquisition when additional measurements provide no meaningful uncertainty reduction. We evaluate B-MUSE through numerical experiments, including interpretable examples, prior-generated inclusions, and a multi-inclusion example from an external dataset, and benchmark it against recent methods. The results show that B-MUSE substantially reduces posterior uncertainty with few adaptively selected measurements while providing boundary estimates. These findings establish a direct connection between BOED and microlocal visibility and demonstrate the potential of uncertainty-driven acquisition to reduce measurement requirements for goal-oriented X-ray CT without training data.

papers.title: Credal Wrapper for Uncertainty Modelling in Sparse Geological Data
papers.abstract: Machine learning models for mineral exploration are trained on a few hundred sparse, expensive samples and used to decide where to drill next, so their epistemic uncertainty (EU), the part that more data could remove, matters as much as their predictions. Yet EU cannot be measured on real data, because the counterfactual that defines it is never observed, so estimators are graded by proxies such as out-of-distribution detection and calibration. We contribute a general simulation protocol that makes EU directly computable for a given model and can grade any EU estimator. It separates two estimands the literature conflates, reducible error and estimator spread, builds an oracle reference for each in a synthetic prospectivity field sampled by clustered drilling surveys, and compares uncertainty measures of an identical ensemble within each simulated world. We use it to ask when credal (imprecise-probability) measures are more faithful than Bayesian model averaging (BMA) in the sparse, low-class regime of geological classification. The credal interval width recovers the epistemic ordering better than BMA when members are few, confirming the small-ensemble advantage reported for credal wrappers; the advantage vanishes by M = 10 and reverses at M = 40. Secondly, the choice of credal functional matters more than the choice between credal and BMA. Lastly, the credal advantage does not widen as training data are thinned, so it compensates for few posterior samples rather than few data. On real drill-hole geochemistry from South Australia, a resampling oracle reproduces the first finding. The protocol applies to any EU estimator whose data-generating process can be simulated.

papers.title: Partial pooling beats synthetic respondents as estimators, not as covariates: a preregistered small-sample tournament
papers.abstract: Survey estimates for population segments, such as media use by sex and age, rest on few respondents per cell, and a growing literature offers synthetic respondents generated by large language models to fill the gap. That literature has not tested them against the small-area estimators a methodologist would otherwise use. We ran ten estimators, preregistered, on identical household-clustered splits of a Korean media panel across five calibration budgets and three holdout regimes. A multilevel partial-pooling model of the MRP family led every calibration-only estimator at every budget, matching at one hundred respondents what direct estimation reaches with roughly four times as many. On unobserved segments, information fixed as a per-segment prior was inert for synthetic panel and previous wave alike; attached as a bias correction it transferred, at the price of estimation noise. No registered synthetic advantage over MRP survived the paired decision rule. Entered instead as a covariate inside the multilevel model, an exploratory hybrid, the same panel improved on MRP on unobserved segments: the information survives where the registered constructions did not. Interval coverage stayed below nominal throughout and worsened with budget for partial pooling, contrary to prediction.

papers.title: EasyFoam: Skill-Oriented OpenFOAM Agents with Evidence-Driven Evolution
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of automating end-to-end OpenFOAM workflows for computational fluid dynamics (CFD). However, current progress is bottlenecked by two critical limitations. First, existing evaluations are dominated by tutorial-level cases and execution-oriented metrics, masking a substantial executability--acceptability gap: successfully executed simulations often fail to satisfy prescribed numerical or quantity-of-interest (QoI) criteria. Second, domain expertise in existing systems is tightly coupled with bespoke agent architectures, limiting its reuse and continual refinement across agent implementations. To address these challenges, we introduce ExtFoamBench, a challenging benchmark for OpenFOAM agents that spans five axes of workflow variation, and separately assesses execution completion, numerical soundness, and QoI satisfaction. Complementing this, we propose EasyFoam, an agent framework that decouples CFD expertise into modular, externalized skills driven by a dual-loop mechanism. An execution loop constructs workflows from explicit task requirements and uses structured simulation evidence to diagnose failures and guide targeted repairs. Meanwhile, an evolution loop distills task experience into reusable skill updates selected through paired evaluation. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that EasyFoam achieves substantially higher task acceptance rates than baseline agents, establishing this work as a starting point for future research toward self-improving CFD agents.

papers.title: Stage-Resolved EBV-Induced B-Cell Programs Across CNS Selection and Multiple Sclerosis Compartments
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is implicated in multiple sclerosis (MS), but whether EBV-conditioned B cells retain stable transcriptional programs after CNS selection remains uncertain. We reanalyzed datasets spanning experimental EBV infection, CNS-homing B cells in humanized mice, early-MS blood, and paired human CSF and blood. A frozen EBV-induced B-cell factor (F12) was transferred without outcome-driven modification and evaluated using anatomical, sequencing-depth, metabolic, coherence-matched, lineage, and exposure controls. F12 did not predict MS activity (AUC=0.487; p=0.489) and was lower in CSF in nine evaluable participants (mean difference -0.0560; coherence-matched p=0.015). It also remained lower in brain than spleen in all five EBV-exposed mice after matched-depth rarefaction (p=0.0313) and coherence-matched calibration (p=0.0225). The splenic TBX21+CXCR3+ transcriptional gate did not reliably represent the state of anatomically selected brain B cells. An enriched 287-gene cross-system bridge lacked B-lineage and EBV-exposure specificity. In human CSF, an early EBV-associated program was depleted (-0.0492; p=0.0197), whereas latency-III and lymphoblastoid cell line-like programs increased (+0.0666; p=0.0092 and +0.0148; p=0.0096, respectively). Opposite early and late program directions persisted after removing shared genes. No external program met the prespecified prospective criterion. These findings support stage- and compartment-dependent remodeling of EBV-associated B-cell transcription rather than persistence of a stable RNA signature. They distinguish cellular trafficking from transcriptional-state preservation and show that cross-system molecular resemblance alone cannot establish ancestry. EBV-directed biomarker studies should integrate host transcription with virologic, clonotypic, antigen-specific, epigenetic, and longitudinal evidence.

papers.title: On the Classification of Nilpotent Lie Superalgebras over Fields of Characteristic 2
papers.abstract: The salient result of this paper is the complete classification of all nilpotent Lie superalgebras in dimensions up to four over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 2. Our method adapts the Skjelbred-Sund method to show that every n-dimensional nilpotent Lie superalgebra arises as a one-dimensional central extension of an (n-1)-dimensional one, and determines precisely when two such extensions yield isomorphic superalgebras. Carrying out this construction for dimensions up to 4, we obtain a finite, non-redundant list of pairwise non-isomorphic examples.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Smoothing Selection for Noisy Scattered Surface Reconstruction: Evidence from Synthetic Benchmarks and Water Quality Data
papers.abstract: Sampling geometry may influence both reconstruction stability and the smoothing needed to control noise. This study distinguishes geometry-dependent failure of exact multiquadric radial basis function (RBF) interpolation from variation in validation-selected smoothing. A synthetic benchmark crossed four response families, four 16-point geometries, three slice levels, five observation regimes, and 24 repeated holdouts, yielding 17,280 method-level evaluations. Clough--Tocher cubic interpolation, exact RBF, and smoothed RBF were compared, followed by a Water Quality Portal pilot with 1,950 complete activities. On the synthetic shared-valid domain, exact RBF achieved the lowest noise-free mean RMSE (0.0206), whereas smoothed RBF performed best under noise (0.1807 versus 0.2414 for cubic and 0.6106 for exact RBF). Clustered-gap support produced the largest noisy exact-RBF RMSE (1.2706). Geometry added little explanatory power for log-transformed smoothing: the combined model had $R^2=0.4259$, compared with 0.4096 for noise alone. Reported failure-regression results suggest a stronger geometry signal, but remain unverified without their original model specification. In the environmental pilot, smoothed RBF achieved mean RMSE 0.9877 with no negative-$R^2$ failures. Conflicting responses at identical predictor coordinates made exact interpolation unsuitable. All environmental smoothed-RBF fits selected the largest candidate, preventing geometry--smoothing correlation analysis. The findings motivate geometry-aware failure screening but do not establish a transferable rule for smoothing magnitude. Independent multisite validation, appropriate coordinate scaling, joint scale--smoothing tuning, and conditioning diagnostics are needed before an adaptive policy can be claimed.

papers.title: Null-Corrected Conditional Coverage in Materials Property Prediction: A Five-Dataset Replication
papers.abstract: Uncertainty quantification for materials property prediction increasingly reports conditional coverage, coverage within strata of the predicted value, alongside marginal coverage. The worst-bin statistics used for this are downward-biased in finite samples, a known defect that applied materials work does not generally correct for. We replicate a single-dataset conditional coverage study across five regression datasets (n = 437 to 21,263), seven interval methods and 50 random splits each, correcting the worst-bin statistic against its expected value under exact conditional validity. The null is simulated from realized per-bin test counts and referenced to each method's own marginal coverage, separating marginal miscalibration from uneven coverage. On the smallest dataset the correction runs from 0.061 to 0.096, between a third and two thirds of the shortfalls actually reported, against 0.009 to 0.011 on the two largest. Split conformal prediction's failure survives the correction on four of five datasets; two conclusions of the antecedent study do not. Conformalized quantile regression, characterized there as a negative case, fails on one dataset only. Cross-fitted normalized conformal prediction, grouped there with the successful methods, fails on three of five. Group-conditional (Mondrian) conformal prediction stays below our significance criterion on every dataset, yet exceeds the null on three of five under an octile refinement of the variable it calibrates on. A level-matched ablation locates that uniformity in group-conditional calibration rather than in the elevated quantile level, and removes Mondrian's apparent width cost entirely. Conditional coverage evaluations should report the null distribution of the worst-bin statistic used, the method's realized marginal coverage, and the resolution of the evaluation partition relative to any partition the method calibrates on.

papers.title: Care, Human Enfeeblement, and the Existential Implications of AGI
papers.abstract: Stuart Russell has named "human enfeeblement" as a long-term societal risk of advanced AI. This paper gives a new interpretation of the enfeeblement danger by interpreting it in light of recent work by Brian Christian, Alison Gopnik, and David Spivak on care and caregiving, and connecting it with the ontological design tradition of Terry Winograd and Fernando Flores. The enfeeblement that threatens is not merely a matter of cognitive off-loading and loss of knowledge, but a form of disengagement with the world which I explain in terms of an erosion of our capacities to care. This paper articulates a conception of care as a constellation of cultivable skills that involve us in the world and with each other, while making life worth living. Designing AI to support our capacities to care addresses the worry recently raised by Demis Hassabis and others regarding the questions of "meaning and purpose" that are looming in a post-AGI world.

papers.title: Annular Obstructions and Skew-Shape Block Identities
papers.abstract: We give three principal results on weighted order ideals, cluster coefficients, and block-statistic enumerators. First, in the rank-two annular exchange model, the frozen row $(2,-3)$ yields the specialized polynomial $1+q^2$, which is not unimodal. Its interpretation as a single-lamination counterexample to Theorem 14 of Kang, Lee and Lim (European Journal of Combinatorics, 2026) depends on identifying this row with the shear coordinates of a bridging curve in the same triangulation. We discuss this geometric correspondence using published annular examples; it is not established by the algebraic calculation or formalized in Lean. Second, the same polynomial fails log-concavity, and the frozen row $(1,-2)$ gives the full-support polynomial $1+2q+7q^2+10q^3+9q^4+4q^5+q^6$, likewise violating log-concavity. These calculations provide obstructions relevant to their Conjecture 1, subject to the same geometric identification. Third, for arbitrary finite skew Young diagrams, we prove the block-statistic identity of Kahane's Conjecture 4.7 (arXiv:2607.11225v2), using an explicit correction of the root convention. The proof uses commuting tableau-transfer matrices, a connected-block inverse kernel, and finite polynomial differential equations, with companion Lean 4/Mathlib formalizations. As a consequence, we obtain a bivariate block refinement that is coefficientwise nonnegative in $t-1$ after a common monomial shift in $q$.

papers.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
papers.abstract: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. This opens the door to future weight-based continual learning that could teach models to drive harnesses in new domains.

papers.title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion
papers.abstract: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Whether networks with brain-like wiring are more robust at lower computational cost is unclear. We address this by benchmarking a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network of the fly visual system constrained by its synaptic connectome (FlyNet) against artificial neural networks. We compare it against CNNs, RAFT, and continuous-time recurrent neural networks without detailed connectome constraints (sCTRNN, CTRNN) on a collision-detection task within a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but, relative to its compute, more robust to common video corruptions than RAFT, while using up to five orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs. The CTRNNs remain more robust than FlyNet across almost all tested perturbations, suggesting that connectome constraints benefit efficiency, through their low edge count, over robustness. Recurrence improves robustness to white-box attacks in RAFT and temporal context improves robustness to common corruptions. FlyNet's position and velocity representations degrade under adversarial textures but recover under counterfactual textures that restore correct classification while staying equally far from training, ruling out unfamiliar textures as the cause of failure. The reverse-phi illusion similarly disrupts these representations and inverts the same low-level motion statistic as the adversarial textures. Optimizing this input statistic alone, without access to the network, suffices to induce classification failure, attributing both perturbations to the same circuit vulnerability. Connectome-constrained models can thus surface adversarial failure mechanisms as testable hypotheses about biological perceptual vulnerabilities.

papers.title: Automatic Continuity for projective clone homomorphisms
papers.abstract: We show that every projective clone homomorphism from a closed function clone containing the automorphism group of a countable homogeneous Ramsey structure $Δ$ in a finite relational language is uniformly continuous. This answers, for such structures, open questions previously raised by Barto, Bodirsky, Marimon, Pongrácz, and the second author in several papers (Bodirsky, Pinsker, Pongrácz, J. Symb. Log. 2021; Barto, Pinsker, SIAM J. Comput. 2020; Marimon, Pinsker, arXiv:2512.01086). Consequently, the polymorphism clone of a first-order reduct $Γ$ of $Δ$ admits a projective clone homomorphism if and only if $Γ$ primitively positively interprets all finite structures; in other words, this ability of $Γ$ is characterised by the absence of non-trivial identities in its polymorphism clone, a purely algebraic condition.

papers.title: r-Process Abundance Variations in Globular Clusters as Fossils of Turbulent Mixing
papers.abstract: Several metal-poor Galactic globular clusters exhibit substantial star-to-star $r$-process abundance variations at nearly fixed [Fe/H], with the ensemble suggesting smaller variations toward increasing metallicity. We investigate whether this chemical structure can be inherited from incomplete mixing in the galactic environments in which the clusters formed. Using parsec-scale simulations of rare-element transport in a supernova-driven turbulent disk, we follow the redistribution of $r$-process ejecta and characterize the abundance structure of gas selected to trace star-forming environments. Rare enrichment events generate strong [Eu/Fe] inhomogeneities that persist across a range of physical scales. As chemical evolution proceeds, the available abundance variance decreases, while spatial averaging over larger regions reduces the differences between their characteristic abundances. The simulations provide substantial pre-collapse $r$-process variance at low [Fe/H] and show the same broad decline toward higher metallicity suggested by the globular-cluster measurements. Our results support an interpretation in which at least some of the observed $r$-process variations are inherited from pre-existing chemical structure in the natal environment, allowing globular clusters to preserve a fossil record of the mixing history between rare enrichment and star formation.

papers.title: Accurate predictions of properties of energetic materials with tabular foundation models
papers.abstract: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN outperforms the best published models for all three properties. It also substantially outperforms a wide range of established machine-learning models, including tuned gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forests and Gaussian processes. This holds both when the models are given hand-crafted molecular descriptors and when they are given learned representations from Chemprop's message-passing neural network. In particular, for all three properties, TabPFN applied to Chemprop's own embedding is more accurate than Chemprop's predictions. TabPFN is also among the fastest models we consider, more than an order of magnitude faster than XGBoost. As TabPFN predicts the entire distribution of the target rather than just a single value, it offers built-in uncertainty quantification, which we compare with the empirical distributions of compounds with repeated measurements. Finally, we interpret the predictions using Shapley values, which rank the features by their importance.

papers.title: Measuring Kaplan--Meier Overestimation Under Competing Risks: Event Ordering, Quantification, and Exact Inference
papers.abstract: Competing risks arise when individuals may experience multiple mutually exclusive event types. Competing events are frequently treated as censoring and analysed using Kaplan--Meier (KM) methods, which overestimate real-world event risks. While the existence of KM overestimation is well known, its determinants, magnitude, and inferential properties remain poorly characterised. We develop a nonparametric framework that treats competing risks overestimation as a statistical quantity in its own right. We show that competing event frequency alone is insufficient to characterise KM overestimation and develop an event ordering theory describing how temporal event allocation influences overestimation. Based on these results, we derive a closed-form Total Overestimation Diagnostic (TOD) that quantifies total KM overestimation directly from routine survival analysis output. We establish exact error equivalence results for both cause-specific and total overestimation. In particular, Product Limit Error Equivalence shows that inference for TOD reduces exactly to ordinary overall survival estimation. Simulation experiments validate the theoretical results and show that independent censoring primarily affects precision rather than overestimation magnitude. Across six benchmark competing risks datasets, cause-specific overestimation is characterised by both total overestimation and temporal event allocation. These results provide a practical framework for assessing competing risks relevance and determining when cumulative incidence methods should be preferred to naïve KM risks. The proposed framework transforms competing risks overestimation from a qualitative warning into a measurable quantity that can be routinely quantified, interpreted, and incorporated into reporting practice.

papers.title: Hedging out the HEDGE Bias: Identifying Dynamic Partial-Equilibrium Effects with Panel LP-IV
papers.abstract: Cross-sectional designs are widely used to estimate dynamic partial-equilibrium effects of an aggregate treatment. We show analytically that these estimates are biased when exposures to the treatment and to aggregate confounders are correlated or the confounders feed back into the treatment. This paper develops the heterogeneous-exposure local-projection instrumental variables (HELP-IV) framework, which compares units while holding the confounder path fixed by instrumenting the treatment and this path with exposure-weighted shock proxies. We prove that HELP-IV identifies the partial-equilibrium effect. We further extend the framework, with the corresponding inference, to multiple exposure margins and confounders, forward-looking outcomes, and cumulative multipliers. Finally, we apply HELP-IV to state fiscal multipliers and regional stock-wealth effects, where it yields partial-equilibrium effects that are smaller than conventional estimates and deliver different implications when ported to macroeconomic models.

papers.title: New linear codes over GF(7), GF(8) and GF(9) from quasi-cyclic codes and Construction X
papers.abstract: We present linear codes with parameters [88,8,64]_7, [90,8,65]_7, [98,7,75]_8, [97,8,72]_8, [44,7,31]_9, [97,8,71]_7, [85,6,67]_8 and [78,8,56]_7. Each has a minimum distance one larger than the lower bound listed in Grassl's tables of best known linear codes; codes with parameters [89,8,64]_7, [96,8,71]_8, [95,8,70]_8, [94,8,69]_8, [77,8,55]_7 and [86,6,68]_8 follow. Seven of the eight codes are obtained from a quasi-cyclic code and a vector that is constant on each block, by Construction X with a repetition code. The remaining one, the [90,8,65]_7 code, is obtained from the first by appending two coordinates. The parameters and all weight counts were obtained by exhaustive enumeration, and a short program that repeats these computations is included.

papers.title: Convergence and global optimality of Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao descent for Gaussian mixtures
papers.abstract: We study explicit Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao descent for fitting Gaussian location mixtures by nonparametric maximum likelihood. The full sequence converges weakly and has finite length in the bounded-Lipschitz metric throughout the original step-size range. These conclusions hold for any fixed data set in any dimension and any initial probability measure. By an earlier conditional optimality theorem, the limit maximizes the likelihood under full-support initialization. Fix any particle step size in $(0,1]$. Initialize the particles by resampling the observations. For an open set of triples of points in the plane, the probability of convergence to a strictly suboptimal fixed point tends to one exponentially as the particle count grows. Without reweighting, a centered Gaussian initialization can give a strictly suboptimal limit. Every finite iterate has a smooth, strictly positive density. The limit assigns positive mass to a nonglobal local maximum of the associated Gaussian sum. We also give the exact pure-transport limit for a one-dimensional initialization with full support and an atom. An exact finite-dimensional representation preserves the truncated likelihood moments and the retained region's contribution to the current dissipation. This lets us transfer an analytic gradient inequality to the measure trajectory.

papers.title: Complexity of Deciding Existence of Maltsev Polymorphisms of Finite Relational Structures
papers.abstract: In this article, we show that the problem of deciding whether a finite relational structure $\mathbf{A}$ admits a Maltsev polymorphism is a computational problem, which can be solved in polynomial time. We provide a proof of this result by reducing the problem to deciding whether a binary relational structure, associated with $\mathbf{A}$ admits such a polymorphism. In our construction of such an algorithm, we make an extensive use of a property of binary relations, which is implied by the existence of a Maltsev polymorphism, the so-called rectangularity property.

papers.title: Reliable and explainable analysis of AVS/RS by Statistical Model Checking and Process Mining
papers.abstract: Automated Vehicle Storage and Retrieval Systems (AVS/RS) are increasingly adopted to boost warehouse throughput while containing operational costs. We present a tool-supported analysis workflow that combines discrete-event simulation, Statistical Model Checking (SMC), and Process Mining (PM) techniques to quantify and explain AVS/RS performance. SMC, implemented through the MultiVeStA tool, delivers statistically reliable estimates of key indicators, such as cycle times and inventory consolidation, across alternative stocking and picking policies with user-specified confidence levels. MultiVeStA orchestrates multiple independent simulations in a black-box manner, enabling automated verification. PM ingests the resulting event logs to uncover the behavioural patterns and bottlenecks that drive those indicators, closing the interpretability gap typical of simulation studies. We instantiate the framework on a new open-source AVS/RS simulator configured according to recent industrial guidelines and evaluate multiple control strategies and different scenarios. Results show that the coordinated use of SMC and PM supports both predictive what-if analyses and post-hoc diagnostics. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first application of a combined SMC-PM workflow to AVS/RS operations, complemented by a reusable open-source simulation and analysis toolchain.

papers.title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
papers.abstract: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. The dataset considered represents $10.6$ years of livetime and is three times larger than previous ARA neutrino searches. This search achieves a $28\%$ analysis efficiency for a neutrino flux corresponding to the current experimental upper limits. No neutrino candidates are observed on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. We set a new upper limit on the diffuse UHE neutrino flux, which is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV. We also discuss lessons learned for future searches on large radio arrays.

papers.title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
papers.abstract: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_ν\gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. The search found no events on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. The resulting upper limit is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV and provides the first constraints on the flux reported by the KM3NeT Collaboration that are complementary to optical Cherenkov and particle detectors. This limit also constrains UHECR source models, and excludes some models with trans-GZK proton populations at the $90\%$ confidence level. This represents the largest Askaryan detector dataset ever analyzed, demonstrating the feasibility and sensitivity of searches with large detector arrays acting as a single observatory. It also underscores the high acceptance and exposure of Askaryan detector arrays to ultrahigh energy neutrinos.

papers.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
papers.abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

papers.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
papers.abstract: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.

papers.title: Ninety-Six Ways to Measure a Scribe: Fragmented Evaluation of Ambient Scribes in Healthcare
papers.abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes have moved rapidly from experimental pilots to enterprise-wide deployment across health systems, promising reduced documentation burden and improved clinician experience. While research evaluating these tools has expanded quickly, there are no agreed-upon protocols or standardized metrics for assessing their performance, making it difficult to compare findings or cumulatively synthesize evidence across studies. Across 54 recent evaluation studies, we identify ten evaluation dimensions and 40 distinct metrics, operationalized in 96 different ways-35 of them (36%) used by only a single study. Assessment is dominated by documentation efficiency and time, measured in 44 of 54 studies. The other dimensions appear at broadly similar rates (16-24 studies each), and safety and clinical outcome least consistently of all. Ripple effects on the broader care system, such as impact on patients' care outcomes, redistribution of work, changes in billing and coding intensity, and downstream use of notes by other clinicians are rarely assessed. Moreover, the metrics used rely heavily on self-report and are fragmented and inconsistently operationalized, which limits comparability and hinders synthesis across studies. As an effort to support more rigorous and cumulative evaluation, in this paper we review the study designs, data sources, and metrics commonly used to evaluate ambient AI scribes in healthcare settings, discuss the limitations of current evaluation practice, and argue for a more holistic approach grounded in a standardized, multi-dimensional set of metrics.

papers.title: UniFlow-RS: Unified Generative Prediction for Heterogeneous Remote-Sensing Tasks
papers.abstract: Remote-sensing foundation models increasingly unify representations across sensing modalities and downstream tasks, yet their prediction mechanisms remain largely task-specific. Separate decoders, prediction heads, and objectives leave prediction fragmented across tasks. This naturally raises a question: can heterogeneous remote-sensing tasks share the prediction process? UniFlow-RS answers this question with a single latent flow-matching predictor shared across tasks. This requires addressing two key challenges: unifying heterogeneous prediction spaces and harmonizing joint optimization across tasks. First, we cast heterogeneous task outputs into structured visual targets in a common latent space, allowing them to be modeled by the same pretrained flow predictor. Task-dependent conditioning further accommodates differences in input configurations. Second, we optimize all tasks with a common Flow Matching objective, eliminating task-specific prediction losses. To mitigate optimization mismatch across tasks and modalities, we introduce Task-Modality Adaptive Timestep Sampling (TMAS), which dynamically allocates training timesteps according to the online learning state of each task-modality group. Using a single shared model, UniFlow-RS handles six tasks and thirteen datasets, surpassing recent task-specific state-of-the-art methods on several benchmarks while remaining competitive on the others. Beyond these benchmarks, the same checkpoint demonstrates strong zero-shot transfer across unseen datasets, task settings, occlusion conditions, and near-infrared false-color imagery, without target-specific adaptation. Codes are available at https://github.com/MindVision-AI/UniFlow-RS.

papers.title: Edge quantum weight of finite Chern flakes and its topological floor
papers.abstract: The zero-point energy of an $LC$ circuit measures the polarization fluctuation of an insulator coupled to it. In a crystal this fluctuation is the bulk quantum weight $K_{\rm bulk}$, which the Chern number $C$ bounds below by $|C|$. We show that a finite Chern flake adds an edge term that survives as the flake grows. The low-frequency transitions of its chiral edge have squared dipole matrix elements that sum to an edge weight $K_{\rm edge}\ge |C|$ per unit area, a floor that follows from the positive absorption of both circular polarizations and the known cancellation of circular dichroism between edge and bulk. At weak coupling, which a growing flake eventually leaves, a circuit slower than the edge modes reads $K_{\rm bulk}+K_{\rm edge}$, averaged over two field directions, and a faster one approaches $K_{\rm bulk}$, so the reading depends on whether the flake is made large or the circuit slow first. In exact free-fermion calculations on lattice flakes with $|C|=1$ and 2 the summed circular dichroism of the edge sector extrapolates to $|C|$ in magnitude, so that the floor is $|C|$. Above the floor, each edge channel adds a number fixed by the boundary shape and its edge velocities, which square and rectangular lattice flakes with one channel follow to within 0.003, while the circular dichroism counts only the net chirality. The avoided crossing of the circuit with the edge mode gives the edge weight in units of the Hall conductance quantum, up to a geometric factor of the capacitor.

papers.title: The Isoperimetric Flow and Synthetic Scalar Curvature for Causal Variational Principles
papers.abstract: An isoperimetric flow is introduced in the setting of causal variational principles. Describing the whole space by the support of a minimizing measure, we define an area functional on subsets by a surface layer integral. Mean curvature is defined via the first variation of this area functional. Using the method of minimizing movement, the isoperimetric flow is constructed as a Lipschitz curve of measures with prescribed volume change. As illustrating examples, we introduce and analyze ``smeared variants'' of the mean curvature flow in Euclidean space and on a Riemannian manifold. In these examples, it is shown that our area functional coincides with the usual area up to specified curvature corrections. As an application of our general results, by analyzing the volume and area of small isoperimetric balls, we introduce notions of local dimension and synthetic scalar curvature.

papers.title: An AI Assistant for Automating Anti-Corruption Expertise of Draft Legislation Based on the TRACE Framework
papers.abstract: We present an AI assistant for automating anti-corruption expertise of draft legislation based on the TRACE architecture, designed to screen bills for corruption risks: pinpoint provisions an expert would criticise and name the regulatory defect in each. The pipeline combines a deterministic parsing core, model-guided single-provision qualification, rule-based factor assignment, and external human oversight. To evaluate the assistant, we constructed an open benchmark from the published conclusions of Ukraine's National Agency on Corruption Prevention (NAZK), comprising 132 draft laws with 474 model-extracted findings. A system flag agrees with a finding when it targets a compatible provision and an LLM judge rates the risk as the same (strict) or partly the same (lenient). On 100 draft laws, the pipeline matches 0.28 of the findings within its top ten flags using the local Gemma 4 31B model, 0.30 with Sonnet 5.5, and 0.43-0.46 across all flags (non-blind; the frozen blind baseline achieves 0.21, 95% CI 0.16-0.26). Across all runs, most misses occur on provisions that the system located but qualified as a different risk, and none of the 32 legal-collision findings was matched. On 21 acts held out from tuning, the pipeline outperforms a monolithic prompt containing the full methodology under the strict measure, though not under the lenient one, and Opus 5.5 adds nothing over Sonnet. The reported scores reflect agreement with model-extracted findings rated by an LLM judge whose two access routes agree on 73 of 74 labels, without human expert validation.

papers.title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto
papers.abstract: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.

papers.title: The elliptic Hall algebra and the combinatorics of affine Springer fibers
papers.abstract: For coprime positive integers $m,n$ and $k\ge1$, we study the symmetric functions $e_k[-X^{m,n}Y]\cdot1$ arising from the elliptic Hall algebra action. We identify their $ω_X$-transforms with the normalized bigraded Frobenius characteristics computed by Boixeda Alvarez--Hameister--Ma for the torus-equivariant Borel--Moore homology of the positive parts of homogeneous affine Springer fibers. We introduce cyclic LLT polynomials and determine their monomial expansions, yielding explicit monomial formulas for these elliptic Hall algebra expressions in terms of cyclic parking functions. These results extend the affine Springer fiber identity and monomial formula of Carlsson--Mellit from integral slopes to arbitrary positive rational slopes.

papers.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
papers.abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.

papers.title: Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties via Symplectic Cuts
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric orbifold of complex dimension $2n$ by compact symplectic cuts.
