Controlled changes in the training distribution show that minority conflict exposure can still lead to widespread shortcut acquisition, reaching 97.9% certified profitable violations on an API task under a 25% conflict mixture after 128 updates. The same contextual checks supply a simple binary penalty that supports joint capability and compliance gains and partially mitigates acquired violations. Learned safety adapts to expanded authorization and transfers across mechanisms into workflows with evolving evidence and approval requirements. On 32 unseen changing-evidence tasks, resource-trained safety increases safe completion from 53.1% to 89.1% relative to task-only training, while both policies achieve full real work. These results connect a verifiable account of reward-driven misalignment with scalable task construction and safety learning that remains useful under changing execution requirements.

papers.title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
papers.abstract: Engineering large and reproducible valley splittings is essential for the scalable operation of silicon spin qubits. In Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, valley splitting arises predominantly from atomic-scale disorder and is therefore inherently random, motivating approaches that introduce a large deterministic contribution. Strain-assisted Wiggle Wells provide a route to deterministic valley splitting by combining an oscillatory Ge concentration in the Si well with shear strain; however, generating the required strain in a manner compatible with large-scale architectures remains a challenge. Here, we propose patterned stressed thin films as a scalable approach for generating shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices. Finite-element simulations show that compressively stressed TiN films can generate shear strains exceeding 0.1% at the quantum well, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of $μ\text{eV}$ in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. We show that this strain can extend across multiple quantum dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, providing a fabrication-compatible approach for scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.

papers.title: Simulation of a Jovian Planet Undergoing Gas Accretion
papers.abstract: To understand the process of planet formation in the Solar System or any other stellar system, we need to comprehend the interaction between forming planets and the protoplanetary disk. This work presents a study of the interaction of the protoplanetary disk with the protoplanet and the following types of orbital migration that can occur, and to verify this interaction, numerical simulations were performed using the magneto-hydrodynamics code FARGO3D. The researchers made five simulations with a 2-Jupiter-mass planet in the protoplanetary disk. The only parameter varied was the initial radial position with the aim of verifying the influence of this parameter on the behavior of planetary migration. As a result of these simulations, we find that the initial radial coordinate is a very significant parameter in how the planet interacts with the gas in the disk and the formation of gas gaps.

papers.title: NS 1987A: A Potential Probe of Crustal Superfluidity with Future X-ray Observations
papers.abstract: Several indirect observations imply that the central compact object in the supernova SN 1987A is likely to be the youngest neutron star identified to date, NS 1987A. We investigate how a future detection of its thermal X-ray emission could constrain neutron-star interiors, using cooling models and a generic high-resolution, large-area X-ray observatory with \textit{Lynx}-like capabilities as a sensitivity benchmark. For the adopted sensitivity and observing window, NS 1987A is detectable at $t\sim60~{\rm yr}$ (roughly 2047) unless rapid neutrino cooling operates, such as the direct Urca process. If the neutron superfluidity in the inner crust is weak, the temperature profile inside NS 1987A is likely not to be isothermal at the detection. In that case, the future direct observation of NS 1987A is a potential probe of the properties inside the inner crust. We compare alternative X-ray observatories and emphasize that both effective area and angular resolution, needed to reduce contamination from the surrounding remnant, determine whether this diagnostic can be realized.

papers.title: Inference Validation for Regulated AI: A Governed Decision Pipeline for LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Deploying large language models in regulated industries requires more than picking the fastest inference engine: it requires evidence that a configuration meets contractual and legal obligations before it serves a single customer request. We describe Runway, an internal validation harness built at MasterControl that builds a governed decision pipeline around NVIDIA AIPerf. The key insight is separating concerns: AIPerf provides the trusted measurement, while Runway provides the experiment design that comes before it and the compliance, cost, and audit decisions that come after. We describe the architecture and the storage model that makes caching and audit one mechanism. We report three findings from Runway sweeps: TensorRT-LLM and vLLM rankings invert with concurrency; a newer, pricier GPU instance can be the cheaper one per request; and speculative decoding behaves differently across engines under load, so engine configuration can outweigh engine choice.

papers.title: Wolfe's Minimum-Norm-Point Method Generalizes the Simplex Method
papers.abstract: Wolfe's method computes the point of minimum Euclidean norm in the convex hull of finitely many points. The method is parameterized by an insertion rule and it has been an open problem whether Wolfe's original rule guarantees a polynomial number of iterations (De Loera, Haddock, and Rademacher; STOC'18). We resolve this question by proving an exponential lower bound. In fact, we establish a tight connection to the simplex method for linear programming that allows us to transfer many lower bounds for simplex pivot rules to corresponding insertion rules of Wolfe's method. These include not only Wolfe's linopt rule via Dantzig's pivot rule, but also many other classical, randomized and history-based rules. As a corollary, we obtain the first exponential example for the Lawson-Hanson algorithm for nonnegative least squares, as well as PSPACE-hardness of deciding whether the linopt rule ever uses a given point.

papers.title: When Does Sliced Inference Pay Off? Resolution, Tiling and Dense Fusion for Small Object Detection
papers.abstract: Sliced inference such as SAHI is the standard remedy for small objects in high-resolution imagery, but its gains are usually measured against low-resolution baselines. We revisit sliced inference with scale as the explicit variable and ask when tiling actually pays off. We compare seven dense detectors from four families on VisDrone and DOTA, under pre-specified hypotheses, calibration-only tuning and a single evaluation on held-out test data. Two findings emerge. First, much of the benefit attributed to slicing is a resolution effect: on VisDrone, a single pass trained at a higher resolution outperforms tiling with box fusion (merging decoded boxes) for every detector that could be trained at that resolution, and at equal compute a higher resolution helps more than a larger model. Second, tiles carry complementary information that box fusion wastes. We introduce SCAHI (Slicing with Coverage-Aware Hyper Inference), which accumulates the dense outputs of all passes with weights that give every image position the same total coverage, and reads objects off a peak grid fine enough to keep crowded neighbours apart. On identical passes, SCAHI outperforms box fusion for every YOLO detector on both datasets and matches it for FCOS. On DOTA, whose images far exceed the resolution a single pass can be trained at, tiles with SCAHI beat the best single pass for every detector, by 4.3 to 5.6 mAP50 at 2048 px, and replacing only SAHI's merge step by SCAHI adds 2.3 to 4.0 mAP50. An ablation attributes the gain to the border weighting and the resolution of the peak grid. Source code is available at https://github.com/beckerio/scahi.

papers.title: Non-Equilibrium Ising-Bloch Transition in Polarization Cavity Solitons
papers.abstract: Polarization cavity solitons in coherently driven Kerr resonators undergo a sequence of dynamical bifurcations as the cavity detuning is increased. Here we show that a stationary localized state containing an Ising wall first becomes a fixed breather and then develops finite chirality and drift motion through a spontaneous non-equilibrium Ising-Bloch transition. Stability analyses identify the modes responsible for the breathing and the motion, revealing controllable dynamics of polarization cavity solitons.

papers.title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization is widely used in active learning loops for materials science. Gaussian processes serve as the de-facto surrogate model family, but require task-dependent kernel choices and can lack the modeling capacity for complex relationships. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have recently emerged as the state-of-the-art for predictive tasks on structured data, without requiring bespoke kernels or hyperparameter tuning. We evaluate two TFMs, TabPFN and TabICL, as out-of-the-box surrogate models on two standard materials science benchmarks, comparing against a large field of baselines encompassing Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost. Our findings indicate that TFMs are highly competitive surrogate models across the two benchmarks, without task-specific training for active learning or GP kernel selection. Our results motivate developing TFMs further as surrogates for active learning in materials discovery.

papers.title: Brief introduction to post-quantum cryptography in industrial applications
papers.abstract: The development of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is directly motivated by the necessity to secure information in the face of the quantum threat. This paper provides an overview of recent developments relevant to PQC adoption across several industrial applications, including IoT, healthcare, civil and infrastructure engineering, and defense. We present a brief, self-contained overview of PQC and its market positioning. We perform implementation experiments on selected quantum-safe methods and quantify several aspects, such as the quantum resources required to break common cryptographic schemes, as well as the performance of the most well-known PQC algorithms. We also discuss the resistance of different PQC classes to quantum attacks and the status of PQC implementations in different programming languages. Finally, we present benchmark results on KEMs and signature algorithms to help select the appropriate algorithm for a specific application based on criteria such as algorithm performance, data lifetime, and level of data sensitivity.

papers.title: ADZE 2.0: rarefaction estimates of allelic richness and private allelic richness for whole-genome data
papers.abstract: Allelic richness and private allelic richness describe how alleles are distributed across populations, but both depend strongly on sample size. Rarefaction makes them comparable by computing the expected number of alleles in subsamples of a common size, and ADZE implemented this approach and an extension to alleles shared only by a set of populations. However, ADZE was developed for microsatellite data and cannot read sequencing data in variant call format (VCF). Here we present ADZE 2.0, which reads VCF, computes each statistic genome-wide or in genomic windows, and can treat blocks of phased SNPs as haplotype alleles. We also implement improved memory handling and multi-threading support. ADZE 2.0 reproduces the ADZE 1.0 estimates for human microsatellite data exactly. On chromosome 22 of the high-coverage 1000 Genomes Project data, private allelic richness for all 325 population pairs took 4.4 minutes on 32 threads. ADZE 2.0 is available at https://github.com/szpiech/ADZE.

papers.title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
papers.abstract: We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[ \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1) =κ\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}} +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $κ$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.

papers.title: An almost sharp $L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$-$L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}} f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} whenever \begin{equation*} \mathcal{U}:= \min{\left\{ \min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}>1, \end{equation*} and we necessarily have $\mathcal{U}\geq 1$.

papers.title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
papers.abstract: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $ζ(s)$ and its derivative $ζ'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $ζ'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $ζ$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Zener diode and ohmic contact resulting from a heavily doped p-n junction: A novel explanation in terms of impurity-photovoltaic-effect resulting from infrared self-emission at room-temperature
papers.abstract: In textbooks, a quantum-mechanical tunneling mechanism based on electron-wavefunction is used to explain Zener diode as well as ohmic contact resulting from a heavily doped p-n junction. In this study, an attempt in particle description is made to explain these devices. Any object at room-temperature emits infrared (IR) photons. The process of heavy doping can cause many defects. The self-absorption of the IR emission could be achieved through sub-band-gap excitations due to defects, creating carriers. In a heavily doped p-n junction device, some of the IR-generated carriers diffuse into the junction which has a built-in field. The built-in field sweeps out the carriers, creating IR photocurrent. The reverse leakage current of the p-n junction is regarded as the IR photocurrent according to a precedent where impurity-photovoltaic-effect is used to explain circuit devices (arXiv:2510.18226). Heavy doping results in not only a great many IR-generated carriers but also an avalanche effect at low voltage, producing Zener breakdown. Additionally, the impurity-photovoltaic-effect can make a reasonable contribution to explaining the temperature dependence of Zener breakdown. If the doping is very heavy, the heavily doped p-n junction can be altered to create an ohmic contact, which can also be explained in terms of impurity-photovoltaic-effect. Not only quantum mechanics, but also this photovoltaic mechanism in particle description can explain the above devices. Considering the wave-particle duality, the combination of quantum-mechanical and photovoltaic mechanisms is suggested to explain these devices. Each mechanism plays a big or small role in the explanation.

papers.title: Release Sooner, Expose Less: Offloading MoE Dispatch in NCCL-EP under Dual-Batch Overlap
papers.abstract: Dual-batch overlap (DBO) hides mixture-of-experts (MoE) communication behind another microbatch's computation, but only after dispatch send releases the GPU. The time dispatch send holds the GPU therefore stays exposed, while network progress after release can be hidden. We evaluate GPUDirect Async - Kernel Initiated (GDA-KI) Free Flow, an NCCL-EP research configuration that leaves WQE construction on the GPU but moves send progression to a host thread. On a GB300 NVL72 system, GDA-KI Free Flow reduces dispatch-send time relative to default GDA-KI at every operating point in the evaluated parameter sweep. An experiment that inserts a GPU delay between dispatch send and receive shows that offload increases the in-flight interval. Depending on the load, 32-96 microseconds of computation or other independent work between send and receive hides the deferred progress, leaving less exposed time than default GDA-KI. In disaggregated vLLM serving with DBO, GDA-KI Free Flow lowers median TPOT by 15-25% relative to NCCL-EP default GDA-KI and by 16-42% relative to DeepEP v1.

papers.title: Law-Invariant Operators for Stochastic Mechanics
papers.abstract: A central objective in stochastic mechanics is to separate deterministic physical behavior from the probability laws governing uncertain inputs. While classical spectral approaches achieve this separation in linear settings, nonlinear responses introduce interactions beyond conventional second-order variability response functions (VRF). Inspired by the spirit of VRFs, this work establishes that, for a fixed physical system, uncertainty propagation is described by a law-invariant operator mapping input realizations to responses, governed by the underlying physics and the deterministic parameters of the system. Different probability laws affect the input sampling and resulting response statistics, but not the mapping operator. We establish this law invariance under complete, invertible coordinate transformations and develop complementary, Fourier, fixed-reference polynomial-chaos (PCE) and finite element method (FEM) transfer formulations. Fourier captures nonlinear cross-frequency interactions and recovers the classical VRF in the appropriate linear limit, PCE describes coupling among stochastic modes, while FEM expresses the deterministic inverse-stiffness action. Neural approximations of these deterministic operators are investigated through analytical and finite-element benchmarks, examining cross-law generalization, the influence of training distributions and stochastic excitation, and the prediction of response fields and statistics. The results demonstrate the potential for reusing learned physical operators across different stochastic laws without retraining, while highlighting the importance of adequate training coverage and the challenges of accurately estimating low-probability events.

papers.title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding speeds up language models by having a lightweight drafter propose future tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Block diffusion drafters such as DFlash predict an entire block in one forward pass, and DDTree builds draft trees directly from their per-position distributions. Each distribution implicitly assumes that the drafter's own greedy continuation is accepted, whereas a draft tree improves over a chain only on branches that leave this greedy path. Once a path forks, the drafter's top-1 accuracy drops from 89% to 18% and its top candidates often miss the true token. Re-running the drafter from the fork token largely restores its accuracy, showing that the errors stem from conditioning on an outdated prefix rather than from limited model capacity. In this paper, we introduce DForkTree, a training-free method that re-anchors each branch on its own tokens. It adjusts the drafter's scores with pointwise mutual information from target-generated n-grams, weighted more heavily after a fork, and a layer-wise GPU search recovers the exact optimal tree under these scores. On Qwen3.5-4B and 9B, DForkTree outperforms all baselines on every benchmark, by up to 41.5% over DFlash and 15.1% over DDTree, with average speedups of up to 4.75x over autoregressive decoding.

papers.title: Lower intermediate dimensions of classical Denjoy minimal sets
papers.abstract: We study the $θ$-intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical $C^{1+δ}$ Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The $θ$-intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions. We use the well-understood gap structure of the irrational rotation map to develop a covering strategy to get upper bounds on the lower $θ$-intermediate dimension, and use results of Banaji to show that these upper bounds are sharp for $θ$ in an interval.

papers.title: HumanSightBench: A Benchmark for Human Visual Perception in MLLMs
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated strong performance on knowledge-intensive and reasoning-based vision-language benchmark datasets, but still struggle to solve the visual questions that people can solve easily. Evaluating the differences between MLLMs and human-level visual perception is challenging due to end-to-end evaluation which combines various skills, or because we are uncertain if individual items are valid. Specifically, observed errors may reflect visual perception, language priors, background knowledge, question ambiguity, and underspecified answers. Our guideline for HumanSightBench is that we construct items that are human-easy by construction and model-hard by evaluation. HumanSightBench contains 2,876 visual questions with short answers across 7 top-level perceptual categories and 21 subcategories. We only include items that pass five inclusion gates: question clarity, answer uniqueness, visual grounding, human solvability, and text-only shortcut filtering. According to the protocol, errors are defined as incorrect answers on human-validated visual tasks with the evaluated interface. The inclusion gates are intended to reduce confounds from ambiguity and external knowledge. The best pass@3 score is 65.6% across eight evaluated MLLMs. No evaluated model exceeds 27.5% on Counting. These results identify capability gaps that are hidden by overall scores and can help future training experiments and held-out evaluation.

papers.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
papers.abstract: Agentic workloads are a major source of LLM inference demand. Existing prefill--decode (PD) disaggregated serving systems offer limited flexibility for runtime adaptation of compute allocation and KV cache management, and rely on coarse signals that only partly capture the diverse and dynamic agent workload. These limitations lead to load imbalance between prefill and decode nodes and eviction of KV caches that agents will reuse. We present Evolving Infra, an agent-adaptive serving framework that adapts compute allocation to agent workloads and KV cache management to agent context management at runtime. We decouple compute allocation from key--value (KV) cache management, allowing nodes to switch efficiently between prefill and decode. Building on this design, an online planner matches the PD split to workload composition, while an agent-aware distributed KV manager guides cache eviction and transfer with signals from agent context management. Across coding, math, and computer-use tasks with GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 on up to 256 GB300 GPUs, Evolving Infra reduces mean end-to-end request latency and P95 TTFT by up to 4.1x and 14x over Dynamo, NVIDIA's production framework. We open-source the system implementation of Evolving Infra at https://github.com/mit-han-lab/EvolvingInfra.

papers.title: On the Abels--Garcke--Grün Model for Incompressible Two-Phase Flows with Unmatched Densities: Phase Separation and Rayleigh--Taylor Instability
papers.abstract: Instability phenomena are ubiquitous in multi-fluid flows. For binary fluid mixtures, phase separation may occur under specific conditions, in which a homogeneous state becomes unstable and spontaneously segregates into different phases, leading to the formation of distinct patterns. Furthermore, when a heavier fluid is superposed over a lighter one in a gravitational field, the fluid interface can be sensitive to perturbations that trigger the Rayleigh--Taylor (RT) instability, i.e., the lighter fluid penetrates upward into the heavier fluid against gravity. We investigate such instability phenomena and the inhibiting conditions for incompressible, immiscible two-phase flows with unmatched densities, within the framework of a diffuse-interface model, which is called the Abels--Garcke--Grün (AGG) model. More precisely, we adopt energy methods to establish several stability/instability conditions for the perturbed system of the AGG model, which is obtained by slightly perturbing the equilibrium profile $(\mathbf{0},\overlineφ)$, where $\overlineφ=\overlineφ(x_3)$ depends solely on the vertical coordinate $x_3$. Notably, for a constant equilibrium profile $\overlineφ=α\in(-1,1)$ satisfying $Ψ''(α)<0$, we establish a threshold for stability and instability of the phase-separation problem. Similar stability results are also established for the perturbed system with $\overlineφ$ satisfying the RT instability condition in the presence of gravity. In particular, if the phase-separation condition fails and $\partial_{x_3}\overlineφ$ is a constant, a larger value of $\partial_{x_3}\overlineφ$, a greater interfacial thickness and a higher surface energy density contribute to inhibiting RT instability.

papers.title: Transactional Data Change for Real-Time Analytics in Lakehouses
papers.abstract: Real-time data analytics has become a key demand for lakehouses. It requires propagating data changes from the data source to the lakehouse in real time, while ensuring ACID guarantees and minimizing resource consumption and impact on analytical query performance. This is highly challenging for a data system according to the RUM conjecture, especially given the read-optimized immutable file storage layer in lakehouses. Existing lakehouses offer only git-style catalog version control on a single table, and they trade data freshness, query performance, and/or resource efficiency to achieve a barely acceptable data-change throughput. In this paper, we propose a novel data synchronization framework, Retina, that enables real-time, cost-efficient, query-performant, and fully transactional data changes in lakehouses. We implement and open-source Retina. Evaluations show that Retina delivers 10-millisecond-level data freshness and over 3.2 million row/s linear-scalable data-change throughput with low resource consumption and query-performance overhead, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art lakehouse systems and lake-compatible HTAP databases.

papers.title: DisasterVLG: Vision-Language Grounding and Evidence-Based Reasoning for Disaster Scene Understanding
papers.abstract: General-purpose vision-language models struggle with crisis imagery due to its inherent noise, ambiguity, and high variability across disaster events - yet timely, accurate scene understanding is critical for humanitarian response. To address this, we introduce DisasterVLG, a large-scale multi-task dataset containing 1.24 million disaster images from 142 countries paired with 33 million structured annotations spanning dense captioning with localization, incident assessment, relational scene descriptions, and crisis-grounded visual question answering (VQA) across diverse hazard types and scene contexts worldwide. Unlike prior disaster benchmarks that focus narrowly on classification, DisasterVLG unifies recognition, grounded reasoning, and uncertainty-aware interpretation. A distinguishing feature is its evidence-grounded annotation design: each VQA instance includes supporting evidence text that links visual observations to answers, alongside positive and negative question pairs, multiple answer formats, and difficulty labels. Visual grounding layer links caption phrases to image regions and relationship statements to subject-object boxes, with explicit labels for visual supports and clues. To support rigorous evaluation, we construct a human-verified test set of 38K images (1.15M annotations) spanning broad geographic regions and disaster types. Experiments with domain-adapted vision-language models demonstrate strong performance across disaster captioning, incident recognition, and grounded VQA, while also exposing the limitations of general-purpose models in crisis-specific reasoning. DisasterVLG establishes a scalable, reproducible benchmark for vision-language models that must reason reliably under real-world uncertainty. We will publicly release the dataset, trained models, and code.

papers.title: Visible Tails: Characterizing Adaptation to Unknown Moments in Heavy-Tailed Bandits
papers.abstract: Heavy-tailed bandit learners must tell a poor arm from an arm whose favorable rewards have not yet appeared. We characterize this obstruction through a scale of one-sided visibility conditions on the optimal reward law: the mean hidden in a rare event is at most a constant multiple of a retained central moment. A quantile-trimmed UCB index that is given the visibility constants attains arm-specific moment rates at every exponent, with no lower bound on the exponent. Conversely, every strategy with a fixed exploration budget has polynomial regret on each law that violates the corresponding condition. For the variance benchmark we determine the order of both budget constants in the visibility level. The frontier depends on the largest exponent the benchmark promises, and the resulting classes are strictly nested. The same index has logarithmic expected regret when rewards are integrable, with a coefficient that can be exponential in the inverse gap.

papers.title: CARE-PO: Controllable Tool-Call Efficiency for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: External tool calls are a major running cost of an LLM agent, while its training objectives align almost exclusively with task completion. In a step-level diagnosis of Qwen3.5 trajectories at two model sizes on GAIA, a long-horizon tool-use benchmark, we find that most contain removable calls, at a similar rate at both sizes. Some methods add an efficiency reward to the objective to reduce the call count, but introduce problems of their own: the anchor they price calls against is computed from the policy's own rollouts (e.g., the group's shortest correct rollout) and so moves with the policy; training can drift toward a collapsed policy that issues no tool call at all, a degeneracy seen in published reports and in our 27B baseline; and a training run delivers a single operating point, so the user cannot trade efficiency against capability. We present CARE-PO (Controllable Anchored Relative Efficiency Policy Optimization) to mitigate these problems. The efficiency reward prices calls against a reference budget anchored to the task's own difficulty and fixed before training. Injecting a successful trajectory from the training data into each online GRPO rollout group and charging for evidence a trajectory never gathers ease the drift toward a collapsed call count. Shaping the cost curve by an effort tag in the prompt yields an efficiency and a capability operating point from a single training run. On GAIA, five of the six operating points across three model sizes improve on their base model in success rate and call count at once. On four held-out multi-hop benchmarks the result is size-dependent: at 27B and 4B success rate is held or raised at a lower call count, while at 9B both operating points trade success rate for fewer calls. The call count remains well above zero throughout training at all three sizes.

papers.title: Enhanced Mid-Photospheric Heating Around a Solar Pore
papers.abstract: We present depth-stratified atmospheric reconstructions of a solar pore observed with the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared SpectroPolarimeter (SCIP) aboard \textsc{Sunrise~iii}. Using spatially coupled NLTE spectropolarimetric inversions, we characterize the thermal, magnetic, and velocity structure of the pore and its surroundings from the photosphere to the chromosphere over approximately two hours. The inversions recover the canonical photospheric properties of pores: a cool umbra with strong magnetic fields dominated by the vertical component. Most photospheric velocities are subsonic, but localized downflows near the pore boundary reach transonic or potentially supersonic values around $\logτ_{500}=0$. At higher atmospheric layers, the thermal contrast between the pore and its surroundings decreases substantially. We also detect localized mid-photospheric temperature enhancements forming a patchy, ring-like structure in the wings of the Ca\,{\sc ii} 8542\,Å line, without a clear continuum counterpart. The temperature excess reaches approximately $300$\,K and corresponds to an excess thermal-energy density of up to $170$\,J\,m$^{-3}$. These regions coincide with an enhanced transverse magnetic-field component and the expanding magnetic canopy surrounding the pore. The structure is detected in all three rasters, although the cadence does not establish whether individual patches persist or repeatedly re-form. While the heating mechanism cannot be uniquely identified, the inferred magnetic topology supports an association with processes operating in the expanding canopy. These results demonstrate the value of pores for investigating the coupling between magnetic topology, convection, and atmospheric energy transport.

papers.title: SkillDuet: Co-Evolving Models and Skills through Response Feedback
papers.abstract: During reinforcement learning, experience can be both internalized in LLM parameters and retained externally as reusable textual skills. Parameter updates alter the model's behavior and the interaction experience from which new skills are extracted. These skills, in turn, guide the model's subsequent interactions and parameter updates. As the model's capabilities evolve, previously beneficial skills may become redundant or detrimental. We present SkillDuet, a framework that coordinates parameter updates and skill evolution through model response feedback. Skills extracted from on-policy trajectories guide parameter updates through OPD at every step. A response-based score, Strength, ranks candidate skills by the magnitude of the shift they induce in the current model's responses, and the highest-scoring skills are periodically consolidated into a persistent global skill set (Global). The updated model and Global jointly guide subsequent interactions, generating experience for further parameter and skill updates. With Qwen3-4B, SkillDuet achieves success rates of 98.57% on ALFWorld and 92.97% on WebShop, exceeding the matched SEED-API baseline by 2.86 and 5.47 percentage points, respectively. Ablations show that response-based skill selection and Global consolidation improve task performance. Further experiments show that the benefits of retained skills depend on both their content and their compatibility with the model. SkillDuet provides a concrete mechanism for model-skill co-evolution and skill-level recursive self-improvement.

papers.title: SAM-VTP: Video Memory and Measured Geometry for Continuous Traversability Segmentation
papers.abstract: Traversability prediction is a core component of autonomous navigation, yet most vision-based methods operate frame-wise and produce temporally inconsistent predictions. We present SAM-VTP (Video Traversability Prediction), which fine-tunes SAM2's video memory pathway for dense, prompt-free traversability segmentation, conditioning each frame on a persistent memory of prior observations. Rather than inferring terrain geometry from appearance, we measure it: slope, roughness and height are computed from depth and fused into the image features. We also introduce an offline continuous supervision pipeline that generates dense per-pixel traversability targets in [0,1] from depth-derived geometry and semantic priors, requiring no robot deployment and no per-pixel annotation, capturing conditional feasibility that binary labels cannot represent. On TartanGround, a large-scale synthetic ground-robot dataset, SAM-VTP improves fuzzy Jaccard from 0.908 to 0.924 and binary IoU from 0.854 to 0.886 over SAM-TP, a frame-wise SAM2 baseline, against a seed-to-seed spread below 0.001, and cuts frame-to-frame flicker by 31%. In closed-loop trials at two field sites, driving the same planner and controller, the baseline's dropouts leave the planner without a feasible path 3.3x more often on a paved course and 6.9x on rough ground, while SAM-VTP runs at 21.4 FPS on the Orin Nano the robot carries.

papers.title: Correct First, Fast Second: What a Local 7B Code Model Can and Cannot Do for GPU Kernel Optimization
papers.abstract: We study how much the interaction strategy around a fixed, locally hosted 7B-parameter code model (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct) affects its ability to replace PyTorch operators with custom CUDA kernels. On 30 KernelBench tasks (levels 1-3, first 10 each, evaluated on a V100), we compare four regimes of increasing structure: zero-shot prompting, profiling-guided prompting, iterative refinement on execution feedback, and a multi-agent loop (analysis, retrieval, generation, evaluation, feedback triage) in which the same model fills four roles around a non-LLM evaluator. Three findings stand out. (1) Correctness, not speed, is the binding constraint: even correct generated kernels average 0.97-0.99x the speed of eager PyTorch, because a 7B model cannot out-write cuBLAS/cuDNN on dense GEMM and convolution; the only real wins are fused memory-bound epilogues. (2) The best strategy depends on difficulty: profiling-guided prompting is strongest overall (43% correct, 27% faster than baseline), but the agent loop is the only method that solves any level-2 fusion problem (3/10 vs. 0/10 for all others). (3) Naive agentic scaffolding is actively harmful: our first agent scored 3% correct, below zero-shot's 30%, and the decisive repairs were matching the agent's ambition to the model's competence and spending compute on best-of-n sampling under a real execution oracle (3% to 33% correct from n=1 to n=8), not on more reasoning steps.

papers.title: From Token Bills to Benchmark Weeks: Making Auto-Research for Data Systems Verifiable and Affordable
papers.abstract: AI auto-research is poised to forge bespoke data systems, from key-value stores and indexes to query engines, each engineered for a specific workload and hardware platform. Yet this promise rests on fragile ground. An agent optimizes what it can measure, not necessarily what users need. Natural-language requirements leave ample room for specification gaming, producing systems that blaze through benchmarks while silently losing updates or violating consistency. Worse, each research iteration consumes tokens, while validating a candidate under real concurrency, memory pressure, and failure conditions can stretch the entire research process into weeks. In this paper, we envision a more cost-efficient and verifiable approach to auto-research. Precise and composable specifications anchor the search, lightweight performance critics prune costly dead ends, and falsification and deductive verification make correctness an integral part of the process rather than an afterthought. By treating correctness, performance, research time, and token cost as equally important objectives, we aim to transform AI-generated data systems from plausible artifacts into trustworthy, production-grade systems whose behavior can be understood, audited, and ultimately relied upon.

papers.title: Evaluating AI Agents for Industrial-Level Chip Floorplanning: A Framework and Empirical Study
papers.abstract: Floorplanning is an early step in turning a logical circuit into a physical chip: it positions large circuit modules and constrains the space available for subsequent logic placement and wiring. These decisions affect congestion and timing, but their physical consequences emerge through downstream implementation. For AI agents, the task requires translating engineering constraints into spatial decisions whose quality cannot be judged by successful tool execution alone. We present an evaluation framework that connects submitted layouts to a prescribed downstream implementation flow, checks geometric validity, measures physical quality, and reports resource use. On one industrial design whose 99 macros occupy approximately 71\% of a fixed L-shaped layout region, we compare our specialized system Nova-SI with general-purpose engineering agents and agents restricted to file access, obtaining complete physical measurements for 39 layout outputs. Under our 0--100 composite quality score, Nova-SI achieves a mean of 57.97 without online feedback from the prescribed power-grid and placement evaluation, compared with 31.17 for the strongest measured general-purpose configuration, GPT-6 Astra. The difference is supported by raw congestion and timing measurements and persists across scoring-sensitivity checks. Layout-level analysis further shows that similar global utilization can conceal substantially different local congestion. Together, the protocol and case study assess agents through the physical consequences of their delivered layouts and provide evidence about system performance on this industrial instance.

papers.title: DPGS-SLAM: Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Dynamic Visual Sensing
papers.abstract: This paper presents DPGS-SLAM (Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM) for dense mapping in environments containing dynamic objects. Objects in dynamic motion remain a significant challenge for dense visual SLAM since dynamic observations can contaminate camera tracking and scene reconstruction. Although 3DGS (3D Gaussian splatting) enables efficient dense mapping, existing 3DGS-SLAM systems may exhibit instability when dynamic objects violate their underlying static-scene assumption. Excluding dynamic observations can reduce their influence on tracking and mapping, but may leave occluded static backgrounds missing or weakly constrained. Our proposed DPGS-SLAM is a monocular RGB SLAM framework that supports provisional representations of insufficiently observed static backgrounds through asynchronous diffusion-based background completion and provenance-aware Gaussian mapping. Dynamic regions are identified through optical-flow-based motion discovery and temporally consistent mask propagation by SAM2. For selected keyframes, a fine-tuned diffusion inpainting model generates plausible background appearance in occluded regions, while metric depth predicted from completed images initializes provisional Gaussian primitives. Provenance labels distinguish generated primitives from observation-supported primitives, excluding generated content from camera-pose estimation and observed-map optimization. When previously occluded backgrounds become visible, eligible generated primitives are removed, and observation-supported primitives are independently initialized from real RGB observations and predicted depth. Experimental results demonstrated competitive camera tracking, with average ATE RMSE values of 1.2 cm on TUM RGB-D and 2.7 cm on BONN RGB-D datasets. On StaDy4D, DPGS-SLAM improved average PSNR by 4.60 dB over WildGS-SLAM using only monocular RGB input.

papers.title: AutoQS: Automated Quantization Strategy Design with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Quantization reduces LLM deployment costs, but effective strategies must balance model quality and storage. LLM-driven search can automate strategy design through repeated proposal and evaluation. This process must identify useful strategies within a limited evaluation budget. The key challenge is that \textit{actual quantization is expensive, while inexpensive proxies may not reflect quantized-model performance.} To address this challenge, we present AutoQS, an \textbf{Auto}mated \textbf{Q}uantization \textbf{S}trategy Design with LLMs. AutoQS keeps weight precision fixed and searches group-size allocations across layers and operators under deployment constraints. Evaluation history guides coordinated LLM proposals, while deterministic validation ensures compatible allocations. An inexpensive quality proxy evaluates candidates, and an candidate repository retains alternative allocations to inform subsequent proposals. Periodic actual quantization complements these proxy evaluations with measured quality and checkpoint storage, providing feedback for further search within the evaluation budget. Experiments on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct show that AutoQS improves seven-task average accuracy over uniform-group GPTQ and AWQ by 0.70 and 1.12 percentage points, respectively, at four-bit weight precision.

papers.title: Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids (DASH): Latency-Agnostic Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models for Humanoid Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models pair a vision-language backbone with an action head, but in closed-loop control the backbone sits on the control-critical path: while it computes, the robot keeps moving, so each executed action is conditioned on an increasingly stale observation. A larger backbone therefore directly blocks reactivity, especially in humanoid dexterous manipulation. We present DASH, a Decoupled Asynchronous System for Humanoids that removes this coupling. DASH splits the policy into a slow vision-language model (System 2) and a fast flow-matching action head (System 1) that run as concurrent processes over the LCM communication protocol, so the control rate is set by the action head alone, independent of backbone size. The action head fuses stale semantics from a frozen backbone with fresh vision from its own ResNet encoder, desynchronized training exposes it to the staleness it meets at deployment, and an adaptive temporal aggregator aligns overlapping action chunks under variable inference latency. On an asynchronous RoboTwin benchmark that charges inference latency in simulated time, DASH holds 20 Hz control rate from 0.8B to 8B backbones while the synchronous rate falls from 9.7 to 4.1 Hz, with higher success at every size. On a real humanoid with dexterous hands, DASH achieves clearly higher pick-and-place success than the synchronous pipeline.

papers.title: Long-distance quantum secure direct communication with Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits
papers.abstract: The Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) code possesses a lattice periodic structure that enables the effective correction of small displacement errors induced by noise in phase space, which is indispensable for quantum computation. The GKP code was also used to construct a long-distance entanglement channel in quantum repeaters and distribute random keys in quantum key distribution (QKD). Using GKP encoding, we propose a quantum secure direct communication (QSDC) protocol that not only transmits the secret message directly, but also helps protect the safety of communication personnel. The exponential attenuation loss of photons can be overcome by the third-generation quantum repeater. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that secure transmission distance exceeding 1000 km is achievable with a 23 dB squeezing level. Furthermore, we establish a cost-based optimization framework to characterize the trade-off among secure communication distance, secrecy capacity, and repeater resources, enabling optimized repeater deployment and providing a systematic design strategy for scalable quantum repeater architectures. The results demonstrate the potential of combining GKP error correction for long-distance QSDC and quantum networks.

papers.title: Model-family selection and recovery-gate design in generator-based noise tomography
papers.abstract: Family selection in generator-model noise tomography, usually quoted as a hardware property, is a hypothesis test whose shot floor is closed form under a purely coherent noise model, $N^{*}=λ_{\mathrm{req}}/(r_{\mathrm{b}} S)^{2}$, controlled by the absolute bias $r_{\mathrm{b}} S$ rather than by the relative residual $r_{\mathrm{b}}$, hence computable for any device from a calibration, before a single shot. The same computation prices the recovery gates: the fingerprint that fixes a family's residual and the Fisher information that ranks designs come from the same map, so there is no design-independent verdict and no family-independent design optimum. Whether a design can move that price is structural: a bias confined to the block every design measures identically is design-blind, while one that reaches the code blocks can be repriced by a factor of sixty-eight; the two platforms are its extremes, at $98.1\%$ and $48.0\%$. At the reference point the floor is $1.1\times10^{7}$ and $6.7\times10^{6}$ shots per component, and that point is the easy corner: the median of its own direction over the sampled points is $8.9\times10^{8}$, $83$ times dearer. At the $10^{5}$ shots a run spends the test has power $0.053$ at a level of $0.05$. Rebuilding the fingerprint under each of the sixty-four designs moves the floor by $68$ on one platform and $1.7$ on the other, and the most precise design costs ten times more shots for the verdict than the cheapest to test. All sixty-four placements are full rank: at three gates the rms varies by factors of $2.7$ and $3.9$ with placement alone, while the optimum over counts is flat. At five qubits the same rule moves the floor by $21$ while the verdict costs $10^{9}$ shots; against a real three-qubit calibration the floor is a requirement on systematic control before it is a shot count, and where that control is missing no budget supplies it.

papers.title: Steering Emergent Behavior in Multi-Agent LLM Systems via Information Networks
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate in groups, each pursuing an individual objective while jointly determining system performance. If an operator controls which agent observes which other agent, but not their payoffs or messages, how should observations be structured to raise collective welfare? We make the information network (who observes whom) a design object, decoupled from the fixed interaction network over which agents act. Ten identical LLM agents play repeated group-decision games; by default each observes only an anonymous summary of the group's previous-round outcome, and a manager with a fixed budget adds directed observation links that reveal peers' past actions. Across 1,080 episodes and six games spanning coordination, anti-coordination, social dilemmas, and discovery, we ask how much information to share and, at a fixed budget, who should observe whom. Disclosure creates behavioral coupling: observation acts as a contagion channel whose welfare effect depends on the alignment between individually attractive behavior and the collective objective. First, the value of information is alignment-contingent: more peer information tends to help or be neutral when individual behavior is aligned with the collective goal, but under free-riding or congestion externalities it amplifies collectively harmful behavior; in a public-goods game the group does best with no information at all. We read this sign separation as a cross-game regularity within one controlled LLM population, not a model-invariant law. Second, at a fixed budget, who observes whom matters primarily when coupling is harmful: a modular "barbell" that lets sub-populations entrench harmful behavior is reliably the worst wiring, reversing the network-reciprocity intuition from human evolutionary game theory. These results argue against a default of full transparency for agent collectives.

papers.title: Compute Regeneration through Re-Productization: Reorganizing Retired Edge AI Silicon into a Delivered Multilingual Service Robot
papers.abstract: Useful edge hardware can lose product support while retaining substantial computation. We treat this as systems design: compute regeneration here means re-productization, retaining the compute module while redesigning the surrounding product organization. Our case is GEdgeBot, a multilingual service robot built around a retired 32 GB Jetson AGX Xavier. A source-grounded inventory shows the box alone supplies inference, while the combined system exposes five on-device AI services, a seven-language speech chain, three sensing domains, and one deterministic seven-byte control boundary. AI and orchestration stay on the Xavier; finite motor-pulse generation on an STM32F407. Audits cover the six-mode control state machine, readiness barriers and sound orientation. Historical single-prototype measurements report 1,782 MB GPU memory with YOLO, Whisper-small, and NLLB-200 resident, a direct-control p99 deviation rising from 0.24 to 49.93 ms under concurrent AI load, and six of six trigger-to-follow demonstrations at 4.35 s mean latency, with conversational voice unavailable. A November campaign restores an isolated inference stack, re-measures AI workloads, and repeats control-frame runs. Driving two execution organisations with the same 6,000 measured 50 ms frame intervals shows the finite-pulse boundary removes host jitter from the pulse train but not the command start phase; its stopping bound is host-enforced, while the MCU 16-bit pulse field is unclamped. A six-check static audit exposes a host--MCU queue mismatch, and a 14-scenario replay executes the audited main() dispatcher across six modes with zero physical device opens and 54 contract-checked frames. Results support an existence claim and a reproducible architectural hypothesis, not fleet-level reliability. The 208 direct-control ratio remains unreplicated; MCU waveform capture and on-site fault injection remain open.

papers.title: Known Good, Known Bad: A Ground-Truth Calibration Protocol for AI Judgment in Science
papers.abstract: Scientific use of generative AI requires evaluation against cases with independently checkable answers. We present a ground truth calibration protocol that compares a verified reference case with reference deviant variants through neutral evaluation, an authority framed recheck, and a line by line audit. Human adjudication distinguishes deviation detection, premise accommodation, unsupported doubt, and correctness of the resulting calculation. An instructor generated organic chemistry demonstration comprises six conversations and 18 responses from an unidentified backend served through the free logged out ChatGPT interface in July 2026. Neutral evaluation detected three of five intended deviations. Both initial misses, involving oxidant stoichiometry and experimental scale, were detected at the authority framed second turn; all five detections persisted at the third turn audit. The fixed sequence supports a descriptive account of recovery across turns. In the scale case, the model initially produced a locally coherent peroxide limited yield. After recognizing the unit problem, it incorrectly retained that limiting reagent conclusion for the corrected scale. Detection and numerical repair therefore require separate assessment. The verified reference attracted speculative concerns while retaining its correct yield calculation. The protocol connects documentary verification of scientific claims and citations with empirical verification of laboratory interpretations. It supplies inspectable transcripts, reference calculations, behavior codes, and a reusable calibration architecture for AI literacy instruction. The pilot demonstrates the protocol's measures in one case family; replicated model evaluation and learner assessment are the next validation steps.

papers.title: Characterizing Scanpath Decoding Pipelines with Perturbation Profiles
papers.abstract: When a scanpath descriptor supports a classification, it is rarely clear what the classification rests on. We propose perturbation profiles. Five transformations each target one stated property of every scanpath (fixation order, the coupling of durations to positions, the duration distribution, orientation and handedness, and fine spatial structure) while preserving a listed set of invariants. The classifier is refit, and the change in participant-held-out AUC is the pipeline's sensitivity to that property. Intervals come from a participant bootstrap that refits the classifier; in simulations they were conservative (99.7% coverage; standard errors about 1.8 times the empirical spread). We profiled nine descriptors on thirteen binary problems from three public datasets, with a within-fold AUC and class-balanced folds and a stated rule for which sensitivities to interpret. Of 565 intervals, 95 excluded zero; 80 were robust to the pooled AUC, 20 fold partitions and longer runs (36 of them within +/-0.05 AUC), and 45 also held with boosted trees. Most came from GazeBase (322 participants). Permuting fixation order raised the AUC of a descriptor based on mean saccade amplitude, because permuted amplitude has as its expectation the mean pairwise distance, a measure of spread. A "comprehension" contrast pooled over two programs was a contrast between their layouts: it vanished among trials of the same program, and synthetic gaze drawn from the layout alone reproduced the program contrast beneath it. For native versus non-native readers, spatial jitter at the scale of text lines reduced recurrence's discrimination. A Python package is released.

papers.title: Solar cycle variations of meridional flow and differential rotation in a non-kinematic dynamo model
papers.abstract: Flux transport dynamo models have emerged as the leading paradigm for explaining the observed solar cycle. However, most of these models are kinematic and axisymmetric. We develop a non-kinematic dynamo model by specifying large-scale flows, such as the differential rotation and meridional flow. Thus, our model does not require the $Λ$ effect or other parameterisations of turbulent transport to generate the large-scale flows; it only solves the fluctuating flows and thermodynamics. Our model is inherently 3D by construction, although it is currently operating in axisymmetric mode because the source for poloidal field generation (Babcock-Leighton $α$) is assumed to be axisymmetric. Our model reproduces solar-cycle variations in both the meridional flow and the differential rotation -- specifically, the torsional oscillation in some agreement with observations. The model naturally exhibits some variability in the solar cycle, even without incorporating stochastic fluctuations, offering a new methodology for modelling the non-kinematic solar dynamo in 3D.

papers.title: Universal Critical Relations and Nonuniversal Scaling in Inverse-Square Ising Chains
papers.abstract: For ferromagnetic Ising chains with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, the critical excess magnetization in a field inversely proportional to spin separation determines the connected correlation. Their slowly varying profile has finite logarithmic integral exactly when the ordered thermal slope is finite. For any finite nonnegative core, an exact tail gives inverse-logarithmic correlations and a square-root cusp. A relative correction $c/\log(n+e)$ with $c>1$ gives continuously varying logarithmic powers and a linear cusp. A lower bound on its disordered susceptibility excludes the usual Kosterlitz--Thouless law.

papers.title: PLDP-IDS: Personalized Local Differential Privacy for Infinite Data Stream
papers.abstract: Existing $w$-event local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms for streaming data impose a uniform privacy window and budget, forcing all users to adopt the most stringent privacy requirement. We study personalized continual frequency estimation under LDP, where each user specifies her own window size and privacy budget, and identify two challenges. First, a single sampling size cannot balance sampling and perturbation errors for privacy groups with heterogeneous requirements. Second, borrowing estimates from groups with larger budgets reduces variance but introduces bias when privacy preferences correlate with the data. We first propose Optimal Population Selection (OPS) and two OPS-guided mechanisms, PLPD and PLPA, which use one privacy-compatible sampling size for all users. Since one size cannot fit all groups and pooling their estimates is biased under privacy--data correlation, we further develop PLPD$^+$ and PLPA$^+$, which combine group-aware population scheduling with bias-aware cross-group fusion while preserving personalized $w$-event LDP. Experiments on real-world and synthetic streams show that, compared with the direct personalized extension of LDP-IDS, PLPA$^+$ reduces the average mean squared error (AMSE) by 52.3\% and 40.8\% on average, respectively, and remains 4.3--5.1$\times$ more accurate than PLPA under strong privacy--data correlation.

papers.title: Agent Self-Improvement with Frozen Weights: The Added Value and Limits of Failure Traces
papers.abstract: We evaluate whether an AI agent's harness, the notes around its model, can learn from the agent's failure traces beyond a matched search that never sees them. It can, but less than it looks. We tested an open 9-billion-parameter model with fixed weights; a larger teacher model wrote its notes. On generated customer-service decisions, where both note writers were told the target rules, notes based on the agent's mistakes improved accuracy by 4.0 percentage points over notes from the same process with the mistakes withheld. That process alone, trying and keeping better-scoring notes, reached about 60% of the total improvement. In full customer-service conversations the same notes showed no demonstrated improvement. Separately, a strict screen of single lessons admitted two customer-service lessons, still awaiting tests on new data, and one tool-use lesson, written without seeing the agent's mistakes, which showed no demonstrated gain on new tool-use tasks. A neutral note with no procedure scored higher than the learned lessons (exploratory). A blind audit judged 146 of 240 tool-use test items defective.

papers.title: Stanley Deser 19th March 1931 - 21st April 2023
papers.abstract: Stanley Deser was Ancell Professor Emeritus at Brandeis University and Visiting Professor at the California Institute of Technology. He was a world-renowned theoretical physicist whose accomplishments include the Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) formulation of general relativity, supergravity with Zumino, the dynamics of flat space with Jackiw and 't Hooft and many other contributions to the quantum theory of gravity. In the 1980s he was instrumental in securing National Science Foundation approval of the LIGO gravitational wave experiment against much opposition. He was awarded the Einstein Medal in 2015 for important contributions to general relativity, in particular the development of the ADM formalism. Other awards include: The Dannie Heineman Prize 1994; Fellow of the National Academy of Sciences 1994; Honorary Member of the Torino Academy of Sciences 2001; Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences 1979, Fellow of the American Institute of Physics.

papers.title: ScrapeBench: Evaluating Legal Compliance of AI Agents in Website Scraping
papers.abstract: AI agents deployed on the open web are becoming more capable of performing actions that may breach contractual provisions and violate computer security laws. In this paper, we introduce ScrapeBench, the first agentic benchmark for empirically evaluating the legal compliance of AI agents with website scraping policies, namely terms of service (ToS) and robots$.$txt directives. Across widely used closed-weight and open-weight AI agents, we find that most agents exhibit low compliance rates (below 5%) when instructed to scrape websites in our sample of 1,626 popular websites that explicitly prohibit scraping. In addition, we observe that even where AI agents actively check the applicable ToS and robots$.$txt, they continue to exhibit low compliance rates. Conversely, in our sample of 269 websites that do not prohibit scraping, we observe that agents sometimes refuse to scrape despite it being lawful, such as Claude Opus 4.6 exhibiting an over-refusal rate of 98.5%. Our human baseline experiments (n = 180 participants) suggest that humans exhibit compliance rates comparable to AI agents but over-refuse at much higher rates.

papers.title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
papers.abstract: For bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring, we establish natural Dieudonné isomorphisms between Ekedahl's biduality pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$, the nilpotent and semi-simple torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud cœur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. In bidegree $(0,i+1)$, this torsion measures the non-smoothness of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group; hence all such groups are smooth for Mazur--Ogus varieties. For a smooth projective surface $S$, we describe the three possible dual pairs via the Galois module $\NS(\bar{S})[p^\infty]$ and the local-local and local-étale parts of the finite Picard quotient.

papers.title: Improving the Trifference Lower Bound via Non-Perfect Hashing
papers.abstract: We strictly improve the Körner-Marton lower bound $\frac14\log \frac{9}{5}$ on the asymptotic rate of trifferent codes. We obtain this improvement by constructing non-perfect $(9,3)$-hash codes with rate above $\log(9/5)$ and then applying the Tetra-code construction, which gives $R_3\ge\frac14R_{9,3}$. More generally, for every $q\ge4$, we prove $R_{q,3}>B_{q,3}+\frac1{250000}$. We also extend the method to $(p,2,3)$-list recovery. For every $q\ge4$ and $0\le p<\frac{q-2}{12(q-1)}$, we prove $R_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)>B_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)$. Here $B_{q,3}$ and $B_q^{\mathrm{LR}}(p)$ denote the respective probabilistic lower bounds. For every fixed $0\le p<1/18$, the rate improvement is bounded below by a positive constant independent of $q\ge4$. For every fixed $0\le p<1/12$, we also obtain a positive rate improvement independent of $q$ for all sufficiently large $q$.

papers.title: On Rankin Invariants of Ideal Lattices
papers.abstract: The Rankin constant $γ_{n,k}$ measures the largest discriminant of a densest rank $k$ sublattice of a lattice in $\R^n$ over all such lattices of rank $n$ and their exact values are mostly open. For a general lattice $L\subset \R^n$ of rank $n$, the problem of determining its Rankin invariant $γ_{n,k}(L)$ is to find the discriminant of such a densest sublattice. There are no general formulas to compute the discriminant of any arbitrary rank $k$ sublattice. This paper specializes to the case of ideal lattices arising from ideals of number fields, and provides two approaches to study Rankin constants: first, we propose a systematic approach to approximate the minimum discriminant by introducing subideal lattices and proving a closed-form formula to compute $γ^{ideal}_{n,k}(L)$, the ideal Rankin invariant of the ideal lattice. Subsequently, we establish necessary conditions on the underlying number field for the existence of an ideal lattice admitting an optimal subideal lattice with a prescribed minimum discriminant. Secondly, we consider ideal lattices with arbitrary sublattices. We improve the current known bounds of the Rankin constants $γ_{5,2}$, $γ_{7,2}$ and $γ_{9,2},γ_{9,3},γ_{9,4}$, and provide an algebraic construction of the lattice that was used in these dimensions.

papers.title: Efficient VLA Inference via Retrieval-Based Speculation and Hardware Acceleration
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to understand and execute complex instructions, but their autoregressive (AR) action generation introduces significant latency on resource-constrained robotic platforms. Speculative decoding can accelerate AR-based inference by parallelizing action generation and verification; however, existing approaches rely on costly draft models, which are inefficient on edge platforms. In this paper, we propose Zora, a hardware-software co-design framework for accelerating AR-based VLA inference. Specifically, Zora introduces a lightweight retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-based draft model that exploits robotic dynamics without additional neural draft models. We further reduce batch verification overhead through a kinematics-guided action-acceptance strategy and a KV-cache-sharing attention mechanism. To address the retrieval overhead introduced by RAG-based drafting, we co-design dedicated hardware support, Zora core, to address the memory irregularity in RAG-based drafting. We evaluate Zora on four VLA models with the LIBERO benchmark. Zora retains comparable accuracy while achieving up to 3.4$\times$ speedup with software-only optimization and up to 7.6$\times$ speedup with hardware support over GPUs.

papers.title: Who Benefits from Wikipedia's Growth Mentorship? The Role of Newcomer Information Needs
papers.abstract: Evaluations of Wikipedia's programs for new editors usually ask whether a program works on average; we ask which newcomers benefit when their question to a mentor gets a reply. English Wikipedia's Growth mentorship system assigns every new account a volunteer mentor, and about a quarter of the questions newcomers send never get a reply. Using the first questions of 34,073 newcomers (2021 to 2026), we compare newcomers who received a reply with newcomers who did not, within groups that are similar on 164 characteristics recorded before the question (propensity score stratification). (1) Does a reply help newcomers keep editing? Yes, in the short term: in the 14 days after the reply, newcomers who received one were 1.8 percentage points (pp) more likely to edit an article (22% vs. an estimated 20% without a reply) and 1.8pp more likely to edit on two or more days. Later in the first year, the only difference that remains significant after correction for multiple testing is in the share who edit an article at least once between six months and one year after the reply (+1.5pp). (2) Does the effect depend on what the newcomer asked? Yes. We sort questions by Morrison's (1993) information-seeking types, which earlier studies measured mostly through self-reports, using a language model checked against human labels. A reply has significant effects for questions about rules and norms (+3.4pp), questions that show the newcomer's earlier editing (+3.4pp) and specific how-to questions (+2.4pp). For newcomers who do not know what to work on, a reply has no detectable effect, and the effect is 4.2pp smaller than for newcomers with other questions. (3) Which replies are followed by more editing? Among newcomers who received a reply, those whose reply came sooner or stayed closer to the topic of their question edited more.

papers.title: Non-log-concave $τ$-polynomials of regular graphs
papers.abstract: For any simple graph $G$ of order $n$, write its chromatic polynomial in the rising factorial basis as $P(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}(-1)^{n-j}c_j(G)x^{\langle j\rangle}$, where $x^{\langle j\rangle}=\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(x+i)$ for $j\ge1$ and $x^{\langle 0\rangle}=1.$ Brenti (1992) introduced the $τ$-polynomial of $G$ and its augmented version, defined by $$τ(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^n c_j(G)x^j~~~\text{and}~~~\overline τ(G,x)=\sum_{j=0}^n j!c_j(G)x^j.$$ He asked whether $τ(G,x)$ is always real-rooted and whether the coefficient sequence of $\overline τ(G,x)$ is always log-concave. In this paper, we prove that for every integer $d\ge4$, there exists an integer $h_d\ge3$ such that $c_2(G)^2<c_1(G)c_3(G)$ for every connected $d$-regular graph $G$ of girth at least $h_d$. For such graphs, the coefficient sequences of both polynomials fail log-concavity at $j=2$, and thus both polynomials have nonreal roots by Newton's inequalities. This gives counterexamples to both questions among connected regular graphs of arbitrarily large girth.

papers.title: Dynamical entropy on local causal horizons: the Einstein equation of state and canonical-energy flux
papers.abstract: For a twist-free null hypersurface, the Hollands-Wald-Zhang (HWZ) representative $S_{\rm loc}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1-Vθ)dA$, local on each cross-section (cut), obeys an exact off-shell Raychaudhuri identity with no term linear in the expansion, so no final equilibrium cut is needed. Given an entropy density $1/4G$, the Unruh temperature $κ/2π$ of an approximate local boost, local equilibrium cuts, and stress-tensor conservation, equating the leading equilibrium change of $S_{\rm loc}$ to matter boost heat yields $R_{kk}=8πGT_{kk}$ for every null direction, hence the Einstein equation with undetermined cosmological constant, an equation of state in Jacobson's conditional sense. On a fixed caustic-free generator bundle with $dA=J\,dA_{\rm ref}$, the functional $S_{\rm L}=(4G)^{-1}\int(1+\ln J-Vθ)dA_{\rm ref}$ obeys an exact balance per reference cell with curvature, shear, and expansion terms all positive, so under null convergence $S_{\rm L}$ is nondecreasing for $V\geq0$ until the first caustic. Conversely, requiring this balance for positive affine parameter on every small bundle and null direction is equivalent to the Einstein equation, given conservation and the stated normalization. Cut-locality, positivity, and first-order HWZ normalization select the density $1+\ln J-Vθ$ uniquely within a two-function class. Both functionals depend on the affine origin; we give their shift laws, identify the anchoring-invariant content, and show the origin is physical data fixed by the equilibrium cut. Near equilibrium, $S_{\rm L}$ agrees with the HWZ dynamical entropy at first order, and the temperature-weighted change of its Hessian equals the HWZ modified canonical-energy flux for stationary-vacuum perturbations. At finite amplitude, $S_{\rm L}$ is only a monotone geometric functional; reading it as entropy requires a coarse-graining postulate, stated but not derived.

papers.title: Do Modern Difference-in-Differences Estimators Change Published Findings in Business Research?
papers.abstract: Staggered-adoption difference-in-differences (DiD) designs are a workhorse of empirical research in business-school journals. The two-way fixed effects (TWFE) estimator that typically implements them can place negative weights on heterogeneous treatment effects. We ask whether negative weights change published findings by reanalyzing staggered-adoption specifications in business-school journals with journal-wide public replication archives. Following Hull (2026), we use large language model agents to identify eligible specifications, replicate the published TWFE estimate, and re-estimate each specification with the DiD-averaging estimator of Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) and the imputation estimator of Borusyak et al. (2024). We re-estimate 355 specifications from 40 papers. Across the 283 DiD-averaging and 306 imputation comparisons that pass Hull's leverage screen, from 28 and 29 papers, TWFE and modern estimates have correlations of 0.61 and 0.70, change sign in 25.1 and 18.0 percent of comparisons, and differ significantly with opposite signs in 10.2 and 7.2 percent. Modern standard errors are 1.61 and 1.30 times those of TWFE. Including the comparisons that fail the screen leaves these figures essentially unchanged. Our results suggest that TWFE and heterogeneity-robust estimators disagree in a non-negligible share of the published staggered designs we re-estimate, and more often than in economics.

papers.title: Spectral function, OPE, and QNMs detect different singular points of black branes with unequal R-charges
papers.abstract: We consider black brane solutions in the STU model, with three R-charges labeled by the parameters $q_1,q_2,q_3$. For equal R-charges $q_1=q_2=q_3$, the solution becomes the Reissner-Nordström black brane. For unequal R-charges $q_1>q_2>q_3\geq0$, there are three curvature singular points at $R\equiv r^2=-q_i$. Only $R=-q_3$ is the physical singularity, and the other two lie beyond it. Their optical times $T_i$, the complex times of null rays from the boundary to these singular points and back, form a right triangle in the complex $T$-plane. We probe these singular points using three observables, all built from the retarded correlator of $T_{xy}$ at zero spatial momentum: spectral function, OPE coefficients, and QNMs. The exponentially small correction to the spectral function at large real frequency is dominated by $T_1$ and $T_2$, which have the smallest ${\rm Im}\,T_i$. The OPE convergence radius is determined by $T_1$, which has the smallest $|T_i|$. A line of QNMs lies along the direction of $1/T_2$, since $T_2$ has the smallest phase $\arg T_i$. Furthermore, there is a second line of QNMs along the negative imaginary axis, which carries information about $T_3$ corresponding to the physical singularity. We derive these results from a WKB analysis and check them numerically. The three observables are therefore sensitive to different singular points of the geometry.

papers.title: A Nested Heterogeneous Multiscale Framework for Power System Dynamic Simulation
papers.abstract: Power system dynamics involve multiple timescales, from electromagnetic transients of the network and inverter-based resources to electromechanical oscillations of synchronous generators and quasi-steady-state evolution of the operating point. Simulating these dynamics with a detailed electromagnetic transient model is computationally prohibitive, whereas existing methods reduce the model to focus on a single timescale and lose accuracy when dynamics of different timescales interact. This paper proposes a nested heterogeneous multiscale framework for highly efficient multi-timescale simulation of a power system represented by one unified detailed model. Rather than varying only the integration step, the framework adaptively shifts the simulation resolution among three nested levels so that the dynamics of interest at each stage are always captured, with the slower dynamics estimated on the fly from short detailed simulations at controlled accuracy.
