In this report, we present a comprehensive evaluation of the Locality Domain (LD) feature introduced in CUDA 13.4. Conducted on a single node equipped with eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs, our study examines three aspects: memory management and access, computation, and communication, to identify the sources of latency and, more importantly, explore how LD can mitigate them. Our measurements show that the benefits of LD depend on data access patterns. Through die-aware adaptations and integration with widely used libraries and tools, we achieve speedups of up to 43.5% for NCCL 2.32.3 (AllGather), 111.3% for nvbandwidth (DtoD), and 37% for DeepGEMM (EP). We also identify non-negligible LD-related GPU memory allocation overhead when allocation sizes exceed 32 MB due to barrier and TLB invalidation, we propose a fix to the GPU driver kernel module (submitted to NVIDIA) and show that overhead could be reduced 7x ~ 10x without requiring any user-code changes.

papers.title: When Does Blockwise Additivity Break? Diagnosing and Repairing the Additive Assumption in Distillation-Based Architecture Search
papers.abstract: Blockwise distillation methods for architecture search, such as DNA, DONNA, LANA and Puzzle, score each candidate replacement block in isolation and combine the scores additively. We ask at which budgets this additivity assumption fails, whether fine-tuning repairs the failure, what diagnoses it, and how it can be repaired cheaply. On DeiT-S, DeiT-B, Swin-T and Qwen2.5-0.5B with seven latency budgets each, an additive integer program trails a pairwise interaction-aware program after fine-tuning by at most 1.6 top-1 points on ImageNet-1k at the mildest budgets, but by up to 17.5 points, and a factor of 1.9 in perplexity, at aggressive ones. After 10,000 fine-tuning steps 3.3-9.9 points remain on DeiT, whereas on Swin-T the gap shrinks to at most about 1.8 points within 500 steps. In a learning-rate sweep with the standard 2,000 steps, 6.0-10.7 points remain on DeiT when each method's rate is chosen by its evaluation-set accuracy. An intervention that keeps the block library and only forbids more than two removals in any three adjacent layers shrinks the DeiT gap from 5.8-17.5 to 0.7-5.2 points, mostly by improving the additive solution: adjacent removals are a major failure pattern. Splitting the additivity error into a metric and a functional part, relative to additive logit changes, indicates where a cheap logit-sum predictor can be trusted. A hybrid search that ranks moves with this predictor and measures only the best needs no pair measurements and, after Holm adjustment, is significantly better than the pairwise program in 10 of 14 ImageNet-1k settings, with no statistically significant losses. An ablation shows that its ranking helps except at the most aggressive DeiT-B budget, where the predictor misleads and random ranking or ten-times-costlier evolution does better.

papers.title: Prediction of antimagnon-polarons with intrinsic momentum-space level attraction
papers.abstract: Propagating hybrid quasiparticles formed by magnons and phonons (magnon-polarons) or photons (magnon-polaritons) typically exhibit level repulsion in momentum space. Level attraction, by contrast, requires an anti-phase channel and has so far been restricted to zero-dimensional systems mediated by dissipative baths. Here we predict the antimagnon-polaron in a continuous magnetoelastic medium, which inherently exhibits momentum-space level attraction. The spin-orbit-torque (SOT)-stabilized antimagnon precesses with opposite handedness, directly reversing the magnetoelastic coupling without requiring an external environment. This intrinsic attraction yields a distinctive 0/π phase-locked simultaneous growth. Micromagnetic simulations confirm this picture, revealing that the SOT-controlled balance between gain and damping drives a collective instability. This ultimately enables a continuously tunable, dc-pumped, single-frequency phonon laser, establishing a novel route for coherent acoustic emission.

papers.title: Certifying the Rydberg-exposure limit of a globally driven controlled-Z gate
papers.abstract: Rydberg excitation enables entangling gates in neutral-atom quantum processors but also exposes them to spontaneous decay. Whether this exposure can be made arbitrarily small through pulse shaping and longer gate times has remained unresolved. We show that an exact controlled-$Z$ gate driven by a single global laser has an irreducible Rydberg-exposure cost in the perfect-blockade regime. The product of the maximum Rabi frequency $Ω_{\max}$ and the average time $T_R$ spent in the Rydberg state is bounded below by $2.9312$, independent of pulse shape and duration. We derive this bound using a sum-of-squares certificate, strengthened by constraints imposed by the shared drive. Using interval arithmetic, we also certify the existence of an exact gate pulse with $Ω_{max} T_R<2.9359$. The unrounded bounds differ by less than $0.16\%$. The bound identifies a fundamental cost of shared-drive entangling dynamics and establishes a benchmark against which future gate-control strategies can be assessed.

papers.title: Patch-Based Generalized Neural Texture Upscaling
papers.abstract: We propose a lightweight neural texture upscaling method. A single generalized MLP is trained on a diverse collection of texture patches and integrated into the texture sampling stage, upscaling low-resolution textures on-the-fly at rendering time. Because the model is generalized rather than overfit to specific content, no per-asset training is required - the same model applies to any existing scene without modifying texture data or the asset pipeline. Storing lower-resolution base textures reduces disk footprint, upscaling at sampling time eliminates the need to store high-resolution textures in VRAM, and sharing a single set of model weights across all textures ensures non-divergent GPU execution. We evaluate our method across multiple texture classes, demonstrating consistent improvement over analytic upscaling methods in perceptual quality.

papers.title: Double Machine Learning for Panel Data: Identification, Specification, and a Bank Regulation Effect
papers.abstract: This paper examines robustness and causal interpretation of panel estimates using double/debiased machine learning. The prototype treatment setup is the 2018 US banking regulation. Under common treatment timing, we characterize identification and nuisance restrictions and derive exact bank-level representations of specified "within" and "first-difference" scores. Simulations assess panel model transformation-induced specification bias and inference under weaker overlap. Empirically, estimates vary with asset-size classification and prior growth. Prior-growth adjustment reduces overlap-weighted estimates across four Machine Learners (ML); doubly robust estimates depend on the fitted propensity and concentrated weights. Both bank groups received relief, so we estimate differential exposure effects. The findings highlight specification issues and the relation between functional-form robustness and causal identification.

papers.title: Breaking dark degeneracies in $k$-essence models with redshift-space distortions
papers.abstract: Dynamical dark energy models are often difficult to constrain with background observations alone due to parameter degeneracies. This is especially true when the dark energy sector evolves through an effective pressureless matter phase, leading to degeneracies between the model parameters and the matter density parameter. In this work, we show that redshift-space distortion (RSD) measurements help break this degeneracy when combined with expansion history probes including Pantheon$^{+}$ supernovae and DESI DR2 BAO measurements. We demonstrate this in the ghost and dilatonic ghost condensate $k$-essence models, restricting the observational analysis to physically admissible solutions by imposing the absence of ghosts and gradient instabilities. Given the small scalar sound speeds in these models, we also explicitly check the validity of the quasi-static approximation used in the growth analysis. Our results show that combining growth-rate data with stability requirements and standard background observations provides a fast and efficient way to constrain potentially degenerate dark sector models.

papers.title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
papers.abstract: We prove a lower bound of $Ω_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ for the worst-case combinatorial discrepancy of $N$-point sets with respect to anchored boxes in every fixed dimension $d\ge3$. Together with Nikolov's upper bound of the same order and Wei's planar lower bound, this settles Tusnády's problem: the discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes is $Θ_d((\log N)^{d-1/2})$ in every fixed dimension $d\ge2$. The proof combines smoothed product test functions, sampling discretization, and an entropy argument for conditioned Gaussian vectors. The matching upper and lower bounds are also formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: When optimized geometries are not optimal: Implications for inverted singlet-triplet gap predictions
papers.abstract: Pseudo-Jahn-Teller distortions can substantially alter singlet-triplet gaps, potentially reversing the predicted excited-state ordering in molecules proposed to exhibit inverted singlet-triplet (INVEST) gaps. In this study, we benchmark geometry optimization methods for 13 azaphenalenes against CCSD(T)-quality reference geometries, assessing their ability to reproduce symmetry lowering and its consequences for singlet-triplet gaps. Among the methods examined, $ω$B97M-D4 reliably describes the distorted geometries and corresponding gaps, whereas the commonly used methods B3LYP and MP2 retain high-symmetry structures, potentially leading to false-positive INVEST assignments. We further assess $ω$B97M-D4 geometries across 337 molecules comprising azaphenalenes, boron/nitrogen-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and non-alternant hydrocarbons. Subsequent L-CC2/aug-cc-pVDZ calculations predict negative singlet-triplet gaps for 85 molecules and identify discrepancies with previously reported INVEST assignments. These findings demonstrate that the choice of geometry optimization method is crucial for reliable INVEST screening, particularly in systems susceptible to symmetry-breaking distortions.

papers.title: Combinatorial Boolean Matrix Multiplication in $n^3 / 2^{Ω(\sqrt{\log n})}$ Time
papers.abstract: For over fifty years, combinatorial algorithms for Boolean matrix multiplication (BMM) and triangle detection saved only polylogarithmic factors over cubic time. At STOC 2024, Abboud, Fischer, Kelley, Lovett, and Meka broke this barrier with a deterministic $O(n^3 / 2^{Ω((\log n)^{1/7})})$-time algorithm, and asked whether $n^3 / 2^{Ω(\sqrt{\log n})}$ time is achievable. We answer this question in the affirmative, giving deterministic combinatorial algorithms for both BMM and triangle detection running in $O(n^3 / 2^{Ω(\sqrt{\log n})})$ time. Following Abboud et al., we decompose $(A,B)$ into pairs of submatrices $(A_k,B_k)$, called \emph{pieces}, each of which is either sparse or pseudorandom in a sense that forces $A_k\star B_k$ to be nearly all-ones on its vertex sets. Whereas their decomposition produces $2^{O(d^7)}$ pieces at regularity parameter $d$, we obtain $2^{O(d^2)}$ pieces, directly improving the runtime exponent from $(\log n)^{1/7}$ to $\sqrt{\log n}$. Prior work found pseudorandom pieces by repeatedly restricting to denser submatrices, paying worst-case vertex losses at each step that compounded across nested recursion levels, together with an expensive derandomization step. We eliminate the extra powers of $d$ by matching the vertex loss at each step to the size of its density jump so losses telescope across scales, derandomizing witness search via $L_d$-norm estimation so the sampler length stays $2^{O(d)}$, and bounding overlap across the recursion with a fractional density-weighted volume budget rather than raw submatrix volume.

papers.title: The determinantal complexity of the 4*4 permanent is 15
papers.abstract: The best known lower bound on the determinantal complexity of the 4x4 permanent is 10. In this short note, I prove that this value is exactly 15: the 4x4 permanent is the determinant of a 15x15 matrix of affine linear forms, and cannot be that of any smaller matrix. To do so, I must establish both a lower and upper bound. To establish the upper bound, I use Grenet's construction of size 2^n-1. Hence that construction is optimal at n=4 (and n=3). This now constitutes the first knwon exact value of the determinantal complexity of the permanent at n=4. Only the value at n=3 was exactly known, prior to this note. The general quadratic bound only gives 8 for n=4. To establish the lower bound, I work from a normal form at a zero of the permanent. In the first row (and column) of the normal form, the linear forms vanish on a linear space inside the singular locus of the permanent. A hessian inequality bounds the size of the matrix in terms of that space. Then, a matrix of sie 14 foces the space into any of nine corordinate types. The forcing is either up to symmetry, or else into a family that degenerates to one of them. I then rule out every case. All involved computations are exact. In respect of the claim, I have made all certificates public.

papers.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
papers.abstract:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups, given one named hypothesis that is a theorem of that library, so that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.05.

papers.title: Ideals of 2-minors of nearly determinantal matrices
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of prime binomial ideals with Cohen--Macaulay quotients and linear resolutions, we introduce nearly determinantal matrices, a class of matrices obtained by repeating variables from the preceding rows in the last row. We characterize the primality of their ideals of $2$-minors in terms of an associated directed graph with row labels. For every prime case, we prove that the quotient is a normal Cohen--Macaulay domain and determine its graded Betti numbers. Finally, a prime ideal in this family has a linear resolution if and only if the matrix has three rows or two columns.

papers.title: NaijaFacts: A Framework for Disentangling Language from Knowledge in Facts about Nigeria
papers.abstract: Multilingual benchmarks for African languages mostly translate generic questions into local languages, measuring linguistic competence but not whether models know facts about Africa. We introduce NaijaFacts, a benchmark of factual and statistical questions about Nigeria, authored by native speakers and grounded in authoritative official statistics, with every question available in English, Nigerian Pidgin, Yorùbá, Igbo, and Hausa. Answering similar questions for the UK and US yields a country by language matrix that disentangles a language effect (the model knows the fact but degrades in a low-resource language) from a knowledge effect (the fact is absent in every language). Across eight frontier and Nigeria-adapted models, the knowledge effect dominates: English-query accuracy is 49-50% for the US/UK but 20% for Nigeria. The language effect is smaller and tracks web representation, degrading from English to Yorùbá (9 points on Nigeria, up to 24 on US/UK questions). We find scale does not help: the strongest models reach 66-79% on the UK and the US but none exceed 31% on Nigerian statistics. Extending to all 54 African countries with our best performing frontier model shows the same profile continent-wide, 96% on culture and 98% on politics against 26% on statistics, so the gap is not specific to Nigeria.

papers.title: Model Merging Does Not Require Uniform LoRA Ranks
papers.abstract: Model merging combines separately fine-tuned experts into a single model without retraining. Standard practice trains every expert at the same LoRA rank, which couples the rank choice across experts even though each domain has its own best rank. We show this coupling is a property of the merge method, not of merging. We train 36 experts on three domains (mathematics, instruction following, multilingual) at four ranks and three model scales, then merge with six methods at uniform ranks and at each domain's own best rank. Giving experts different ranks costs averaging and utility-based selection nothing, and gains them up to 1.8 pp of multi-domain accuracy, while the conflict-resolution methods are inconsistent and can lose up to 4 pp. The split has a simple cause. Merging keeps only a fixed share of the pooled spectral components, and methods that choose them by size discard many that would have reduced loss. They also tend to discard the same expert: the instruction adapter has the smallest singular values, so it is dropped almost entirely and IFEval falls by 16 to 25 pp. Choosing components by their effect on loss instead keeps all three experts, and leaves accuracy nearly flat across an 8$\times$ rank range (0.7 pp, against 6.7 pp for TIES at 4B scale). Rank can therefore be chosen per expert whenever the merge operator does not select by magnitude.

papers.title: ARIA: Anti-diagonal Reduced-cost Index-masked Adaptive BLMS Algorithm
papers.abstract: The block least-mean-square (BLMS) algorithm supports high-throughput adaptive filtering but incurs high computational cost as the filter length and block size increase. This letter proposes anti-diagonal reduced-cost index-masked (ARIA) adaptive BLMS, which reduces coefficient-update multiplications through anti-diagonal index masking and tap-wise step-size scaling while keeping the filtering exact. Mean-square error (MSE) analysis establishes an explicit step-size bound, and misadjustment. An extension, ARIA-MF (ARIA with masked filtering), also applies the mask during filtering; its analysis shows that the excess MSE is redistributed across block rows while its block average is approximately preserved. Simulations validate the analysis and shows very good agreement with the estimates

papers.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
papers.abstract: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).

papers.title: EEGDash Corpus: A Training-Ready Public Corpus for EEG Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on tens of thousands of hours. The largest clinical archives restrict redistribution, while public datasets use different formats and licences. Here, we rebuild the 77 redistributable datasets of the REVE pretraining corpus that reach its 200 Hz input (14,075 hours across 7,272 subjects) and release them as eegdash-corpus-v0, with raw-file access by name through EEGDash and a checksummed Zarr store on Hugging Face, converted with REVE's preprocessing recipe. Every dataset keeps its licence, and any subset of datasets can be selected by name. To test whether this public store pretrains REVE-Base, we train the model twice from scratch with REVE's trainer and score it on seven public OpenEEGBench tasks. First, under linear probing, the frozen encoder reaches 0.331 in chance-adjusted balanced accuracy, against 0.333 for the released model (untrained: 0.200), a difference smaller than the spread between our two pretraining seeds. Second, after fine-tuning, it reaches 0.273 against 0.325 published (0.301 in our rerun), and part of this gap comes from the scoring pipeline. A public, training-ready EEG corpus can therefore pretrain the frozen representations of a foundation model and provide a shared base that other groups can audit.

papers.title: SonoDyno: A Sonic Dynamometer for Engine Speed and Load Estimation from Audio
papers.abstract: Controllable engine sound synthesis, Active Sound Design and engine order analysis all build on the relationship between the sound of an engine and its momentary operating state: its speed and its load. Recordings of engine sound are abundant in archives, sample packs and online video, yet they rarely carry time-aligned annotations of that state, which limits their applicability to controllable engine sound generation. We present SonoDyno, which estimates the engine speed, the cylinder count and an engine-normalized load intensity from a microphone signal alone, with no tachometer, no bus access and no prior knowledge of the engine configuration. A convolutional scorer of 124,302 parameters reads the energy at the engine orders, the harmonics of half the rotation frequency, in each frame at three time-frequency resolutions to jointly score cylinder count and speed, and a decoder imposes the rotational dynamics of the engine on the speed trajectory. A second head estimates the load intensity, the position of the torque between the engine's drag floor at 0 and its full-load ceiling at 1, from the order levels at the decoded speed. On recordings of engines it has never heard, with microphone position, engine type and cylinder count unknown, SonoDyno places 93 to 97% of the frames within 2% of the true speed, identifies the cylinder count with 80% accuracy and confuses the octave on fewer than 2% of the frames. On an unseen engine of a known type, the load intensity has a mean absolute error of 0.12, and the sign of the torque, driving or braking, is right on 91% of the frames. General pitch trackers fall behind even when the harmonic order of each engine is supplied: on our validation recordings and at a tolerance of 5%, the best of them places 62% of the frames within the tolerance, against 96% for SonoDyno.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the IPM equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ via isopycnal coordinates
papers.abstract: We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. We prove that the stably stratified state, in which heavier fluid lies below lighter fluid, is nonlinearly stable: small perturbations decay over time and the fluid returns to equilibrium. Our result holds in the sharp Sobolev setting $H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ for every $s>2$: this threshold cannot be improved, since the equation is ill-posed in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$. This result follows from a proof of global well-posedness at critical Besov regularity, with smallness required only in a norm invariant under the natural scaling of the equation. We also prove optimal decay rates for suitably localized initial data. The main difficulty is that the stabilizing effect of stratification acts only in some directions, while the nonlinear transport acts in all of them. Reaching the sharp regularity threshold requires two main novelties. First, we rewrite the equation in \emph{isopycnal coordinates}, which follow the level sets of the density: in these coordinates the transport becomes one-dimensional, and the anisotropic stabilizing mechanism can be exploited at minimal regularity. Second, we establish new \emph{anisotropic commutator estimates} which allow us to control the remaining nonlinear terms. Finally, we show that the estimates obtained in isopycnal coordinates can be transferred back to the original variables.

papers.title: Fano's Inequality and Channel Capacity in the Individual-Sequence Regime
papers.abstract: We derive an individual-sequence analogue of Fano's inequality, replacing entropy by Lempel--Ziv (LZ) complexity and probability of error by empirical error frequency. In the setting considered, an arbitrary encoder maps a message to a channel input sequence $\{x_t\}$, the channel maps the input to an output $\{y_t\}$ in a completely arbitrary manner, and a block finite-state decoder produces an estimate of the channel input from the output. The individual-sequence Fano inequality lower-bounds the empirical symbol-error frequency in terms of the LZ complexity of the channel input conditioned on the channel output. This leads to a channel coding converse: reliable communication at a given rate is possible only if that rate does not exceed the individual-sequence LZ channel capacity, defined as the LZ mutual information maximized over channel inputs and minimized (worst-case) over a noise set. We also prove a matching achievability theorem for the class of \emph{symbol-wise invertible} channels, in which the channel output at each time $t$ is $y_t = f(x_t, v_t)$, $v_t$ being a `noise' variable, and $f(\cdot,v)$ is a bijection for every fixed $v$. This class includes group-additive channels $y_t = x_t \oplus v_t$ studied by Feder and coworkers. For such a channel, any rate below the LZ capacity is achievable via a randomized code (with shared randomness between encoder and decoder) with vanishing \emph{expected} per-message error frequency, simultaneously for every $v^n$ in a given noise set $\mathcal{N}$, provided $\mathcal{N}$ is closed under block permutations; this condition is satisfied by any noise set that depends on $v^n$ only via its type class with respect to such blocks. The achievability uses a universal decoder that requires no knowledge of the channel and no feedback.

papers.title: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization
papers.abstract: Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through this transport-information correspondence, UCN quantifies the information-theoretic cost associated with discretization in terms of the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions characterized by the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we generalize the local-map discretization framework by allowing an arbitrary representative point for each cell and establish an exact decomposition of the associated transport cost into contributions from the conditional covariance of the probability distribution and the displacement of the representative point from its probability-weighted centroid. Consequently, the resulting transport cost is exactly represented by the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus establishes an exact transport-information correspondence for finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded sets.

papers.title: The integral Chow rings of $\mathcal A_3$ and $\mathcal M_3$
papers.abstract: Over $\mathbb C$, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal A_3$, the moduli stack of principally polarized abelian threefolds. Along the way, we compute the integral Chow ring of $\mathcal M_3$, the moduli stack of smooth genus-three curves. The ring $\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal A_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, along with three classes supported on the locus of decomposable abelian varieties, subject to 16 relations. The ring $\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal M_3)$ is generated by the Chern classes of the Hodge bundle, with five relations. In particular, we find that the top Chern class of the Hodge bundle, $λ_3$, has order 504 on $\mathcal A_3$ and 252 on $\mathcal M_3$. For $\mathcal A_3$, this removes the factor of 4 from the bound $252\mid\operatorname{ord}(λ_3)\mid 1008$ of Ekedahl and van der Geer.

papers.title: Community Search under Member-Specific Tolerances
papers.abstract: We study community search when each member has its own tolerance for differences in position, as when members of a group interact repeatedly and influence one another. A latitude-consistent community (LCC) contains the query vertex, is connected, has minimum degree at least k, and bounds its diameter by the smallest member tolerance. The bound is exactly the condition under which every interaction in a connected closed group stays accepted under bounded-confidence dynamics for every choice of positive weights. It also prevents rejection under social-judgment dynamics, whereas the pairwise condition and other natural relaxations preserve neither guarantee. Finding a maximum LCC is NP-hard even in the plane, and with unbounded dimension, deciding whether an LCC exists is NP-complete for every fixed k>=2. LatSweep fixes the answer's smallest tolerance and turns the coupled bound into a best-first sweep over candidate thresholds, yielding an exact branch-and-bound algorithm, a (1,2)-bicriteria approximation and two feasible heuristics. Across eight graphs with up to 1.8 billion edges, six with synthetic positions and tolerances, the exact algorithm proves optimality on all but 9 of 3,700 efficiency queries; in a shared implementation on two large graphs, its branch-and-bound solver proves more queries than a reimplemented maximum-(k,r)-core algorithm, a mixed-integer program and CP-SAT. In simulations of closed groups, LCC groups keep every accepted interaction under uneven influence, whereas 3-40% of pairwise-compatible groups lose some. On three location-based networks, tolerance-agnostic groups often place another member's home beyond a member's estimated travel radius. Enforcing every member's tolerance causes no measurable loss of co-visits relative to spatial communities of the same size. Relative to the larger pairwise-compatible groups, it can cause a size-adjusted loss.

papers.title: Dual Flow: Joint Image-Measurement Interpolation for Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Generative model-based approaches to linear inverse problems typically use the acquired noisy measurement to condition or guide sampling in the image domain. In this work, we introduce Dual Flow, a novel joint-flow model for solving linear inverse problems by jointly estimating the clean image and corresponding noise-free measurement from the observation. Specifically, Dual Flow formulates image reconstruction and measurement denoising as a coupled estimation problem, using coupled flows in the image and measurement domains. The acquired noisy measurement is used only to initialize the measurement state; thereafter, image and measurement states are jointly updated based on their current values. By construction, the final image and measurement estimates are guaranteed to satisfy the underlying forward model. We derive the sampling updates for the joint-flow which involves the conditional mean of the clean image given the joint state. We further derive a closed-form expression for a sufficient statistic of the joint state and show that the required conditional mean can be obtained by solving an image-domain Gaussian denoising problem involving operator-dependent, correlated noise. We train a velocity-prediction network using this formulation to estimate the conditional mean from the derived sufficient statistic. Extensive experiments across various linear inverse problems and image datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both distortion metrics and perceptual quality. Dual Flow requires no hyperparameter tuning beyond the number of inference steps and achieves shorter reconstruction times than competing methods. Additional analyses assess robustness to model mismatch, as well as the ability to generate diverse plausible reconstructions and characterize reconstruction uncertainty.

papers.title: A General Theory of Dynamic Mechanism Design: Joint Optimization of Contracting, Information-Production Technology, and Disclosure
papers.abstract: We develop a general theory of dynamic mechanism design that jointly optimizes contracting, information-production technology, and disclosure across a broad class of economic environments with general allocation constraints. Hidden actions, endogenous information acquisition, learning, and disclosure interact through dynamic incentives. We accommodate correlated private information, interdependent preferences, and potentially infinite-dimensional allocations. We introduce joint consistent perfect Bayesian equilibrium, establish a dynamic revelation principle, and recursively characterize incentive compatibility. Under private values with informational interdependence, we characterize joint incentives through choice optimality, reporting-envelope first-order conditions, and global integral monotonicity. We derive an exact dynamic information-rent identity, conditional revenue equivalence, and dynamic virtual surplus. Comparing first-best, two second-best, and third-best contracts distinguishes information rents, hidden-action implementation costs, and direct information-production expenditures, revealing nonadditive interactions of either sign and branched outcomes. Applications show Milgrom-Weber revenue-ranking reversal with endogenous acquisition, no efficient first-price equilibrium under Gaussian signals, and absent, interior, or full financial-contract disclosure.

papers.title: Lusztig sheaves, local systems, and the extended Springer resolution
papers.abstract: The Springer resolution of the nilpotent cone is used to give a geometric construction of the Springer correspondence by applying tools in the derived category of perverse sheaves, particularly the decomposition theorem. In this paper we continue earlier work of the authors on the extended Springer resolution, a map introduced by the first author that factors through the Springer resolution. Our first main result shows that applying the decomposition theorem to this map yields a sum of Lusztig sheaves in all Lie types, each corresponding to a triple of so-called minimal cuspidal datum. We also study the simple perverse sheaves that occur as summands of the resulting sheaf. Our second main result proves that every simple perverse sheaf corresponding to orbits that are Levi-regular must occur, generalizing earlier work in the type A setting to all Lie types.

papers.title: When can multi-fragment 2D/3D registration be trusted? Calibrated certification and uncertainty-driven view planning for pelvic fracture fluoroscopy
papers.abstract: Registering a segmented CT to fluoroscopy can locate every fracture fragment but can guide surgery only when trusted. After each shot, our closed loop registers all fragments, bounds their errors with a calibrated sandwich covariance, flags implausible or ambiguous ones, and stops or plans the next view. On simulated fluoroscopy of 60 held-out fracture CTs with realistic image uncertainty, 95% bounds covered 83% of unflagged fragments and 91% of those within 5mm, but from the second view on 14% failed by over 5mm, a third with bounds of at most 2mm. A fragment's shift when a view was added separated tightly bounded failures best (exploratory; AUC 0.94, bound 0.81). Requiring that the newest view moved no fragment beyond its bound, preferred post hoc, lowered false stops at 2mm from 23% to 6% overall, with 345 instead of 362 correct ones but more trajectories uncertified; delaying the stop did not, and other signals at equal acceptance left 10-15% false. With a segmentation error shared by all views (median Dice 0.89), 21% of this rule's stops were false against 10% without it (15 cases; exploratory). Minimax planning certified sooner than the clinical protocol without the check (4.20 versus 4.72 shots, Holm p <0.001), but no criterion reached the pre-specified endpoint, a true 2mm error, significantly sooner, even in the true basin. On real fluoroscopy of five intact pelves no 2mm certificate was false. Trust takes evidence across views, not only a calibrated local bound.

papers.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges on Small Evaluation Sets
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge is a common substitute for costly human evaluation, and aggregating several judges is the standard remedy for any single judge's bias. Judge pools mix judges of very different reliability, while the human-labeled sets that validate them hold a few hundred items or fewer. In this regime the per-item mean weights weak judges as heavily as strong ones, and confusion-table models such as Dawid-Skene must estimate a per-judge error table from too few items. We propose AGORA (Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments), an item-response-theory aggregator that places every item on one latent quality scale and describes each judge by a sensitivity parameter and ordered rating thresholds, so judge reliability is learned from all items jointly and without human labels. Across three benchmarks, AGORA matches or exceeds Dawid-Skene on large evaluation sets, and its advantage widens as the set shrinks toward a few hundred items. It remains accurate as pools grow more uneven, a label-free dispersion statistic indicates in advance when trust weighting helps, and its learned trust weights track per-judge human validity. Code is available at https://github.com/JunhyungAhn/llm-as-judge-irt.

papers.title: Neuromorphic Camera for Multi-Target Pointing Acquisition and Tracking in Free Space Optical Communication
papers.abstract: Pointing, Acquisition, and Tracking (PAT) in Free-Space Optical Communication (FSOC) applications must achieve both low jitter and a large Field of View (FoV) to support beacon acquisition and multi-target tracking. While conventional frame-based sensors provide the necessary angular coverage, their performance is limited by latency, available frame-rate, and motion blur. This work explores and demonstrates the application of an event-based vision sensor for PAT tasks in FSOC. The system employs a neuromorphic sensor that asynchronously records brightness changes (events) with microsecond-level temporal resolution. The main contribution of this paper is a comparative analysis of event-based tracking algorithms for the simultaneous acquisition and tracking of multiple optical beacons that operate directly on this asynchronous stream. The performance of these strategies is validated on an experimental dataset representing realistic operational conditions for dynamic High-Altitude Platform (HAP) and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks. The analysis compares key metrics, such as tracking accuracy and processing latency, under various signal-to-background conditions.

papers.title: Ranking and Unranking Permutations in Heap's Order
papers.abstract: Heap's algorithm is a permutation generation method with very low constant overhead. Its element-interchanging mechanism, however, prevents the standard factorial-base Lehmer code from being applied directly, and to our knowledge no explicit Rank/Unrank algorithm for the Heap order has been published. This paper describes the block structure of Heap's algorithm in terms of rearrangement operators: the net effect of a block-internal traversal is a tail-preserving operator and the block-boundary swap is a top-level swap operator, and together they yield a closed-form recurrence for the block transitions. On this basis a bottom-up Unrank algorithm and a top-down Rank algorithm are built from one and the same closed-form in-block mapping; both run in $O(n^2)$ time and $O(n)$ space and require no factorial-scale precomputed table. The supporting proofs use a synchronized strong induction on the dimension to establish the bijectivity of the trailing-element mapping, closed forms for the final arrangement and for the trailing sequence, the dichotomy of its cycle structure, and the reciprocity of Rank and Unrank. The Heap order is in fact the colex order of the mixed-radix code.

papers.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
papers.abstract: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every nonlinearity is a quadratic detection - an interference, a balanced reading or a camera - and the output is a Born probability: attention |<q|k>|^2, the form of the Born rule, normalised per row, a measured product for the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout; between detections, classical control rescales and re-encodes. With its denominators held at the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share to 10^-13. On e-SNLI natural language inference it reaches 77.45 +- 0.91 % accuracy, level with a same-size softmax transformer (76.62 +- 0.36 %) and an order-free bag of embeddings (77.79 %). Exactness buys the sum, not the best ranking. Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 44 % of pairs, of the 53 % some deletion changes, against 31-32 % for the softmax model's integrated gradients; the model's own gradient x input does as well (43 %), as does a bag of embeddings' (43 %, seed 0), and leave-one-out does better. Holding the denominators helps the low end: the five words ranked last change the answer in 1 %, against 6 % free. The same weights compile exactly to simulated optoelectronics, and their attention to qubits. On ibm_kingston, reading only the attention, the device gave the model's answers in all three Hadamard-test runs (the two shortest pairs and one without its deciding word) and both compute-uncompute runs (one circuit per overlap); uniform attention answers otherwise on two of the three inputs. With the device's row sums the evidence correlated with the exact one at 0.997 and 0.962 by Hadamard tests; with compute-uncompute, 0.971 and 0.48.

papers.title: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models
papers.abstract: Visual place recognition (VPR) localises a camera by retrieving similar geo-tagged images, and current foundation-model VPR models are accurate across cities, seasons and illumination, but not robust to adversarial perturbations: under a white-box attack on the ranking at an imperceptible budget of 1/255, SuperVLAD and BoQ keep at most 0.2% top-1 recall (R@1) on four benchmarks. We propose anchored rank-adversarial fine-tuning (ARAFT), which fine-tunes a released model with a listwise rank loss on each adversarial query's hardest positive and an anchor to the clean descriptor of the frozen pretrained model. Checkpoints are selected under a clean-accuracy budget fixed in advance, and the full trade-off is reported. Within five validation R@1 points of clean cost, plain adversarial training has no admissible checkpoint, whereas ARAFT raises robust R@1 from zero to 47.3 on SuperVLAD and 55.3 on BoQ; plain adversarial training exceeds this only at about three times the clean cost. Against unbudgeted plain adversarial training on the test sets, ARAFT matches its robust R@1 at 2/255 with about ten more clean R@1 points. At 4/255, plain adversarial training is 6-9 robust R@1 points ahead, while ARAFT still keeps its ten-point clean advantage. Developed on SuperVLAD, ARAFT transfers to BoQ without re-tuning, and its robustness holds against stronger optimisers, with no sign of gradient masking.

papers.title: Geometric Classification of Imaginaries in Lovely Pairs of Pseudofinite Fields
papers.abstract: In [Pil07], Pillay showed that every imaginary in a proper pair of algebraically closed fields is interalgebraic with an imaginary of a certain algebraic form. In this paper, we establish an analogue for lovely pairs of pseudofinite fields. After naming countably many constants, we prove that every imaginary in lovely pairs of pseudofinite fields is interalgebraic with an imaginary of the same algebraic form as [Pil07] in the corresponding pairs of finite extensions of pseudofinite fields.

papers.title: Diffusion Plug-in Priors for Self-Supervised Ultrasound Video Restoration
papers.abstract: Ultrasound videos suffer from hardware-constrained spatial resolution and signal-dependent speckle, while paired low- and high-resolution acquisitions are rarely available. We propose UltraDiff, a self-supervised framework for joint ultrasound video super-resolution and despeckling that uses a frozen pre-trained diffusion model as a plug-in prior. Rather than retraining the model, UltraDiff restores each frame by optimizing the sampler's latent seed under a range-constrained maximum a posteriori-inspired formulation. We derive a speckle-aware data-fidelity term from a Rayleigh scale-family model and characterize its relative-residual and locally variance-adaptive weighting properties. To address degeneracy near zero intensities, we introduce a stabilized surrogate fidelity that is bounded below and strictly convex in log intensity for positive observations in its unclamped form. Total-variation regularization complements the removal of mixed noise, and a temporal seed update warm-starts each frame from the optimized seed of its predecessor, accelerating the convergence. On EchoNet-LVH with simulated speckle and additive noise, UltraDiff with a natural-image prior improves peak signal-to-noise ratio by 1.24\,dB over the strongest baseline, and ultrasound-related priors yield further gains. On 100 real EchoNet-Dynamic videos, UltraDiff reduces the mean absolute error of zero-shot ejection fraction prediction from 7.31 to 6.37 percentage points compared with DUP. These results support ground-truth-free ultrasound video restoration using frozen diffusion priors and a speckle-aware fidelity, without paired training data or model retraining.

papers.title: Rasterization-based discontinuous integration on the GPU
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a method based on rasterization in computer graphics for the integration of discontinuous functions accurately and efficiently on the GPU. The proposed method takes advantage of the massively parallel architecture of GPUs via a modified graphics pipeline, where discontinuities are encoded through geometric primitives and processed in the rasterization stage, and multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) is used to improve integration accuracy across subdomain interfaces. We present both hardware- and software-based pipelines and compare their performance in terms of accuracy as well as computational effort on modern GPU hardware with adaptive quadrature on the CPU. For the tested hardware, at approximately comparable median relative error, the hardware pipeline is up to around $100\text{x}$ faster than adaptive quadrature, while the single- and double-precision software pipelines achieve up to $840\text{x}$ and $1200\text{x}$ speedups compared to their adaptive quadrature counterparts. We use the finite cell method as model problem, where cutcells represent discontinuous integrands at the interface of the physical and fictitious domains and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method using numerical benchmarks. The end-to-end finite cell solution runtime is reduced by a factor of $8.3$ to $9.5$ in the single-precision pipeline and by a factor of $62$ to $72$ in the double-precision pipeline at the prescribed integration settings. Therefore, results indicate that the rasterization-based integration method is a promising alternative for the accurate and efficient integration of discontinuous functions in demanding applications on the GPU.

papers.title: Comment on "Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings" (arXiv:2610.26833)
papers.abstract: We discuss the relationship between quantum Hamiltonian embeddings (arXiv:2610.26833) and prior developments in Quantum Cognition Machine Learning (QCML), including QCML's earlier implementation on IBM quantum hardware. We examine the novelty claims and the computational role of encoding the training data in a shared ground state. We assess the scope of the trainability and generalization guarantees and identify missing comparisons with relevant classical alternatives. For the reported experimental model, whose inference is entirely classical, the paper does not establish a computational advantage for quantum training.

papers.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.

papers.title: Sheaf-MPNN: A Library for Sheaf Neural Networks as Message Passing
papers.abstract: Standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) implicitly assume that neighboring nodes share the same feature space, which contributes to oversmoothing and poor performance on heterophilic graphs. Sheaf Neural Networks (SNNs) remove this assumption by giving each node and edge its own vector space and learning restriction maps that transform features as they move between neighbors. These maps define a sheaf Laplacian that drives diffusion over the graph, but existing implementations often assemble it explicitly as a global sparse block matrix, which adds memory and computational overhead and can hinder scalability. In this paper, we introduce Sheaf-MPNN, a PyTorch Geometric library that reformulates sheaf diffusion as local incidence-wise transport and aggregation, eliminating the need to construct the global Laplacian. Sheaf-MPNN implements fifteen families of SNNs under a unified message-passing framework, each supporting both homogeneous and heterogeneous graphs, and directed and undirected settings, with diagonal, general, orthogonal, and low-rank restriction maps and attention-based predictors. We further provide a unified benchmarking suite covering node- and graph-level tasks, heterogeneous graph learning, and computational efficiency, enabling systematic and reproducible comparisons across architectures. We establish theoretical equivalence between these message-passing formulations and their original counterparts and identify the architectural mechanisms needed to preserve their propagation dynamics. This unified perspective provides a principled foundation for implementing, comparing, and extending sheaf-based architectures within standard graph learning frameworks. Source code is available at https://github.com/alessioborgi/sheaf-mpnn.

papers.title: TxBench: Verifying Public Incident Data to Benchmark Smart-Contract Attack Detectors
papers.abstract: Malicious transactions on smart contracts cause billions of dollars in losses. To evaluate their detectors, most datasets copy the attack transactions that public incident databases cite and pair them with random transactions. However, these databases never check their citations against execution, and random transactions rarely resemble attacks. We present TXBENCH, a benchmark that verifies both attacks and legitimate transactions against their execution. TXBENCH labels a cited transaction as an attack only when its execution takes value from others and independent evidence ties it to its incident. Its legitimate transactions perform the same operations as attacks and carry positive evidence of legitimacy. Applying these checks to two public databases, we find that they share only 10.6% of their 1,850 cited transactions and that only 1,012 are verifiable attacks, worth $868.2 million. A blind manual review confirms 98/100 sampled attacks and 100/100 legitimate transactions.

papers.title: When Listwise Deletion Works: Causal Diagrams and Complete-Case Regression
papers.abstract: Listwise deletion (LWD) appears more common than imputation: at least 50% of the observational causal studies we review in leading journals state or imply it, while 7% describe an imputation model. We develop a framework for when complete-case regression consistently estimates the population average treatment effect (ATE). With a constant unit-level treatment effect, two checks suffice: whether covariates and the missingness indicator satisfy the adjustment criterion in an augmented causal diagram (DAG), and whether the estimator pools within-covariate comparisons appropriately, possibly using inverse propensity weighting. A collider--mediator illustration highlights the first check: the same missing-at-random (MAR) mechanism can require different adjustment choices. With heterogeneous effects, conditional effects must be transportable to the population and be reweighted to its population distribution. These formal results provide practical checks for applied researchers to run complete case regressions, recover existing guidance as special cases, and are illustrated with applications across fields.

papers.title: A transition calculus for 0-pseudodifferential operators with applications to gas giant geometry
papers.abstract: A gas giant Riemannian metric $g$ on a compact $n$-dimensional manifold-with-boundary $M$ blows up at the boundary $\partial M$ at the rate $1/x^α$, for $α\in (0,2)$, where $x \in C^\infty(M)$ is a boundary-defining function. Such metrics arise in the modeling of acoustic waves in gaseous planets. De Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykkänen-Mazzeo [arXiv:2403.05475] showed that, if $α> 2/n$, the Laplace-Beltrami operator $Δ_g$ is essentially self-adjoint and has discrete spectrum. Moreover, its spectrum is stable under truncations of $M$. The proof leverages the 0-calculus of Mazzeo-Melrose. We extend this theory by introducing a 0-transition calculus for studying families of 0-operators. We demonstrate a parametrix construction for $Δ_g$ that is stable under truncations. Using this, we study the behavior of the resolvent of $Δ_g$ under truncation and extend the characterization of the spectrum obtained by de Hoop-Ilmavirta-Kykkänen-Mazzeo. In particular, we prove that (on appropriate functional-analytic domains) simple eigenvalues admit asymptotic expansions in the truncation parameter $ε$ and that the corresponding eigenfunctions admit joint asymptotic expansions in $(ε, x)$.

papers.title: Toward Quillen stratification for the odd primary Steenrod algebra
papers.abstract: Fix an odd prime $p$ and let $A$ be the mod $p$ Steenrod algebra. There is a normal sub-Hopf algebra $D$ of $A$, and we show that the cohomology of $A$ is $F$-isomorphic to the subalgebra of the cohomology of $D$ which is invariant under the $A$-action. We also show that the sub-Hopf algebras of $A$ with bounded profile function detect nilpotence in cohomology.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform
papers.abstract: The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.

papers.title: Evolved Spiking Neural Networks for EEG Seizure Detection: Calcium Dynamics and Delay Mechanics
papers.abstract: Neuroevolution can discover compact network designs that are hard to specify by hand. The EONS framework evolves the topology, weights, thresholds and delays of neuromorphic spiking networks without gradients. We tested whether giving integrate-and-fire (IF) neurons an activity-dependent calcium current (Ca-IF neurons) improves evolved networks for EEG seizure detection, with calcium parameters fixed, shared across a network, or evolved for each neuron. On 10 held-out CHB-MIT patients never seen in training, per-neuron calcium raised the record-level Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) from 0.592 to 0.726 over 20 independent runs (p = 0.008) and lowered the false-alarm rate from 0.17 to 0.10. Fixed or per-network calcium gave no significant benefit. IF networks with evolved synaptic delays of 1-3 ticks gave a similar gain (p = 0.005), whereas axonal delays did not. On Siena, with unchanged settings, per-neuron calcium gained +0.096 MCC over IF in one patient-disjoint split (p = 0.011) and +0.059 in the other (p = 0.052). These results suggest that calcium and delays may make the evolutionary search more effective, and motivate testing on more data and in neuromorphic hardware.

papers.title: Proceedings of the CSCW 2026 Workshop on Women's Health as Cooperative Work: Participatory AI Across Care, Community, and Policy
papers.abstract: This submission indexes contributions to the CSCW 2026 workshop, "Women's Health as Cooperative Work: Participatory AI Across Care, Community, and Policy," held on October 11, 2026. The workshop examines women's health as cooperative work spanning patients, caregivers, clinicians, communities, institutions, and digital technologies. Contributions explore participatory AI, coordination breakdowns, the distribution of care labor, governance, decision-making authority, and accountability across care, community, and policy contexts. The index provides paper titles, authors, affiliations, thematic areas, and unique report numbers to support discovery of the corresponding individual arXiv submissions. The workshop proposal is separately published under DOI 10.1145/3785651.3818821.

papers.title: Quantifying out-of-distribution data severity with Wasserstein distances: benchmarking large language models for alloy property prediction
papers.abstract: General-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rival domain-specific pipelines on scientific prediction, but their performance under distribution shift is untested. Across six alloy and crystal-structure datasets, we benchmark LLMs against traditional, BERT-based, TabPFN, and text-regression baselines under random cross-validation and six out-of-distribution (OOD) protocols shifting input and target distributions, with severity quantified via a standardized Wasserstein distance. We isolate the LLM's advantage over k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) retrieval: it beats k-NN on all eight tasks at a fixed 5% reference budget, on seven of eight when independently optimized, and in 72.5% of 120 OOD task--protocol configurations against an optimized baseline. No model family is uniformly best; the LLM is often strongest under severe shift, and error increases with target-space but not representation-space severity. Self-reported LLM confidence tracks both shift and error, more consistently than a density-only control from the same retrieved samples, and a matched-cohort check finds no substantial evidence of memorization.

papers.title: LOLPlay: Benchmarking Real-Time Visual Agents in League of Legends
papers.abstract: Visual agents need to coordinate reasoning and action while their environment evolves during inference. We introduce LOLPlay, a benchmark in native League of Legends with 36 champion-specific tasks spanning resource management, combat, cooperation, and objectives. Agents interact through screenshots and mouse-keyboard actions; automated initialization and 82 executable subgoal checks distinguish partial progress from completion. Across 324 task evaluations of three models at three reasoning-effort settings, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate of 25.0% at low and medium effort, and the highest subgoal success rate of 40.3% at medium effort. However, high effort improves neither metric over low effort for any model. For Astra, longer requests leave fewer interaction rounds, suggesting a cost to additional reasoning in real-time control. Trajectories reveal incomplete subgoal composition and actions executing after the observed scene changes, motivating agents that combine visual reasoning with timely action.

papers.title: Automatic Generation of Novel Highly-Functional Molecular Sequences
papers.abstract: While multiple methods now exist to generate functional sequence variants from existing annotated examples, it is unclear how well such methods can be used to generate sequences that exceed the functionality of those contained in the example set. Using two complete fitness landscapes, we quantify how effectively generative tools can search sequence space and find rare, novel, highly functional sequences, focusing on variational auto-encoders and information-theoretic methods. We find that an information-theoretic method that does not require training and runs significantly faster than standard Machine-Learning/Artificial Intelligence (ML/AI) methods also is significantly more effective in finding rare highly-functional sequences. We discuss the application of this novel method to discover rare polypeptides with anti-bacterial properties that are specific to bacterial, but not eukaryotic, cell membranes.

papers.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
papers.abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

papers.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
papers.abstract: We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful solution strategies. The second stage extends these capabilities to tool-dependent reasoning through a scalable pipeline for constructing diverse and automatically verifiable tasks grounded in real-world data sources and deterministic computation. Finally, reinforcement learning further strengthens long-horizon reasoning and interaction with external tools and environments. Despite this compact training recipe, Axion 1.0 achieves strong performance across a broad suite of agentic benchmarks and is competitive with leading commercial models on several of them. Equally importantly, Axion 1.0 is open beyond model weights: we release the complete recipe, including data construction, generation, filtering, verification, prompts, and training code, enabling the entire development process to be reproduced and extended. Axion 1.0 demonstrates that strong agent foundation models can be both open and simple, offering a practical and reproducible path toward advancing open agentic intelligence.

papers.title: The quantum magic of top quarks
papers.abstract: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.

papers.title: Harnessing Mutual Coupling in Cell-Free mMIMO
papers.abstract: This letter investigates a cell-free massive MIMO system with $L$ access points (APs), each employing a small fixed-form-factor, uniform linear array of $N$ potentially closely spaced antennas. Utilizing multiport communication theory, we analyze the impact of mutual coupling on uplink and downlink spectral efficiency (SE) under various impedance-matching strategies. We compare two deployment regimes: ($i$) increasing $N$ while $L$ is kept fixed, and ($ii$) increasing $N$ while fixing the total antenna count $M = NL$. Numerical results show that, with a full matching network, mutual coupling itself becomes beneficial when an AP serves several user equipments, which is the typical operating regime of user-centric cell-free networks. Furthermore, with full matching, antenna densification can enhance SE or allow for a reduction in the number of APs without performance loss. Since full matching networks remain of manageable size in the small arrays of distributed APs, unlike in large centralized arrays, cell-free networks offer a natural setting for exploiting mutual coupling.

papers.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
papers.abstract: We study strong positivity and Hodge--Riemann relations for real $(1,1)$-forms satisfying generalized $m$-positivity conditions. We prove that every good prefix, defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant, has a strictly strongly positive product and satisfies the Hodge--Riemann relations in every bidegree. Allowing factors on the boundaries of these cones, we show that the hyperbolicity cone of every nonzero prefix product equals the polarizing component of its natural exterior-algebra quotient. This gives the full mixed Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary $m$-positive forms without a semipositivity assumption. We also prove the relations for weakly $(m,l)$-positive forms, defined by $(m-l)$-positivity on every codimension-$l$ subspace, when $p+q\le m$ and $\max\{p,q\}\ge l$. For $l=1$ and $m\ge2$, the associated $(m-1)$-th power map is a diffeomorphism from the weak $(m,1)$-positive cone onto the positive $(d-1,d-1)$-cone. For smooth closed forms satisfying the ordinary, weak $(m,l)$-positive, or good-prefix hypotheses pointwise, Dinh--Nguyên's method gives the corresponding hard Lefschetz theorems and Hodge--Riemann relations on the cohomology of compact Kähler manifolds. We also discuss numerical criteria, generalized Hessian equations, and intersection inequalities for generalized $m$-positive forms.

papers.title: An Experimental Study of Hybrid Retrieval, NLI and Open-source LLMs for Scientific Claim Verification
papers.abstract: Claim verification is the task of deciding whether a source text supports a claim, contradicts it, or lacks sufficient evidence. Natural Language Inference (NLI) models can judge whether a single sentence supports or contradicts a claim, but they struggle when the evidence is spread across several sentences. Conversely, Large Language Models (LLMs) can reason across sentences, but may draw conclusions the text does not support. In this experimental study, we test whether a conservative fusion rule, labeling a claim Support or Contradict only when both models agree and defaulting to Not Enough Evidence otherwise, combines their strengths. We construct a benchmark of 2,035 claims from SciFact and CliniFact (858 Support, 152 Contradict, 1,025 Not Enough Evidence). We retrieve the top five most relevant sentences per claim using a hybrid of semantic and lexical (BM25) retrieval, which slightly outperforms either method alone. These retrieved sentences are then provided to every verification model. We then compare a DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli NLI baseline against Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen3 8B, and Mistral 7B. Qwen3 achieves the highest Macro-F1 (0.7937), followed by Llama 3.1 (0.7204) and Mistral (0.6388), while the NLI baseline reaches only 0.3157. Contrary to our hypothesis, fusion degrades performance, dropping Macro-F1 to 0.7392, 0.6730, and 0.5991, respectively. To understand this decline, we analyze agreements, disagreements, and common error patterns between the NLI and LLM verifiers. Our error analysis shows that NLI and LLM disagreements often result in correct LLM predictions being overturned.

papers.title: Sharp Fréchet--Hoeffding Bounds under Selectively Incomplete Observation
papers.abstract: Incomplete records can sharpen bounds on joint outcome probabilities even when no pair of outcomes is jointly observed. I derive sharp pointwise Fréchet--Hoeffding bounds combining known population marginals with selectively observed records, without restricting the observation mechanism. I establish an exact reduction of the identification problem to finite-dimensional optimization, yielding computable characterizations of both bounds. Illustrations involving income mobility, potential outcomes, and split questionnaires demonstrate how incomplete records can improve identification relative to the classical bounds.

papers.title: VideoEditor-MoE: Scaling Complex Video Editing with Mixture of Experts
papers.abstract: Complex video editing requires understanding complex instructions while jointly fulfilling multiple editing requests. Meeting these demands through dense model scaling substantially increases computational cost. We introduce VideoEditor-MoE, the first open-source mixture-of-experts framework for video editing. Beyond sparse MLP-MoE layers, MoE-Attention expands attention capacity through routed key--value experts while preserving global interactions among video tokens. Initialized from a 5B video editing model, VideoEditor-MoE scales to 14B and 56B parameters, with approximately 8B parameters activated per token in both variants. Comparisons with existing methods and two complementary baselines, Explicit-MoE and MLP-MoE, assess its benefits over explicit expert guidance and MLP-only expert architectures. Further analyses demonstrate that all experts remain active and reveal that learned routing responds more strongly to sample content and diffusion noise levels than to human-defined editing categories. Spatial analysis further indicates sensitivity to object-level semantic features. We also identify decoupled weight decay as a strategy for stabilizing expert scaling.

papers.title: The maximum packing fraction of disordered bidisperse discs: theory and predictions
papers.abstract: Predicting the highest packing fraction that disordered packing of bidisperse discs can achieve, $ϕ_{max}$, is an important unresolved problem. Such a predictive theory is hindered by the density dependence on the packing protocol and by ensuring disorder. In bidisperse packings, this is more complicated because $ϕ_{max}$ is not a number but a function of the disc species size ratio, $D$, and one of the disc species concentration, $p$. These difficulties have been overcome in monodisperse disc packings by using the cell order distribution (COD)~\cite{Bl21}. Focusing on size ratios that prohibit rattlers, a COD-based theory is constructed here. It introduces bidisperse statistical closure equations, which combine an explicit disorder criterion with consistent cell and edge statistics, and yields $ϕ_{max}(p,D)$ and structural predictions. The a-priori disorder-guaranteeing criterion proposed here ensures fast exponential a decay of the occurrence probability of ordered clusters with size. Using a constrained maximum-entropy analysis to ensure maximum disorder, the occurrence probabilities of all the possible cell and edge configurations are derived in terms of $p$ and $D$ and they are found to be binomial. All the results are assembled to yield an exact prediction of $ϕ_{max}(p,D)$.

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VII. Step kinetics
papers.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the kinetics of attachment of new segments of the crystalline lattice (pyramids) at steps on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs(-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb(-1-1-1) surfaces. Diffusion species are gallium adatoms at high coverage or gallium adatoms connected with nonmetal atom creating stable pyramids. These pyramids arrive at the steps, and cannot be attached be directly because the Ga adatom at the pyramid base cannot be attached directly. Therefore they are incorporated into the step by additional nonmetal atoms glue atoms arriving from the vapor or detached from other segments of the surface terraces.

papers.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. VI. Surface diffusion on a nonmetal-terminated surface
papers.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate surface diffusion of adsorbates on the nonmetal-terminated surface of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. These surfaces are wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e. GaN(000-1) surface, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e. GaP(-1-1-1) gallium arsenide, GaAs (-1-1-1) and gallium antimonide GaSb (-1-1-1) surfaces. The mixed coverage consists of Ga adatoms in the first layer with a nonmetal atom attached above them forming a triangular-based pyramid. The pyramidal structures are stable during surface jumps involving rotations around one of the basal Ga adatoms. Thus, the diffusion proceeds via rotation (pivot) of the pair of the other basal Ga adatoms around an immobile Ga adatom moving them into new, originally empty sites. Using an energy-path determination procedure, the diffusion barriers were obtained as the difference between the initial site energy and the activated complex state energy. The detachment energy of the NM adatom was obtained assuming a final state in atomic and molecular form. The energy barrier for detachment to the atomic state is high for all atoms, on the order of 5 eV. For the molecular state these barriers are different: smaller for nitrogen, on the order of 1 eV, which is related to the high dissociation energy of the N2 molecule. For P and As the barrier is above 2 eV. For Sb it was not determined. Accordingly, the surface diffusion length is macroscopically large, indicating that all NM adatoms arrive at the steps.

papers.title: Recovering Missing Degrees of Freedom in Simulation-Trained Field-Level Generative Models
papers.abstract: Simulation-trained generative models are emerging as a powerful framework for field-level inference in cosmology, particularly in strongly nonlinear regimes where analytical approaches become intractable. However, the finite size of training datasets often leads to variance shrinkage, indicating that part of the realization-level variability of the underlying physical process is not captured by the learned generative dynamics. In this paper, we interpret variance shrinkage as a diagnostic of missing effective degrees of freedom and introduce physics-informed latent modifications to the generative dynamics of a continuous normalizing flow.
